in writing. it is in the interest of hungarian farmers that hungarian agriculture is guaranteed gmo-free. this objective is also enshrined in the hungarian constitution. the current gmo authorisation system is also very vulnerable to the preservation of gmo-free status. it's very difficult to install and maintain a protective dryer. on the one hand, very expensive scientific studies are needed to establish the protective formula, which the breeders do not add from their patented seeds. on the other hand, the decision to maintain the prohibitions is taken by the other member states on a proposal from the commission, on the basis of the opinion of the european food safety authority, which has always taken a positive stance on the gmo issue. the commission has always proposed the abolition of member states' safeguard quotas, against which it is almost impossible to obtain a qualified majority. the proposal for a new gmo licensing scheme, which will be voted on today, offers a much more secure opportunity than the current system to preserve the gmo-free status of hungarian agriculture. it would be easier to base a ban not only on environmental and health grounds but also on other grounds, including a number of agricultural grounds. this would make it much less likely to attack hungary for the ban in an international or national judicial forum than in the current situation. so it's very important to me that we have an effective tool in our hands as soon as possible that makes the ban simpler and more defensible than the current system. i therefore support the adoption of the proposal containing the agreement of the council and parliament.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your support. the new legislation on restricting the cultivation of gmos is a major step in the fight against gmos in europe. the result of a right and responsible decision. it was a success for all of us, one of the keys to which was the excellent austrian-hungarian-croatian cooperation. the result achieved is outstanding for hungary, as it allows our agriculture to be guaranteed at european level that it is free of gmos, as enshrined in the basic law. i would like to say that many of us would have liked to see more, stricter regulations. but we must admit that in the circumstances a realistic compromise has been reached. in fact, despite the continuing resistance of member states supporting the cultivation of gmos, the main objective of ensuring freedom of choice for member states was finally achieved. however, there is still a lot of work to be done in research and food safety, and the long-term health effects of gmos still need to be addressed. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to discuss the matter with the council. as the regulation of gmos shows, environmental protection is a european issue that does not stop at national borders. the safe cultivation of gmos in europe should be based on a dialogue between member states that choose gmos and those that reject them, based on mutual respect. the necessary measures should be taken to avoid cross-border pollution and responsibility for the damage caused should be assumed.
in writing. the new gmo regulation, which the european parliament is discussing at second reading following the agreement with the council of 4 december, gives member states more flexibility than the council's proposal to ban the cultivation of gmos, but represents a significant step back from the position adopted by parliament at first reading. the new directive can be counted as a partial success at most, but more likely as a failure. a number of important issues, such as damage from cross-border pollution and liability for damage caused by the cultivation of gm crops, remained open. the council has not been able to achieve a lasting and satisfactory solution to the latter question, namely the effective application of the 'polluter pays' principle, since it has unfortunately not supported the stricter position of parliament to require mandatory measures to prevent and control pollution. this is linked to the issue of financial liability for damages, mainly attributable to biotechnology companies, which is also only vaguely referred to in the final text. in practice, this means that the innocent party, i.e. the member state affected, its authority, farmers and taxpayers, can continue to bear the burden of pollution. the council should have been more decisive in defending the legitimate interests of the gmo-free member states. in addition, reform of the authorisation and risk assessment procedure at union level remains essential. we cannot allow the possibility of a ban by a member state to lead to a more superficial authorisation of gmos in the eu.
in writing. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and the survival of marine fish stocks is at risk. i support the proposal for a sustainable fisheries agreement between the european union and são tomé and príncipe, which seeks to place the west african tuna fisheries within a more sustainable framework than the one currently in place. the justified measures taken to maintain marine fish stocks have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not pose any threat to the natural values of these areas, unlike marine aquaculture areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability requirements. these are justified only for marine fisheries and aquaculture. in future, efforts should be made to clearly differentiate between the concept and regulation of marine and freshwater aquaculture.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos. i believe that there is still no complete consensus on gmos among member states or experts. this is also shown by the fact that this debate has been going on in the european parliament for five years now. progress has been made in this process, and it is not the end of the debate between those who oppose and those who support the cultivation of gmos. i believe that member states should be given the right to restrict the cultivation of gmos, and that requires a uniform directive. i think it is right that the member states should have more room for manoeuvre on gmos and should be able to set the level of restriction they wish in a transparent manner. in addition, restrictions will also apply in the defined border zones of neighbouring countries. uniform regulation can also address concerns in member states about legal attacks on biotech companies. of course, the member states have a great deal of responsibility for implementation, and deadlines must be met and respected. in this respect, the eu institutions are also bound by obligations, such as those in trade agreements. they should be negotiated in a coherent way, as is the case with the current ttip. the right of member states to prohibit the cultivation/marketing of gmos for health reasons, in order to conserve biodiversity and ecosystems should be maintained after the conclusion of trade agreements.

in writing. the european parliament's environment committee wants to get a political resolution adopted by parliament calling on the european commission to introduce legislation requiring the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat in processed foods. this request raises serious economic and internal market concerns. the commission's impact assessment shows that although 90% of consumers are interested in the country of origin of meat products, 80% of them would not support the indication of the country of origin of meat if this would result in an increase in the consumer price of food. the introduction of mandatory marking would increase the costs of meat processors significantly, by 30%. the processors would pass on all the additional costs (according to the commission, 90% of these costs) to the consumers, and the impact study therefore expects a consumer price increase of 6-9%. therefore, the country of origin mark should not be introduced on meat products. the majority of these products are typically purchased by poorer people who would no longer be able to afford these products following a significant price increase. finally, i should like to point out that the food fraud known as the 'horse meat scandal' last year could not be prevented, despite the fact that the indication of origin has been mandatory for beef since the crisis caused by bse in 2000. i therefore ask the commission, regardless of the ep's position, to refrain from introducing a mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance.

in writing. unfortunately, all over the world, not just in europe, the balance between the employer and employee side is becoming imbalanced: employers have an increasingly strong and workers a decreasingly strong influence on working conditions. in this environment, one of the most effective tools workers have is the strike. the right to strike has been a right of workers and their trade unions in europe since the 20th century, and the ilo convention no 87 on freedom of association and the right to organise, to which all eu member states are party, has recognised this right in practice, if not expressly. since 2012, the employers' side of the ilo has been debating the right of workers to strike, and this effort has been quietly supported by governments in asia, africa, and even some european governments. this is completely unacceptable. the role of european governments and the european commission is not to blindly serve business interests but to ensure the conditions for social dialogue and to promote a balanced dialogue between the parties. the best example of behaviour that is the opposite of the true role of governments is my own country. since the 2010 amendment to the hungarian strike law, the precondition for striking has been for the parties to agree on sufficient conditions. this made it practically impossible for hungarian workers to exercise the right to strike. it is clear that the creation of decent working conditions is not possible without maintaining a balance of power and dialogue, which is based on the right to strike.

in writing. international law, including eu law, is based on ensuring that the most vulnerable members of society, children, are protected in the most effective way under all circumstances. one of the instruments is the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of illegal removal of children, which has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention establishes a system of international cooperation among the contracting states to resolve cases involving the illegal removal of children. in most cases, the source of the problem is the divorce of parents of different nationalities who try to obtain custody of the children by exploiting the lack of international cooperation. the biggest problem in these cases is the different legal frameworks in different states. the convention is intended to provide a remedy, a solution, to such cases. it is therefore essential that as many states as possible accede to this convention.
in writing. the hague convention on the civil aspects of illegal removal of children is a very important legal instrument. all the member states of the european union are part of it. the convention provides a system of cooperation for contracting states to find solutions to cases of illegal removal of children. these problems are most common in parents going through a divorce. the spouse from the other state can take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states in order to obtain child custody. the biggest problem in such cases is the national nature of the legal systems of the states. often the courts of both states concerned consider the matter to be within their jurisdiction and award custody to the parent of their own nationality. the convention aims to resolve such situations at international level by stipulating that the law of the state of the child's residence is applicable and that the case falls within the jurisdiction of the court of that state. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of children who have been illegally removed. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance that all states which have not yet done so should accede to the convention.
in writing. gabon's accession to the hague convention is a necessary step to ensure that the member states party to the convention can take the broadest possible action against the smuggling of children abroad. i support this proposal because the protection of children is of paramount importance in all circumstances and all possible legal means must be used.

in writing. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and the survival of marine fish stocks is at risk. i support the proposal for a protocol to the sustainable fisheries agreement between the european union and senegal, which seeks to place the west african tuna fisheries within a more sustainable framework than the one currently in place. the justified measures taken to maintain marine fish stocks have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not pose any threat to the natural values of these areas, unlike marine aquaculture areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability requirements. these are justified only for marine fisheries and aquaculture. in future, efforts should be made to clearly differentiate between the concept and regulation of marine and freshwater aquaculture.

in writing. i voted against a political resolution on the indication of the country of origin of meat ingredients in processed foods. this proposal would require the european commission to legislate for the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of meat in processed foods. this request raises serious economic and internal market concerns. the commission's impact assessment shows that although 90% of consumers are interested in the country of origin of meat products, 80% of them would not support the indication of the country of origin of meat if this would result in an increase in the consumer price of food. the introduction of mandatory marking would increase the costs of meat processors significantly, by 30%. the processors would pass on all the additional costs (according to the commission, 90% of these costs) to the consumers, and the impact study therefore expects a consumer price increase of 69%. therefore, the country of origin mark should not be introduced on meat products. the majority of these products are typically purchased by poorer people who would no longer be able to afford these products following a significant price increase. finally, i should like to point out that the food fraud known as the 'horse meat scandal' last year could not be prevented, despite the fact that the indication of origin has been mandatory for beef since the crisis caused by bse in 2000. i therefore ask the commission, regardless of the ep's position, to refrain from introducing a mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance.
in writing. - the natural need of consumers to have the exact origin of meat and meat products indicated on the label is finally being met. the eu/non eu type of designation of origin has been abandoned by consumers. between 30 and 50% of all meat slaughtered in the eu is consumed as processed products. the eu's traceability system in its current form was not suited to trace the origin of a food throughout the food chain. a country or regional designation of origin will help to prevent and detect misuse of foodstuffs for falsification. the resolution is therefore to be supported, but i still very much regret that it is not stated whether the animal has been fed gmo feed or not. unfortunately, there's no progress on this, and we're asking for more.
in writing. the shortcomings of the european food safety system were highlighted by the horse meat scandal in 2012. the horse meat scandal has called into question the traceability and transparency of the european food chain. therefore, the decision to adopt this resolution believes that there is a need for traceability of meat used in processed foods at union level. this could prevent the deliberate misleading of consumers and the like from occurring in the case of food counterfeiting. if we label meat products by country of origin, we would force supermarkets with a large market share to use only meat products from a reliable source in their products.

in writing. the commission has today issued a communication on the implementation of the energy union and the eu's plan to tackle global climate change. i agree with the need to encourage the widest possible interconnection of european energy networks (especially gas and electricity lines). many member states are heavily energy dependent on certain third countries, which significantly limits their freedom of movement in energy procurement. the independence of a country depends to a large extent on the development of its energy dependency, and therefore diversification of energy procurement should be a fundamental interest of all eu member states. the key is to be able to provide significant eu support for the interconnection of energy networks. the commission's decision to transfer a larger amount to finance the so-called juncker investment package from the budget of the european network and telecommunications facility, which is the same instrument used to finance the above objective, is not a good sign. on the other hand, i welcome the fact that the communication identifies as a priority the improvement of energy efficiency and the strong promotion of the transition to renewable energy production. however, the commission should refrain from any action that would impede the use of renewable energy. for example, we should not restrict the planting of useful varieties of trees that provide biomass feedstock, the production of first-generation bioethanol from surplus crops or the promotion of combustible biomass plants. finally, i do not agree with the significant inclusion of agriculture in the greenhouse gas reduction target. agriculture accounts for only 10% of emissions, but a significant reduction in emissions - particularly for ammonia and methane - would lead to a collapse of european livestock production and a decline in crop production.

in writing. long-term financing, the european long-term investment funds, can play an important role in achieving the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, promoting high levels of employment and strengthening competitiveness. european long-term investment funds provide long-term financing for infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or listed smes for which there is no readily identifiable buyer for the equity or debt instruments issued. in the absence of common union rules, divergent measures at national level may occur and divergent national requirements may lead to distortions of competition, different levels of investor protection, increased legal uncertainty and a decline in investor confidence. the smooth functioning of the internal market and a high level of investor protection require uniform union rules.
in writing. ‒ european long-term investment funds contribute to the long-term financing of the european economy, in particular for sustainable infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or listed smes, covering an area where bank financing has not always proved possible or successful. they can also provide income to investors who prefer a return, albeit lower, but secure in the long term, such as pension funds, insurance companies, foundations, municipalities. european long-term investment funds can thus contribute to meeting a previously insufficiently met demand in the money market as a complement to the banking system. their uniform eu regulation could be an important step towards completing the banking union. all of which justified my yes vote.
in writing. ‒ the long-term investment funds are the vehicles designed to boost non-bank investment in the real economy across europe. this is an efficient new tool that will give a major boost to financing long-term investment, as supported by president juncker’s plan. this new financial tool helps us to solve the complex economic situation we are faced with, achieving economic growth, increasing financial stability and ensuring consumer protection at the same time. i voted in favour, supporting this new tool.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on interchange fees for card-based payments, as the smooth functioning of the internal market requires the completion of an integrated market for electronic payments, which would also help to reduce transaction costs for consumers. the distinction between domestic and foreign payment transactions should be avoided, as this would be detrimental to both traders, entrepreneurs and consumers. card-based payment transactions are an area which, by its nature, needs to be addressed at european level. the commission's efforts to remove obstacles to the efficient functioning of card-based payments and, in this context, mobile and internet payments based on card payments are therefore welcome. these and similar actions are what citizens expect from the european union and can really bring it closer to its people.

by proposing amendments. we are used to having very tight deadlines for european semesters, and we have been working with this. the first and most important point is that we believe that the committee on the internal market and consumer protection considers it very important that there should be an independent pillar, a dedicated pillar, in this respect, dealing with the governance of the single market and the internal market. the second very important point is that we wanted to deal with those areas which have added value in the internal market, which serve economic growth, which focus on job creation. these are not areas that we have invented, but the imco committee has studies, these are the latest studies that focus on these key areas. and these are the key areas that we've covered in our report. overall, we believe that our achievements so far, which have been precisely in the area of transposition of legislation in relation to the internal market, are too quantitative. and we are not concerned with how qualitatively the member states transpose these laws. we believe that there is a need to focus much more on the quality of implementation. we can also imagine key sectoral indicators in this respect that would be much better indicators of the progress we have made. the crisis has clearly demonstrated the need to renew the economic model of the european union. and that is to increase our competitiveness. we have opportunities, but we haven't used them. the european union must therefore take strong supportive action to increase cross-border trade, to keep pace with a changing world and to invest more in digital technology, digital industry, which is also part of the juncker plan. we believe that repositioning the internal market would in any case contribute to making progress in the areas of economic growth and employment and to achieving the objectives of the eu 2020 strategy. this dedicated pillar i'm talking about, it's clearly going to be about the real economy. the real economy that we need to revive the most. it is essential that we define priorities in this respect too. we have had our interpretations of the internal market up to now, but this has not yet been extended to the real economy, so that we can achieve real results and take effective steps, and i believe that these should be taken, further steps should be taken in this respect. the same is true of the question of governance: much more control is needed and strong political support is needed to make it happen in the internal market. so the mechanisms that we have built up have to be actually operated, if necessary, then strengthened. i would like to mention one very big sadness that i find difficult to digest, unfortunately the part on the governance of the internal market was in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the import into the union of agricultural products originating in turkey. while i consider it important to make the union acquis clear, transparent, easily understandable and accessible to all, the regulation is of particular importance for the functioning of the preferential system applicable to imports into the union of agricultural products originating in turkey. for example, for products for which union regulations require compliance with a certain import price, the application of the preferential tariff regime depends on compliance with this price, which is becoming increasingly difficult to monitor. it is therefore essential that the provisions, as amended many times, are available in one place in an orderly manner.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council suspending certain concessions on imports into the union of agricultural products originating in turkey. it provides for the development and harmonisation of trade preferences for imports of agricultural products originating in turkey into the union and provides for a number of preferential concessions for exports of meat and live animals from the union to turkey. the review of the provisions prohibiting trade in live bovine animals and beef to turkey, which have been in place since 1996, can thus be taken to a new level. furthermore, it is possible to eliminate problems such as the removal of barriers to preferential exports to turkey. i therefore consider that the regulation contributes to the protection of the commercial interests of the union. i believe it is important above all that eu legislation is clear, transparent, easy to understand and accessible to all. the above report contributed to this by adopting a simple, uniform structure of the above provision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment to the agreement on the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, which aims to ensure a more sustainable fishing of marine fish stocks, better protection of marine resources and the development of fishing methods. it is clear that 30% of the world's seas are overfished, and the survival of marine fish stocks is at risk. the justified measures taken to maintain marine fish stocks have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. consequently, freshwater aquaculture should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries. efforts should be made to define and regulate freshwater aquaculture clearly now.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which clarifies the objectives of the gfcm: the development, conservation, optimum use and rational management of living marine resources, and the promotion and sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea. i welcome the fact that the amended agreement revises the structure and content of the current agreement in order to bring it into line with the modern tools of regional fisheries management organisations and that the agreement also introduces the definitions necessary for the correct interpretation of the agreement. i support the proposal because i believe it is important to promote common fisheries management, the establishment of fisheries restricted areas to protect our wildlife, the modern and efficient collection, processing and dissemination of data and the development of an integrated fisheries policy for the union. i agree with the rapporteur that the development and proper exploitation of marine living resources in the mediterranean and black seas is a common interest and with the conviction that the conservation and sustainable exploitation of marine living resources in the application area and the protection of marine ecosystems in which these resources occur play an important role in the context of blue growth and sustainable development.

member of the commission.– madam president, i esteem this exclusive privilege to be allowed to speak twice here today. thank you for the opportunity to participate in today’s debate. these discussions are always very inspiring for me, with the flow of – mostly – good ideas which we use in our work. i would like to react quickly to what ms záborská said about humanity. this is very much what i feel in my heart, and we must be strong in combating the increasing intolerance we now have in europe. we had a discussion about this last week with vice-president timmermans. we are planning a big conference for october this year, where we want to gather together with all important stakeholders in the european union to discuss how to combat not only anti-gypsyism but also anti-semitism and other forms and signals of increasing intolerance in europe. i would like to add something regarding the commission policy: i would like to call the policy we want to have a practical policy. we do not need big new legislation, new committees, big glossy conferences. we already have legislation in place, so what we need is stronger enforcement of the existing legislation and very precise insistence on observing the law. this is our main principle: that we are all equal before the law. this is something we need to use in the member states, in everyday policy and everyday action. we are now assessing the national strategies which we collected from the member states. i appreciate the hungarian input, because i know it was the idea of hungary in 2011 to start to work on the national strategies, which enable us to look at new methods and the new instruments we are going to use in the member states and to help best practices to be shared by all. so, for instance, i spoke to the deputy minister in the romanian government who presented to me the new policy the government wants to start in romania to help not only roma citizens but all those who are in need, people suffering from poverty, to overcome these problems. i asked them, please, to implement this as soon as possible, and then in one year’s time i would like them to share their experience with others. it is part of the role of the commission to help ensure that best practices are transferred and to coordinate these actions. in the newly—submitted national strategies we see a lot of innovation, a lot of good ideas, a lot of effort to get rid of the things that do not work, and not to waste time, energy and money, and a really big effort to solve the problems. i hope the strategies will be as good when put into practice as they look on paper. in all the strategies we see ways of combating unemployment and poverty, ways to increase education and access to services, including housing – very practical things. a last comment regarding financing. you said here that well—targeted funding is necessary. it is not only the european social fund which should be used in the most practical and effective way. in this respect the commission – and i personally, because i was very active for four years in eu funding – are helping to share best practices and to share information on what works and what has been funded from the european social fund. but there are also governments financing projects and programmes for roma integration and combating poverty, because most of these programmes concern not only roma citizens but also all those who suffer from poverty. here we see increasing interest from governments in using their resources to help the situation. a last comment regarding the ngos. i very much appreciate the work of ngos and activists working on the ground because they are doing the right work and the proper work to help the situation. i am convinced that if we find a way to introduce multiannual financing of these ngos – which, in fact, work in place of the state doing the work which the public sector should otherwise do – they should have more stable financing. this would, in turn, save time and energy for the real work, as they would not be spent chasing money to survive. i apologise for taking so long but the debate was very inspiring and i felt i wanted to add these practical points.
president-in-office of the council.– madam president, honourable members, i have followed the debate with great interest and i will reiterate that politicians play a great role in shaping public opinion. they can do good but they can also cause a lot of damage. this is why i fully share the opinion that there is no room for hate speech in parliamentary chambers. many of you have made the suggestion that there should be a commemoration date of the roma genocide. i must say that the council has not yet taken a position on this subject. at the same time, i find it symbolic that we are having a discussion on the possibility of a memorial day to commemorate the roma genocide on the day when my country, latvia, commemorates victims of the soviet totalitarian regime. without prejudice to the council’s eventual position on the matter, as a representative of a country whose people suffered a great deal from totalitarian regimes, i understand the historical, political and educational value of having such a date. irrespective of when we celebrate international roma day or when exactly we commemorate victims of the genocide, there is an urgent need to address the poverty, marginalisation and discrimination faced by roma communities. as part of the eu and national action, we have a duty to ourselves, to our values and of course to roma, to tackle public misunderstanding, raise awareness and fight intolerance because, as we look back, so too must we look forward to ending stigmatisation, to properly integrating roma – and indeed all minorities – into european society and to showing that every european has a place in europe. it has been a pleasure to have this dialogue with you on this really vital issue.

in writing. since the first world roma congress in 1971, international roma day has been celebrated. this is an opportunity to pause for a moment and take stock of the situation of the roma. i look around and i see that the roma are still not full citizens of my country. roma in my country have a life expectancy 10 to 15 years shorter than their majority counterparts. their living conditions in many ghettos are comparable to those of people in the third world, with poverty continuing to increase and their opportunities for escape decreasing. since the change of regime, the number of roma excluded from the primary labour market has increased, and the unemployed have begged for years for public service, which is often humiliating and does not provide a real livelihood, but they often do not have access to it. in hungary, almost two-thirds of roma children attend segregated educational institutions. and the minister in charge is standing up for a school administrator who was found by the court to be discriminatory, and the court's response was to amend the law. while eu and national development funds are shared by a political body whose ruling party leader is now unable to account for the expenditure of nearly 2 million euros. the eu is also responsible for the situation: despite a lot of good plans and resources, no tangible change has been made. and it is safe to say that the situation of the groups with the worst capacity for advocacy is the best indicator of what the future of europe holds.
in writing. the uprooting and uplifting of the roma is a shared responsibility of all of us. but how do we live with that responsibility? from brussels and strasbourg, we sometimes shake off the question: we organise a few round table conferences, decide to commission further studies and background analyses, and then allocate billions more to programmes. but i'll take my chances, with a few exceptions, we have very little information about their end use. just one example: in hungary, the national roma municipality - which until now had been run by a fidesz mp - was recently investigated after it was revealed that huf 600 million of funds received from the european union were spent on luxury offices and cars instead of creating jobs. the gypsy self-government system in hungary has been plagued by corruption, inefficiency, and embezzlement for years. a bottomless pit, where we pour european taxpayers' money, and the gypsies at the end of the line don't profit. it is untenable that we do not adequately control these uses of resources, that we do not take into account efficiency. it's a scandal that pro-government politicians are invading and looting the self-organized gypsy community. a few days ago, i was in brussels to meet the gypsy mayor of cserdi, who has almost completely eliminated unemployment and crime in his village through his own initiative, his own unique and sometimes radical programmes. we should learn from him and support people like him who want to do something, not pour money into corrupt systems that make the gypsy problem worse.

i'd like to invite my fellow congressmen to a very important program. next tuesday at one o'clock there will be a public hearing where the hungarian victims of bank fraud, of violations of the law will speak, the so-called "debt-debtors", the victims of loans based on swiss francs, so to speak. many people ask when they see the poster, "but this problem has already been solved in hungary, right?" they converted these fraudulent swiss franc loans into national currency. yes, but not at the exchange rate at the time of the recording, which was around 160 forints, but at the current market rate, 260 forints. so it's not true that the problem is solved, that people are still being driven to suicide, that tragedies are happening. i ask you to come and find a solution to this problem that affects millions of people in europe, because not only in hungary, but also in croatia, romania, poland, there are such crude constructions.
media pluralism and media freedom are among the most important common core values of the european community and the european union. in recent years, many hungarian mps, the tavares report and various european institutions have drawn attention to the fact that these basic values have been endangered in hungary. the independence and freedom of the media is not guaranteed as in other european countries. since then, the government has taken some steps, but it must be said that there are no longer any guarantees of political independence of the civil service. there is no public service television in hungary, and the distribution of radio frequencies is extremely one-sided. i must say that this is not a hungarian issue, it is a question of the fundamental values of the european union, and that is why it is the fundamental task of the european parliament to draw attention to the violation of these freedoms.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the creation of the european globalisation adjustment fund has so far proved to be a highly important tool for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. in my experience, the subsidies granted so far have helped the redundant workers to re-enter the labour market. the request of the greek government is in line with the criteria laid down when the fund was set up, and i therefore supported its adoption.
in writing. ‒ on 3 february 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for the benefit of greece. the request was sent to the commission on 4 september 2014. the commission has concluded that the application complies with the requirements for mobilising the egf, as laid down in article 4 (1) (b) of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013 of the european parliament and of the council of 17 december 2013. according to the greek authorities, the main events leading to the redundancies were: (1) the reduction in household disposable income due to the increase in tax burdens, the decrease in salaries (affecting both private and public sector employees) and the increase in unemployment, which led to an extraordinary decrease in purchasing power and forced consumers to prioritise their spending and, despite their importance, to significantly reduce the amount spent on daily information; (2) the liquidity problems of the greek banks dramatically depleted the credit resources available to businesses and individuals. the coordinated package of personalised services to be co-financed shall include career guidance, training, retraining, vocational training, self-employment support, job search support, training and mobility support. the fidesz-kdnp delegation supports the motion in solidarity. it is important that dismissed workers receive appropriate support for their reintegration into the labour market.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important institution of solidarity within the union; it is an active employment policy instrument that shares the burden of returning to the labour market between the worker, the member state concerned and the union, and the result helps both the worker who is able to return to work, the member state that is forced to deal with unemployment and the union that aims to increase employment. two requests submitted by greece request assistance for a personalised service for the reintegration into the labour market of 705 workers to be made redundant in 46 broadcasting and publishing companies in the attica region. the commission considers that the request fulfils the eligibility criteria set out in the regulation and that the provision of the service started well before the aid was granted. on the basis of all the above, i consider that the request should be supported.
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ when using the european globalisation adjustment fund, it is important to improve the employability of workers through personalised training and recognition of their previous professional experience. it is expected that continuing training should be adapted not only to the needs and individual aspirations of the dismissed employees but also to the actual business environment.
in writing. ‒ on 3 february 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for greece to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. in their request, the greek authorities state that the main events leading to the redundancies were: (1) the reduction in household disposable income due to the increase in tax burdens, the decrease in salaries (affecting both private and public sector employees) and the increase in unemployment, which led to an extraordinary decrease in purchasing power and forced consumers to prioritise their spending and abandon products that they do not consider essential in their daily lives; (2) the dramatic reduction in credit resources available to businesses and individuals due to the liquidity problems of the greek banks. the sales of the companies in the sector (newspapers, magazines, etc.) decreased by 60% between 2009 and 2013 due to the weakening of demand for their products. the coordinated package of personalised services to be co-financed shall include career guidance, training, vocational training, self-employment support, job search support, training and mobility support. the fidesz-kdnp delegation supports the motion in solidarity. it is important that dismissed workers receive appropriate support for their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ the current hungarian government has so far barely initiated the use of the european globalisation adjustment fund. it has been and is primarily self-employed in order to address the loss of certain jobs and the negative effects thereof. as a result of the government's successful economic policy, hungary is currently experiencing an increase in jobs rather than a decrease. the european union - despite our protests - is treating the european tobacco industry rather harshly. tobacco, grown in europe for centuries, provides livelihoods for 80,000 farmers and employs 350,000 seasonal workers a year, mostly in the poor regions of bulgaria, spain, greece, italy, poland, hungary and romania. it is a well-known fact that european production differs from that of the major exporting countries of the developing world in that, although smaller in quantity, it is of higher quality, more stable and more traceable. these latter characteristics contribute to the mitigation of the public health consequences of smoking. in the course of the cap reform, the commission has succeeded in getting eu support for tobacco production to end completely from 2015, despite the opinion of the european parliament. european tobacco production under control will decline significantly, and this could lead to a significant increase in imports of less controlled tobacco products produced outside the eu and to illicit imports. those measures and effects pose a significant risk of the loss of many jobs in the tobacco production sector. in response to my written question on this subject, the commission considers that the european globalisation adjustment fund is the only viable instrument.

in writing. ‒ on 6 february 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for the benefit of ireland. its purpose was to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant as a result of changes in world trade due to globalisation. the application was sent to the commission on 19 september 2014 and found to meet the necessary conditions. the irish authorities argue that the ltai layoff wave is primarily the result of major changes in eu trade in goods and services, which in turn is the result of a technological shift towards the production of new generation aircraft and parts; a change in the wider practice of aircraft parts manufacturing, together with the impact on the fundamental market factors underlying the business model of ltai, and a change in the location of global aircraft manufacturing. the coordinated package of personalised services to be funded shall include career guidance and career planning, egf training support, training and continuing education programmes, higher education programmes, entrepreneurship/self-employment support and income support, including the egf course contribution scheme. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp delegation, i believe it is very important to support the motion. it is essential that redundant workers receive adequate support for their re-placement.

my colleague and friend, mr balczó, and i were very worried about how to vote on this issue. we were in an even more difficult situation than most of our fellow mps, because we as hungarians had to vote on whether the european union should give support, financial support to the ukrainian government, which we know exactly does not serve its interests, especially those of transcarpathian hungarians. at the same time, as hungarians, we know that transcarpathian hungarians are going through inhuman suffering. first, because of so-called military obligations: this is not their war, yet they have to sacrifice their sons and their husbands. and on the other hand, because of the inhumane social conditions, because of the poverty, we're basically stuck with the african, third world income ratio. we say about africa and the so-called developing countries that people have to live on one euro a day. now there are salaries and pensions of 30 euros a month something has to be done about it.
ukraine needs the support of the union. but the financial support that this parliament has just voted for is not the real, real purpose. it is entirely devoted to the imf's reform programme. at the same time, there is a social crisis in ukraine. this is the main reason why eu funding is needed. these amendments were rejected by a majority of votes cast. stabilization of ukraine would require peace first and foremost. a ceasefire is important, an end to the bloodshed, but it doesn't create lasting peace. real peace and stability should take into account the legitimate interests of all concerned, including the right of indigenous peoples to self-determination.
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ in view of ukraine's protracted economic and structural problems, i believe that it has submitted a well-founded request to the commission for macro-financial assistance of eur 1.8 billion. in order to achieve its european orientation, ukraine is facing a serious internal political crisis, a difficult economic situation and, in foreign policy, a protracted military conflict with many human casualties. the war in eastern ukraine, russian trade restrictions and the intensification of the gas dispute have resulted in price increases, unmanageable tax burdens and utility bills for the already weak ukrainian economy. this has led to an economic downturn, currency devaluation and a decline in international reserves, creating a significant external financing gap for 2015. the european union must therefore make rapid and effective efforts to restore and preserve stability in the country. we need an economically stable, developing ukraine, where people do not suffer, and where adequate living conditions are ensured. the objective of macro-financial assistance is to contribute to addressing serious problems in the economic and financial sphere, such as the weak balance of payments and the budgetary situation. i voted to pass the bill because it is a way to show our solidarity with a country and a people at war with a nuclear power. at the same time, the european parliament and the council can demonstrate that the union is capable of acting swiftly, decisively and in line with its political commitments.
in writing. ‒ in line with the fidesz-kdnp parliamentary group, i believe that by providing macro-financial assistance to ukraine, which we supported in today's vote, we have shown that we are not leaving the ukrainian people alone and are helping our eastern neighbour. the ukrainian people are facing not only problems caused by the war but also economic problems. the uncontrolled increase in inflation in recent times has caused difficulties in people's daily lives wages in shops are increasing many times overnight. the ukrainian economy is on the verge of bankruptcy and it is in the union's interest that this does not happen. by accepting the macro-financial assistance, the european union is contributing to the economic stability and development of ukraine and, at the same time, of the wider eastern european neighbourhood. in addition to strengthening our cross-border economic relations, it is even more significant from the hungarian point of view that by adopting the report, the fidesz meps are helping to improve the economic conditions of transcarpathian hungarians.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the fidesz-kdnp delegation, i would like to live with the following explanation of vote. in addition to strengthening our cross-border economic relations, it is even more significant from the hungarian point of view that the fidesz meps, by adopting the report on financial assistance to ukraine, are helping to improve the economic conditions of transcarpathia hungarians.
in writing. ‒ today i voted for ukraine's chance, as the ukrainian economy is in a deep crisis, rooted in long-standing structural problems, which are further aggravated by the armed conflict in the eastern regions and the illegal russian annexation of crimea. macro-financial assistance is a specific union crisis management mechanism available to the union's partner countries facing acute balance of payments problems. it is important to note that in ukraine, we are talking about a struggle for freedom, a struggle that rejects dictatorship. the ambitious macroeconomic adjustment and structural reform programme of the government that took office in february 2014 has been supported by the imf financial assistance programme and the union's macro-financial assistance operations. the current package can also be seen as a kind of reinforcement of the fight against corruption. however, it must be ensured that the financial assistance reaches the ukrainian people and not the oligarchs, and that it cannot be allowed to be used for military purposes.
in writing. ‒ by accepting macro-financial assistance to ukraine, the european union is contributing to the economic stability and development of ukraine and, at the same time, of the wider eastern european neighbourhood. in addition to strengthening our cross-border economic relations, it is even more significant from the hungarian point of view that the adoption of the report by the hungarian meps will help improve the economic conditions of transcarpathian hungarians.

in writing. ‒ previous financial support by the union together with the imf to the macroeconomic adjustment and structural reform programme of the ukrainian government: supported by the imf financial assistance programme and the union's macro-financial assistance operations. however, reform efforts have been hampered by the armed conflict in the country, the war without a declaration of war launched by russia, and trade restrictions. the external financing gap caused by the higher than expected economic downturn and capital outflows can only be filled by additional financial support. on the one hand, europe has an interest in the continuation of the ukrainian reform process, and on the other hand it cannot leave ukraine to suffer the consequences of russian intervention. that's why i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ macro-financial assistance to ukraine contributes to economic stability and development in ukraine and in the wider eastern european neighbourhood. in addition to strengthening our cross-border economic relations, it is even more significant from the hungarian point of view that by adopting the report, the fidesz meps can contribute to the positive development of the economic conditions of transcarpathian hungarians.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report, including the mfa loan to ukraine, in agreement with the commission's proposal and the position of the eit of 19-20 march 2015. i made my decision in the knowledge that this is an unusually large sum, as the political and economic stakes are high, not only for the ukrainians but also for the eu. it is also right in itself to contribute to the stabilisation of the economy of an important neighbour and partner of the union, even if its financial stability is affected by structural or financial reasons. however, ukraine is also suffering from the ravages of war, continued economic pressure and blackmail in the energy supply sector as a target of russian expansionist ambitions that turn partner solidarity into eu solidarity, the eu's most internal affair. the expansionist ambitions of the putin regime through ukraine threaten to destabilise the whole of europe, not least in the area of economic and financial structures. the mfa loan could provide the kiev government with an effective means of circumventing this, of avoiding a financial collapse. at the same time, we must once again make our ukrainian partners aware of the importance of conditionality for the eu, in particular in terms of the consistent and effective implementation of the reform programme undertaken. it is also important to recall on the eu side the requirement that these aspects be represented in a unified and consistent manner by each member state without exception in its relations with the russian and ukrainian sides.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i consider it important that the european union should show its solidarity with the ukrainian government and people in the current difficult financial and economic situation of the country. i am confident that this financial assistance will act as a catalyst to support reform efforts and thus gradually restore confidence in the ukrainian economy. finally, i believe that this report reaffirms the european union's commitment to the ukrainian reform process and, more broadly, the commitment of the eu institutions to the union's objectives of economic stability and development in the eastern european neighbourhood.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the annual tax report. i myself agree with the holistic approach to taxation, which can be a real practical tool to stimulate growth and deepen economic and monetary union. but i'd like to focus on one thing. i agree that securing the revenue fund is an important part of the budget's sustainability. this requires effectively the elimination of tax evasion in the member states, the elimination of tax fraud and tax avoidance schemes and the fight against aggressive tax planning and tax havens. however, the european parliament must also take into account in future the loss of tax revenue and the degree of strengthening of the black and/or grey economy caused by over-taxation of certain sectors or products in certain member states. i will give just one example: in my country, hungary, the highest vat rate is 27%, which also affects a significant group of basic foods. i am convinced that such distortions of the tax systems of individual member states do not serve the tax policy interests of the union.
in writing. the revision of the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework is essential to allow member states to spend the eu funds not used in 2014 this year. the smooth continuation of cohesion policy and rural development programmes in 2015 is particularly important for hungary, where six out of seven regions are considered to be disadvantaged. unfortunately, the current hungarian government has only managed to wrestle away eu aid that could be used to make up for two billion euros less than governments before 2010. nevertheless, in the context of cohesion policy, about 95% of public investment in hungary over the last five years has been made from eu funds. cohesion policy cannot therefore lose out in budgetary debates! in order to achieve the real objective of cohesion policy, which is to bring disadvantaged regions closer to the european average and raise living standards, the conditions for use need to be made more flexible in the next budgetary period. it is important that member states pay particular attention to increasing renewable energy and energy efficiency and to supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for two thirds of european jobs, in order to reduce regional disparities. it is unfortunate that the current hungarian government is currently seriously lagging behind in all three areas.

mr president, the protracted economic crisis has clearly shown how fragile the european financial system is in certain situations. this is why the european union has put in place a number of measures to guarantee the safety of its citizens. one of the most important steps was the strengthening and harmonisation of financial supervisory systems within the euro area. however, the inadequate functioning of supervisory systems is a particular problem in a number of non-euro area member states, including hungary and, more specifically, albania. in recent weeks, two major companies in my country have had to suspend their operations: the first is buda cash, which is suspected of having falsified its reports for years, and the second is questor, which is suspected of having issued bonds worth up to 150 billion forints, or almost half a billion euros, without authorization and collateral. the hungarian national bank, which has recently been responsible for the state supervision of financial institutions in orban, has clearly failed in this activity. i believe that the european commission's failure to act as guardian of the treaties has contributed greatly to this situation.
in writing. ‒ the creation of the european globalisation adjustment fund has so far proved to be a highly important tool for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. in my experience, the subsidies granted so far have helped the redundant workers to re-enter the labour market. the french government's request is in line with the criteria laid down when the fund was set up, and i therefore supported its adoption in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group.
in writing. ‒ on 23 february 2015, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund for france to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by mory-ducros as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. the redundancies were made in 84 plants in france. according to the french authorities, the redundancies at mory-ducros were caused by the bankruptcy and liquidation of the company. the commission notes that the french authorities have not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. between 2007 and 2012, as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, road freight transport by vehicles over 3,5 tonnes decreased by 13,7% in the eu and by 21% in france. the personalised services to be provided to redundant workers comprise the following single measure: counselling and guidance for redundant workers. the fidesz-kdnp delegation supports the motion in solidarity. it is important that dismissed workers receive appropriate support for their reintegration into the labour market.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an important institution of solidarity within the union; it is an active employment policy instrument that shares the burden of returning to the labour market between the worker, the member state concerned and the union, and the result helps both the worker who is able to return to work, the member state that is forced to deal with unemployment and the union that aims to increase employment. between 2007 and 2012, as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, road freight transport by vehicles over 3,5 tonnes decreased by 13,7% in the eu and by 21% in france. in parallel with the decrease in the quantities to be transported, a price war broke out within the sector, the various costs increased, which resulted in a continuous narrowing of the operating margin. as a result, the french transport company mory-ducros went bankrupt and was liquidated. 2804 workers were made redundant, of whom 2513 are in active labour market. on the basis of all the above, i consider that the request should be supported.
in writing. ‒ in its conclusions on strengthening cooperation to modernise and improve social protection, the council supported the commission's proposal to establish a mechanism for implementing this measure in the context of enhanced cooperation based on the work of the high level group of officials. the council stressed that this cooperation should cover all forms of social protection and, where necessary, help member states to further develop and strengthen their social protection systems in line with their national priorities. of course, the organisation and financing of social protection remains a matter for the member states, and this is unchanged. i voted in favour of the resolution because it is very important that all objectives should be covered by uniform funding criteria.
in writing. ‒ the draft council decision aims to set up a social protection committee of an advisory nature to facilitate the coordination of social protection policies between the member states and the commission. i consider the council's initiative to be justified in the light of the social tensions caused by the economic crisis and the union's social objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the decision to establish the social protection committee because i consider it important to modernise social protection systems in a comprehensive way, also in order to ensure high quality and sustainable healthcare for all. i also agree with the point in the draft which stresses that we should create the possibility of better coordination in employment and social policy and socioeconomic policy, while fully respecting the competences of the member states. the draft also addresses the need for a more effective monitoring system that takes account of the social and labour market situation within the gmu, using appropriate social and employment indicators in the context of the european semester.

in writing. every year, between 25 and 30 000 people die in accidents on europe's roads, and about 1.5 million are injured. that is why i am delighted that this important topic has finally been brought to the plenary and that after a decade, the 112-based ecall system can become a reality. this will help to save lives and bring us closer to our goal of reducing the number of fatalities and fatal accidents on the roads of the union. i cannot agree with those who oppose the introduction of the system on the grounds of the protection of personal data for two reasons. first of all, because to me, every life that we save is worth taking care of and bringing in. and that puts all other data protection laws on the back burner. on the other hand, i don't understand the comments about the vehicle identification. we all use gps every day, just like we use our cell phones. they can also identify your current location or even your driving habits. besides, it won't save any lives, it'll just make our journey easier. shouldn't we then value ecall more, which can save hundreds of lives a year, while significantly reducing the lasting damage to those affected by accidents, by providing timely alerts and assistance? moreover, the system would be free of charge and accessible to every driver in europe, and not least would result in significant financial savings. that's why i support the initiative.

in writing. the eu alcohol strategy is designed to address an important social and economic problem. a shocking fact is that excessive alcohol consumption is the third most common lifestyle-related cause of disease in europe. more than 60 chronic diseases including alcoholic liver disease, pancreatitis, cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and obesity are identified as risk factors. it is also important to emphasise that alcohol dependence is a cause of other social problems ranging from domestic violence to workplace conflicts. in itself, moderate and cultured alcohol consumption is in line with the norms of a healthy lifestyle and the hungarian health objectives. the problem is excessive drinking at inappropriate times, such as drunk driving, which we need to tackle effectively. however, we must be careful about measures that call into question and unilaterally restrict moderate drinking, such as redundant and unjustified labelling procedures. the resulting increase in consumer prices would push the market towards lower quality spirits without control and disproportionately affect small and medium-sized enterprises. it is therefore very important that the european commission involves all stakeholders - consumers, health organisations and producers in particular - in the adoption and implementation of the alcohol strategy. this is the only way to achieve our health goals effectively.

in writing. ‒ the international convention on the training, certification and watchkeeping of fishing vessel personnel is designed to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels are properly qualified (certified by official documentation) and fit for work (ascertained by medical examination). this is necessary to minimise the potential threats to life and/or property and the marine environment at sea during operations on board fishing vessels. i believe that the crews of fishing vessels should also be provided with adequate knowledge of sustainable fishing methods in order to maintain marine fish stocks. it follows that the common fisheries policy should pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries, than it has done so far. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats.

in writing. ‒ article 19 of the mff regulation provides for the revision of the mff in the event of late adoption of new rules or programmes implemented under shared management, in order to allow for the carry-over of resources not used in 2014 to subsequent years in excess of the corresponding expenditure ceilings. the amount of the decommitted commitment appropriations for programmes implemented in 2014 under shared management in accordance with article 19 of the mff regulation is eur 21 043 639 478 in current prices, corresponding to the parts of the programmes due in 2014 that were not committed in 2014 and that could not be carried over to 2015. i support the maximum possible carry-over of appropriations to the 2015 financial year, as this avoids unfair treatment of member states, regions and operational programmes, accelerates the implementation and delivery of cohesion policy and helps to avoid the concentration of payments at the end of the mff. as a member of the fidesz-kdnp delegation, i supported the adoption of the report in line with the pp's position.

in writing. ‒ i fully agree with parliament’s position concerning the ecall emergency device. from 31 march 2018, all new cars and light commercial vehicles will be equipped with an ecall emergency device that will automatically dial the 112 emergency number in the event of an accident, sending details of the accident to emergency services. the quicker response from the emergency services to accidents on roads across europe could save about 2 500 lives in the eu every year. and this is free of charge for all of our citizens.
in writing. ‒ the biofuels agreement provides a balanced compromise between the eu's environmental objectives and the legitimate interests of agricultural operators and biofuel producers. the global increase in land use due to the production of so-called traditional biofuels from agricultural raw materials is not uniform across the european union. the new legislation takes better account of the specific situation of the central european region than in previous drafts, where, without endangering food production and rainforests, a large amount of biofuel can be produced by simply increasing yields, providing a secure livelihood for those who depend on agriculture. in line with the fidesz-kdnp group's position, i believe that the directive voted today offers an opportunity to increase hungary's export revenues and secure long-term sales of our agricultural products. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote, we hope to end a three-year negotiating cycle and move closer to a solution that is acceptable to the majority of participants. i believe that we should not use a single system for first generation biofuels, but take into account the natural capacities and potential of individual member states. for example, in many of the new member states, it remains possible to use land not used for food production for biofuel production, and to use land lying fallow for crop production, thereby increasing crop yields. a study by the university of utrecht published in january 2015 suggests that huge amounts of biofuels can be produced without increasing the risk of indirect land use change (iluc). the commission considers that the measures under assessment are proportionate to the objective of the scheme and that the aid is necessary to achieve the objective of the scheme. according to the same study, hungary could produce about 1.2 to 5.2 billion litres of bioethanol from maize, which would not have any negative impact on the use of land. in these countries, large amounts of biofuel can be produced without compromising food production, by increasing yields and mapping the land. this provides jobs and income for farmers, but it doesn't stop investors. we must not be satisfied with today's result. we must continue to encourage science and industry and, to the extent possible, support the development of environmentally friendly and sustainable alternatives.
in writing. ‒ the biofuels agreement provides a balanced compromise between the eu's environmental objectives and the legitimate interests of agricultural operators and biofuel producers. the global increase in land use due to the production of so-called traditional biofuels from agricultural raw materials is not uniform. the new legislation takes better account of the specific situation of the central european region than in previous drafts, where, without endangering food production and rainforests, a large amount of biofuel can be produced by simply increasing yields, providing a secure livelihood for those who live off agriculture. the hungarian delegation's presence also led the european commission to develop a calculation methodology for low-land-use change ethanol by 2017. we will continue to strive to develop criteria that are favourable to hungarian farmers. in line with the fidesz-kdnp group's position, i believe that the directive voted today offers an opportunity to increase hungary's export revenues and secure long-term sales of our agricultural products. that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the second reading of the draft resolution, which aims both to reduce emissions of harmful substances and to allow for further technological developments. i believe that the complexity of biofuels requires a multi-faceted approach. in addition to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, we are talking about an existing sector that also provides jobs, which stimulates further investment and job creation in rural areas. it is also important to note that this can reduce the external energy dependence of the european union and that some of the by-products of biofuel production are valuable nutrients or fuels. i therefore consider it important that an informal agreement on the draft legislation has been reached between parliament and the eu's specialised ministers, so that a compromise solution has been found. the directive requires member states to transpose its content into their national law by 2017 and to ensure that first generation biofuels (i.e. energy sources from cereals grown on land) can account for no more than 7% of transport energy sources by 2020. personally, when developing the indirect land use directive, i supported a higher inclusion rate of 4 to 7.5% of the target (so-called first generation) biofuels from arable crops and i feel that this has created a healthy balance.
in writing. ‒ today, 90% of nylon waste used for purchases in the european union is used once before it becomes a highly polluting waste, not at all, or a waste that is difficult to decompose. this is a huge environmental burden, as 8 billion plastic bags are discarded in nature every year. the new european legislation approved is therefore designed to reduce excessive and sometimes unnecessary waste generation. thanks to the previously introduced law on environmental product taxes, hungary is already meeting the 2025 targets of the newly approved directive, with an exemplary result in europe. as a member of the fidesz-kdnp group, i supported the adoption of the new eu legislation, as it will not only effectively reduce nylon waste but also encourage environmentally conscious consumer habits. this will help to create a cleaner, more liveable european environment.
in writing. ‒ today, pollution is so widespread that we must tackle it at every level and in every possible area. the amendment to the directive requires member states to limit the number of lightweight plastic carrier bags on a continuous basis in order to reduce littering. these are dangerous to the environment in many ways, and it is important that we pay attention to them. because of their thinness and weak texture, they are unlikely to be reused, and people throw them away more often than thicker bags, thus avoiding their entering the waste treatment system. the amendment of the directive offers several options for a sustainable limitation of the number of lightweight plastic carrier bags, such as reducing the number to 40 pieces per person per year by the end of 2025. the commission will also consider the possibility of member states ensuring that, by the end of 2018, no free lightweight plastic carrier bags are given away at the time of purchase in their shops, or of using another method to ensure that the number of plastic carrier bags is reduced in an equally effective way. i consider the adoption of this amendment to be very important, because by its entry into force member states will have to reduce the number of lightweight plastic carrier bags and report this in annual reports to the commission, which will then be able to monitor compliance effectively. if this amendment to the restriction is not implemented, the number of plastic carrier bags would increase in the future, with unforeseeable consequences for nature.
