in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the second reading of the draft recommendation, as i consider it of the utmost importance to minimise the use of so-called plastic bags in the european union. as we know, it takes five seconds to make these bags, and 500 years to completely decompose them. the recycling rate of these bags is almost zero, and in fact, much of it is buried in landfills, mainly in rural areas. in 2010, it was estimated that over eight billion plastic bags ended up in landfills, so i think this legislation is good for everyone, because it's a huge environmental problem. the adopted recommendation requires member states to reduce the annual consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags per person to less than 90 by the end of 2019 and to less than 40 by the end of 2025 or to guarantee that consumers will not be able to receive such plastic carrier bags free of charge after 2018. it is for these reasons that i supported the second reading of the recommendation, which provides for a transitional period but obliges member states to radically reduce the use of plastic carrier bags.
in writing. ‒ i completely agree to have legislation to reduce the consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags, as the statistics show over 8 billion plastic carrier bags are littered in the eu every year. more than 90% of the european citizens support to have measures to reduce the usage. the new legislation will oblige member states to adopt measures ensuring that the annual consumption level does not exceed and ensuring that they are not given these plastic bags for free at stores and sales points by the end of 2017.

in writing. ‒ reliable and accurate european statistics serve two essential purposes as a public good: as a building block for policy-makers' decisions and as a picture of the state of the economy and society, providing assurance for other governments and the financial market. however, events in recent years have shaken the confidence of the public and the markets. since then, we have seen how misleading and false statistics can add to political and economic turmoil. the sovereign debt crisis was certainly exacerbated by public and market scepticism about the accuracy of statistics on the public debt and the government deficit. this should be taken as a warning, as public confidence in the credibility of statistics is key to creating a culture of fact-based policy-making and accountability. in this respect, the timing of the report is excellent. we need to rebuild public confidence in statistics. i believe that the previous initiatives should be strengthened. the statistical code of practice adopted by the commission and the member states must be implemented and strictly observed, and i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ powerful global forces are working to transform europe into the united states. in the model state of democracy, the establishment of the united states was relatively easy on the lands taken from the exterminated indigenous people. in europe, the process is stalled, resisted by nation states and nationalist sentiment, by people, by organizations. the european commission, on the other hand, is trying to write off everything that is national. this proposal is contrary even to the principles of protocol 2 to the lisbon treaty, which are intended to guarantee the limited autonomy of the countries and proportionality, and i could not accept it.
in writing. ‒ second reading of the proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics. i supported the council's position on the text adopted at first reading, as proposed by the rapporteur.
in writing. ‒ a fact-based approach to policy issues requires the reliable and efficient functioning of the european statistical system and its adaptation to economic change. i consider it particularly important that the professional independence of the heads of statistical authorities in the member states be guaranteed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the recommendation, as all efforts to promote the professional independence of the european statistical authorities should be supported, as should the ease of comparison and accessibility of statistics from the member states. there are member states where the heads of national statistical offices are chosen on the basis of political considerations, or where the publication of certain reports is delayed or refused on the basis of political decisions. these practices must be stopped. the staff of statistical offices may be selected on the basis of strictly professional criteria and shall carry out their duties independently of any pressure from political or other interest groups. the recommendation contributes to meeting these expectations by providing high-quality, regularly updated statistical data that provide a reliable basis for responsible decision-making.
in writing. - this is a very important area. the report examines, at second reading, the recommendations for the collection and systematisation of european statistics. all initiatives at european level that strengthen the independence of statistical authorities should be supported. authentic and comparable data shall be used as a basis for establishing the true economic situation. i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and their fisheries. this report also clearly shows that 30% of the world's seas are overfished, and the survival of marine fish stocks is at risk. the justified measures taken to maintain marine fish stocks have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. consequently, freshwater aquaculture should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries. efforts should be made to define and regulate freshwater aquaculture clearly now.

in writing. ‒ the accession of croatia to the european union requires the updating of the agreements concluded by the eu and its predecessors to take account of the new situation. hungary, including fidesz-kdnp, has consistently argued in favour of accepting croatian integration aspirations, and i therefore voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing an ec-russia partnership, to take account of the accession of croatia to the union.
in writing. ‒ the protocol incorporates croatia as a party to the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european community and russia with effect from the date of accession of croatia. this is a necessary technical amendment which i voted in favour of. as regards eu-russia relations, i would draw the commission's attention to the fact that hungary was excluded from the third round of eu compensation for the damage to the fruit and vegetable market caused by the russian agricultural embargo, which was granted at the end of last year, as were croatia, slovenia and romania. the quantity of advance requests received in hungary last september was more than 10 000 tonnes, which is an order of magnitude higher than the quantity allocated to the country in the second round. this was mitigated by the free allocation of 3 000 tonnes in the second round, which hungary was only able to use partially due to the short time available. that framework is no longer available to my country, although it would be very justified. on the basis of the above, i call on the commission to provide farmers in hungary, croatia, slovenia and romania with additional compensation to reduce their losses caused by the crisis of overproduction. it can do so by extending the time of use of the second-round framework or by announcing a new framework of 3 000 tonnes which can be freely used.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of croatia to the eu, it has become necessary to include croatia as a party to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the ec and croatia. the council may adopt a protocol to this effect only with parliament's consent.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of the parliament's approval of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union and its member states, of the protocol to the partnership and cooperation agreement establishing a partnership between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the russian federation, of the other part, to take account of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union.
the bologna process, the reform of european higher education, was launched 15 years ago. we would have expected the report to have a real balance sheet of what has been successful, what has been a failure, what needs to be changed. unfortunately, this has not been the case, although we must face the fact that the main objective of creating a training system that meets the demands of the labour market has not been achieved. and it's not because the bologna system was used to dismantle the two-tiered, dual system of higher education that had been working well, the college-university system. and here's the report that says that there needs to be stronger consultation within the higher education community to end opposition to the bologna reforms. it's not marketing that's needed, it's real balance sheet preparation, evaluation and change.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted a comprehensive report on the follow-up to the implementation of the bologna process, with a report by ms krystyna lybacka. in line with the fidesz-kdnp group's position, i believe that the report's targeted recommendations will lead to progress in higher education. the bologna reforms have launched the european higher education area and have led to significant achievements over the past 15 years in making higher education systems more comparable, increasing mobility, ensuring quality assurance systems and the recognition of diplomas, improving the quality of education systems and increasing the attractiveness of european higher education. within the bologna process, much remains to be done in terms of adapting education systems to labour market needs, improving overall employability and competitiveness, and enhancing the attractiveness of european higher education. the european parliament calls on the countries of the european higher education area to implement the reforms agreed by them, which aim to accelerate the achievement of the objectives of the bologna process and to enhance the credibility of the european higher education area. unfortunately, some member states and their higher education institutions still do not recognise each other's degrees and qualifications in the european higher education area, which can lead to disadvantages. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. - the house of honor. the bologna process is a great new trend in european education, which will result in a new, interconnected, free and efficient network of higher education that can compete globally with other large systems of higher education and contribute to strengthening the common european spirit. i agree that this process has made significant progress in the last 15 years. among the recommendations in the report, i find particularly important that scholarships should be used to ensure that higher education is accessible to as many young people as possible. i also consider it essential to make further progress in the areas of credit transfer, interoperability, student and teacher mobility and quality assurance. the positive effects of the bologna process can also help the development of the public education system if the ideas on teacher training and the involvement of secondary school teachers are realised. overall, it is in our common interest to continue, broaden and deepen the bologna process: a path towards a more successful, more civilised and more cohesive europe.
in writing. ‒ the implementation of the bologna process is crucial to have a high-quality, coherent and transparent higher education sector, which exists in an excellent way. this document summarises the european system of higher education, and i fully support the s&d position on bologna process in an understandable, accessible and credible way in order to ensure compatibility and comparability of standards and quality across different higher educational systems, support mobility and internationalisation, while respecting the diversity and autonomy of individual countries and universities.
in writing. ‒ the european cinema in the digital age report aims to support and promote european cinema, its distribution and awareness, so that everyone can benefit from its cultural heritage. the film has both cultural and economic value in society. an audiovisual sector that contributes to economic growth, job creation and stimulates innovation in the european digital market. film education can have a significant impact on individuals, influencing the development of young people's personalities and their perception of the world. the introduction of film education at all levels of education in the member states therefore plays a very important role and has long-term benefits. interacting with european films is the best way to learn about the history, culture, traditions and languages of our european neighbours. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european commission and the executive agencies in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors has stated that the agency's accounts for the financial year 2013 are reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it is important to emphasise that errors in payments still occur and that the supervision and control systems are only partially effective. it shall draw attention to the principles of cost efficiency and cost discipline. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of granting budgetary discharge to the european commission. however, during the debate on the dossier in the committee on agriculture, some lines were raised by the rapporteur with which i do not agree. fortunately, we were able to rule them out. the classification of smaller eu support programmes such as the school milk and school fruit schemeinto the rural development pillar would be an ill-considered solution. in hungary, in the current eu funding cycle, 72% of eu aid is allocated to cap pillar i (direct aids + market measures) and 28% to cap pillar ii (rural development). the transfer of the financing of small eu support programmes to pillar ii would effectively bring these programmes to a halt, as rural development would not have sufficient additional resources to finance these programmes. their budget must therefore remain in pillar i, where the necessary funds are provided. bringing the member states' paying agencies under union supervision would, on the one hand, significantly limit national sovereignty in the use of union funds and, on the other hand, infringe the provisions on the division of competences in the eu treaties. therefore, this solution should not be accepted either.
in writing. ‒ the committee on budgetary control presented 52 reports on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of certain eu institutions for the financial year 2013. all reports are based on the court's examination and recommend the closure of the accounts of the institution concerned for the financial year 2013. i voted for the motions on that basis.
in writing. ‒ the opinion of the committee on transport has been incorporated to a large extent in the report on the discharge for the general budget of the eu for 2013. the report summarises in detail the budgetary tasks to be carried out in the regions of the member states in order to allow the most efficient use of resources. i voted for the 2013 discharge.
in writing. ‒ the youth unemployment rate has been at a dramatic level for years and is rising steadily. the eu has developed a number of instruments to support member states in tackling the threats facing many young people. one of those instruments is the youth employment initiative, which aims to contribute to the achievement of the policy objectives of the youth guarantee in those parts of europe where youth unemployment is highest. member states have not yet made sufficient use of this tool, which is available to regions with unemployment rates above 25% for those aged 15 to 25. one reason for this inadequate utilisation rate is the lack of public funds needed for projects aimed at providing young people with employment, traineeships or training. the member states most affected by youth unemployment are also those with the greatest difficulties in coping with co-financing. to enable the member states concerned to launch these important projects, the european commission has decided to take urgent action to release €1 billion. the increase in the envelope will be used to increase the pre-financing of the 2015 operational programmes, giving a new impetus to the fight against unemployment. i agree with the political objectives of the european commission and the means it has set up to achieve them.
in writing. ‒ in the fight against youth unemployment, and in particular for the member states most in need, the european parliament today amended the european social fund (esf) regulation to provide more rapid assistance to over 7 million unemployed young europeans through the european youth initiative (eyi). the previous rules across europe were less suitable for launching more flexible and effective measures, so hungary independently initiated programmes targeting young people. on this basis, the greatest reduction in youth unemployment has been in hungary over the past two years. just a reminder: in hungary, the unemployment rate for the 15-24 generation was only 11% in 2002, but by 2010 it had almost doubled and increased by half (27%). today, it's about 20 percent, which is better than the french, belgian or swedish data. the increased amount of pre-financing and the procedural changes may also be more beneficial for hungary, which is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the codification reports noted by andrzej duda help to structure european union legislation in a uniform way. as a result, the union acts to be consolidated are repealed and replaced by a single legislative act by a single legislative decision, provided that the changes do not involve substantial amendments. this procedure, based on the interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament, the european commission and the european council on better law-making, facilitates the coordination of legislative processes and contributes to making them more transparent for union citizens. i voted in favour of these reports because, as a member, i consider it essential to improve the quality of legislation and to simplify it.

in writing. ‒ during eu accession, the hungarian parliament of the time voted virtually unread on the treaty of lisbon, paragraphs 107 and 108 of which, dealing with state aid, have just been voted on. if they had read it, they could not have signed it in this form with such a minimal national interest-enforcing intention, because it prevents the less developed countries from catching up by harshly restricting state aid, whereas all the now-developed central countries used state aid methods freely when their economies were still in the upswing stage. i had to reject both of them to express my disagreement with the eu's rules which put the periphery and the centre in the same category and thus virtually exclude the periphery from being included.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the european commission in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for the financial year 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors states that it has obtained assurances as to the reliability of the annual accounts for the financial year 2013 and as to the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. it draws the attention of the european commission to certain weaknesses in the reliability of first-level checks carried out by member states and to the need to strengthen efficient and effective financial management. it calls on the member states to ensure greater transparency in their cooperation with the commission. the report of the people's party rapporteur ingeborg graessle was voted on by the committee at its meeting at the end of march and it was decided to grant the discharge and to close the accounts for 2013. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out, in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for 2013, the financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds. the report concludes that the investigations have provided sufficient assurance that the annual accounts of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2013 are reliable and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. in terms of payments, despite the corrective measures, there are still errors. however, the final accounts report states that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of granting budgetary discharge to the european development funds. it is of the utmost importance that the european commission manages these resources responsibly. this is particularly the case when the member states themselves finance the development programmes and not the eu budget. the commission should therefore take due account of the observations and suggestions of the european court of auditors. we want the eu institutions to manage the resources entrusted to them responsibly. they should set an example to the eu member states in the area of responsible budgetary management.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the european parliament in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court found that parliament had used the funds for the right purposes and that the institution had operated its system of supervision and control in a satisfactory manner. the court's audit did not reveal any major shortcomings, but it highlights the need to continue to improve transparency and efficiency in political and administrative activities. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp parliamentary group, i supported the granting of the exemption.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union in respect of the council in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. in its 2013 annual report, the court of auditors concluded that, on the basis of its audit work, the payments made by the institutions and bodies in respect of administrative and other expenditure for the financial year 2013 were, overall, free from material error. the basic reason for the refusal of the discharge was the interinstitutional dispute between the council and parliament on discharge. the council refuses to cooperate with parliament in the discharge procedure, which means that the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament cannot discharge the budget. the panel decided at its meeting at the end of march to postpone the granting of the exemption. as the people's party chairman of the report, i voted in committee and in plenary to support the postponement of the discharge.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european court of auditors in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the report notes that the court's annual accounts are audited by an independent auditor, so that it can apply the same transparency and accountability as for audited entities. the financial statements give a true picture of the court's financial situation. the report welcomes the court's internal reform programme and recommends that the duration of each audit be reduced so as not to compromise the quality of the work. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. as the people's party chairman of the report, i voted in favour of granting the discharge in the committee vote and in the plenary vote.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for the economic and social committee in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. in its annual report, the court of auditors' audit work found that payments for 2013 were free from material error and no significant errors were identified in respect of human resources and public procurement. it points out that translation costs vary widely across the eu institutions and calls on the translation task force to identify the reasons for this and propose a solution. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. as the people's party chairman of the report, i voted in favour of granting the discharge in the committee vote and in the plenary vote.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european data protection supervisor during the closure of the 2013 financial year. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors has found that the payments made in respect of the entitlements to the administrative and other expenditure of the european data protection supervisor for the financial year 2013 were, on the whole, free from material error and that the supervisory and control mechanisms in place for administrative and other expenditure had effectively ensured the correctness of the payments and functioned efficiently. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the report did not identify any serious deficiencies in human resources or public procurement. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. as the people's party rapporteur, i supported the discharge in the committee vote and in the plenary vote.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a comprehensive financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the performance, financial management and control of the agencies in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. in its report, the court of auditors stated that it had obtained assurance as to the reliability of the annual accounts of the agencies for the financial year 2013 and that the underlying transactions were legal and regular. it is necessary to reduce errors in the accounting policies of each agency. the court expressed concern about the geographical location of the agencies, many of which are far from the central european institutions, which entails additional travel costs and makes it difficult to implement the centralised budget. it considers that the recruitment procedure system needs to be improved, the reporting system made more efficient and the geographical balance of staff needs to be improved. the final audit report concludes that the financial review was carried out in an orderly manner and that no major deficiencies were found during the investigation. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ the european court of auditors has prepared its annual report for the financial year 2013, which was presented to the european parliament's plenary and then to the committee on budgetary control. following the presentation of the report, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the implementation of the budgets of the agencies and offices in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for the financial year 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the final report on the annual accounts of the european union agencies and offices for the financial year 2012 concludes that the financial controls were carried out in an orderly manner and that the audit found no deficiencies. the problems highlighted in the report and to be addressed by the agencies include the need to increase transparency in public procurement procedures, to make the conflict of interest procedure more effective and to further strengthen internal control systems. at its march meeting, the cont committee decided to accept the report and to close the accounts of that authority for 2013. i supported the adoption of the report in the committee vote and in the plenary vote on 29 april.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which examined and assessed the performance of the eu agencies in a detailed and balanced way. these agencies play an important role in supporting the policies of the union and it is therefore essential that they communicate their results to european citizens in a more effective way. in addition to detailing the positive trends and encouraging them to continue, i think it is right that the report also highlights areas where the agencies need to improve their performance. such as visibility and democratic accountability of agencies, or the consistency and comparability of documents.

in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of granting a budgetary discharge to the european chemicals agency. it is of the utmost importance that the european chemicals agency manages these resources responsibly. therefore, the european chemicals agency should take due account of any observations and suggestions made by the european court of auditors. we want the eu institutions to manage the resources entrusted to them responsibly. they should set an example to the eu member states in the area of responsible budgetary management.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the european institute of innovation and technology in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013. the court of auditors stated that the institute's annual accounts were reliable but that it could not find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. the final report highlights that the main problem with the european institute of innovation and technology is that, for the second year running, the agency has not been able to adequately demonstrate the legality and regularity of the grants paid. the court's inquiry also revealed irregularities in payment procedures and calls on the agency to strengthen its handling of public procurement procedures and staff matters. at its meeting at the end of march, the committee decided to postpone the granting of the discharge, considering that further clarification of the agency's 2013 financial management is required in order to receive the final accounts. i voted with the european people's party in both the committee vote and the plenary vote, in favour of postponing the granting of the discharge.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for artemis in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court's annual report stated that it had obtained assurance that the institute's annual accounts were reliable but could not find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. it highlights the lack of an internal control system and of a comprehensive set of rules for detecting and dealing with incompatibilities. it is concerned that the agreement with nfa does not contain practical arrangements for ex post controls. it also highlights the low rate of budget implementation. the report points out that the committee did not recommend granting the exemption until these were clarified. at its meeting at the end of march, the committee decided to postpone the granting of the discharge, considering that further clarification of the agency's 2013 financial management is required in order to receive the final accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to postpone the granting of the discharge.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union for clean sky in the context of the closure of the 2013 accounts procedure. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the court of auditors stated that the audits had provided it with assurance as to the reliability of the annual accounts for the financial year 2013 and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. it stresses that, although the delay in payment of budget appropriations has decreased compared to previous years, it is still high. welcomes the further improvement of the management, administrative and financial procedures, but calls for the integration of gmt tools to be improved and for ex post controls to be introduced. the report considers that the functioning of the internal control system needs to be made more efficient. it considers it important to adopt a comprehensive policy on conflicts of interest. the final audit report concluded that the financial and regularity reviews did not reveal any serious deficiencies. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the european court of auditors has prepared its annual report for the financial year 2013, which was presented to the european parliament's plenary and then to the committee on budgetary control. following the presentation of the report, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the implementation of the budgets of the agencies and offices in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for the financial year 2013. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the final report on the annual accounts of the european union agencies and offices for the financial year 2012 concludes that the financial controls were carried out in an orderly manner and that the audit found no deficiencies. the problems highlighted in the report and to be addressed by the agencies include the need to increase transparency in public procurement procedures, to make the conflict of interest procedure more effective and to further strengthen internal control systems. at its march meeting, the cont committee decided to accept the report and to close the accounts of that authority for 2013. i supported the adoption of the report in the committee vote and in the plenary vote on 29 april.
in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out, in the context of the closure of accounts procedure for 2013, a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the eniac joint undertaking. on the basis of the court's report, the institution has obtained a sufficient degree of certainty that eniac's annual accounts are reliable, but has not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as regards the legality and regularity of the transactions. the report highlights that the court has for the third year running identified weaknesses in the legality and regularity of the annual budget. information on the ex post control strategy is not sufficient to demonstrate the operational effectiveness of the control tools. there is little information on the contribution of the member states to the union payments. it notes that eniac has taken comprehensive measures to address the conflict of interest. the report draws attention to the fact that the exemption was not recommended by the panel until these open issues were clarified. at its meeting at the end of march, the committee decided to postpone the granting of the discharge, considering that further clarification of the agency's 2013 financial management is required in order to receive the final accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to postpone the granting of the discharge.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation by the european court of auditors of its annual report for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out, in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013, a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the fuel cell and hydrogen joint undertaking. the committee's primary task is to ensure and monitor the proper and efficient implementation of the community budget. the report welcomes the fact that the court of auditors has found the accounts of the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking for the financial year 2013 to be reliable and that the underlying financial transactions were legal and regular in all material respects. it recognises concrete measures to prevent conflicts of interest. requests that the joint undertaking submit to the discharge authority a report on the economic and social benefits of the completed projects, and at the same time a report on the contributions of the members. the final audit report concludes that the financial and regularity reviews of the joint undertaking have not revealed any serious deficiencies. the committee decided at its meeting at the end of march to grant the discharge and to close the 2013 accounts. i voted in committee and in plenary to grant the discharge.
in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of granting a budgetary discharge to the fuel cell and hydrogen joint undertaking. it is of the utmost importance that the fuel cells and hydrogen joint undertaking manages these resources responsibly. the joint undertaking should therefore take due account of any observations and suggestions made by the european court of auditors. we want the eu institutions to manage the resources entrusted to them responsibly. they should set an example to the eu member states in the area of responsible budgetary management.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out, in the context of the closure of the accounts procedure for 2013, a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the joint undertaking for research on innovative medicines. the court found the institute's annual accounts to be reliable, but it could not find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as to the legality and regularity of the transactions. the error rate in the legality and regularity of transactions is above the threshold and this has been the court's objection for the third year running. the final report shall also invite the joint undertaking to develop an action plan with clear and concrete measures and deadlines to avoid conflicts of interest and to strengthen transparency. present this report to the discharge authority. it also recommends that a full and adequate financial evaluation of the rights and obligations of the joint undertakings be carried out. the european people's party supported the granting of the joint undertaking's exemption in the plenary vote, as a result of the swift and effective action taken to address the identified deficiencies and the action plan adopted.

in writing. ‒ following the presentation of the annual report of the european court of auditors for the financial year 2013, the european parliament's committee on budgetary control carried out a financial audit of the general budget of the european union concerning the fusion energy development and iter european joint undertaking in the framework of the 2013 closure procedure. the court of auditors' report states that it has not been able to find sufficient and appropriate audit evidence as regards the legality and regularity of the transactions of the joint undertaking. the exemption report shows that the joint undertaking's letter of intent also reports a significant increase in risk. it also expressed concerns that the joint undertaking did not have a system in place to monitor cost fluctuations on a regular basis, did not have detailed financial statements, and did not have an approved staff policy. it asks to submit a report to the discharge authority on the payments made by the members and similarly on the current level of implementation of the projects, any risks, future developments. although significant progress has been made in the internal control system, a number of measures still need to be implemented in this area. the european people's party supported the granting of the joint undertaking's exemption in the plenary vote, as a result of the swift and effective action taken to address the identified deficiencies and the action plan adopted.

in writing. ‒ as long as money fulfilled its original functions of facilitating the exchange of goods, mediating value and preserving it, there could be no problems. since it has been used for speculative purposes, it has caused enormous economic and social problems and conflicts. the proposal is another attempt to curb the financial liberalisation implemented during the 1990s, but it is doomed to failure from the outset, since these investment funds also serve financial speculation. i didn't vote for him because of his weakness. a real result would have been achieved by regulations similar to the glass-steagall act of 1933, significantly restricting the scope for financial speculation, including effectively separating commercial banking from investment banking.
in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of the adoption of a draft law on the import of textile products from certain third countries not subject to eu import regulations. this is an apparently technical amendment which brings the existing comitology procedure into line with the treaty of lisbon. accordingly, powers should be conferred on the commission either for the traditional comitology procedure and thus for decision-making in the member states or for commission legislation with strong council and parliamentary control. in this connection, i am opposed to any attempt to treat the legislation to be amended in a uniform manner (the so-called omnibus approach). most of the delegations are not only technical issues, many of them also have a significant political dimension. therefore, the legislation to be amended and the powers contained therein should be examined and decided on a case-by-case basis. because of the political implications, this cannot be ignored.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the eu has only had bilateral textile trade agreements with russia and serbia. with the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, that council regulation has lost its meaning.
in writing. ‒ at its meeting on 9 february 2015, the bureau adopted the guidelines proposed by the secretary-general for the 2016 budget. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, including the countries of the former soviet union, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe. the member states are currently facing heavy burdens of public debt and financial consolidation, and parliament should pursue a responsible budgetary policy and exercise restraint in this regard. at the same time, it is necessary to ensure that sufficient resources are made available to the new parliament to enable it to exercise its powers and to ensure the proper functioning of the institution.

in writing. ‒ the proposal concerns the revenue and expenditure appropriations for the operation of the european parliament for the financial year 2016. the report of the committee on budgets, taking into account the priorities proposed by the secretary-general for 2016, the significant additional expenditure on parliament following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, and the political priorities adopted by parliament in the last legislative period, concludes that the increase in parliament's current expenditure in 2016 compared to 2015 should not exceed 2%. further increases in expenditure can only be justified by the need to strengthen the security of parliament's buildings and it systems. in view of all this, it proposes that the motion be adopted. i have voted in favour of the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for a resolution on budgetary issues relating to the increased workload of the ep for 2016. the presentation focuses on security issues, including building security and information security.
i voted against the report on the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office. as a hungarian mp, i did not do this merely out of personal conviction, as the hungarian parliament adopted a resolution on the draft regulation establishing the european public prosecutor's office in october 2013. in this regard, it found that this was contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. the eppo should be able to provide the necessary legal advice to the national authorities in the member states, in particular to the national authorities responsible for the prosecution of serious criminal offences. and he also found that it extends beyond the law of our basic law on the functioning of the european union. by the way, yesterday in this debate, you talked about this function as the european public prosecutor. it should be noted that, as many would like, there is no single european state yet, and many of us are here to prevent that!
in writing. ‒ efficient and decisive action is needed to combat misuse, fraud and crime of eu funds. however, i abstained as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation from the vote on the interim report on the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office, as this report does not take into account the objections of the national parliaments, including the hungarian parliament, to subsidiarity and sovereignty (yellow-ground procedure). this right, granted by the treaty of lisbon, has been exhausted, since the commission has not taken any account of the objections raised by the national parliaments in relation to the eppo. the unresolved issues of subsidiarity and national sovereignty remain unresolved. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the national prosecutors' offices are not obliged to provide information to the public. the issues of jurisdiction are not clear. thus, while fully agreeing with the aim of taking effective action against those who commit crimes against the financial interests of the union, because of the many unresolved issues in the current interim report and because the national parliaments' concerns were ignored in the process, i could not support the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the annual report 2013 of the european investment bank. however, i would like to draw attention to what the report itself rightly mentions, namely that we must bear in mind the importance of supporting smes, their drive for innovation and sustainability. however, the primary objective of investment must be to create quality jobs. the projects supported should have a greater impact on job creation, which can only be truly beneficial if it means quality jobs where a well-qualified workforce is needed. otherwise, there will be no one to create new smes and innovative start-ups. in order to avoid losing more generations, the eib should invest in measures that create sustainable jobs for the younger generation in addition to the youth employment initiative, and this should be coordinated with appropriate education/training systems, which are clearly lacking in some member states. the commitment by vice-president katainen to increase the eib's potential in youth employment and education is welcome. we expect to report on the results of this in the next annual report. however, in this area we cannot rely solely on the commission and the eib, the responsibility of the member states is indisputable. the eib's activities are not a substitute for economic policy and structural reforms in member states aimed at job creation.

in writing. developing countries have a disproportionately high number of people with disabilities, who very often live in extreme poverty and lack basic human rights. the european year of development is a unique opportunity to do something for them. but ending poverty and inequality can only be achieved by mobilising sufficient and adequate resources for all and better targeting marginalised groups such as children, women, the elderly or people with disabilities. illegal capital outflows from developing countries amount to us$1 trillion, or ten times official development assistance. it is therefore necessary to strengthen the tax collection capacity of developing countries by strengthening the areas of tax administration, financial management and public financial management. international collaboration is needed to improve the quality of statistics, data and information, including data disaggregated by income, gender, age, racial and ethnic origin, migration status, disability, geographical location and other characteristics relevant to the national context. this is the only way to ensure transparent and effective implementation of assistance and financing, in particular by signing and effectively implementing the provisions of the un convention against corruption.
blue-card question. – mr president, i listened quite carefully to the explanation by my colleague, but my question is rather of a general nature. when we are talking about this battle, as the commissioner has pointed out already, it is about money, nothing else: money from the point of view of the governments; and money from the point of view of the criminals. does she think that the current policies of the european commission are adequate in order to prevent future crimes?
any measure or initiative that would harmonise, simplify or make tax practices more transparent within the eu is welcome. and the fact that from this year onwards the rate of taxation of radio and audiovisual media services, telecommunications services and electronic services provided to private individuals will be determined by the tariff key of the place of residence of the private consumer. well, this is very important for my country, hungarian businesses, because until now they were at a huge disadvantage, because they could only provide services at the highest vat rate in the union, i.e. 27%, and everyone else was cheaper than them. however, in addition to the fact that this in itself raises the question of overdose, there are two other things that pose dangers. hopefully, a european tax union will solve all of this, but until we get there, we face two dangers here. one is that the idea of a 'mini one-stop shop' seems very good, but here it is important to be careful that individual operators do not collect, say, the amounts corresponding to the highest tax rate in the member state. this is important because for some euro services it does not make such a marked difference. it is also possible to distort trade by allowing certain suppliers to supply only one type of market or a few markets where vat is the lowest. i therefore ask, and i propose, that we consider establishing a common vat rate for services which are the most european and operate across borders.
the court of justice of the european union recently ruled that member states should be able to reduce the tax on books stored in digital form. we may be happy about this, but the answer is not that simple. so the first question that comes up is, what is this digital form, what do we consider to be part of this circle? and then we're not happy anymore, because it turns out that only the books that appear on physical media, on cds, on flash drives. at the same time, books downloaded from the internet, for example, are already considered as a service. i'm afraid that any exceptions we make in this area will only complicate the system. but that is not what we are interested in at all, we are interested in simplification, because i think all the speakers have said that we have a common interest in making our businesses, especially small and mediumsized enterprises, which are poorer in capital and have fewer opportunities, competitive in this area. so we should have a system in place to support these companies that have suffered a significant competitive disadvantage in this area. at the same time, i would like to draw attention to another aspect of the issue of vat reductions: it is clear that this is a budgetary issue, a matter for the member states. we're not here to complicate things. simplification, acceleration, and the first step of that is to have a very good piece of legislation that creates the framework for that.
in writing. in the context of quality healthcare, it should be emphasised that patient safety is also closely linked to labour shortages. unfortunately, there was very little mention of this in the report. the european union is facing a growing shortage of health workers. the commission estimates that by 2020 there will be a shortage of around 1 million healthcare workers in europe's healthcare systems. the reasons are complex, including the rise in the average age of workers, the lack of the necessary replacement, the increase in the demand for care of an ageing society. however, for hungary and several other new member states, the real problem is the migration of health workers. in europe, we are witnessing a reverse labour dumping: the old member states are luring doctors, nurses and social workers from the new member states abroad with the promise of wages five to ten times higher, creating a serious problem of security of supply in the countries concerned. as the member states most affected by migration cannot be expected to raise the salaries of health workers to a similar level in a short time, it is essential that the european commission address the problem as a matter of priority. it is not enough to draw up eu action plans and studies, concrete assistance and european solidarity are needed to remedy the deteriorating situation.

in writing. - my fellow members of parliament! an integrated strategy and clear legal rules are needed to ensure that the digital revolution shaping our world can deliver on our core values and that the changes brought about by development benefit all european citizens. as a politician of the mszp and also as a member of the political leadership of the european internet foundation i actively support the european commission's proposal for a digital single market. however, in order to create a digital environment that allows cross-border cooperation with the necessary guarantees and at the same time ensures the rights of consumers and citizens, as envisaged by the social democrats, not only a single digital market is needed, but a digital union. europe must play an active role in the digital revolution, and it is in hungary's interest to be part of the digital union. the progressive innovations brought about by the digital revolution are bringing about major changes in the functioning of almost all sectors, including tourism, which is a major driver of europe's economy. as vice-chair of the european parliament's committee on transport and tourism, i therefore attach great importance to the debate on the creation of the digital union.

written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ the codification report, noted by andrzej duda, helps to structure european union legislation in a uniform way. as a result, the union acts to be consolidated are repealed and replaced by a single legislative act by a single legislative decision, provided that the changes do not involve substantial amendments. this procedure, based on the interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament, the european commission and the european council on better law-making, facilitates the coordination of legislative processes and contributes to making them more transparent for union citizens. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it essential to improve the quality of legislation, to simplify legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation (codified text). as an alternate member of the delegation to the eu/iceland joint parliamentary committee and the eea joint parliamentary committee responsible for relations with switzerland and norway, i consider it particularly important to draw attention to the fact that the amendments will make cooperation more effective. one of the main elements of this is the bilateral safeguard regime, the implementation of which requires the adoption of safeguard measures under uniform conditions. i think it is important to note that the european parliament, through its work in the consultation procedure, is making a tangible contribution to making the legislation more effective in a way that is understandable to the electorate.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of consulting the european economic and social committee in shaping the institutional future of the european union, because the eesc has shown in its work that it can make a useful contribution to the development of common european solutions by integrating the perspectives, interests and knowledge of the various economic operators and by directly representing them, especially in the wake of the crisis. i consider this to be particularly important in the current period of economic governance, and particularly in order to assess and validate the economic aspects of the non-euro area member states. i also took into account that the treaty of lisbon itself assigns an important role to the european economic and social committee and i believe that analysing and asserting the perspectives beyond the government, the council and political actors can also be useful in exploiting the potential of the new institutional structure.

in writing. the reduction of financial speculation is a welcome objective. unfortunately, this solution is fragile and, at first sight, extremely bureaucratic, and it also requires the member states to exercise their competence. and yet, the regulation does not address the root of the problem, and so it is not able to stop the rampant financial speculation that we are seeing today as a symptom of the greek crisis. the proposal is unacceptable because the present situation is unsustainable, with the eu divided into debtors' and creditors' camps. it is very timely that the free flow of capital should be replaced by controlled flows of capital, otherwise the fundamental objective of preventing financial manipulation to plunder economically weaker member states cannot be achieved.

in writing. ‒ i would like to stress that official development assistance should prioritise basic social services for all and public goods that the private sector can provide less effectively, such as basic education, social safety nets, healthcare, and sanitation, water and energy infrastructure, so that developing countries can reach their full potential. it is important that accessibility should be a fundamental criterion in international public funding to support universal and inclusive services and infrastructure. i supported the adoption of the report in agreement with the fidesz-kdnp group.
in writing. ‒ the third financing for development conference will be held in addis ababa in july 2015. the conference brings together high-level representatives from political life, international actors, non-governmental actors and business actors. the aim is to decide on the amount of money to be allocated to international development and to support the implementation of the eu and global development framework post-2015, including the sustainable development goals, which are planned to be adopted in new york in september 2015. the report aims to establish an international partnership for development finance that effectively supports the above objectives. the report highlights the european union's leadership in international development and stresses the importance of shared responsibility, and calls on emerging and middle-income countries to make significant commitments. the report urges the european union to immediately re-commit itself to a target of 0.7% of gni for official development assistance (oda). at least 50% of official development assistance and at least 0,2% of gni to be reserved for least developed countries and taking into account budgetary constraints. these objectives are in line with the policy pursued by fidesz-kdnp, in particular with regard to the settlement of the migration issue. that's why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ patient safety and the fight against drug resistance with particular reference to antimicrobial resistance is not a new topic for those involved in the management of health systems. i am convinced that responsible and targeted use of antibiotics in both human and veterinary medicine, and global strategies to control infections across all sectors of healthcare (hospitals, long-term care and outpatient facilities) are the cornerstones of effective interventions to screen for and prevent the transmission of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. i would like to stress the need to ensure that health policies do not fall victim to the cuts caused by the economic crisis and austerity measures, and that the objective of applying the highest possible patient safety standards set by the eu is not jeopardised. on behalf of the fidesz-kdnp group, i supported the adoption of the report
in writing. between 50 and 70% of meat products tested by european consumer organisations in 14 eu member states were found to be contaminated with antibiotic-resistant bacteria. if you have a problem with cooking or eating, you have a good chance of getting these bacteria during a hospital visit or even a visit. it's a good sign. the proposal attempts in many respects to find a way out of a situation which is not in the least rosy and should therefore be supported. it would be helpful if the old member countries did not lure the health workers and researchers of the new member countries with better salaries, which are largely covered by the colonization of the new member countries. they should be training their own specialists before the bacteria that are pooping on the border win.
in writing. ‒ antibiotic resistance could threaten the lives of up to 10 million european citizens by 2050. the report submitted shall contain reasonable and feasible proposals to minimise this risk. it is particularly important that patients are given adequate information about the possible long-term effects of each treatment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on safer healthcare, which helps prevent and control healthcare-associated infections. the report deals with the control of serious cross-border health threats, which i believe is of common european interest. the report highlights the sad fact that 8-12% of patients in hospitals in the union experience avoidable adverse events in healthcare. i believe that it is essential for the safety of patients and for quality healthcare that healthcare professionals are able to work in a safe and decent working environment. i personally welcome the improvement of the eu surveillance system for healthcare-associated infections and regret that the relative progress of member states in patient safety is uneven. i agree that health systems should not be affected by restrictive measures and that adequate funding for these systems should be maintained; therefore member states should in particular avoid harmful measures. the report calls on member states to ensure that an even more patient-centred approach is introduced and that adequate healthcare professionals are available to this end; and encourages member states, including hungary, to ensure equal access to healthcare services for patients in order to eliminate health inequalities.
oral explanations of vote
i supported the adoption of the report because small and medium-sized enterprises must be given a prominent role in the green economy. the global annual market for this economy is in the order of €1 trillion and could double by 2020. why is it important that smes play a key role in this economy? because economic development cannot be an end in itself, and 67% of jobs in the european union are in small and medium-sized enterprises. therefore, they should also be assisted in this respect by means of loans and grant aid. in this context, i find it strange that the benefit for smes in the european fund for strategic investments is extended to large companies with 3,000 employees, so that it does not really help this group of companies that create jobs.
written explanations of vote
in writing. ‒ it is well known that more than 98% of eu enterprises are smes, and these smes account for 67% of the total employment level in the union and 58% of the gross value added. this means that smes are the backbone of the european union's economy and an important driver of long-term economic growth and job creation in the 28 member states. it is important that policy-makers fully understand the potential of the green economy, but also recognise the difficulties currently faced by smes, in particular in greening their products, production processes, business practices and services. the commission's green action plan for smes is an initiative to further encourage smes to extend the benefits of green growth. the enormous potential of the green economy can only be fully exploited if the right framework for research, development and innovation (r & d & i) is in place. although various public funding schemes may provide some incentives for r & d & i, the biggest incentive is an open, stable and innovation-friendly regulatory and investment framework. clearly, green growth has great potential, but this potential can only be fully exploited if a number of basic conditions are met. such conditions include a stronger emergence of entrepreneurial thinking, the development of open and innovation-friendly rules, diversification of access to finance or the expansion of opportunities for knowledge sharing.
in writing. every year, there are many excellent statistics showing that more than 98% of eu enterprises are smes and that smes account for 67% of total employment and 58% of gross value added in the union. but the subsidies, the tax breaks, the big corporations are getting the bulk of it. perhaps the most tangible element of the proposal is that it calls on the commission and the eib to ensure that smes, including green and innovative enterprises, are the main beneficiaries of the support provided under the proposal during the implementation phase of the european investment plan. i'm all for any solution that can help small businesses overcome the disadvantages of multi-channel, including this one.
in writing. ‒ the changing environment and the emergence of a smart and green economy present both challenges and opportunities for all actors. the situation of small and medium-sized enterprises is particularly important as they are important employers and can also represent a breakout opportunity for many. these enterprises are flexible and creative in adapting to market changes and are able to mobilise significant intellectual capital. among the instruments proposed, those relating in particular to research and innovation and training and to regulatory rationalisation appear promising.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the green growth opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), as i consider the role of smes in the green economy to be important. the report points out that more than 98% of enterprises in the union are smes and that smes account for 67% of the total employment level in the union and 58% of the gross value added. the report supports the vision of green growth and the circular economy and highlights the significant economic and employment potential of these areas for different sectors. it stresses the need to look at green growth in a broader perspective, which i believe is lacking in many member states. i find it regrettable that the hungarian government does not have this perspective and that it does not exploit the potential of green energy. the report's recommendations include that the eu needs to radically change its entrepreneurial culture so that more people start their own businesses and explore more business opportunities, especially in the area of green growth. in this process, the added value of the eu budget in supporting smes, micro, social enterprises and cooperatives to access finance and international markets (both in terms of operations, research and development, start-up incentives, deregulation and, for example, knowledge management) will be highlighted. i hope that the recommendations of the report will be implemented in hungary as soon as possible.

mr president, the situation in europe as a whole is serious as regards illegal immigration and asylum. it is not only serious in the southern countries where tragedies reach the threshold of media attention, but also in states where the population has not yet experienced this phenomenon on such a scale, such as hungary. today, it has the second highest number of immigrants per capita in the world after sweden, according to frontex data. it's increased by 20 percent in a few months, and most of them are not eligible for refugee protection, but are clearly economic migrants. illegal immigrants should therefore be distinguished from refugees eligible for asylum and from illegal economic immigrants. europe will not be able to deal with the growing migration crisis unless it makes this distinction with clear consequences at the policy and regulatory level. it is clear that in terms of refugee policy, moral considerations, international treaties, obligations are the starting point. the management of illegal economic migration should remain a member state competence.
in writing. first, we need to clarify the concepts to avoid political demagoguery. immigration and refugee issues are not directly linked. refugees should be recognised as persons who are persecuted in their country of origin or habitual residence, or who have a well-founded fear of persecution, on account of their race, nationality, membership of a particular social group, religion or political opinion. regardless of the economic status of the refugee. this is a matter of solidarity. neither the eu nor the member states have a choice on this issue: we must remain in solidarity with refugees and with member states facing disproportionate refugee pressures. this solidarity also prevents the criminalisation of refugees. throughout history, hundreds of thousands of hungarians have been accepted in all parts of the world, having fled from various regimes. they weren't treated like criminals either. the immigration issue is different in that the european union and its member states can decide whether to allow legal immigration from third countries into the eu. this issue, together with the demographic challenges facing europe, is indeed one of the most important issues of our time. but we must find solutions to this question together in europe, responsibly, on the basis of facts and not on the basis of the fears and prejudices of citizens. the so-called national consultation in hungary, which links immigration to terrorism and which raises politically driven, polarized questions. this is all the result of irresponsible politics.
in writing. the commission's proposal is an important step forward in the common european asylum and immigration policy. it recommends effective and rapid measures to save lives and to resolve the crisis caused by the refugee crisis affecting the mediterranean region in a humane manner. it initiates the distribution of refugees among member states and provides financial and technical assistance to the countries to which refugees arrive. the solutions developed will be available to all member states concerned, including hungary, at a later stage. it is crucial that the commission proposes to strengthen the common european asylum policy, to make legal migration possible, to exploit its economic benefits and to effectively integrate immigrants. one of the key issues for the future of europe is to give migrants a real chance to live their lives as equal european citizens. we need to create proper educational opportunities, employment programs, child care, and community opportunities. this kind of integration is in the common interest of all of us. this allows newcomers to europe to play a useful economic role, to be equal members of communities, and helps to prevent radicalisation and xenophobia. there are also public conditions for integration. any statement or action that arouses anti-migrant sentiment, especially if it comes from the leaders in charge, is poisoning the atmosphere, damaging europe and all the member states. instead of resentment, we need rational dialogue, instead of closure, we need solidarity and cooperation.
