in writing. ‒ in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the new anti-money laundering regulation, already agreed with the council, which now obliges member states for the first time to identify the beneficial owners of companies, other legal persons and asset managers in a central database. the new directive aims to combat money laundering, tax-related crime and the financing of terrorism. money laundering has become one of the most profitable and largest businesses in the world today. according to the imf, the volume of money laundering is equivalent to 2 to 5% of the combined gdp of all countries on earth. the initiatives now proposed will finally coordinate and integrate existing standards and create a more targeted and focused risk-based approach to combat money laundering more effectively across the eu. i believe that member states should be able to require foreign entities on their territory to report any suspicious activity to the financial intelligence unit in the member state concerned. the commission has also received comments from the czech authorities, which have not provided any information on the measures taken by the czech republic to comply with the requirements of article 3 of the regulation. unfortunately, the interconnection of registers is essential for the usability of this information due to the cross-border nature of business transactions and the interconnectedness of the internal market. therefore, the registers should be urgently linked and made available to the authorities and obliged entities.

in writing. ‒ money laundering has become one of the most profitable and largest businesses in the world today. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the new money laundering regulation, which has already been agreed with the council, and which now for the first time requires member states to identify the beneficial owners of companies, other legal persons and asset managers in a central database. the new directive aims to combat money laundering, tax-related crime and the financing of terrorism. unfortunately, the interconnection of registers is essential for the usability of this information due to the cross-border nature of business transactions and the interconnectedness of the internal market. foreign entities must comply with the requirements of the country in question regarding the transparency of information.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the recommendation on the prevention of the use of financial systems for the purpose of money laundering or terrorist financing. i agree that in order to reduce the problem, targeted measures beyond criminal law are needed. i would also point out that the socialist and democratic group believes that much more effective measures are needed to eliminate tax havens in third countries, but i myself am firmly convinced that the existence of 'quasi-tax havens' and of secret and opaque tax agreements within the union's borders is unacceptable. the fight must be intensified in this area as well. i would also like to stress that this problem is closely linked to the issue of government corruption in some member states, which is also being legalised in some places by means of legislation. although the recommendation does not deal with this issue in detail, i believe that in the future we will have to pay more attention to this as it may also have a negative impact on the resources provided by the union.

in writing. many small businesses in the country have gone bankrupt because they could not access the income they were entitled to after working honestly. in many of its confused subcontracting chains, companies with interests in several countries were found. this regulation regulates insolvency proceedings involving several countries very well, and it clearly serves legal certainty, which is why i supported it wholeheartedly. it can be of great help to smes, which have been unable to take the costly and complex legal path.
in writing. ‒ given that the plenary did not fully share the principles of the hungarian people's party and the epp in its assessment of key issues, i had no choice but to abstain from the final vote in order to allow the dialogue to continue in the interinstitutional dialogue. mandating certification of origin at a later stage in the production chain would impose an excessive economic and administrative burden on european smes, while at the same time reinforcing control mechanisms in the countries of origin of minerals that contribute to a fair distribution of the resources of the system. i therefore aim to create a balanced regime that promotes sustainable development in countries of origin affected by armed conflict, without the economic effects of applying these rules being comparable to embargoes.

in writing. ‒ i agree with the eu's efforts to tackle more effectively than at present the financing of armed groups operating in conflict zones, one of the forms of which is that these groups finance their activities through mining and trading of minerals. so we offer alternatives to the acquisition of major minerals, such as gold in the first place, but also tin, tantalum, tungsten, which are easy and legal ways to acquire these minerals. the proposed voluntary self-certification scheme can be a good tool for importers who decide to carry out this activity responsibly. with this legislation, the union is contributing to international efforts to address the problems of resource-rich countries exposed to armed conflict, such as those in the african great lakes region. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the draft legislation.

in writing. ‒ mining and marketing of various ores and metals is one of the main sources of funding for conflicts of the war and civil war type in the world. these are usually mined under inhuman conditions, using slave, forced and child labour, with no regard for the rights and freedoms of workers, and with environmental destruction. the resources thus generated are, in a significant proportion of cases, used in an opaque way to maintain the repressive machinery of dictatorial regimes, to purchase weapons, to finance crime and terrorist activities. in my view, the fundamental values on which the european union is founded require us to do everything possible to combat this practice, to establish strict rules that promote ethical and responsible behaviour on this matter by european operators, while respecting the requirements of a market economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on self-certification for importers of minerals and metals from conflict-affected and high-risk areas. i agree that the mineral wealth in these areas while representing a huge development opportunity may be controversial if the revenues from them are used to fuel or sustain violent conflicts that undermine efforts towards development, good governance and the rule of law. in these areas, breaking the link between conflict and illegal mining is a critical element in guaranteeing peace, development and stability. the proposal highlights the sad fact that human rights abuses are widespread in the extractive industries, including child labour, sexual violence, enforced disappearances, forced evictions and the destruction of ritually or culturally significant sites. i therefore consider it important that parliament has today sent a strong signal to the european commission and the council to put an end to this phenomenon. the socialist and democratic group has unanimously supported the report, which is a step towards demonstrating that respect for human rights is more important than the economic interests of multinationals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the exemption of cadmium used in lighting and display lighting applications and its amendment to adapt it to technical progress. the proposal states that the commission has provided a new, specific exemption for cadmium in a directive. they claim that it is already used in displays due to its low energy consumption, highlighting its positive effects and that quantum dots without cadmium are not technically feasible yet. on the contrary, i agree that there has been a significant development in the market and therefore cadmium-free quantum dots can be expected to have energy saving properties similar to those of cadmium quantum dots. it is also a fact that, based on the eco-label information, when comparing televisions of the same size, displays using cadmium-free quantum dots showed a lower energy consumption compared to cadmium quantum dots. the commission's justification for the exemption is therefore based on an outdated situation as regards the feasibility of replacing quantum dots containing cadmium. in order to resolve the conflicting situation, i support the request to the commission to repeal this delegated directive without delay.
in writing. ‒ the delegated act in question would have provided significant relief to bioethanol importers. under the guise of simplification, it would have abolished the quarterly reporting obligation and most of the procedural obligations relating to import licences for ethyl alcohol. consequently, a huge increase in ethanol imports would take place on the union market, which would lead to the bankruptcy of the hungarian bioethanol producers. this must be prevented, as bioethanol production provides a stable income for maize farmers and a significant amount of non-gmo and healthy feed, which is needed more than ever in the eu and hungary. this legislation would have given an advantage to the major bioethanol exporting countries over union producers. many of these countries are now in eu free trade negotiations, and i'll just mention ttip. beyond that, i have environmental concerns. bioethanol is produced from gm crops in the major ethanol exporting third countries. on the other hand, these places are cutting down rainforests and forcing farmers off their land to establish huge monocultures of maize, rapeseed or palm for bioethanol production. if large quantities of foreign bioethanol were allowed in, the eu would also contribute to the negative effects mentioned above. for these reasons, i voted in favour of a move which was also in line with the line of the european people's party of attacking the delegated act.
in writing. ‒ the delegated act in question would have provided significant relief to bioethanol importers. under the guise of simplification, it would have abolished the quarterly reporting obligation and most of the procedural obligations relating to import licences for ethyl alcohol. consequently, a huge increase in ethanol imports would take place on the union market, which would lead to the bankruptcy of the hungarian bioethanol producers. this must be prevented, as bioethanol production provides a stable income for maize farmers and a significant amount of non-gmo and healthy feed, which is needed more than ever in the eu and hungary. this legislation would have given an advantage to the major bioethanol exporting countries over union producers. the eu is currently negotiating free trade agreements with several of these countries. the elimination of duties and market access should be negotiated in free trade negotiations and not decided in a commission act. in addition to the above, environmental concerns are also raised. bioethanol is produced from gm crops in the major ethanol exporting third countries. on the other hand, these places are cutting down rainforests and forcing farmers off their land to establish huge monocultures of maize, rapeseed or palm for bioethanol production. if large quantities of foreign bioethanol were allowed in, the eu would also contribute to the negative effects mentioned above. for these reasons, and in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i supported the challenge of the delegated act.

mr president, the resolution adopted by a large majority today gives the un concrete answers about the measures taken by the european parliament in recent years. i would like to highlight a few specific references. the first is that the resolution calls on the three eu member states, finland, ireland and the netherlands, to ratify the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities as soon as possible. the other specific reference is that it urges the european commission to involve the european parliament as soon as possible in the dialogue with the un commission so that we can conduct this dialogue together. the third is to urge the commission to adopt the european accessibility act as soon as possible. fourthly, to provide a separate budget for the eu framework for monitoring the implementation of the un convention, so that it can do its job effectively. i would like to point out that after the un has examined the european union and made its recommendations, the three european parliament committees, empl, libe and peti, will prepare a joint report on the process. finally, i would like to thank you, because i think it is symbolic that the factions have been able to work together and that such a transversal cooperation has been achieved.
in writing. a unique historic opportunity for the un to examine whether the eu is properly implementing the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the european parliament must not miss the opportunity to respond to the un on its own behalf. this is what the resolution is about, giving concrete answers to the un about what the european parliament is doing for people with disabilities. the resolution calls on the three eu member states - finland, ireland and the netherlands - which have not yet ratified the convention to do so as soon as possible, and those which have already done so - including the eu itself - to speed up the implementation of the convention. we urge the european commission to formally involve parliament in a constructive dialogue with the un and to draw up the long-awaited european barriers code. the eu framework for monitoring the implementation of the convention, of which the ep is a member, needs funds to be able to operate effectively. it is important that following the un final report, the european parliament's empl, libe and peti committees will also produce a joint report on the subject, expected later this autumn. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the motion because it promotes the effective implementation of the un convention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, as i agree that persons with disabilities have the same rights as non-disabled citizens, that their dignity is inalienable and that they are entitled to equal treatment, to independent living and to full participation in society. i believe that people with disabilities are one of the most vulnerable groups in our society and that their integration into the labour market is one of the greatest challenges for social and labour market policy. i support encouraging those member states which have not yet ratified the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities to do so without delay. i consider it important to develop an ambitious proposal for a european accessibility pact and to ensure that people with disabilities are fully involved at all stages of the legislative cycle. i support accessibility not just in the physical sense, but in the sense that public services should be accessible. i believe that the motion gives a comprehensive picture of the problems that exist and that a comprehensive legislative work must be launched to solve them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament resolution calling for a stronger and more effective joint action against xylella fastidiosa. on the one hand, the commission should ensure that sufficient financial and human resources are available to implement strategies against this pest. producers should receive adequate financial support for the application of good agricultural practices which are crucial for the control of xylella fastidiosa. it is also necessary to provide union compensation to farmers who have suffered damage as a result of the felling of olive trees. finally, appropriate resources should be allocated to research on xylella fastidiosa and other harmful plant pests. horizon 2020 should be allocated to such cases, among others.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa in olive trees, as it calls for a solution to a highly dangerous infection that poses an immediate threat. it is important to note that in addition to the oil trees mentioned in the title, the pathogen poses a risk to almond and peach trees and ornamental plants. the proposal draws attention to the fact that, depending on the type of bacterium, it poses a potential threat to vines, citrus and other crops and can cause damage of unprecedented scale and devastation with dramatic economic, environmental and social consequences. in this sense, it is not only dangerous for the southern european production regions. i agree that such an infection causes serious economic damage, not only to producers but also to the entire production chain (including cooperative and privately owned plants), tourism and distributors. one element of addressing the emerging threat is to prevent the import of infected products into the union through targeted measures, including, where necessary, the imposition of more stringent measures. i am confident that the eu will find a solution to stop the infection, but i believe that this requires a faster response to eradicate this type of infection. in this respect, i agree with the proposal in the motion to review the implementation of the eu's official plant health control system.

madam president, turkey has declared its intention to join the union and has shown its willingness to introduce effective reforms, to establish good neighbourly relations and to adopt the necessary international standards. however, the country still fails to guarantee freedom of speech and the press, there is no legal framework to combat corruption, the separation of powers and the independence of the judiciary leave much to be desired, and turkey's neighbourhood relations are very tense. turkey has a strategic role to play in the eastern and southern european neighbourhood policy, particularly in the fight against terrorism in syria and iraq. it also plays an important role in european energy security. in view of these considerations, it is necessary to continue to cooperate with it. however, the euro-turkish dialogue must remain based on values. we can rightly expect turkey to fulfil its own commitments to guarantee fundamental human rights, to refrain from any action that has a detrimental impact on neighbourly relations, to settle its relations with greece and cyprus and to normalise its relations with armenia. a century after the armenian genocide, this step can no longer be delayed.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to express the european parliament's concern that the funding of the common security and defence policy has been reduced in terms of the amount of resources available. the report urges the development of a more flexible and coherent funding system. it also identifies a number of problems to be solved, such as duplication, lack of transparency, lack of flexibility in the different procedural rules and mechanisms. furthermore, the lack of transparency of financial instruments for missions and operations. the report highlights the objective of cost-effectiveness and efficiency. it shall also initiate the reform of the athena mechanism and the military operations of the csdp. i agree with the above objectives and, in line with the position of the ppe group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

mr president, i would like to congratulate mr tarabella and the shadow rapporteurs for compiling this really informative report because in this way we can see how the eu can be a bit more efficient, even more than some reluctant member states and governments. i welcome very much the merger and the increase in volume where the school milk and vegetable schemes are concerned. in my amendments i have contributed by proposing to enhance national and local consultation in this regard, because i think that we must keep two beneficiaries in mind, namely the children on the one hand and the local suppliers on the other. at the same time, we should not benefit governments through this scheme. hungary, for instance, collects 27 % of vat on school supplies as on all other foodstuffs. so i would just like to the urge the commission to examine whether or not we could run this school scheme as vat exempt.
in writing. i would like to point out that school milk and school fruit schemes operate in different forms and with different success rates in the 28 member states of the european union. the latter depends only to a small extent on the eu legislation, but the circumstances in which the educational institutions of the member state operate and the financing of education by the member state are just as important, as are the eating habits. the objective of consolidating the programmes and establishing uniform rules for implementation, as set out in the commission's original proposal, cannot therefore be achieved. we cannot put the same coat on every eu member state. therefore, the amendment of the current programmes should be reconsidered. the proposal on the table cannot be accepted because it would lead to changes which would benefit only some member states while preventing others from carrying out programmes efficiently and on a country-by-country basis. the highly successful hungarian programmes would therefore receive less eu funding in the future than in the current situation. for these reasons, i shall vote against the adoption of the proposal. i welcome and support the commission's move to suspend the amendment of the school milk and school fruit programmes. the current system needs to be maintained with minor adjustments. such corrections shall not result in a reduction of member states' competences and flexibility.

in writing. ‒ i welcome and support the commission's proposal to review the strategy for the enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. intellectual property-intensive industries generate around 39% of total economic activity in the eu (worth around eur 4.7 billion per year) and approximately 26% of total employment (56 million jobs). however, since the entry into force of the convention on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights (trips, 1 january 1995), only a limited number of significant intellectual property agreements have been concluded, even though technological and societal changes have transformed the field of intellectual property rights. the report as important issues of the present and the future clearly identifies the need to stimulate research and innovation, the challenge of access to medicines and the environmental challenges. i also welcome the fact that all initiatives concerning external policies are linked to internal policies and that, accordingly, there should be a thorough review of the internal improvement of its rules on intellectual property.
in writing. ‒ as intellectual property rights affect a very significant part of the eu's economy and jobs, enforcement of these rights both within the eu and in third countries is crucial to the union's economic interests. the report represents, in my view, a decisive step forward on this issue, and i therefore voted in favour of both reports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the strategy for the enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. i believe that it is right to seek greater coherence between intellectual property rights protection and other policies, since measures to protect intellectual property rights also contribute to the success of the fight against tax evasion and organised crime, which currently represents one of the greatest challenges for the union. in addition, concerted policies will also allow global standards to be improved. however, i also agree with the recommendation in the report that there should be a public debate and broad information on the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights and their consumer implications. i also find the report's further suggestions for better data provision, access to medicines and bilateral free trade agreements useful.
in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the commission issued a communication on intellectual property regulation, which includes a 10-point action plan. the action plan aims to increase the effectiveness of action against commercial infringements of intellectual property rights, both at union level and within member states. the rapporteur agrees with the commission's vision of a new comprehensive ipr strategy, which aims, inter alia, at a more transparent business model, a higher level of consumer information and a more cost-effective and more accessible system of protection of intellectual property rights, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. as we approach the paris climate summit, it is important to assess the efforts and intentions that have been made so far. the declarations of intent submitted cover 34% of the world's energy-related carbon dioxide emissions. unfortunately, 34 percent is still not high enough. if more countries cannot be persuaded to support the convention, the conference will not be successful. in terms of the scale of emissions, the commitments of china and india are key. while it is understandable that securing economic growth is a top priority for these countries, long-term objectives should not be lost sight of: the effects of climate change are projected to be felt most strongly in china and india (floods, crop yield declines), which will also have a significant impact on economic performance. europe's leadership in the fight against climate change can only succeed if partners are involved.
on behalf of the verts/ale group.– madam president, energy security has become a primary concern over recent years in europe, especially in the light of the russia-ukraine crisis. the commission has rightly identified the fact that reducing energy dependency is a key to strengthening energy security in europe, especially considering that approximately eur 400 billion is spent yearly by the eu on energy imports. yet the strategy they came up with has not managed to translate this high-level ambition into the most needed actions. the own-initiative report of the european parliament contains several more forward—looking elements than the commission proposal. i would like to thank our rapporteur, mr algirdas saudargas, and the shadow rapporteurs for their constructive work in this regard. these achievements include the chapter entitled moderating energy demand and reiterating the position of the european parliament on 2030 climate and energy targets. however, in my opinion, this own-initiative report only gives a partial answer to energy security challenges. i fear that the extreme dependency on russia will simply be turned into a dependency on other external fossil energy suppliers. this is not what we should be aiming for. the future energy policy of the eu, as also mentioned in the energy union package, should be fully coherent with other eu policies and be based on reduced energy demand, energy savings and the use of renewable sources with the increased role of consumers/prosumers. it should also tackle the pressing issue of energy poverty. unfortunately, in many areas the report does not set clear directions and it lacks long—term thinking when it comes to concrete measures. i would like to highlight the selection of projects of common interest – pci’s – where we experience a strong bias towards fossil fuel projects, which is neither defendable nor in line with the decarbonisation pillar of the energy union package. the report mentions several types of technologies, including shale gas, liquefied natural gas (lng) and carbon capture and storage (ccs), which should be supported. this would lead to a severe lock-in effect in the european energy system. the report remains very much focused on gas and other conventional energy sources and does not tackle the multiple forms of energy dependence – technological and financial fuel dependence. also, it does not acknowledge the important role of renewables – we only find a few hints in the strategy. the eu should, rather, take steps towards an energy transition using sustainable renewable sources of energy, which are becoming increasingly cost—competitive with conventional sources and provide multiple benefits, including more jobs, opportunities for the local economy and lower energy import costs. (the speaker agreed to take a blue-card question under rule 162(8))
it's a two-card draw. - mr. deputy, i have to go. in his speech, he mentioned extreme dependence on external sources and that one extreme dependence can be replaced by another, although he also mentioned the importance of shale gas. frankly, i think shale gas is a very environmentally damaging story, and i wouldn't go into that too much, but do you see an opportunity to just replace the energy efficiency with the stressful import that we're operating in here like these jellyfish?
that's a two-card answer. thank you for asking. shale gas, we agree, is a very serious source of pollution. i didn't mention its importance, i just put it on the table as a problem. investments in energy efficiency and renewables can help europe to break its dependence on russian gas. instead of linking europe to this fossil fuel system by developing gas infrastructure, what we need instead is the money we spend on these developments or part of these developments, some network developments are needed, some new sources are needed, but this money should be used to build a sustainable, renewable energy system ... (the president took the floor from the member...)
one of the biggest challenges facing the european union today is to secure its energy supply. our continent is dangerously vulnerable to outside suppliers. when we look for a cure for this, we also need to recognize that there are more vulnerable people among the vulnerable. the gas crises of 2006 and 2009 made it clear that central and eastern europe is the most vulnerable region today. in hungary, for example, 80% of the co-operative houses are heated with gas from the only imported source. we have to change this situation, we have a duty to increase security of supply. i think the saudargas report can serve as a compass for this work. i agree that our task is to achieve a single energy market, to apply existing legislation, to increase energy efficiency and diversification, and to develop infrastructure. the best rules are useless if the power lines are missing. the commission and the council should therefore pay particular attention to compliance with the requirements of the energy package. it should encourage energy market players to make better use of existing infrastructure, such as bi-directional interconnections, and to build out the infrastructure that is still missing. my fellow members of parliament! if we continue along this path, the energy union can become a realistic goal. (the opponent has consented to answer a question marked with a blue card under article 162 (8) of the rules of procedure. )
it's a two-card draw. - mr. deputy, i have to ask you to leave. on energy security, you mentioned infrastructure, you mentioned delivery capacity. this is really important. but going back to the example of hungary, you mentioned, no matter how we increase infrastructure, if we can't find new sources of supply - maybe in the short term - then this dependence will not change. so how do you see the diversification of gas resources in hungary in the short term?
that's a two-card answer. thank you very much for the question, mr. representative. i argued for two-way transportation when it came to infrastructure development, to get new sources. hungary has made considerable efforts in recent years to improve its infrastructure. he also built storage facilities and interconnectors. now it's up to our neighbors, if you will, to create the possibility of two-way gas, and thus really get gas from other sources. thank you, thank you.
russia is no longer a predictable partner when europe's energy security is at stake. the annexation of crimea, the events in eastern ukraine and the anti-competitive pricing by gasprom make it very clear that we must wake up and not put europe's energy security in the hands of a single monopoly supplier. in parallel, we must also put an end to the separate energy policies of the member states, which threaten europe's energy independence. we do not need nuclear power stations to be built with separate agreements or gas contracts to be covered by separate agreements, because that would undermine the solidarity which can be the basis for the foundation of the european energy union. on the contrary, we must go further than the proposal on the table in the european parliament, for example by trying to include in the european energy union the possibility of the member states buying energy together, because this increases our bargaining power and can ultimately serve the energy security of the european union and the member states.
in writing. the development of a single eu energy policy has its drawbacks, which arise from differences between member states. the solution is to come together, but there are differences that can only be bridged by mutual sacrifice. the development of a community energy policy will be a long process and i believe we are on the right track, but i am afraid that the crisis will slow down efforts at member state level, as countries will focus more on public debt and budget deficits. i agree with what the report says about sticking to the targets, because energy efficiency measures and bio-energy investments help to reduce energy consumption and create jobs, thereby reducing unemployment. it is clear, however, that energy policy is not a stand-alone policy, nor can it be separated from other policies, since an investment or measure automatically affects processes and areas which are essentially part of another community policy. this is why strategies and objectives need to be coordinated across all areas to achieve maximum efficiency and to support each other across policy activities.
in writing.– free movement of persons is one of the most important achievements of the european union since its foundation. the absence of internal borders makes it therefore crucially important that our common external borders are controlled reliably and consistently. in order to better manage the growing flow of travellers, we need to modernise the european border control system, by increasing its efficiency and effectiveness. the result should be smooth and easy travel for the majority of third-country travellers who cross the eu borders yearly on the one hand, and an impossible mission for those who abuse free movement, such as organised crime and terrorist organisations, on the other. we look forward to the findings of the commission’s impact assessment and the pilot projects currently being carried out, to understand what new architecture will be implemented, what the single system for entry-exit should look like, what biometric identification should be applied, how data retention and protection would be handled. the recent dramatic increase in migrants through the mediterranean and the balkans makes it even more urgent to adopt the smart borders package, in order to strengthen border control and guarantee the protection of our citizens.
i think that at the end of this debate, there are a few things worth remembering. my first observation is that there are three actors here: one is olaf itself, the other is olaf's supervisory committee, and the main actor is the commission. i would very much like, for the dignity of this house and to reassure the taxpaying citizens of europe, to see these organisations not bringing their problems to parliament but bringing solutions with the guidance and cooperation of the commission. that is what we want, not to be here to serve one of the most discreet bodies in the european union with a public debate.
in writing. the debate on the motion for a joint resolution is held because of the facts contained in the 2014 annual report of the olaf supervisory committee. in that letter, olaf's directorate-general made serious criticisms of the management, administration and case management of the european anti-fraud office, which cannot be ignored and we are obliged to express our views on the matter as members of the committee on budgetary control. the report strongly criticises the procedure in which 423 cases were opened at one time on 1 february 2012 by decision of the director-general without substantive examination of whether olaf's competence in those cases was based on fraud, corruption or any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the union. another problem is that the director-general of olaf ignores the recommendations of the supervisory board, having implemented only 8 out of 50 recommendations of the dg. the access of the supervisory board to the information necessary for the performance of its tasks is also not guaranteed, nor is the stable functioning of the secretariat of the bank guaranteed. the resolution calls on the european anti-fraud office and its director-general to address these problems. all the necessary conditions should be provided for the effective functioning of the supervisory committee and its tasks, and the committee on budgetary control of the european parliament has a duty to speak out in this regard. i support the joint motion for a resolution in its entirety.
in writing. according to olaf's 2014 report, the current hungarian government has investigated five out of every ten cases of corruption. since 2010, the hungarian government has been given the title of the second most corrupt member state in the eu. the hungarian authorities did not suspect any abuse last year, while 28 complaints were received from the private sector. despite the fact that the government and peter polt have no idea that we're losing billions in the eu because of institutional corruption, and that the united states is banning government officials. olaf's report is one thing: today the hungarian government is fighting the eu with the money of european taxpayers, trying to build an illiberal state in hungary with european money. last week in brussels, jános lázár openly admitted this when he accepted the billions of euros in eu fines imposed by the orbán government for its corrupt public procurement. we are not surprised that the hungarian government is trying to undermine the european public prosecutor's office, to weaken its jurisdiction. the commission has also taken note of the fact that the hungarian authorities have not yet provided any evidence that the fides corruption is continuing. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the compatibility of the aid with the internal market. after the fall of the orbán government, we will investigate cases of suspected corruption, we will not let hungarian people, businesses lose eu funds because of their corrupt government.

in writing. ‒ the kyoto protocol amendment was adopted by 192 member states at the doha climate change conference in december 2012. this established the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, which runs from 1 january 2013 to 31 december 2020. for this period, the european union and its member states and iceland have committed to a joint emission reduction of 20% compared to 1990 levels. the second commitment period is therefore a very important stage in the fight against climate change. however, an amendment shall enter into force only after it has been accepted by at least three quarters of the parties to the kyoto protocol. the adoption of the draft council decision is therefore a significant step forward in efforts to prevent climate change. the committee on industry, research and energy, of which i am a member, therefore supported the conclusion of the amendment, and i myself supported it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and on the joint fulfilment of the obligations arising therefrom. as this is a long process, i think it is important that we make continuous adjustments to reduce emissions. the kyoto protocol, which sets binding international emission reduction targets, was signed in 1997. in 2012, the council committed to propose a joint reduction commitment of 20% of 1990 levels for the second commitment period by the union. i believe it sends a strong message that the union and its member states are making efforts and are taking a leading role in the international fight against climate change. i welcome the draft council decision on this together with the rapporteur. i share the regrettable view that the eu has a duty to convince the main polluting countries that they are not part of such agreements, and that it must use all the political, diplomatic and economic instruments at its disposal to do so. i am confident that these processes and further commitments will be an important negotiating point in the new international agreement to be concluded in paris in the second half of this year.
in writing. ‒ iceland is not a member of the european union, but has committed to a 20% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared to 1990 for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. the agreement sets out commitments to be undertaken by the eu member states on the one hand and by iceland on the other, and its support is therefore logically linked to the support of the doha amendment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft resolution on iceland's commitment to the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol. as a member of the european parliament's delegation to switzerland, norway and iceland, i believe it is important that environmental principles apply not only to eu member states but also to eea countries. i believe that there is an openness on both sides in terms of commitments, as the experience of the past few months has shown me. i also welcome the fact that not only the member states of the european union but also iceland have committed themselves to the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol (2013 to 2020). as the draft notes, iceland is a party to annex i of the kyoto protocol and has met its individual target for the first commitment period. the icelandic authorities have not provided any evidence that the measures are in line with the commitments made by the icelandic authorities in the framework of the commitments. in 2009, iceland indicated that it would fulfil its commitments jointly with the eu and its member states during the second commitment period. it is important to note that iceland participates in the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) and is subject to the greenhouse gas emissions monitoring system regulation. therefore, the rights and obligations applicable under the joint fulfilment of the member states should be extended to iceland by union legislation.
in writing. ‒ with today’s vote we gave our consent to the commission recommendation to the council to allow croatia to adhere to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union. the act of 2011 concerning the conditions of accession of croatia to the european union simplified its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states. it is no longer necessary to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols: the act of accession simply states that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols by virtue of the act. we voted therefore in favour and welcome this concrete step towards mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states.
in writing. the international nature of crime and the need to adapt the conditions for prosecuting it to this challenge, within certain reasonable limits, have enabled me to support this report. it is in our common interest that croatia should also become part of the eu system of legal aid in criminal matters by acceding to the convention and protocol.
in writing. ‒ by acceding to the union, croatia has undertaken to accede to a number of conventions previously concluded by member states under article 34 teu. in this connection, the council, on a recommendation from the commission and after consulting the european parliament, shall adopt a decision fixing the date of entry into force of the conventions for croatia and making the adjustments necessary on account of the accession of the new member state. support for the report therefore essentially supports the completion of croatia's accession to the eu.
in writing. ‒ with today’s vote we gave our consent to the commission recommendation to the council to allow croatia to adhere to the convention on the fight against corruption involving officials of the european communities or officials of member states. the act of 2011 concerning the conditions of accession of croatia to the european union simplified its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states. it is no longer necessary to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols: the act of accession simply states that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols by virtue of the act. the council, in order to take a decision determining the date on which this convention will enter into force in relation to croatia and making all the adjustments required by reason of the accession of this new member state to this convention, will act on a recommendation by the commission, after consulting parliament. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommended that parliament give its consent to the commission recommendation. we voted therefore in favour and welcome croatia’s contribution to the fight against corruption involving officials of the european communities or officials of member states of the european union.
in writing. corruption cases are high on the news, with cases of economic crime linked to sports and politics coming to light every day. such processes, which cause very serious moral and social damage, must be prevented by all possible means, and i therefore gladly supported the report that croatia should also be part of the eu's anti-corruption system by acceding to the convention.

mr president, a balanced relationship between the european union and russia is crucial for the whole continent. relationships are at an all-time low. the report adopted is, beyond legitimate expectations, a de facto indictment of president putin, who is being described as a dictator and an aggressor. relations will not improve if the union does not take into account russia's legitimate interests. the ukrainian crisis is also a conflict between the us and russia, in which the eu has unilaterally become the representative of us interests. maintaining and increasing sanctions is pointless and harmful. it is pointless because it has not shaken the popularity of president putin, but it is also harmful because it causes very serious economic losses to some eu member states, including hungary, and therefore the sanctions must be reversed.
in writing. ‒ mr gabrielius landsbergis has done a thorough job and gives a broad overview of eu-russia relations. i agree with the report and with the view of many european politicians that relations between the eu and russia have reached a low point. the situation is not expected to improve until the minsk agreements are fully implemented. the illegal annexation of crimea, the hybrid war launched against ukraine, the deliberate destabilisation of the country confirm that russia has violated international law and norms. in order to resolve the situation in eastern ukraine, i believe we must insist that the only way forward is through a negotiated political consensus, since the military actions have already claimed thousands of lives and caused great suffering to the population. the european union therefore has the task and responsibility of enhancing the dialogue between the parties, monitoring it and creating the conditions for an early peaceful settlement. in the light of all this, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. normally, problems in international relations are resolved through diplomacy, negotiations. those who resort to sanctions should not be surprised if the response is similar. i am convinced that it is not in the interests of the european citizens to further escalate tensions which have already caused enormous economic damage, and therefore the report cannot be accepted. europe cannot be a servant of the us or other countries' policies, but must make its own way.
in writing. ‒ as the report points out, the eu and russia are dependent on each other in the long term to face and respond to global challenges together. however, today, as a result of president putin's regrettable change of policy, russia has not only lost sight of the need to increase freedom, strengthen democracy, respect human rights and the rule of law at home, but is also threatening these fundamental european values abroad with its aggressive foreign policy, using trade in raw materials and energy as a tool of political pressure and even provoking armed conflicts at times. moreover, russia finds collaborators in this policy from certain member state governments and political forces, and there is a strong suspicion that it is not financing such a political force itself. i am convinced that the eu cannot stand by and watch this happen, and the report seems in many respects to be an adequate response to this policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report because it provides an accurate and thorough picture of the current state of eu-russia relations and a fair analysis of the reasons, in particular the russian aggression against ukraine, the illegal annexation of crimea and the facts of moscow's continued expansionist policy. i agree that russia is now a dangerous challenge and a close security risk to the union, while the eu is still striving to become an important strategic partner again. i consider it a virtue of the report that it argues for the strengthening of the common foreign and security policy, supporting the efforts of the high representative mogherini. i agree that in all respects, but especially in respect of the minsk agreements and the maintenance of sanctions, the eu must demonstrate unity in strengthening them where necessary. the european parliament, the council and the commission have also adopted a resolution on the situation in the middle east, which calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of the virus and to ensure that the situation in the region is not further worsened. i also expect that our present resolution will send a strong signal to the international community and to moscow that the eu stands united and consistent in its support for ukraine's european democratic development, territorial integrity and autonomy, and thus against putin's further european expansionist ambitions.
in writing. ‒ securing energy supplies is one of the biggest challenges facing the european union. the gas crises of 2006 and 2009 made it clear that central and eastern europe is the most vulnerable region today. we need to change this situation by working together, and it's our duty to increase security of supply. i think that the saudargas report, as voted by the committee on industry, research and energy, has provided a good guide to the direction we should take. however, the plenary vote brought together some political groups to vote in favour of an amendment condemning the technology used in research into non-conventional energy sources and recommending that member states do not authorise activities for the exploration and exploitation of non-conventional energy sources until it is proven that they are completely safe. in line with the people's party's position, as a member of the fidesz-kdnp delegation i abstained from voting on the report, as i consider it extremely important that all possible domestic resources are explored in compliance with the mandatory standards in order to increase european security of supply.

in writing. ‒ the report prepared in the committee on industry, research and energy summarises in an excellent way what is perhaps the most important issue of european politics in the 21st century, the problems of energy policy, and advocates an adequate response to these, closer european integration and, ultimately, the creation of the energy union. it proposes measures to address the main challenges in this area: reducing energy demand, increasing domestic energy production and developing energy technologies, building a fully integrated and well-functioning internal energy market and establishing solidarity and coordination mechanisms. overall, it is a really long-term strategic document, which i was happy to support.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european energy security strategy, which sets out a comprehensive approach towards the energy union. in my view, the creation of an energy union is an essential, fundamental interest of the european union. in its creation, it should take into account not only economic but also climate, environmental, trust and social aspects. i think it is important to stress in the context of the crisis in ukraine that the issue of ensuring a reliable energy supply is more important than ever; so is the issue of diversifying energy supplies and over-dependence on energy imports. that is why i agree that energy efficiency, new and renewable energy sources and research and development should be given priority, which can not only create energy security but also jobs. the report focuses on the role of carbon capture and storage and calls for significant research and innovation efforts in this regard, and addresses the risks of nuclear power generation. in the case of projects of common interest, i supported the initiative that the european union should only support projects where all the necessary environmental permits have been obtained.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of the joint motion for a resolution was motivated by the facts and problems identified in the 2014 annual report of the olaf supervisory committee. the olaf dg has made serious criticisms of the management, governance and case management of the european anti-fraud office, which cannot be ignored. the report strongly criticises the procedure in which 423 cases were opened at one time on 1 february 2012 by decision of the director-general without substantive examination of whether olaf's competence in those cases was based on fraud, corruption or any other illegal activity affecting the financial interests of the union. another problem is that the director-general of olaf ignores the recommendations of the supervisory board, having implemented only 8 out of 50 recommendations of the dg. the access of the supervisory board to the information necessary for the performance of its tasks is also not guaranteed, nor is the stable functioning of the secretariat of the bank guaranteed. the resolution calls on the european anti-fraud office and its director-general to address these problems. all the necessary conditions should be provided for the effective functioning of the supervisory committee and its tasks, and the european parliament has a duty to speak out in this regard. i supported the joint motion for a resolution in the plenary vote.

in writing. the corruption scandals that have erupted in recent weeks, the related arrests, resignations have shaken fifa, and they also foresee the possibility of renewal and purification of the organization. at the same time, we cannot forget that in qatar, the host of the 2022 world cup, guest workers working on stadium construction are living and working in inhumane conditions, which have already led to the deaths of more than a thousand people. it is common practice for workers to have their passports taken away, not be paid for months, not have access to adequate drinking water while working in the desert heat, and live in inhumane conditions in overcrowded workers' hostels. if no substantial improvement occurs, some estimates suggest that up to 4,000 people may die before the world war ii-related construction is completed. the european union cannot remain silent, we cannot stand by and watch the continuing violation of human rights guaranteed by the conventions! we can't leave without the responsibility of the sponsoring companies. how long will these companies lend their name and money to modern day slavery? it is intolerable that in the 21st century, in one of the richest countries in the world, we are held in virtual slavery and ruthlessly exploited by our fellow human beings. the commission and the member states must act immediately to ensure that human rights are fully respected, and we must set an example! if qatar is unwilling to take substantive and immediate action, i do not consider the boycott of the qatari-hosted world cup to be unjustified.
in writing. palmyra in syria may be the latest world heritage site to be vandalized by islamic state fighters. we see every day that the cultural purge of daesh is going on relentlessly. in iraq, they are executing the destruction of a 2,000-year-old christian community, the expulsion of the indigenous yazidi and turkmen populations, the eradication of ancient cultures. the trade in movable art is also a major source of funding for terrorism. this time, the walls of palmyra, one of the most special collective heritages of humanity, the remnants of assyrian civilization, are under attack by the islamic state. the greatest destruction in modern world history is being carried out by jihadists before our eyes, exhausting the concept of a crime against humanity. however, violence has now targeted the christian community in the palmyra area. the jihadists have removed a number of christian leaders in syria, this time father jacques mourad, who ran the nearby mar elias monastery, was kidnapped by extremists. the monastery has been home to many refugees from the civil war-torn area, regardless of religion. it is noteworthy that local muslim leaders have also demanded the immediate release of the monk from the international community. i recommend that international and european governments and security services make every effort to detect similar crimes in the region and to free the hostages. this is not just a religious issue, but a matter of standing up for basic human rights.
madam president, i would like to ask the european parliament and the european union to set up a professional body to examine what we mean by national self-determination today in the final sense of the rule of law and in legal terms. i cannot accept that when the interests of the western world demand it, for example in the case of kosovo, national self-determination means something different than, say, in the case of crimea. i cannot accept that the concept of national self-determination and autonomy in south tyrol is different from that in the case of, say, the szeklerland, the upper, the lower and the transcarpathian regions. the european union talks as much about the rule of law as it does about values. the rule of law means that law is predictable, objective and not dependent on political expediency. it would therefore be important to state, on the basis of research, with the involvement of experts, for example by examining and using the decision of the human rights court on kosovo, that the concept of national self-determination should be interpreted uniformly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, given that i had already supported another important report on eu-russia relations on a closely related subject. in this resolution, the ep delivered a clear verdict for the world and for moscow on the illegal annexation of the crimean peninsula and the ukrainian military violence as the main cause of the deterioration of relations. the report referred to here, focusing on the black sea region, adds important geopolitical and military aspects to all this and sets out clear european expectations towards nato and other strategic partners in assessing and managing putin's policy. i regarded as a particularly important political insight the report's statement that putin is currently testing the limits of tolerance of the eu and the democratic international community in the mediterranean for his further expansionist aims. i believe that these putinist aspirations, which may even pose a direct threat to some eu member states, make it a direct task and responsibility of the eu and the ep to respond effectively to the russian challenge. in this context, i believe it is important for the future of european foreign and security policy to heed the warnings and recommendations of the report.

in writing. i recognise that there is a need to treat refugees fleeing immediate danger to their lives for political reasons differently from the masses of migrants arriving at the eu's borders for economic reasons mostly to escape from starvation, which is also a threat to their lives. however, they are all entitled to assistance based on european solidarity. instead, it exacerbates the problem and causes almost irreparable political damage when the government of one member state portrays all refugees as potential criminals and terrorists in the eyes of the general public. this is both a threat to the eu's already difficult-to-build solidarity and cooperation on this issue and a threat to our chances of more effective international action and the international fight against terrorism. unfortunately, this is exactly what the orbán government is doing, when it incites against refugees in a pr campaign, while denigrating the commission's migration agenda and quota proposal as simply 'madness'. this etuc meeting is the right level, forum and opportunity to rein in this dangerous populist policy before it further undermines the chances of a more effective common european migration and foreign and security policy. i ask that the etuc and the president of the commission use all their influence to this end.

mr president, the european fund for strategic investments is not a stand-alone project but part of the 315 billion euro investment package, the juncker plan. the union's commitment is eur 16 billion, with eur 5 billion from the european investment bank. we expect private investors to pay 15 times that 21 billion. this is not the economic miracle weapon you're expecting, this is the miracle shopping. and what is it that attracts investors? the fact that the responsibility for high-risk investments should be borne by the states with public money. i quote the report: the additional substantial contribution of the member states to its capital is necessary, which is essential. so this is really a european ppp of a gigantic scale. we in hungary have very negative experiences with this type of cooperation. the member states, represented by the council, will not have a say in the decisions. they will have no representation on the steering committee or the investment committee. and if the report emphasises that the investment fund can only work well if the member states continue with structural reforms, which is known to mean austerity. real positive change can only be achieved by abandoning neoliberal economic policies and by finding a common solution to the debt crisis.
in writing. the juncker investment package would mobilise eur 315 billion of capital for european transport, energy, digital and social investments and help businesses, especially smes, with up to 3000 employees access finance through venture capital loans. the three pillars of the package are the creation of a new fund, the european fund for strategic investments, the establishment of a list of feasible improvements and the adoption of an internal market roadmap to remove administrative obstacles. the european union and the european investment bank (eib) contribute a total of eur 21 billion to its capital. of this, €16 billion is provided by the eu's eu contingency guarantee and a further €5 billion by the eib. on the basis of the eur 21 billion, the eib is expected to issue aaa-rated bonds worth eur 60 billion, with a triple leverage. this generates approximately eur 315 billion of capital investment, including a further five times leverage. this could provide a good basis for giving the economies of the eu member states a new, economically sound impetus to overcome the crisis.
in writing. in my view, the juncker package will also open up significant opportunities in agriculture in terms of private investment backed by the eu banking guarantee. however, it should be avoided that only the most competitive and larger agricultural enterprises have access to investments. i therefore agree with the view expressed in the opinion of the committee on agriculture that the investment incentive programme should be focused mainly on small and medium-sized enterprises. first of all, they have the potential to create jobs. hungary has good experience in this area, as the hungarian government has a successful policy of job creation. on the other hand, i would remind my colleagues that the eu's agricultural policy is based primarily on subsidies, and that will not change in the foreseeable future. we want the current cap to remain and not be replaced - even partially - by a kind of eu investment incentive scheme. such a tool can only complement the current cap system.
in writing. i welcome the outcome of the negotiations on the creation of the european fund for strategic investments, which is in line with the objectives of the hungarian economy, as it will provide a new type of financing opportunity for domestic financial services providers and companies. the fund will also support risk finance for smes and mid-caps across europe. it will help the companies concerned to bridge the capital gap by providing larger amounts of direct capital investment and additional guarantees for high-quality securitisation of sme loans. the efsi will be fully operational by the end of the year. it is estimated that the investment package could add up to eur 330 to 410 billion to the european union's gdp over the next three years and create between 1 and 1.3 million new jobs, so the estimates are very impressive. from a hungarian point of view, the greatest success is, of course, that the investment package is completely separated from the resources of cohesion policy. the eur 5 billion transfer concerns the cef 2.8 billion and the horizon 2020 programme for research and development with eur 2.2 billion. the proposed reduction is a success for horizon 2020, which finances research and development projects, as compared to the commission's original proposal. it should be noted that for the horizon 2020 programme, the priority lines of basic research for us are not affected by the reallocation, including the programme that aims to widen the participation of new member states.
in writing. the eu institutions have only been able to agree on the rules for the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) to be set up as a matter of urgency after lengthy negotiations, and the outcome is very worrying: there are no guarantees that the new fund will only be used to implement sustainable long-term developments, coherent with existing eu policies, such as projects for the green economy and energy saving. although parliament has achieved some successes in the negotiations, the new fund still draws a significant amount of money from the eu's horizon 2020 research and innovation framework programme and the european connectivity facility (cef). the way in which projects are selected is also problematic, and although a scoreboard will help to assess the expected impacts, much more is needed: full transparency and consistent application of sustainability criteria, as the envi committee's opinion suggested. the selection should be made in line with the union's environmental, energy and climate policy objectives. the new fund does not reflect decades of development policy experience, lacks precise selection criteria, detailed objectives and conditions for involving stakeholders. the efsi should not be allowed to be used for development projects that are not covered by the cohesion fund, that are environmentally and socially harmful or that are not sustainable. we must not allow the financing of the costly deployment of traditional energy sources or outdated technology in some member states, which would make them uncompetitive, to be financed from eu public money.

in writing. ‒ on 15 april 2015, the commission adopted a new proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf. the proposal is to mobilise eur 630 000 from the fund to provide technical assistance to the commission. the technical assistance shall be aimed at financing the supervision, the information and knowledge-base platform and the advice to be provided to the member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. the commission has proposed that the requested amount for 2015 be used to finance the following activities: 1. monitoring and data collection2. information3. the creation of a knowledge base/application interface4. administrative and technical support5. assessment on the basis of the above, in view of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2015, the hungarian people's party delegation supported the adoption of the proposal in agreement with the european people's party.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. the commission has now proposed to mobilise eur 630 000 from the fund for technical assistance. the commission intends to finance, as part of the technical assistance, the establishment of a monitoring, information and knowledge-base platform and to organise advice to member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. the requested amount is within the 0,5% limit of the fund available for this purpose, the proposal is agreed by the committee on social affairs and employment and its adoption is supported by the committee on budgets, which has the appropriate powers. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as it helps workers who have been displaced by the consequences of structural changes in world trade and the global financial and economic crisis and supports their reintegration into the labour market. i agree with the report that financial support for redundant workers should be dynamic and that these tools should be made available as quickly and efficiently as possible. the regulation extends the scope of eligible measures and beneficiaries to include self-employed entrepreneurs and young people, and supports initiatives to promote the creation of new businesses. these, and a higher contribution from the fund, will, in my view, make the eu solidarity instrument more effective and visible for workers. i support the report and support the continued work on the standardised application procedure and the use of the electronic data exchange system (sfc2014) by the managing authorities, which will allow for the simplification and acceleration of the processing of applications. i am confident that along the lines set by the ep, we can really help workers with much more effective implementation by the commission and the member states.
madam president, in october 2008, french president nicolas sarkozy proposed the creation of an eu economic government. the proposal was so openly about the creation of a superstate that the name was changed. since then, it's been about economic governance, not an independent body. the result is the same: the removal of economic and budgetary autonomy from the member states. the report states that before the adoption of draft budgets by member states, the finance committees of the national parliaments invite the eu commissioners responsible for economic governance to their parliaments. the eu commissioner, the commissioner, thus becomes the central, intermediate commissioner, who implements the will of the people. and all in the name of democracy. that is why i did not support the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the crisis has shown that europe needs to take steps to improve its economic model and restore its competitiveness. this requires both public funding and targeted investments. however, the potential of economic governance is currently not being exploited. effective economic coordination aims to kick-start europe's engine of growth and jobs and ultimately also to empower citizens. economic and employment policy coordination will be complete when a significant part of this coordination covers all possible means of stimulating the real economy, which would otherwise be left out of the broader coordination of the european semester. i voted in favour of mrs beres' report, as i believe that economic policy governance must be strengthened if the union is to be a driving force for growth and job creation. this requires the reintroduction of the highest level of political oversight, the elimination of any artificial distinction between action at eu and national level, and the development of more effective means to ensure that the eu's single market really benefits citizens and businesses.
