in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it makes useful suggestions for improving employment while taking account of global environmental challenges. i agree that the inefficient use of resources, the unsustainable pressure on the environment and climate change are reaching a level beyond which the irreversible impacts on our society and the natural environment cannot be prevented, and that increasing social exclusion and inequality is a challenge for societies. i believe that a significant part of the potential for sustainable job creation in the green and inclusive transition remains untapped, and the extent of this varies significantly from one member state to another. i agree that investments in renewable energy and energy efficiency will create a large number of jobs and will help to maintain the competitiveness of the european economy and industry and reduce europe's energy dependency. the proposal calls on member states to commit to a just transition timetable and to set ambitious environmental targets. this is done by ensuring adequate social protection and pay; healthy and safe working conditions; targeted investment in education, training and skills development programmes; respect for labour rights and the strengthening of workers' right to information, consultation and participation. i believe that the hungarian government is currently failing to meet almost any of these criteria, so i would recommend the recommendations of the report as a suitable recipe.
mr. president, i supported this report, but i would have supported it even more if they had changed the name, the title a little bit. it was titled in my native hungarian: "report on tax evasion and tax avoidance as a challenge to governance, social protection and development in developing countries". i would be very pleased if we could vote on a report next time on the same subject in the european union. moreover, because the commission, one of the main institutions of the european union, is headed by none other than mr juncker, the world's leading tax-avoidance master, i do not believe that the european union has the legal basis to educate developing countries, the so-called developing countries, on this issue. not to mention that - of course - the diversion of revenues to offshore locations is a very common practice in europe that should be addressed here.
in writing. ‒ the report raised questions and gave proposed answers to them which i believe require our particular attention. it examined the problems and their consequences in the context of the current system. administrative barriers, economic barriers, negative competition can all have negative long-term consequences. it is crucial to highlight that illicit money flows, i.e. unrecorded private money flows involving capital that has been illegally raised, transferred or used, have increased significantly. in 2011, developing countries lost more than usd 630 billion in domestic resources due to illicit money flows, representing 4.3% of developing countries' gdp. unfortunately, this particularly affects developing countries, as they are heavily dependent on corporate taxation, with a significant proportion of their national income coming from corporate tax revenues. i welcome the call to strengthen financial support and technical assistance to developing countries and regional tax administration frameworks. i also believe that in the fight against tax avoidance, solid solutions and an action plan are needed to increase transparency and cooperation.
in writing. ‒ in developing countries, domestic sources are the main source of finance. in these countries, the average tax rate to gdp is between 10% and 20% and in many countries it is below 15%, whereas in oecd countries it is between 30% and 40%. efficient mobilisation of domestic resources and strengthening of tax systems are essential to achieving development goals that allow the long-term overcoming of dependence on foreign aid. efficient and equitable tax systems are also crucial for poverty eradication, the fight against inequalities, good governance and state-building. the report therefore calls on the commission to put forward an action plan to support developing countries in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion and in the establishment of fair, balanced and transparent tax systems. it also urges concrete and effective measures to support developing countries and regional tax administration frameworks in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion and in the development of fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax policies. i agree with the findings and recommendations of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to identify targets to be met in the fight against tax evasion and money laundering in developing countries in the run-up to the third financing for development conference in addis ababa in july 2015. the report calls for greater transparency and efficiency in national and international tax systems. the european parliament calls on the commission to draw up an ambitious action plan to achieve these objectives. i agree with the above objectives and, in line with the position of the ppe group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax evasion and tax avoidance as a challenge to governance, social protection and development in developing countries. the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion is also a major challenge in the european union. the report detailed the significant political, administrative and technical barriers faced by developing countries in raising tax revenues. in order to reverse this trend, i support the commission's proposal to present as soon as possible an action plan to support developing countries in their fight against tax evasion and avoidance and in the establishment of balanced and transparent tax systems. at the same time, i stress that we must give even greater priority to tackling the problem of tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and tax evasion within the eu, setting an example for developing countries. failure to do so risks the union's credibility.
in writing. ‒ the pp group and the fidesz delegation welcome the commission's strategy in this important area, as the unsustainable use of resources causes both environmental damage and economic risks. it should be noted that the road we are on now leads to an ecological and economic dead end. humanity is already exceeding some of the limits of our planet's resilience, within which we must remain if we are to avoid reaching the tipping point that will lead to adverse ecological changes. improving resource efficiency would be beneficial both from an economic and a safety perspective. dependence on resources must be reduced. this requires a radical change of attitude. i welcome the legislative and economic incentives that are driving change. the report we're about to see today was about innovation and sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that we need to take immediate steps to achieve a circular economy. the material affects all the devices that generate waste today. the amount of this waste is unsustainable and we need to encourage green design, recycling, repair and ultimately zero waste. the european parliament wants us to use resources more efficiently, which will reduce our dependence on them and reduce material costs. improving resource efficiency means leaving behind the current linear economy, characterised by a take-make-consume-throw-away model of production and consumption. in a circular economy, virtually all non-renewable materials circulate in a closed cycle. an important element of the proposal is eco-design, which makes it easier to repair, reuse and refurbish products. other important elements are waste prevention measures; mandatory local, municipal and industrial targets until 2025; the polluter pays principle; higher recycling targets; minimising incineration and drastically reducing the amount of waste landfilled. hungary is in the last third of the eu-28 list for the latter value, which is in dire need of change. this package will not only save resources, i.e. money, in the long run, but it will also reduce the annual level of greenhouse gas emissions.
in writing. ‒ the epp group and fidesz delegation welcome the commission's strategy in this important area, as they propose, together with the rapporteur, to amend the legal basis of the regulation in line with the opinion adopted by the european parliament in 2010, by granting co-decision powers to the parliament. it is crucial that food safety is the ultimate objective of the european commission's proposal and that the regulation should reflect the changes in community law since the adoption of the maastricht treaty (1992). in my view, the most appropriate and rapid way of dealing with critical situations arising from a nuclear accident or other radioactive emergency is to use implementing acts. i also welcome the fact that the draft report also states that the european commission is obliged to report to parliament and the council on the measures adopted in the event of a nuclear accident or other radiological emergency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that a high level of human health protection should be ensured in the definition and implementation of all policy activities. i agree that the european union must have up-to-date legal instruments, including rapid and tailor-made decision-making procedures, to deal with situations such as those following the chernobyl or fukushima accidents. as is well known, after nuclear accidents, significant amounts of radioactive material are released into the atmosphere, which can contaminate food and feed to a significant degree from a health point of view, causing life-threatening diseases and health conditions. i therefore consider it important to have rules which allow certain agricultural products to be placed on the european market only if they comply with common provisions to protect public health. the report's finding that higher doses of radiation have a harmful and destructive effect on human cells and are carcinogenic should be emphasised. i therefore support the introduction of low limit values for the maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination in foodstuffs exposed to such radiation, taking into account the cumulative dose resulting from long-term consumption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion which highlights that investment in the real economy in europe has been declining over the past several decades, despite the huge growth of the european and global financial sector over the same period, and points out that the real economy remains heavily reliant on banks, which makes the economy vulnerable to the tightening of bank lending. i also welcome your observation that the large-scale state intervention since the start of the crisis, due to the failure of the financial sector, has resulted in abundant liquidity, but has not led to an increase in the demand for financing in the real economy. i agree with the rapporteur that restoring the stability of the banking system in the union has become a priority over long-term investment and financing of the real economy. i consider it important to call on the commission to undertake an in-depth country-specific analysis of the current situation in capital markets with a view to assessing, in the context of a comprehensive economic analysis, where and to what extent there are obstacles to investment at eu level through capital markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the establishment of a capital markets union. the proposal gives an excellent overview of the situation resulting from the malfunctioning of the capital market. it rightly stressed that although large-scale state intervention since the crisis has generated liquidity, this has not increased the demand for financing in the real economy. i think it is right that the proposal has given particular attention to the different economic and cultural composition of european smes in different member states. i agree with the call on the commission to encourage the most efficient possible distribution of savings, more investment opportunities, greater transparency and portfolio diversification for savers and investors by deepening and diversifying the sources of finance available to businesses. this is done by building on existing, well-developed european business finance structures. i particularly welcome the point in the motion which stresses the importance of widening access to financial education, especially for small investors and smes, to strengthen their confidence in capital markets and to understand the advantages and disadvantages of capital market investments.

ask you to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ forced labour violates human rights and human dignity for millions of men,women,young girls and boys. the struggle against this most violent form of exploitation has been central to many of the major political and philosophical movements for emancipation. the struggle for emancipation, which aimed to free man from political and cultural domination and physical dependencies, always attacked slave labor, which prevented the exercise of other rights. yet, in the 21st century, forced labor still affects 21 million people who are victims of exploitation that generates $150 billion a year for the organizers and perpetrators of this crime. the 2014 protocol to the 1930 ilo convention on forced labour updates the convention by providing it with new instruments and binding legal force to combat forced labour. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ today, new forms of forced labour are spreading, including the use of people lured abroad with the promise of work opportunities to perform the most difficult and humiliating jobs, abusing their vulnerable position, often through physical violence and constant psychological aggression. the draft council decision aims to encourage the eu to ratify as soon as possible the 2014 protocol to the international labour organisation's 1930 convention on forced labour, thereby contributing to the success of the union's efforts to ensure human rights and decent work for all and to combat trafficking in human beings within and outside the union. i voted in favour of parliament giving its assent to this council decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation because i agree that we must also take action against this form of exploitation. the recommendation describes forced labour as a 21st century phenomenon, still affecting at least 21 million people globally who are victims of exploitation. it is a sad fact that, although debt slavery officially no longer exists on the european continent, 880,000 people in the european union and 1.6 million people across the continent are still trapped in these new forms of forced labour. these include men and women lured by offers of foreign work but actually trapped by their supposed employers, migrants exploited by human traffickers, and vulnerable children torn from their homes. i therefore agree that these new forms of trafficking and exploitation must be tackled by means of the law and by strong enforcement action. this is the objective of the 2014 protocol to the 1930 international labour organisation (ilo) convention on forced labour, to which this recommendation of the committee on employment and social affairs of the european parliament was addressed.
in writing. ‒ the eu has enshrined the prohibition of forced labour in its primary legislation by incorporating the charter of the fundamental social rights of workers and the european social charter of the council of europe into the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the european union should pursue the protection of human rights and fair work through its policies. i voted in favour of accepting the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of the adoption of the buşoi report. the convention on tariffs and trade provides for the possibility of prohibiting the import of certain products on animal welfare and health grounds. the european union has therefore prohibited the import of seal products, as permitted by gatt rules. canada and norway challenged this decision at the world trade organisation, but the wto dispute settlement panel (court) accepted the eu's trade restrictive measures. this is a precedent-setting judgment in wto jurisprudence. the protection of human and animal health and the protection of nature are more important than free trade. therefore, the european union - on animal health and animal welfare grounds - may legitimately prohibit, for example, the import of cloned animals and foodstuffs derived from them, and the import of other foodstuffs or substances that have not been clearly identified as safe by science.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1007/2009 of the european parliament and of the council has completely banned trade in seal products in the european union, with two exceptions. the order was challenged before the wto by canada and norway. the competent bodies of the wto rejected two exceptions to the regulation. the purpose of the proposal to amend the regulation, which is now being examined, is to bring it into line with the recommendations and decisions of the wto on the matter. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as i believe it is important to regulate trade in endangered species and products derived from them. i believe that we can only be effective in such matters if we are united. the proposal does not prohibit indigenous communities from pursuing seal hunting in a sustainable manner for subsistence purposes in accordance with the un declaration on the rights of indigenous peoples and other relevant international agreements. however, even in this case, due attention should be paid to the welfare of the animals. the proposal prohibits indigenous communities from engaging in commercial activities and calls on the commission to establish detailed rules on the marketing of seal products.

in writing. ‒ cloning is not currently used for agricultural purposes in the european union. however, certain third countries are making use of this possibility, including the united states, canada, argentina, brazil and australia. cloning can be used, for example, to produce breeding animals of excellent quality. a large number of scientific studies have demonstrated that animal cloning poses risks to animal welfare. cloning is a matter of great concern to european citizens: a eurobarometer survey in 2010 showed that the european public considered animal cloning to be unprofitable, unsafe, unequal and a cause for concern, with only 18% of respondents supporting the technique. in line with the rapporteur's opinion, i am of the opinion that the negative consequences of cloning, including on animal welfare, are of incomparably greater importance than any possible positive effects. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to ban the cloning technique, but i believe that the proposal has failed to respond adequately to the legitimate concerns expressed repeatedly by citizens and the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe it sets out with sufficient precision the lessons we have learned from the hearings of commissioners-designate. by selecting the right dates for the election and nomination, the current members of the european parliament were able to participate in the process of appointing commissioners in 2014. the european parliament's hearings of commissioners became a practice in 1994 and have since become indispensable for parliament to make an informed assessment of the commission in its vote of confidence in the commission as it takes office. the report stresses the importance of setting deadlines for each member state to nominate its candidate and of making the process of the hearing more interactive, including the use of social media. in practice, formally, the whole parliament votes on the commission as a whole and the opinions of individual committees on individual commissioners have no legal significance, but the composition of the commission or the distribution of the portfolios may change. it should be added, however, that the hearings are not intended to attempt to change the political composition of the commission. because the unsuccessful candidates will be replaced by another candidate appointed by the same government.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament's committee on budgets discussed and adopted in july 2015 a report on the protection of the financial interests of the european union, including the strengthening of the performance-based control of the common agricultural policy. the system for checking the regularity of agricultural payments is becoming increasingly costly, with almost 40 million transactions audited each year. there is certainly a need for rationalisation and simplification in this area. the report makes recommendations, such as the introduction of control systems based on risk analysis and the elimination of parallel control processes, among others. i supported the finnish people's party rapporteur's motion.
in writing. ‒ following two rounds of reforms of the common agricultural policy (cap), the rules have become more fragmented and complex, and more errors are being made because of the more complex rules, and the objectives of the cap must be met while ensuring mutual understanding and trust between all eu institutions, national and regional bodies in order to implement the cap effectively. i believe that a more effective and efficient reform of the cap requires simplification and a reduction in administrative burdens in order to achieve the cap's objectives. taking into account the views of users, it is important that they are not overwhelmed by a disproportionately high number of tests. i also urge the cap to be less bureaucratic, with the aim of reducing the error rate and introducing tools that allow the distinction between error and fraud. i welcome the proposal that when using the findings of the checks and imposing any sanctions, a distinction should be made between non-intentional omissions and fraud, since omissions do not generally cause any financial damage to taxpayers. in this light, i am calling for a less bureaucratic cap that is clearly feasible and can be interpreted with the aim of reducing the error rate and introducing tools that allow the distinction between error and fraud, while ensuring that farmers remain able to produce the essential food that is the essence of the policy.

in writing. ‒ the report finds that after two rounds of cap reforms, the rules have become more fragmented and complex, leading to more errors being made locally. it therefore calls for a less bureaucratic cap with the aim of reducing the error rate and for the introduction of tools that allow for the distinction between error and fraud; it also urges that national authorities and farmers be given clearer guidance in order to reduce the error rate.
in writing. ‒ in my view, the protection of the financial interest of the european union is key; it is what drives the simplification of the common agricultural policy in general and in this case as well. i supported the report - which i helped to draft as a shadow taxpayer - because i believe that the level of bureaucracy and other constraints should be reduced, but in a way that simplification does not give rise to fraud. the simplification of the control system is necessary because, despite the many simplifications, the system is still not user-friendly. the controls are overlapping and, of course, impose an unmanageable burden on the beneficiaries: the member states' paying agencies, the certifying and central bodies, the tax authorities, the european commission (at both levels) and the european court of auditors all have audit or control roles. i believe that the common agricultural policy should stimulate agricultural production, ensure a decent standard of living for farming communities, stabilise the market and produce affordable food. all these wishes are enshrined in the treaty and should not be present as an unattainable barrier.

in writing. ‒ cultural heritage is one of the pillars of european culture and our common heritage for future generations, and its main value derives from its cultural value. an integrated approach to cultural heritage is needed if cultural dialogue and mutual understanding are to be achieved. such an approach can lead to increased economic, social and territorial cohesion, while contributing to the achievement of the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. cultural heritage contributes to the creation of new innovative jobs, products, services and processes and can also be a source of creative ideas, thereby fuelling the economy. the european parliament therefore calls for the mid-term review of the strategy to give greater weight to the role of european cultural heritage as a strategic resource for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. in line with the position of the fidesz-kdnp group, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i am firm believer that preserving and promoting our cultural heritage is an important part of our political and institutional activity. both the commission and the council indicated the need to have an integrated approach towards the domain of cultural heritage, and consequently it is important to enhance the cooperation and coordination among themselves in this area. this report calls for setting up of a single eu portal dedicated to cultural heritage as well as a better involvement of local communities and the private sector in the preservation and promotion activities related to cultural heritage. i see this as an opportunity especially for those national minorities, such the hungarian minority in romania and slovakia, to help them protect and preserve their traditions, culture and language.
in writing. ‒ in line with the report, i believe that an integrated approach to cultural heritage is needed, as it is a well-known fact at the level of the european institutions that cultural heritage issues are the responsibility of several directorates-general of the european commission at the same time. their work is therefore complementary and it is therefore vital that they enhance cooperation between them in this field and coordinate their activities concerning cultural heritage. in addition, european funding for cultural heritage has been provided under several eu programmes. some of these are creative europe, horizon 2020, the european fund for rural development, the european agricultural fund for rural development, etc. the information on these funding opportunities is available, but it is scattered across numerous websites, written in strong technical jargon, and translations are available in only a few official languages of the european union. it is therefore important to communicate information more effectively to potential beneficiaries. the european year of cultural heritage could be the perfect expression of the union's renewed commitment to this cultural heritage. with the right planning, such an initiative could give a big boost to the cultural heritage sector and highlight the huge potential it holds. i welcome the fact that the report also makes specific recommendations on the training, skills and knowledge and mobility of cultural heritage professionals and on the access of such young professionals to the cultural labour market.
in writing. ‒ the report deals with tangible, intangible and digital cultural heritage. it stresses that cultural heritage issues fall within the competence of several european commission directorates-general at the same time and urges their cooperation and coordination of their activities concerning cultural heritage. it also points out that european funding for cultural heritage is also provided under several eu programmes, information on funding opportunities is scattered across numerous websites, written in strong technical jargon, and translations exist only in a few official languages of the european union. the report therefore calls for the creation of a single eu portal dedicated to cultural heritage, which would bring together all the information on all eu programmes supporting cultural heritage in one place. it points out that the european year of cultural heritage could be the perfect expression of the renewed commitment of the union to this cultural heritage, and that the initiative could give a major boost to the cultural heritage sector and highlight the enormous potential it holds. it considers that, in order to achieve a meaningful result, the european year of cultural heritage should be adequately budgeted and the activities organised within it should be accompanied by a large number of actions at member state level.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur that i object to the points in the commission's reply which do not provide a guarantee to exclude water and sanitation services from trade agreements such as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership and that there are no guarantees to prevent further liberalisation of water and sanitation services. in my view, the uniqueness of water and the natural monopoly of water supply, and its indispensable nature for human life and health, justify the concerns raised by the growing trend in europe towards the re-nationalization of water services. the natural monopoly on water supply means that the vast majority of water suppliers are water service providers both in europe and worldwide, which means that considerable expertise and experience can be relied upon. we need to keep this practice in mind.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative has been in existence since 1 april 2012 as a new mechanism for participatory democracy. such an initiative requires at least one million signatures from at least seven member states. the european citizens' initiative right2water had over 1.6 million verified signatures at the time of its submission and has since gained over 300 000 new signatures. it managed to get signatures from all member states (of which 13 reached their quota), making it the first successful european citizens' initiative. its main objectives are: • to oblige the eu institutions and the member states to ensure that the right to water and adequate sanitation is extended to the whole population;• to exclude water supply and water management from the scope of internal market rules and to exclude water services from liberalisation;• to intensify the union's efforts to achieve universal access to water and adequate sanitation. jean-claude juncker, the commission president-elect who ultimately won the european elections in may 2014, publicly supported the right2water european citizens' initiative. the european commission published its formal response to the initiative in march 2014, stating: • water is not a commodity;• the provision of water services is normally the responsibility of local authorities, as they are closest to citizens;• water and sanitation services should be excluded from the concession directive.
in writing. ‒ european citizens can ask the commission to submit draft legislation. this could be done in the framework of a so-called european citizens' initiative, but of course only in those areas where the commission has the power to do so. the initiative must be signed by at least one million people, representing at least one quarter of the member states of the union. the citizens' initiative 'right2water' is the first example of the use of this new democratic tool. i agree with the rapporteur that the ownership and provision of water services is clearly a matter of concern to europeans and that this interest cannot be ignored. i agree with the substance of the report, which is why i voted in favour of it. the report calls on the commission to prepare a legislative proposal together with, if necessary, a possible revision of the water framework directive and the drinking water directive which would recognise universal access to water as a human right. the report stresses the obligation of member states to ensure access to water for all, regardless of the provider. in addition, member states should ensure that service providers provide safe drinking water and better hygiene conditions. i also agree that the provision, distribution and treatment of water and sanitation services should continue to be excluded from the concession directive, even in its future revision. it is also important to note that water and sanitation services should be excluded from any trade agreements that the union is negotiating or intends to negotiate.

mr president, my dear officer, ladies and gentlemen, the european commission's cohesion reports are milestones in the history of cohesion policy. this is no different with the sixth cohesion report, which examines the union's regional development policy in the light of the devastating economic and financial crisis and links it closely to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. cohesion policy is the union's number one investment policy, the most monitored and evaluated spending area of the eu budget, with a budget of over €350 billion for the period 2014-2020. its effectiveness, its indispensable nature, is particularly evident in crisis situations. cohesion policy can offer a real and immediate solution, even in emergency situations, to growth and job creation. in the light of all this, i would like to stress at the outset that cohesion policy must continue to play an important role beyond 2020 and that economic integration and solidarity cannot be abandoned within the union. my report placed a strong emphasis on the need to put an end to recurrent liquidity problems in regional development policy. we have to settle a very large payment arrears. by the end of 2014, a payment backlog of eur 24,8 billion had accumulated, undermining the effectiveness, credibility and sustainability of cohesion policy. the second idea, which was emphasised in my report, is to reinforce the original role of cohesion policy. the objective of cohesion policy, as defined in the treaty, is to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion in all regions of the union, with particular regard to the less developed regions. understandably, the objectives of cohesion policy have evolved over time and the policy has become increasingly linked to the union's current strategy. however, i believe it is important to give greater emphasis to the original objective of cohesion policy, namely to reduce development disparities, and to ensure that the contribution to the union's current overall strategy remains compatible with the reduction of regional disparities. the third idea i highlighted in my report is the future of cohesion policy. the year 2019 will be a pivotal one, with a newly elected parliament and a new commission to tackle the final tasks of the europe 2020 strategy, the development of the new multiannual financial framework and the establishment of the post-2020 cohesion policy framework. the debate on the future of cohesion policy must therefore start now. in addition to the three main points, i would like to briefly mention a few key aspects which have received particular attention in my report. i consider it important to take measures to ensure efficiency, simplification and results orientation. i would like to stress the importance of simplification, since a large part of the irregularities stem from non-transparent standards and requirements. reducing the administrative burden on beneficiaries would be a huge step towards increasing efficiency. the results orientation is reinforced by thematic concentration, but the concretisation of objectives also requires the maintenance of sufficient flexibility to provide tailor-made responses to the needs and problems of the regions. my report focuses on the issue of unemployment, in particular youth unemployment and the capacity of smes to create jobs. finally, i believe that the territorial dimension has received little attention in the sixth cohesion report, despite the fact that it is an essential tool for strengthening economic, territorial and social cohesion. ladies and gentlemen, in preparing my report, i have had the opportunity to work very constructively with the shadow rapporteurs of the other groups, with the members who tabled the amendments. i would like to thank you for that cooperation here and now. the sixth cohesion report is a great opportunity to give new impetus to the eu's cohesion policy and to highlight its effectiveness and usefulness. i would like to reiterate that the eu cohesion policy must continue to play an important role beyond 2020 and that the eu budgetary resources for the policy cannot be reduced. only a well-funded cohesion policy can ensure that the eu's solidarity is upheld, that less developed regions are included, that new jobs are created and that the economy is developed. i thank you for your kind attention and look forward to your comments.

in writing. ‒ in accordance with the guidelines of the european people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the protocol amending the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and guinea-bissau. the report on the new protocol also clearly shows that the european union will have to limit its sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. the reasoned measures taken to maintain them have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries.
in writing. ‒ in my view, the fisheries agreement with guinea-bissau is even more important, and may even be considered the most important of the agreements currently in force. i regret that the abolition of unilateral tariff concessions and the entry into force of the so-called economic partnership agreements impose severe restrictions and may entail serious risks and dangers for the country. i agree with the rapporteur that it is important for parliament to give its consent to the conclusion of this protocol, given its serious importance both for guinea-bissau and for the eu fleets operating in its waters. furthermore, the agreement and its background and future prospects need to be assessed and considered in more detail, as the first fisheries agreement between the eu and guinea-bissau was signed 35 years ago and the progress achieved in sectoral cooperation is very modest. this needs to be changed urgently. the agreement should promote the genuine sustainable development of the guinean fishing industry and related industries and activities, increasing the added value resulting from the exploitation of the country's natural resources.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries agreement between the eec and guinea-bissau, which has been in force since 1980, is considered the most important of the agreements currently in force. on 10 february 2012, the parties agreed on a new implementing protocol covering the period from 16 june 2012 to 15 june 2015. following the military coup d'état in the republic of guinea-bissau on 12 april 2012, the union has suspended the procedures for the signature of the protocol. however, elections were held in may 2014 and the new implementation protocol to the eu-guinea fisheries agreement was finally signed on 24 november 2014. the protocol is of major importance both for guinea-bissau and for the eu fleets operating in its waters. i supported the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ the proposed fisheries partnership agreement offers fishing opportunities to 94 fishing vessels, with a catch of 15 750 tonnes in the waters of the exclusive economic zone of the republic of madagascar. in compensation for the use of the fishing grounds, the european union will finance the malagasy fishing industry with eur 700 000 per year and will provide a general contribution of approximately eur 866 250 for the first two years of the agreement and eur 787 500 for the second two years. the agreement provides for a contribution from the european union to the republic of madagascar totalling eur 6 107 500 for the four-year period of the current partnership agreement. the rapporteur recommends adopting the proposal, but sees the potential for further development of the fisheries partnerships to come, and makes proposals to this effect. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the marrakesh convention aims to simplify the customs treatment of goods and thus trade worldwide, which requires close cooperation between the customs authorities of the individual states parties. the convention is expected to bring significant economic benefits, in particular for developing countries and least developed countries. measures to facilitate trade can also bring significant relief to smes. the agreement also has the capacity to recognise, in an innovative way, the different enforcement capacities of different nations by inviting developing and least developed countries to determine when specific provisions of the agreement will be applied and by linking the implementation of some rules to assistance provided by developed nations. that's why i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ the marrakesh agreement aims to simplify the customs treatment and trade of goods worldwide. in this regard, close cooperation between the customs authorities of each of the states parties is required. the amendment of the convention is expected to have a positive impact, in particular for developing countries and least developed countries. measures to facilitate trade can also bring significant relief to smes. the agreement innovatively recognises different national enforcement capacities. it calls on developing and least developed countries to determine when they will apply the specific provisions of the agreement, and further links the implementation of some rules to the assistance provided by developed nations. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on trade facilitation was concluded at the 9th wto ministerial conference in december 2013. the agreement is less a legal commitment and more focused on cooperation to implement best practices that governments can support and follow. it contains some 40 provisions to speed up the movement, release and clearance of goods, including those on the publication of laws, regulations and procedures, the use of electronic payments, the reduction of formalities and documentation requirements or the uniform application of border control procedures. the rapporteur considers the expected benefits of the agreement, in particular for developing and least developed countries, and the recommendation clearly advocates the european parliament's support for the council's draft decision.
in writing. ‒ the report targets the agreement on trade facilitation, which is not only innovative because it is the first multilateral agreement on new rules to be negotiated under the auspices of the wto since its inception almost 20 years ago. the approximation is pioneering and allows developing and least developed countries to categorize their commitments and to define the timetable for their implementation. this will require increased transparency and cooperation between customs authorities. i welcome the report's approach, since the provisions on transit are of particular importance for landlocked countries wishing to trade through the ports of neighbouring countries.
in writing. ‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterway was adopted by the diplomatic conference organized by the central commission for shipping on the rhine and the danube commission with the participation of the un economic commission for europe. the treaty entered into force on 1 april 2005, thereby facilitating the harmonisation of contracts and standards for inland waterway transport in the field of transport, which contributes to the effective functioning of the internal market. the budapest convention is an agreement that falls partly within the exclusive competence of the union. consequently, member states cannot ratify it or accede to it without the union's authorisation. belgium ratified the convention on 5 august 2008, following the entry into force of the rome i regulation (on the law applicable to contractual obligations) on 24 july 2008. therefore, in order to resolve the current unregulated legal situation, it is necessary to grant a retroactive authorisation. austria has indicated its intention to accede to the convention and poland has indicated its intention to ratify it. the participation of those member states will promote the wide application of the convention, bringing benefits to citizens and businesses. the draft decision therefore authorises belgium and poland to ratify the budapest convention and austria to accede to it. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterway was adopted by the diplomatic conference organized by the central commission for shipping on the rhine and the danube commission with the participation of the un economic commission for europe and entered into force on 1 april 2005. in the field of transport, it contributes to the internal market by harmonising contracts and standards for inland waterway navigation. eleven member states are already parties to the budapest convention, while fifteen member states have indicated that they do not have inland waterways covered by the convention. austria and poland have indicated their wish to accede to the convention. their participation will promote the widespread application of the convention, bringing benefits to citizens and businesses. furthermore, belgium has ratified the convention. it therefore authorises belgium and poland to ratify the budapest convention and austria to accede to it. for these reasons, i support the rapporteur's proposal that parliament give its consent to the delegation of power.

in writing. ‒ the rapporteur takes the view that, in parallel with population growth and the emergence of new technologies, the number of people living in cities is gradually increasing in europe and worldwide. in 1950, 50.5% of the european population lived in urban areas. this is up from 72% in 2014 and could reach 78% by 2030. globally, the urban population is expected to double from 29% in the 1950s to 80% by 2050. the report aims to address the urban policy challenges of eu policy. the rapporteur believes that only through active and coordinated eu policies will cities be able to fulfil their function in the future and offer their inhabitants living conditions that meet their needs, and that urgent eu policy action is needed to be able to effectively influence the consequences and pace of european urbanisation.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the report 'investing in jobs and growth - promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion in the union'. the report, cited by tamás deutsch, focuses on the union's investment policy of the first order, cohesion policy, which is the most audited and evaluated spending area of the eu budget with a budget of over €350 billion for the period 2014-2020. the effectiveness and credibility of cohesion policy can only be sustained if the very large payment deficit is eliminated and the order of magnitude of eu budgetary resources devoted to cohesion policy is maintained. the report pays particular attention to unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and the capacity of smes to create jobs. to promote job creation, deutsch tamás calls for a coordinated use of the european social fund and the european regional development fund, and recommends reducing the administrative burden on final beneficiaries in order to increase efficiency. the document confirms the original objective of cohesion policy, which is to reduce development disparities. it also underlines its contribution to the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of smart, inclusive and sustainable growth and its role in mitigating the negative effects of the economic crisis. the deutsch report is one of the most important regional policy documents of the 2014-2020 cycle, and has received overwhelming support in both the committee and plenary votes.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the european commission prepares a cohesion report every three years on progress made towards achieving economic, social and territorial cohesion... looking back at the 2007-2013 programming period, the sixth cohesion report reports that cohesion policy has successfully dampened the effects of a significant - on average 20% - fall in public investment in the eu. however, regional disparities have deepened recently and, following the improvement since 2000, employment has fallen again and competitiveness has deteriorated in several member states, mainly in the south. looking ahead, the report identifies energy efficiency, employment and support for smes as promising areas for sustainable job creation for investments to be made between 2014 and 2020. the rapporteur welcomes the eu's new european investment plan, which will complement structural and cohesion investments, but points out that this should not have a negative impact on the cohesion policy budget and long-term strategic programming, as the regions most in need of investment incentives often have smaller administrative and absorption capacities, making them unsuitable to participate in the new investment plan.
in writing. ‒ the report by tamás deutsch focuses on the union's number one investment policy, cohesion policy, which is the most audited and evaluated spending area of the eu budget with a budget of over €350 billion for the period 2014-2020. the deutsch report contains ideas with which i very much agree. one of the key ideas in the report is that the effectiveness and credibility of cohesion policy can only be sustained if the very large payment backlog is eliminated and the order of magnitude of eu budgetary resources devoted to cohesion policy is maintained. the report focuses on the issue of unemployment, in particular youth unemployment and the job creation capacity of smes. to promote job creation, deutsch tamás calls for a coordinated use of the european social fund and the european regional development fund, and recommends reducing the administrative burden on final beneficiaries in order to increase efficiency. the report confirms the original objective of cohesion policy, to reduce the development gap, while emphasising its contribution to the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of smart, inclusive and sustainable growth and its role in mitigating the devastating effects of the crisis. the deutsch report is one of the most important regional policy documents of the 2014-2020 cycle, and has received overwhelming support in both the committee and plenary votes. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as i consider it important to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion in the european union. i am glad that the pro-government side of the hungarian government has finally expressed the importance of this and that the european union (and its financial support) is indispensable. the report also welcomes the creation of the european fund for strategic investments, which can once again provide a significant source of development funds for developments in the member states. however, it should be noted that since this is a direct and transparent resource, it will not be possible for it to be distributed to the government's political allies without public procurement. the report mentions climate change and energy dependence as one of the objectives of cohesion policy. however, i find it paradoxical that while some member states - and hungary in particular - are naturally and happily spending eu funds, they are imposing a special tax on certain renewable energy sources. the report calls on all actors concerned, in particular the central authorities, to develop multi-level governance and coordination mechanisms to support country-specific recommendations. the spirit of this proposal can also be interpreted as a country-specific recommendation where each application is allocated to a single political leader. i believe that in order to promote cohesion, more emphasis should be placed on local communities rather than on the development of complex programmes, as the report refers to in several places.
in writing. ‒ 2012 has been declared the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. the main objective was to facilitate the creation of an active ageing culture in europe, based on a society that is open to individuals at all ages. the various levels of the union have made a significant contribution to achieving the objectives. however, not everyone was able to exploit its full potential due to the delay in the implementation timetable. the eu website was widely praised for its cost-effectiveness, but its traffic was below the results of previous european years. activity on social media also appeared to be limited by participants and stakeholders, at least at eu level. at union level, the european year 2012 and other ongoing policy activities such as the white paper on pensions, the demographic forum, the european innovation partnership on active and healthy ageing and the planned accessibility package complemented each other well. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ 2012 has been declared the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. the main objective was to facilitate the creation of an active ageing culture in europe, based on a society that is open to individuals at all ages. i welcome the specific objectives of this initiative, which include raising awareness of the value and diversity of active ageing and combating age discrimination, as well as combating age-related stereotypes and supporting activities to help remove barriers. in line with the rapporteur, i believe that the initiatives launched in the framework of the european year 2012 should be monitored and continued; the sustainability of the results is key. i welcome the two main outcomes of the european year 2012: the principles on active ageing and the promotion of solidarity between generations and the active ageing index, and i encourage member states to make more active use of them and to set targets to be achieved through comprehensive active ageing strategies and to monitor progress towards these targets.
in writing. ‒ 2012 has been declared the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations. the rapporteur shall evaluate the events and initiatives that have taken place and make recommendations for the dissemination of the results. it considers the two main outcomes of the european year 2012 to be the principles of active ageing and solidarity between generations and the active ageing index, and encourages member states to make more active use of them and to define objectives to be achieved through comprehensive active ageing strategies. he also mentions the forthcoming european union convention on demographic change as another important achievement. it stresses that the demographic changes facing europe should be seen as an opportunity rather than a burden on european society. a key element of this would be to recognise the social usefulness and positive role of older people in society and to strive to improve intergenerational dialogue. it also considers it necessary to develop a 'silver economy' that meets the needs of an ageing population, based on the economic opportunities arising from public and consumer spending related to the ageing population and to certain products, services, innovative solutions and the needs of the population over 50 years of age, generating new jobs and growth.

in writing. ‒ the strategy outlined by the european commission in its 2011 white paper on transport was to make the transport system competitive, to increase mobility, to remove barriers in key areas and to promote growth and jobs. the proposals would also significantly reduce europe's dependence on oil imports and reduce carbon dioxide emissions from transport by 60% by 2050. the rapporteur reiterates that the european parliament supports the implementation of the white paper on transport, but points out that to achieve this, very difficult targets have to be met by 2050 and very challenging targets have to be met by 2020/2030. it points out that the complex transport system that needs to be transformed and made more efficient, cleaner, safer and more reliable cannot be achieved by a few minor changes. it considers that there is a significant gap between the objectives and the means needed to achieve and finance them, and that very ambitious objectives are difficult to achieve unless more detailed and well-founded plans for their achievement are developed, which include realistic and achievable short- and medium-term objectives, and which then lead to the achievement of long-term (2050) objectives. i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ by regularly promoting gender equality, we recognise that educating girls is one of the most rewarding development investments. i welcome the report in that sense. the report covers a number of objectives of high importance to the people's party, such as inclusive and equitable high-quality education and teacher training, professional skills development aimed at increasing employment, lifelong learning opportunities, the fight against stereotypes, and digital education. we can all experience that despite the eu's strong political commitment to equality, gender inequality is still underpinned by deep-rooted social barriers: fewer girls are choosing science or engineering courses, while more women are choosing careers in social care. i am firmly convinced that, in the interests of a common success, in the interests of a fruitful and constructive report, it would have been extremely important to respect the subject matter of the report and, under the umbrella of human rights, not to violate the principle of subsidiarity. we can of course encourage the member states to take certain measures, but education is first and foremost a matter for the member states and we must avoid, even with good intentions, interfering in areas where we have no competence. i regret to note that the report, despite its positive points, is in many places beyond its scope. i therefore abstained from voting.

in writing. ‒ as an alternate member of the delegation to the eu-iceland joint parliamentary committee and the eea joint parliamentary committee responsible for relations with switzerland and norway, i agree with the report that the eea agreement is a key factor in economic growth and the most powerful and comprehensive instrument for extending the single market to third countries. i consider it important that the substantive single market legislation is implemented in the eea efta states in a timely manner and with the least possible delay, and i share the view that this process can be further improved and accelerated. i also share the view that the strong links between the eu, the eea efta states and switzerland go beyond economic integration and the expansion of the single market and contribute to stability and prosperity for the benefit of all citizens and businesses, including smes. i believe that the gradual transposition and implementation of internal market legislation and the continuing flourishing and enduring relationship between the eu and switzerland have contributed to peace, prosperity and growth in europe over the last decades. i supported the report for all these reasons.
the decision on migration proves that the european union is unable to find a solution to the immigration crisis. in fact, the resolution adopted and the statements made by some of the leaders can be interpreted as an invitation to europe. it's not thousands of refugees coming to europe, it's hundreds of thousands of illegal immigrants, and if things don't change, millions. this year, 195 220 people have crossed the border illegally in hungary. this invasion threatens european identity, culture and the peace of the people. the hungarian government must stop applying the legislation that has lost its function, only then can it fulfill its duty to protect the country's sovereignty, while protecting the schengen borders. the immigration crisis must of course be seen from a humanitarian perspective, but at the same time we must not lose sight of one fundamental principle: europe belongs to europeans and hungary belongs to hungarians.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of today's resolution on migration and immigrants in europe, because it does not focus on the essential issues that reflect reality. the resolution does not even mention wars in syria or libya as a cause of this migration, nor is it tough enough on stopping trafficking networks. the hungarian people's party delegation cannot accept the commission's current migration package in this form, because it has not been able to provide answers to the burning questions that have been ringing for weeks. it does not clearly state that our primary task is to protect europe's external borders. the text does not clearly distinguish between genuine refugees and immigrants who risk their lives and those of their families in the hope of a better life to reach countries that distribute social benefits more widely and therefore do not want to cooperate with the authorities in other member states. the quota allocation mechanism in the package is not a sufficient solution to the present situation. the majority of immigrants, even after the allocation of quotas, will make their way to states with higher social assistance as soon as they have the opportunity. and until then, there's no point in talking much about quotas, about distribution, as long as the number of people entering the union by the thousands every day at europe's external borders is increasing, while only a fraction of them are eligible for refugee status.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i could not vote for the keller report because it does not deal with real problems, and therefore does not provide a solution to the current crisis. mandatory quotas are not helping. the biggest problem is that today a fraction of the refugee influx is willing to register, to cooperate with the authorities, and to accept the refugee status of, say, poorer member states. most of them are heading for the member states that promise more social assistance, and they are doing everything they can to get there. it will do so after the quota allocation, moving as soon as possible to states where it can count on more social assistance. and in the meantime, there's no point in talking much about quotas, about distribution, as long as we can't protect europe's external borders, and the number of people entering the union by the thousands every day, while only a fraction of them are eligible for refugee status.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution, particularly as it is the most serious challenge facing the european union today, one that is testing european solidarity and for which the commission's proposals envisage not only short-term but also long-term structural measures. i agree that all member states should be obliged to take their share of the refugee allocation, and that governments that fail to do so should face eu sanctions. i think it is important, in the context of the whole process, that the use of european funds allocated to the reception of refugees is strictly controlled so that they can be used only for measures and campaigns for the benefit of refugees and not against them. i believe that this package of measures is only the first step towards tackling other types of migration with new community instruments and i wanted to contribute by voting to accelerate this process. i hope that this clear position of the european parliament will have an impact on the member states responsible for the actual measures, as well as on the council, and will lead to swift and effective action, in addition to the commission's proposals.
the european union wants to be an active player in the middle east peace process, and this is welcome. both the israeli and the palestinian sides have their own roles to play in the peace process. however, the adopted decision lacks some essential elements. the union calls for an end to the israeli occupation of the west bank, the gaza strip and east jerusalem. condemn the policy of collective punishment that israel is pursuing against the palestinian people. call for the release of palestinian political prisoners, including members of the legislative council. strongly condemn the increasing violence of the settlers. the current resolution, although a step forward on a similar subject compared to what was previously adopted by parliament, was not able to support it because of these shortcomings.
in writing. ‒ six groups (ecr, verts/ale, gue/ngl, alde, ppe, s&d) tabled a motion for a resolution on this subject, which has succeeded in producing a joint compromise proposal. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it is also a way for the european parliament to promote a greater and more meaningful role for the union in promoting the middle east peace process. i consider this an important objective, because it is really a european problem, because of the links with the refugee crisis and the rise in anti-semitism and terrorist acts in europe. i also consider it important that, by this resolution, the ep almost unanimously supports the active commitment shown by the high representative mogherini to facilitate the peace process. i also considered in my vote that credibility is a fundamental prerequisite for effective eu foreign policy action; this requires the objectivity and impartiality of our common policy, which we must continually demonstrate in our common documents such as this resolution and in practical steps. i supported the resolution as a strong reference for the european tasks ahead of us in improving the security, humanitarian and political situation of the palestinian population. however, i would have liked to see it in the text and i urge the eu to give equal weight to preventing terrorist acts from gaza and other palestinian territories, to curbing the influence of hamas and to setting up a strong palestinian administration to ensure this after the forthcoming elections. the sovereignty of israel and the legitimate security interests of its citizens should also be a lasting element of a credible and effective union policy in the middle east.

in writing. ‒ the economic and financial crisis has led to an increase in poverty and social exclusion and long-term unemployment, placing disabled people at increased risk of poverty across the european union, and at the same time a dramatic increase in the number of european citizens unable to settle for more than a year. in addition to employment-enhancing instruments, more attention should be paid to solutions that can facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of people with even the most basic skills and non-competitive knowledge in the short term, so that they can exploit the benefits of more innovative solutions in the social economy later on. any improvement in the economic and financial situation in the member states should be accompanied by intensive support for inclusive and sustainable growth and quality employment. in order to transition them into the social economy, member states should promote lifelong learning among older workers and the long-term unemployed, including those with disabilities, who continue to face physical, information and communication barriers. member states should take into account best practices in adapting national tax systems to social enterprises and socially responsible investments and, where appropriate, increase tax benefits and incentives for such types of enterprises that employ vulnerable groups, such as persons with disabilities.

in writing. ‒ the eu has set the path forward in the europe 2020 strategy and cannot give up on the very ambitious objectives it sets the eu has important short-term challenges to face such as economic and financial sustainability, social well-being and especially job creation, taking into account in particular the most vulnerable groups, such as young people, women and the elderly, the long-term unemployed. to achieve these goals, the social economy must play a central role. however, i think it is important to emphasise that social economy should not be confused with corporate social responsibility. social innovation and social enterprise therefore play a key role in the development of the social economy, which requires the promotion of education and training, improved funding, better visibility at european and national level, and the exchange of information and best practices, to promote the development of the social economy in the eu and in the member states, in order to create a more favourable legal environment.

in writing. ‒ the report states that the social economy must play a central role in achieving the eu's objectives. companies operating in the social economy have proven to be more resilient to economic shocks and have been able to offer innovative solutions for social cohesion and inclusion or job creation. in addition, social enterprises have strong links with local and regional daily life and can therefore offer solutions tailored to specific needs. it concludes that social innovation and social enterprise play a key role in the development of the social economy and that to stimulate this, progress is needed in the following areas:- education and training,- improvement of funding,- better visibility at european and national level and exchange of information and best practice,- promotion of the development of the social economy in the eu and the member states,- creation of a more favourable legal environment.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which provides a comprehensive overview of the challenges and benefits of social economies. i agree that social innovation is a major contributor to sustainable growth. i think this approach can work for smaller settlements, in the context of a so-called social eco-village. so i started a pilot project on this. i think one topic has been under-reported in the material, and that is that these companies can play a big role in reducing energy dependence across europe.
in writing. ‒ today, many studies conclude that automation will lead to the disappearance or significant reduction of existing jobs in the future. the creation of the digital single market, the completion of the energy union, investments in research and development, innovation and the development of transport networks also offer significant job creation opportunities. the employment of those with no or very low qualifications should also be strengthened, including support for persons with disabilities through improvement of working conditions and conditions, by introducing and supporting appropriate and effective incentives. special programmes to improve employability should be developed and implemented to re-integrate citizens who have been out of work for several years into the world of work. a financial and economic structure should be established to promote participation in continuing education and training, including the increasing number of persons with disabilities who, due to ageing, require access without barriers, including reasonable accommodation, as this will ensure that the workers of the future are highly qualified. the forecasting of future skills needs requires close involvement of labour market actors, including employers' and workers' organisations, and industry players at the forefront of it and robotics developments, at all levels. i voted in favour of the report on creating a competitive eu labour market for the 21st century.

in writing. ‒ despite its many positive features, i did not vote in favour of the report, mainly because it should have painted a more realistic picture of the unemployment situation. i'll just give you an example. i think that perhaps not in all member states, but in hungary for example, the data is heavily distorted: the public employment system, which provides about 160 euros per month, is taken into account, in addition to the fact that people who take up work abroad and people who work even one hour a week are considered to be employed in the same way as full-time workers. it should also be mentioned that it would be important to speed up the work of eurostat at eu level, where data are processed with a delay of 2-3 years, so in my opinion they do not reflect timeliness. in addition to statistical data, i am pleased that the report sets out a number of important solutions for creating an efficient labour market. i think that the concept of a european minimum wage, which i have mentioned on several occasions, is very important. the report rightly calls on the commission and the member states to introduce a european framework for minimum wages with the aim of addressing wage disparities by means of a basic level per member state to guarantee a fair income in accordance with national practice by law or by agreement.
