mr president, there is much to welcome in the decisions of the informal european council and the home affairs council. this is indeed the way to go. may i, nevertheless, point out two things? one is that the eu candidate countries of the western balkans, on the direct land route of migration could have been – and should have been – invited at least to the informal council. politicians, especially from the former soviet bloc, should have been more keenly aware of the difference between making decisions for someone and with someone. anyway, history teaches us that messing up the western balkans is not necessarily a very good idea. i would also remind our colleagues in the council that taking a decision by a qualified majority – which i personally welcome – is a courageous step only if they are willing to go the whole way. unless there is a willingness to go the whole way and have sanctions for non-compliance, this just adds to the political theatre on this question – of which we already have too much.
mr president, i am shocked to hear the malicious, biased and untrue attacks repeatedly made against hungary. it's about reversing the law that's in place, when we should be focusing on effectively supporting genuine refugees. to provide effective assistance to those living in the large refugee camps in the middle east. they are the real refugees, not the ones who throw concrete at the hungarian border or who stage a siege at calais. we should concentrate on cooperation with third countries where people in need can receive adequate humanitarian aid without risking their lives. where it is still possible to determine, without loss of life, who may qualify for refugee status. this would prevent thousands of people from vomiting in an inhuman way, and when they reach their destination, they would find that they cannot remain in the union. we need to speak with responsibility, we need to act with solidarity, we need to provide humanitarian aid, we need to protect the external borders of the union. we will enforce the eu rules with everyone and we will say, we will say honestly, that we cannot accommodate everyone. just so we can help the refugees who are really in need. and i think everything else is gonna be a hypocrite sooner or later.
you can love viktor orbán and the hungarian government or not, but one thing is certain: on the issue of mass illegal migration, they express the opinion of the majority of hungarian people, both in words and in their actions. moreover, they express the opinion of the majority of the european people by wanting to protect their country and wanting to protect europe. maybe our liberal friends remember that this used to be what they called "democracy". when decision-makers were not forced to believe the ideas of a small elite and the media that most people thought were bizarre, but were told the opinions of the people. and there was a term called "freedom of speech". our friends in the west have come to take it for granted that mass illegal immigration is something that should only be discussed in the kitchen and in private. this is over now.
in writing. i consider it extremely important that the western balkan candidate countries, and in particular serbia, are given a prominent place in the eu institutions' migration resolution processes. when we consider that the bulk of land-based refugees are arriving in the eu via this so-called balkan route and the approach of cold weather, two things become clear: the need for the commission to treat serbia and the other western balkan candidate countries as serious partners. where possible, it should be treated in this respect as is the case in the member states. serbia is an island between eu member states and therefore cannot be bypassed in the search for european solutions. and closely related to this, i think it is right to expect the european commission to show maximum efficiency and speed in the process of providing financial assistance to serbia and the other western balkan countries.
in writing. the mass arrival of refugees is one of the biggest challenges facing the union since its foundation. how we deal with this crisis will determine how europe is seen in the world and how we are seen by our own citizens. our task is to find a humane and rational solution, a new balance between the requirements of international law and security needs, to provide refuge to those in need, while protecting and strengthening the fundamental values of our union. the past period has shown that narrow nationalist solutions lead nowhere. barbed wire, walls, water cannons, tear gas, rubber bullets, violence, denial of rights do not stop refugees, but only cause immeasurable suffering and deprive the displaced of any remaining human dignity. while many citizens, communities and cities in europe have shown generosity and humanity in recent times, the organised institutional response is often weak and uncertain. last week, europe's leaders made a courageous decision to put aside the resistance of nationalists playing small-time politics and move towards a stronger common european policy. but that's not enough. we need to mobilize europe's resources to help and integrate refugees, and to get these resources to where they really need to be supported, to cities and to civil society, to communities.
in writing. ‒ forced labour violates the human rights and dignity of millions of men, women, young girls and boys. the struggle against this most violent form of exploitation has been central to many of the major political and philosophical movements for emancipation. the struggle for emancipation, which aimed to free man from political and cultural domination and physical dependencies, always attacked slave labor, which prevented the exercise of other rights. yet, in the 21st century, forced labor still affects 21 million people who are victims of exploitation that generates $150 billion a year for the organizers and perpetrators of this crime. the 2014 protocol to the 1930 ilo convention on forced labour updates the convention by providing it with new instruments and binding legal force to combat forced labour. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ we welcome today’s vote, with which we authorise and recommend member states to ratify the international labour organization’s (ilo) forced labour convention. this is one of the ilo’s eight fundamental conventions which are at the base of international labour standards. this particular protocol seeks to address gaps in implementation and to make progress on preventing trafficking for labour exploitation as well as protecting and compensating victims of forced labour. it is crucially important that the use of forced labour is suppressed in all its forms irrespective of the nature of the work or the sector of activity in which it may be performed. we therefore strongly support the ratification of this ilo convention by all member states, convinced that all measures must be put in place in order to eradicate a practice to which young boys and girls are often exposed and which is still present in some of our member states.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution because trafficking in human beings and forced labour are the most serious violations of human rights and must be combated by all means. ratification of the protocol will also help to ensure that the rights of victims of such crimes are better protected across europe. it is deeply regrettable that despite the fact that 80 years have passed since the original convention on forced labor came into force, millions of victims continue to be victimized worldwide.
in writing. ‒ the 1930 convention is one of the eight ilo founding conventions setting out basic international labour standards. the 2014 protocol contains important additions to address the shortcomings of the original convention, but it cannot be ratified by the member states as some parts of it fall within the competence of the union. the draft decision is therefore intended to authorise the member states to ratify the parts of the protocol which fall within the competence of the union. at its last plenary session, the european parliament gave its consent to a similar draft council decision authorising member states to ratify the protocol in respect of social policy aspects, and this draft would do the same in respect of aspects related to judicial cooperation in criminal matters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation, as the convention on forced labour is one of the fundamental international labour standards and its updating is essential. the reasoning of the recommendation emphasizes that when the 1930 convention was adopted, the international labour conference called on states to eliminate and criminalize forced labour as soon as possible. yet, 80 years later, the ilo estimates that there are still at least 20.9 million victims of forced labor worldwide. this and related phenomena - such as trafficking in human beings, exploitation - must be stopped! in my opinion, one of the peculiarities of forced labour is that it is not guaranteed that there is a system of adequate remuneration and other benefits for the work. i am curious how the hungarian government explains the public service system's allegedly labour-infringing monthly salary of around 150 euros, and how the government is coordinating its policies and action plan to effectively and permanently eliminate forced labour. i should note that the coordination process also includes educating and informing people and ensuring that the scope and enforcement of legislation relevant to the prevention of forced labour extends to all workers and all sectors of the economy, protecting citizens, including migrant workers, against potentially abusive and unfair recruitment and placement practices.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with community decision-making, i voted in favour of the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ 5-[2-amino-propyl]indol and other synthetic psychoactive substances have a high degree of toxicity with adverse effects on the human body. these chemicals can cause rapid heartbeat and hyperthermia, but they can also cause pupil dilation, restlessness and tremors, and epileptic seizures, among other things. in addition, they may interact with other substances, medicines, or stimulants in the body. since the beginning of 2012, several member states have reported that these psychoactive substances have been known to cause deaths. the wider availability of these new psychoactive substances on the black market could seriously undermine the eu's fight against drug trafficking and use. on this basis, i supported the eu's imposition of control measures and criminal sanctions on these substances.

in writing. ‒ agree with the commission's proposal to provide financial assistance from the european union solidarity fund (eusf) under point 11 of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 for the disaster in bulgaria (classified by the eusf as a 'major natural disaster' due to exceptionally severe winter weather conditions) and for two floods in greece (classified by the eusf as a 'regional disaster' due to floods in evros, central greece) in early 2015. the commission carried out a thorough examination of all three applications in accordance with the regulation establishing the european union solidarity fund. the european union is providing a total of eur 16 274 765 to bulgaria and greece for damage mitigation. on the basis of the above, as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i supported the adoption of the proposal in agreement with the european people's party.

in writing. ‒ geographical indications are used to designate the origin of goods by indicating the country, region, county, locality, manufacturer, producer to which the goods are most closely related. at present, at european level, protection of origin is granted only to agricultural products which meet the conditions, are produced by a traditional process and are of high quality. at present, the protection of these products varies from one member state to another, with some member states not granting protection to products from other member states. following the research carried out on the subject and the consultation of the parties concerned, this own-initiative report calls on the commission to submit a legislative proposal also for products which are not agricultural products and which, due to their traditional production, form part of the european cultural heritage. i voted in favour of the report because such a regulation would significantly improve not only the international competitiveness of the member states but also that of europe.
in writing. ‒ geographical indications are used to designate the origin of goods by indicating the country, region, county, locality, manufacturer, producer to which the goods are most closely related. at present, at european level, protection of origin is granted only to agricultural products which meet the conditions, are produced by a traditional process and are of high quality. at present, the protection of these products varies from one member state to another, with some member states not granting protection to products from other member states. following the research carried out on the subject and the consultation of the parties concerned, this own-initiative report calls on the commission to submit a legislative proposal also for products which are not agricultural products and which, due to their traditional production, form part of the european cultural heritage. such a system would significantly improve not only the international competitiveness of the member states but also that of europe.
in writing. ‒ agriculture and the food industry are of particular importance in the hungarian economy. the same is true of wine production, which is closely linked to these industries, but the country has a number of other products of traditionally high quality outside the agricultural area. internationally recognised designations such as the segepe pepper, the gyula sausage, the mako onion, the tokaji wine or the wild bull's blood not only contribute to the image of the country of origin, but also maintain the quality requirements of the products and provide significant added market value through protection in the form of collective rights. the concept of geographical indications is applied in general to all the indications used in the market to identify the geographical origin of products. at present, at european level, the protection of origin granted by geographical indications applies only to agricultural products which fulfil the conditions. this own-initiative report calls on the european commission to come forward with a legislative proposal covering products which are not agricultural products but which, due to their traditional production, form part of europe's cultural heritage. such a system would significantly improve not only the international competitiveness of the member states but also that of europe. that's why i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ geographical indications are used to designate the origin of goods by indicating the country, region, county, locality, manufacturer, producer to which the goods are most closely related. at european level, protection of origin is currently limited to agricultural products produced by a traditional process and of high quality. the protection of these products varies from one member state to another under the rules in force. in some countries of the union, products from other member states are not protected. this report is the result of research and consultation with stakeholders. the document calls on the commission to take the initiative to protect products which are not agricultural products but which, due to their traditional production, form part of europe's cultural heritage. such a system would significantly improve not only the international competitiveness of the member states but also that of europe.

in writing. the resolution in question helps to preserve the european union's enduring values and valuable expertise, which is a significant part of europe's historical, cultural, economic and social heritage, and i was happy to vote in favour of it. the extension of the protection of geographical indications in the european union to non-agricultural products would support and facilitate the protection of european handicrafts resulting from traditional knowledge and skills. through designation of origin, it would facilitate better access to the eu common market and to markets outside the union, contributing to the development of social and territorial communities and rural areas.
in writing. ‒ there has long been a uniform eu-wide protection for agricultural products originating in a specific geographical area, which have certain characteristics or are produced by traditional processes. in its green paper 'taking advantage of europe's traditional expertise: a possible extension of the protection of geographical indications to non-agricultural products in the european union', the commission examined the extension of such protection to non-agricultural products. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to add a geographical indication to the list of products which have been protected at eu level since 1992, in addition to foodstuffs. this will provide consumers with the right information, but it will also help to protect cultural heritage, boost local businesses and promote local products. a geographical indication is therefore a name or sign indicating the origin of a product. the sign usually also symbolises the traditional process, special knowledge or local culture required to produce the product, which is why it cannot be used by other businesses without authorisation. the european commission has identified more than 800 products that would be affected by such a new regulation, including antwerp diamonds and murano glass, as well as fish fingers, herring and porcelain. the proposal is in fact a strong signal to the european commission to take the initiative to propose a uniform system of geographical indications as soon as possible and to take account of existing systems.

in writing. ‒ following the conclusions of the european summit of 12 july 2015, the european commission presented on 17 july 2015 its proposal to amend the common provisions for the 2014-2020 programming period in order to provide the liquidity needed to implement the greek cohesion programmes. the proposal envisages an increase in the advance payment, a 95% co-financing ceiling and the abolition of national co-financing for greece. the commission considers these measures necessary because the crisis in greece has led to continuous negative growth rates, liquidity problems and a lack of public resources to create jobs. i voted in favour of the commission's proposal, but i think it is important to emphasise a few points. in particular, i consider it essential that the proper use of the surcharges be closely monitored. i would also like to point out that these measures violate several fundamental principles (e.g. co-financing, subsidiarity, additionality, equal treatment), and it is therefore important to emphasise that this is a specific, one-off step which in no way can create a precedent or affect the future nature of cohesion policy. given that the commission proposal raises not only legal and policy concerns but also budgetary concerns, i therefore consider it necessary to clarify the actual budgetary implications as soon as possible. it is important that the proposals contained in the commission's draft do not involve any modification of the multiannual financial framework and do not affect the cohesion envelope of greece or the other member states.

in writing. ‒ in greece, the financial crisis has led to a risk of liquidity shortages and a lack of public funds for public investments essential to a sustainable recovery. in order not to impede the implementation of programmes supported by the european regional development fund, the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), the commission proposes that the ep and the council amend regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 of the european parliament and of the council laying down general provisions on the above-mentioned funds as regards specific measures for greece. the proposed amendment is an exceptional measure to provide immediate support to greece to access and use the remaining union funds from the 2007-2013 cohesion policy programming period before the end of 2015. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) is an important institution of solidarity within the union: it helps workers whose jobs have been lost as a result of globalisation to find a job as soon as possible and to find a permanent job in a competitive sector. an active employment policy instrument that shares the burden of returning to the labour market between the worker, the member state concerned and the union, and the resulting benefits for the worker who is able to return to work, for the member state that is forced to deal with unemployment and for the union that aims to increase employment. germany applied for a financial contribution from the egf in respect of 2881 redundancies at adam opel ag and one supplier, belgium in respect of 5111 redundancies at ford genk and 11 suppliers and downstream processors, and italy in respect of 1249 redundancies at the alitalia group. all three applications fulfil the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation, with germany being eligible for a total of eur 6 958 623, belgium for eur 6 268 564 and italy for eur 1 414 848. i voted in favour of the motions accordingly.

in writing. ‒ belgium has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf in respect of the 5111 redundancies at ford genk, of which 3701 were caused by ford genk and 1180 by 11 suppliers or processors. the application complies with the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation. i agree with the commission that the conditions laid down in the egf regulation are met and that belgium is therefore entitled to a financial contribution under that regulation. in the province of limburg, ford genk was the largest employer. the redundancies cause significant damage to the economy of limburg, as they result in the loss of more than 8000 jobs in total, the majority of the redundancies affecting eu citizens aged between 30 and 54. on the basis of the above, and in view of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2015, i supported the adoption of the proposal as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation in agreement with the european people's party.
in writing. ‒ belgium has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf in respect of the 5111 redundancies at ford genk, of which 3701 were caused by ford genk and 1180 by 11 suppliers or processors. the application complies with the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation. the european parliament agrees with the commission that the conditions laid down in the egf regulation are met and that belgium is therefore entitled to a financial contribution of eur 6 268 564 from the total cost of eur 10 447 607 to be granted under that regulation. in the province of limburg, ford genk was the largest employer. the redundancies are causing significant damage to the limburg economy, with a total loss of more than 8000 jobs, the redundancies affecting mainly eu citizens aged between 30 and 54 years, an increase in the unemployment rate of between 1,8 and 2 percentage points (the region's unemployment rate rises from 6,8% to 8,8%), a decline in gdp of between 2,6% and 2,9% and a potential decrease in labour productivity of 10,9% due to the very important role played by the automotive industry in the region in terms of labour productivity. on the basis of the above, in view of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2015, the hungarian people's party delegation supported the adoption of the proposal in agreement with the european people's party.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in development cooperation, taking into account that the un 2030 agenda for sustainable development highlights local authorities as important actors in the organisation and achievement of development goals, alongside governments, parliaments and other international organisations. in line with this, the eu should continue to support local authorities in developing countries. their involvement is essential to ensure transparent and accountable governance and to achieve the post-2015 targets as close as possible to the people. i agree that the key goals and challenges of the development programme depend on local action. i also find it important that the report mentions the role of local authorities in conflict prevention and management. i therefore support the report's call for decentralised cooperation and the recommendation that member states coordinate their efforts to make room for local authorities in their development programmes. as the largest donor of development aid, the eu plays a key role in achieving the sustainable development goals. and by promoting decentralised cooperation, we have a good chance of achieving these goals by 2030.

mr. president, in the wake of the volkswagen scandal, we have to confront the true value system of the car manufacturers. the case of the engine tampering was not just a one-time mistake, but it also shed light on their general attitude. let me give you a concrete example of what i'm talking about. one of the largest engine factories in the world is located in hungary. audi produces engines here, including some two million tricks that the volkswagen group was recently caught with. the factory did not have enough capacity, so audi decided to expand and chose a natura 2000 site as the site. given that audi contributes almost 10% of hungarian gdp, it did not encounter too much resistance from the authorities. only one environmental activist questioned the legality of the investment. audi tried to settle with him out of court, then tricked him into a court of law and sent him to prison. since then, the innocent audi has been exposed as a manufacturer of millions of fraudulent engines, the natura 2000 site has been destroyed, compensation measures have failed, the court sentenced ferenc zák to three years in prison, and audi and volkswagen remain proud owners of the european environmental management standard iso 14001. i'm sure, ma'am, but how long?

mr. president, honourable members of parliament, hungary is in mourning. it is my sad but heartfelt duty to report here before the european parliament, the political body directly elected by the peoples of europe, that one of europe's sages, one of the greatest figures of hungarian democracy, died yesterday: göncz árpád, former writer, a great figure of the 1956 freedom revolution, the first man of the republic of hungary for ten years after the change of regime, the president of the republic. it is a great honour to be able to commemorate in this house one of the great sages of europe, one of the main architects of eastern european democracies, and it is perhaps symbolic that today, when events are taking place in this house, they may have taken us out of the political day-to-day. göncz árpád was a hungarian writer, translator, politician, sentenced to life imprisonment for his role in '56, released after six years. he became a member of the first hungarian parliament after the change of regime, became its president, and then for ten years the president of the republic of hungary. since then, there has been no leader of hungary like him, popular, loved by the hungarian society, who received the "vision for europe" award in 2000 for his work in creating a united europe. later, his daughter, göncz kinga, became your colleague, a member of the european parliament. i just want to say goodbye to him with a quote, to leave us, the politicians of today, his thinking. he said, "somewhere, the real secret to popularity is not always conforming to the demands of popularity". our relationship to power is what we're measured by. who used it for what. let's remember göncz barad.

in writing. ‒ in my view, the success of tunisia's democratic transition depends on future economic and social development. it is an undeniable fact that the country has significant long-term growth potential. implementing the expected reforms and the benefits already existing - such as human resources and an open economy - will together unlock this potential, boosting the country's economy in a more sustainable and inclusive way. the tunisian economy has suffered a significant decline in recent years both domestically and internationally, especially in terms of trade with europe, which remains the main partner. in this context, it is essential that tunisia is made a priority for the union and that the union makes concrete economic and investment commitments to support the country's fragile democratic transition, bearing in mind that the success of the tunisian experiment is in the interest of the region as a whole and of the union as a whole. the participation of tunisia in union programmes should therefore be considered in this light. i particularly welcome the objective of promoting cooperation in the fields of university education, general education, training and youth, for example in the framework of erasmus+ and other programmes aimed at building personal relationships.
in writing. tunisia is the only country where the export of democracy has not led to bloody conflict, so far. i supported the resolution that this should continue to be the case, because the growth of trade and tourism can stabilize the economy, thereby improving the country's viability, while also reducing the propensity to migrate, which is the key question of our time.

in writing. ‒ the regulations on the introduction of the european small claims procedure and on the european order for payment procedure are intended to simplify crossborder judicial proceedings within the european union and to reduce the financial burden of such proceedings. these provisions are mainly in favour of consumers and smes, as the regulation contains rules which generally facilitate the enforcement of claims before the courts. experience shows that the scheme has been well received and its application has reduced the duration of procedures by an average of 40%. this amendment, taking account of the practice of recent years, seeks to make the rules of the regulation more responsive to the needs of the workforce. significant simplification, for example by modernising the rules for electronic service or by amending the threshold. the tripartite discussions on the dossier resulted in a basically favourable compromise, and i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the increase in the threshold for using the european small claims procedure. by allowing the use of the simplified procedure for cross-border claims between eur 2000 and eur 10 000, the proportion of cases where the cost and duration of dispute settlement can be significantly reduced could be increased. i believe that this change will further increase the number of cases where businesses and consumers can achieve cost savings. the threshold for small claims should be kept below the average amount of claims, thereby ensuring the necessary procedural guarantees for larger claims. it should also be borne in mind that the procedure will be used more frequently if the threshold is raised, thereby making it part of the daily routine in the courts. this will facilitate access to the necessary information for potential users of the procedure, in particular consumers. however, raising the threshold above eur 10 000 does not seem feasible at present and the rapporteur therefore supports the value proposed by the commission.

president of the council. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, five years ago, as you have just said, a few days after the disaster, hungary informed the council of the red mudslides in the west of the country, their effects, and the measures taken by the hungarian authorities to deal with the consequences for man and the environment. shortly after the accident, on 20 december 2010, the council, in conclusions on improving environmental policy instruments, invited the member states and the commission to strengthen the implementation of eu environmental legislation. a considerable body of european union legislation is in place to prevent accidents such as the one in hungary. it includes legislation on integrated pollution prevention and reduction and on the management of waste from the extractive industries, which i believe you referred to. industrial accidents are covered by the environmental liability directive. the management and disposal of waste in a member state is the responsibility of that member state, and each member state is responsible for the transposition and implementation of european union legislation, under the control, of course, of the commission. in particular, member states should ensure that the competent authorities monitor the operation of waste management facilities in the extractive industry. they must also ensure that the necessary measures to prevent contamination of water and soil have been taken and that regular checks are carried out to verify compliance with these measures. it is the commission's responsibility to check that member states are fulfilling these obligations to implement eu legislation. it has the power to take legal action against a member state which fails to fulfil its obligations. in addition, the commission has the right of initiative to submit new proposals to the council and the european parliament if it considers that further action at european union level is necessary. it goes without saying that the council will treat any proposals with due care. i am sure the commissioner will have an opportunity to comment on this. in particular, it is important to fully implement the existing environmental inspection rules in close cooperation with the relevant actors. cooperation projects in the field of environmental inspections, including at regional level, facilitate the full implementation of eu environmental legislation, in particular on waste. ladies and gentlemen, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle, as well as the obligation to repair damage to the environment, are now part of the fundamental principles of international environmental law on the one hand, and of the acquis of the european union on the other. they are enshrined in the treaty on the functioning of the european union. in the specific case of the 2010 disaster in hungary, i would draw your attention to the fact that, in accordance with the polluter pays principle, the company responsible for the disaster was subject to heavy penalties.
member of the commission.– madam president, honourable members, as mr la via has stated, the red mud accident which happened on 4 october 2010 in ajka had a very serious impact: 10 people died and more than 150 were injured; 400 houses were flooded, 40 square kilometres of land were affected. about one million cubic metres of red mud flowed downstream, causing the greatest environmental disaster in the history of hungary. relief and rehabilitation expenditure amounted to 35 billion hungarian forints – that is to say about eur 115 million. today, five years later, the main lesson to be drawn is that, in order to prevent this kind of disaster, two conditions have to be met. first, we need to have good legislation in place. secondly, the legislation then has to be fully and effectively implemented. and, of course, it is also important to keep legislation under review, to update it and to make sure it is fit to address new challenges. although nobody can guarantee that other accidents will never happen, we are today in a better situation than five years ago, thanks to the improvements in our legislation. there is, indeed, a large and solid body of eu legislation applying to extractive activities, which includes measuring industrial emissions, preventing major accidents and managing extractive waste, as well as protecting water and natural resources. the commission keeps the implementation of the legislation under close scrutiny and has proposed measures to update and enhance it. since the red mud accident took place a number of legal changes have been adopted to reinforce the mechanisms available to address hazards and accidents in extractive industries. today, the industrial emissions directive and the directive on control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances set out requirements on industrial inspections that are more stringent than those applicable at the time of the accident. they also include more detailed obligations to inform the public and to enable it to participate in relevant planning procedures. this will result in safer installations and will increase awareness and make for better preparedness. the commission has been working with member states to ensure the effective implementation of these new inspection requirements. the commission is also cooperating with impel, the network of european environmental inspectorates, to promote best practice in the conduct of inspections. the commission has recently also considered the feasibility of an industrial risk-reducing facility or fund in the framework of the environmental liability directive to deal with the environmental consequences of major accidents. an assessment of this option has been carried out with a high level of participation by stakeholders. in the opinion of the commission, the results do not provide sufficient grounds to propose a new financial mechanism. however, the commission wishes to underline that, although the environmental liability directive in its current form does not impose mandatory financial security schemes at european union level to cover for damage due to industrial accidents, it allows member states to do so and obliges them to develop financial security instruments and markets. extractive waste is one of the larger waste streams in the european union. the transition towards a circular economy should therefore bring about significant improvements. increasing the efficiency of extraction processes will help reduce waste generation and associated pollution. more efficient techniques will allow the remining and processing of quarrying waste. more efficient waste-recovery systems will reduce the pressures on our natural capital. we can reduce our dependence on extractive materials through urban mining – recovering valuable materials from the products we no longer need, for example by getting the gold from used mobile phones. hungary was also devastated by the baia mare disaster of 2000 when cyanide used in gold mining in romania leaked into the danube river. if we can get more gold from used electronic equipment, we can use less cyanide. the revised directive on waste electrical and electronic equipment will ensure that member states collect 85% of such waste, increasing the potential supply of gold from recycling. finally, the commission is using horizon 2020 funding to boost research and innovation, to develop clean and sustainable production of primary and secondary raw materials, to reduce waste generation and to develop environmentally-friendly technologies that prevent hazardous waste generation. in our 2014-2015 work programme we specifically allocated more than eur 150 million to a focus area on waste: a resource to recycle, reduce and recover raw materials.
on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, i thank the commissioner, mr la via, for his thoughts and for his remembrance, and as a former resident of the area i would like to recall very briefly the disaster of red mud that spilled from the reservoir of the mal zrt. near ajka exactly five years ago, on 4 october 2010, and that flooded three towns: kolontárt, devecsert and somlóvásárhely. as a result of the disaster, as mentioned earlier, it is worth remembering that ten people died, more than two hundred were injured, and hundreds of houses were rendered uninhabitable. the unprecedented destruction forced an exemplary stand. in the emergency situation, hungary simply stood as a human being. the authorities' decisive and professional action has received widespread international recognition. the position of the civilians became a symbol of the deep-rooted solidarity of hungarian society. the colontár, devecser and somló market are the symbol of the unity. it is extremely important to me that the decision on the lessons of the disaster mentions this. i am pleased that the environment committee has unanimously adopted a draft resolution which, in addition to a sound assessment of the causes of industrial accidents, sets out future tasks. for me, kolontár's real lesson is the failure of the polluter pays principle. in fact, although eu legislation provides for liability, without mandatory financial guarantees the polluter will not be able to recover the damage he has caused. it is therefore essential that the european commission continue to work towards the creation of a union disaster insurance system capable of applying the 'polluter pays' principle to large-scale industrial disasters. the european solution is in our hands, it is time for the union to do its homework from the colonels.
on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, when we talk about this disaster, the first few thoughts i think we all have to have are about the people involved in the accident and the victims and their relatives. undoubtedly, this disaster caused incredible devastation in one of the most beautiful areas of hungary, defining the fate of this entire region, including the families of the survivors, for a very long time. what we've done, and there were many contributors to this report, i think everyone has done their job with a lot of self-control, and in that sense we've really managed to focus a little bit more on the broader picture than just one disaster, and maybe it's true that we've managed to learn some lessons from the events. two very important lessons for me: one, which mr. hölvnyi said, is the principle of 'the polluter pays'. it is a long-term task to be able to develop a european system of safeguards to deal with any disaster that may occur in the union. however, we must not forget that in this case, the hungarian authorities considered this facility to be in perfect order a few days before the accident, and issued the relevant documents. in english, if there is control, there is also responsibility, and that's a very, very important part of it. the other very important lesson that i think is worth mentioning here is that, yes, that's when the whole country is moving. that was a very nice example. individuals, institutions, corporations, companies, everyone was trying to help those in trouble. at the same time, the aid that was collected on the roads that were otherwise maintained by the state, this was because the accounting was no longer so clear, it was not very clear who's contribution went where. i think these are very important lessons that we should all take to heart.
on behalf of the verts/ale group madam president, five years ago kolontár suffered perhaps the worst environmental and industrial disaster in hungary's history. so on the fifth anniversary, the first and most important thing we do is to remember those ten victims and the hundreds of injured who suffered in this disaster. on the other hand, it is also clear that we as politicians have a duty to do everything possible to prevent such a disaster from happening again. the lessons from the collateral damage are multi-layered. we have seen that hungary has implemented eu legislation incorrectly, and that the incorrect implementation of the mining waste directive has also played a role in the disaster. there were also serious problems with the implementation of legislation, and the disaster was caused by the incorrect application of the legislation on hazardous waste. and as mentioned, the weak performance of the authorities also played a very important role. the previous commission prepared a document on official environmental controls, which has not been seen since in the new commission's diary. i think that on the occasion of the fifth anniversary we rightly expect the commission to come forward with a proposal on environmental audits. at the same time, as many others have mentioned, a very important lesson of the disaster in the colombier is that the 'polluter pays' principle cannot be applied effectively in europe today. the commission has already proposed a number of measures to help the environment, such as a system of compulsory environmental liability insurance and the creation of a common european industrial disaster fund. these must be examined and the appropriate means must be found to prevent what happened in hungary five years ago, when a loss of 40 billion forints, or about 120 million euros, had to be covered by the hungarian taxpayers, the hungarian budget, and those who caused the damage did not contribute a single penny. we expect the commission to i voted in favour of the report on financial services regulation. i consider the strict regulation of financial services to be particularly important as a hungarian, since i am faced with the consequences of bank fraud, abuse and behaviour that is contrary to consumer protection rules every day when i investigate the complaints of hundreds of thousands of hungarian foreign currency creditors. it is not only in this area that financial services need to be regulated, but also, for example, the fact that despite all this, despite the tragedies of foreign currency loans, the various credit structures, credit cards are being forced on the hungarian people in a terrible and violent way, whether at the airport or elsewhere, this too needs to be regulated very strictly.
in writing. ‒ the report proposes to amend the previous regulations on payment services in the internal market. the amendment aims to enable existing and new payment service providers, irrespective of the business model used by payment service providers, to provide their services under a clear and harmonised regulatory framework. payment transactions must be secure, protecting consumers against the risk of fraud. member states, the commission, the european central bank and the european network of central banks should ensure fair competition in this market, avoiding any discrimination against any of the existing market participants. any payment service provider should be able to offer authorised online transfer services. this provision will support consumers, it will increase their sense of security, and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. in trade and services, in addition to the rise of card payments, there is a dynamic development of new payment methods such as online, mobile and other. given that these are largely cross-border transactions, i supported the report, which provides a clear and harmonised regulatory framework at eu level, in the interests of consumer safety. it aims to ensure that payment transactions are secure and protect against the risk of fraud.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the parliament and the council to adopt a directive of the european parliament and of the council on payment services in the internal market, and to amend directives 2002/65/ec, 2013/36/eu and 2009/110/ec and repeal directive 2007/64/ec. the committee on economic and monetary affairs, accepting the report by antonio tajani of the italian people's party, proposes that parliament propose an amendment to the commission's draft at first reading. i supported the proposal of the committee on economic and monetary affairs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the supplementary report. there is a constant flow of technical innovation in the area of payment services and it is therefore inevitable that our community rules will follow these changes. i welcome the strong emphasis in the report on the security of card payments, without which there can be no effective integrated market for card payments. i consider it important that the report provides detailed listings of individual distortions of competition and that it further strengthens the data protection aspects of the original text. in assessing the supplementary report, i also noted that it emphasised the need to have a harmonised regulatory framework and to ensure a high level of consumer protection.

in writing. ‒ the committee on petitions, on the basis of the petitions received, tabled a motion for a resolution on the spanish legislation on mortgages and risky spanish financial instruments. in spain, the number of evictions is unacceptably high, largely due to abusive behaviour of financial institutions towards their clients. the draft calls on financial institutions in the european union to stop this behaviour and to avoid evictions of single-dwelling families, on the spanish authorities to reduce the number of evictions with the means at their disposal and on the commission to initiate legislation to address the problem. i voted for the motion.

in writing. just five years ago, the worst industrial disaster in the history of my country occurred, when almost one million cubic metres of highly alkaline red mud was released into the environment, flooding several communities, killing ten people and injuring some 150 people, as well as contaminating large areas, including four natura 2000 roads. i naturally supported the resolution, since it is a matter of concern that similar industrial sites exist in several member states and that the risk of such accidents still exists today. it is incomprehensible that in the last five years, little seems to have been learned from the events, the effectiveness of the implementation of relevant union legislation and international agreements remains low, delays in controls persist and virtually none of the shortcomings in relevant union legislation have been addressed. i am particularly concerned about the mining waste directive and the european waste register.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the fifth anniversary of the kolomna oil spill. i was involved as a co-author in the process of developing the document, which has succeeded in putting the focus on environmental aspects instead of praising the dubious achievements of the hungarian government. the proposal covers not only red sludge but also hazardous waste from other industrial production. the resolution also calls on the commission to take steps to establish a transparent financial mechanism that can be used in the event of a disaster. other concrete elements of the proposal include the 'polluter pays' principle, the preference for best available techniques, the more effective involvement of civil society and stricter enforcement of relevant eu and other international rules and on-the-spot checks. the proposal also calls for transparency in both public and private disaster funds.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which rightly highlighted that greater equality between men and women, reducing the gender pay gap, would increase economic performance, contribute to poverty reduction and have a positive impact on society in general. the report examined in detail the issue of equal opportunities for men and women in employment, highlighting all the areas where almost all member states need to improve. i consider it important that the report noted that the small decline in the employment and wage gaps between the sexes in recent years was due to the economic crisis, as some member states tend to attribute such changes in statistical indicators to their own merits. however, this prevents us from achieving real results in reducing the wage gap and increasing employment and competitiveness. at the same time, i would point out that access to lifelong learning, vocational training and mentoring networks cannot be limited to women. it is important for both sexes to have this opportunity throughout europe.
in writing. ‒ this is a very important piece of legislation, and there are a number of important community measures in the area of equal opportunities and equal treatment between men and women. the results of the application shall be reviewed annually. i voted to approve the report.

on behalf of the verts/ale group.– madam president, today we vote on our report concerning the climate agreement in paris. at the moment, when the environmental credibility of the european institutions has been shaken by scandals within the car industry, i find it extremely important to send a very strong signal with this report. the report itself is a strong signal, and i would like to thank mr pargneaux, our rapporteur, for that. still, there are some important considerations to raise. being ambitious is not merely a question of restoring europe’s credibility; it is also a scientific necessity if we want to limit climate change to two degrees. evidence shows us that we need to phase out carbon emissions by 2050 to limit climate change to two degrees, and it is possible, but without this phasing out it becomes an illusion to put us on a track which keeps us below the two-degree target. that is why i am deeply concerned about the amendment tabled by the ppe group, because i believe that if we water down our commitment to decarbonisation till 2050, we will step on a track which takes us beyond or above the two-degree limit. also it is important to mention that the indcs which we already have are clearly not enough to reach our goal of keeping climate change below the two-degree target. this means that we need mechanisms to raise ambition within the european union and at global level at the paris talks. one last point: to phase out co2 emissions, the first step for that is to phase out fossil subsidies, and that is something we have to do very soon.
the european union should first of all clarify one question: when, in retrospect, does it consider the paris climate conference to have been a success? what this report shows is that there is a major objective, to prove what should no longer be, that the european union is the engine, the front-runner in the fight against climate change, and now we are setting more ambitious goals. it says that by 2030, a 40% reduction is just a lower limit, and by 2050, it's all about eliminating carbon dioxide emissions. these goals are unrealistic and do not achieve the desired result. they're not realistic because they don't take into account the economic impact, the cost, the impact on energy costs, and they don't achieve the goal because it's a global problem. the european union is responsible for 9% of emissions, while the united states and china account for 35%, and therefore they should be forced to make mandatory emission reductions, and this is not mentioned once in this paragraph 82. the other aspect is that nuclear energy is not included as a clean energy source for fossil fuels and climate change. that is also unacceptable under paragraph 82.
i would also like to turn to a subject which is a subject of debate for the representatives of the european union in paris. mr eck has already mentioned that other sources of pollution do indeed occur compared to those we have known so far. we're always angry about cars and heating and this and that, but let's not forget that agriculture is also one of the biggest emitters of carbon dioxide, and not just from animal agriculture, but also, unfortunately, from methane emissions from untreated forests. so if we're going to build a future, i'm asking everyone to be mindful not just of the conditions that have been so often announced, but also of the new phenomena that we haven't anticipated.
in writing. the traditional annual un climate change conference is not far behind. paris is much more than that, because our planet is about to take a historic step. the kyoto protocol on reducing carbon emissions expires this year. therefore, a reasonable agreement to reduce emissions signed and ratified by all carbon-emitting countries is needed to prevent global warming with irreversible consequences. the european union has already made a firm commitment, which requires the rest of the developed and developing world to follow suit. i believe that the new agreement should be dynamic, providing for continuous monitoring and the possibility of reviewing reduction commitments. it is also important that the richer, more fortunate countries provide financial and knowledge support to developing economies to help them transition from the traditional fossil-based development phase to the new technologies and environmentally-friendly economic development. fortunately, there is a generation growing up in hungary that is more concerned about the environment than their parents, avoiding chemical, genetically modified foods, preferring local vegetables, eco-tourism, community gardens - and politicians have a duty to help and support this process.

in writing. draft amending budget no 6/2015 contains mainly technical adjustments to the revenue side of the union budget. it takes into account the revision of the projections for traditional own resources and for vat and gni resources, the budgetary transfers and financing of the corresponding corrections for the united kingdom, and thus modifies the distribution of contributions to the union budget between member states. the draft amending budget no 6/2015 was adopted by the council. the gni-based national contributions to the budget compared to the original 2015 budget are reduced by eur 2,26 billion as a result of a higher than expected revenue of eur 1 133,5 million from traditional own resources (customs duties and sugar levies) and as a result of the surplus in 2014 being entered in the budget by the budgetary amendment of 3/2015. on the basis of the above, the hungarian people's party delegation supported the adoption of the proposal in agreement with the european people's party.

in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument for immediate budgetary measures under the european migration strategy. the proposal aims to supplement the resources available in the general budget of the european union for 2015 for the financing of measures to deal with the refugee and migration crisis by a commitment appropriation of eur 66,1 million over and above the ceiling of the multiannual financial framework. the report of the committee on budgets concludes that the ceiling of the relevant commitment appropriations in the 2015 budget does not allow for sufficient funding of important and urgent union priorities and recommends that parliament give its consent to the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument to such an amount. i voted for the motion accordingly.

rapporteur.– mr president, i would like to begin by thanking the shadow rapporteurs with whom i worked together on this report on the european citizens’ initiative (eci). cooperation was exemplary and, a pleasant surprise for me, the vote in the committee on constitutional affairs (afco) was unanimous. i hardly have to note how rare this unanimity is and that is in itself a message, an indication that the eci is properly regarded as a key instrument in the framework of the institutional structure of the european union. now the underlying idea is both straightforward and subtle. the citizens of europe should have the means to launch legislative initiatives on issues of concern at the european level. everyone is aware of the reality of the remoteness between the eu and its citizens, and the eci is one way of bridging it. let me add here immediately that the right of legislative initiative by citizens does not undermine the representative democracy that is the core value of any democratic system – ourselves in other words. no, the eci enhances european democracy by introducing a form of civic action that communicates in parallel with what we are doing. nor is the eci a form of direct democracy where citizens foregather to take legislative action. that may have worked in the classical greek city states but is nonsense when 500 million citizens are involved. what the eci can do is to adopt a single issue and mobilise a sufficient number of individuals in a form of collective action. the mobilisatory element should not be underestimated. the process of collecting a million signatures in a year demands organisational skills, enthusiasm and commitment to doing something political in europe. from that perspective the eci is a way of bringing citizens into the european political field in an unmediated fashion. ultimately there will always be some tension between the politics of representation and political involvement from below. the idea that a given number of citizens can act together on a single issue of concern adds something new to the political palette of europe and, let it be noted, is already available as a form of political action in some eu member states. what differentiates the european political field from that of a member state is that legislation is initiated by the commission. the eci changes this by adding the citizens to those with the right of launching legislation. this shift therefore changes the equation in european politics by adding a new actor. so much for the underlying theory behind the eci; practice to date has not really fulfilled the promise of the instrument. over 50 initiatives have been organised and none, not one, has reached the statute book. by anyone’s failure criteria this is 100%. indeed, in my consultations with civil society i have detected a clear sense of disappointment with the way in which the commission has handled the ecis that it has received. there have been complaints of bureaucratic dilatoriness – the ‘insolence of office’, the ‘law’s delay’, to quote shakespeare – and a general sense that while the commission has dealt with the instrument with complete correctness legally, it has rather missed the political point, that of civic involvement. so the burden of my report is intended to address these shortcomings and to urge the commission to respond to the voice of the citizens with greater flexibility than hitherto. i have every hope that the promised reform of the eci will make it a genuinely effective instrument. (applause)
the european citizens' initiative would be the instrument to ensure that citizens can participate directly in the decision-making process of the union. but this device is very weak. a million signatures would be enough to get the commission to submit a proposal on the matter. of the 51 initiatives, 3 have been successful and none of them are legislation. the reporter is trying to fix this system. but that's not enough anymore. the migrant crisis has demonstrated how far the political elite of the union - respecting the exception - is from the opinion of its own population. a number of polls have shown how different the public's view of this important issue is from that of the political elite. the institution of the european union referendum should therefore be introduced. that would be true direct democracy. (the intervener agrees to answer a question for a blue card under article 162 (8) of the rules of procedure)
that's a two-card answer. your question is, if we can't get something through here, is it a waste of time to give the public direct decision-making? it is not a waste of time to create a clear and decision-making framework for this, unlike the citizens' initiative we are discussing. just as there may be referenda in your country that make specific decisions, the mechanisms for this should be found in the european union.
rapporteur.– mr president, i would like to thank everybody who has taken part in this constructive debate. i think everyone has been constructive, perhaps with one or two exceptions. i am particularly grateful for the supportive words from vice-president timmermans. there are some issues, which i think have some saliency, that i would like to pick up on (i cannot, obviously, do a summary of everything that has been said). i think the point made by mr goerens about the revalorisation of democratic legitimacy is something that we must think about very seriously. connecting the citizens has come up in a fair number of contributions. then there is the follow-up problem, on which others spoke (mr terricabras notably). nobody knows this, but actually i have a very old and very rusty degree in law, and one of the things i take away from this is that when it comes to legal regulations applying the rules – to quote mr timmermans – there is always some leeway in how one interprets these things. here i would like to call for more flexibility: apply the rules but, where there is a grey area, think about the million people who have been involved. finally, three short issues. treaty change has come up: my own take on this is that yes, treaty change will happen one day, but not in connection with the eci, so primary law is not really a part of this. secondly, as i understand it at the moment, an eci can call on the commission to act in particular ways, but as things stand cannot interdict legislation. this could well be reconsidered. certainly, that is the input i have had from civil society. as i understand it, ecis cannot affect current processes, even if inputs from stakeholders are widely regarded as a viable part of policy information – and whatever the status of citizens in the european political field, they are stakeholders. i would like to end by saying that i very much thank mr timmermans. as far as the eci is concerned, the ball is in his court, and i am sure that his team will do everything to make it viable.
my fellow members of parliament! the refusal to grant the european council discharge is unfortunately not new. the council annually ignores parliament's right to carry out the final vote. this is the fifth year that parliament has refused to give the council's final accounts. the council does not take part in the discharge hearing of the committee on budgetary control, it refuses to answer questions sent by parliament during the final discharge procedure, and it does not forward the documents necessary for the discharge procedure and which are made available to the european parliament by any institution other than itself. we have no information on the background, costs and outcomes of the council's various real estate transactions, nor do we know the details of the costs and outcomes of the council's institutional modernisation. the european parliament's committee on budgetary control cannot take a substantive decision on the financial management of the council. the council does not even meet the most basic expectations of transparency and accountability. it shall be exempt from the rules and procedures which apply to all the institutions of the european union. the european people's party therefore supports the rapporteur's proposal that parliament should not grant the council a discharge.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament, the council and the commission agreed in the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making that community law should be updated and that its scope should be reduced by repealing acts that are no longer applicable. it is necessary to remove from the union acquis acts that are no longer relevant in order to improve the transparency and security of union law. the present case concerns a change of a purely technical nature. commission regulation (ec) no 1881/2006 laying down maximum levels for certain contaminants in foodstuffs has fully transposed the provisions of directive 76/621/eec and regulation (ec) no 320/2006 and it is therefore necessary to repeal the latter. for these reasons, i supported the adoption of the report in line with the european people's party line.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing council directive 76/621/eec fixing the maximum level of erucic acid in oils (tar oils) and fats (eating fats) and council directive 320/2006 establishing a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar industry. the committee on agriculture and rural development of the ep proposed only a technical clarification in its amendment, and recommended the commission's proposal to parliament for adoption, which is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the rules of competition for the production and marketing of certain agricultural products and on the establishment of a common organisation of agricultural markets. the proposal aims to repeal provisions relating to the common agricultural policy which are no longer relevant. some of these have been replaced by subsequent acts or have been repealed because of their temporary nature, thus simplifying and reducing the substance of eu law. the report introduces article 114 tfeu on the approximation of laws on the establishment and functioning of the internal market as a new proposal. the aim is to harmonise the dual legal bases of agricultural and internal market policy in respect of the fixing of maximum levels of erucic acid content of oils (food oils) and fats (eating fats). accordingly, the european parliament and the council, acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure and after consulting the economic and social committee, shall adopt measures relating to the establishment and functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i supported the agriculture committee's proposal to bring it into line with the dual legal basis (agricultural and internal market policies) used when directive 76/621/eec was adopted on the fixing of maximum levels of erucic acid in oils (oilseeds) and fats (eating fats). this is important because of the establishment of a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar industry.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to the council to repeal council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings (see next point). the directive was also applicable between the member states of the union and switzerland by means of a separate bilateral agreement concluded in 2004. on the other hand, the european union and switzerland signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 27 may 2015, which amended that 2004 bilateral agreement in line with the 2014 oecd global standards for the automatic exchange of financial account information. the council intends to take a decision on the ratification of this agreement and, in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union, it is required to consult the european parliament before taking such a decision. in its report, parliament's economic and monetary affairs committee recommended that the council adopt the draft decision and thereby give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i have accordingly supported the council's draft decision.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which is an important part of effective action against fraud and tax evasion. tax fraud knows no borders and it is therefore particularly important that tax fraud by natural and legal persons established in the union involving financial institutions established in third countries is prevented by appropriate arrangements. i strongly agree with the point in the report that 18 months after the entry into force of the agreement, the commission should assess its effectiveness. only in this way can we be sure that we have actually prevented taxable persons from concealing income for which tax has not yet been paid by using the facilities provided by swiss financial institutions.
in writing. ‒ the european union and switzerland signed an agreement on 27 may 2015 on the automatic exchange of financial account information to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement is an important step in their efforts to act against tax fraud and tax evasion and updates the 2004 agreement which ensures that switzerland applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of savings income on interest, which is why i supported it in the vote.
in writing. ‒ council directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation was amended by council directive 2014/107/eu to align it with the oecd global standard on the automatic exchange of account information for tax purposes, extending the automatic exchange of information to the full range of income. however, following the 2008 evaluation of council directive 2003/48/ec on taxation of savings, the commission proposed a revision of that directive, which was finally adopted by the council in 2014. if member states now apply the provisions of both directives, they will have to operate a dual system of collection and supply of data for the same data. to avoid this, the commission proposed to the council to repeal council directive 2003/48/ec. the treaty on the functioning of the european union requires the council to consult the european parliament before taking a decision. in its report, parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs recommended the proposal with amendments for approval by parliament. i supported the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of adopting the report, which helps member states to avoid additional administrative burdens caused by dual data collection and delivery systems. the fact that the commission's proposal to repeal the 2003 savings tax directive was based on the oral opinions of parliamentary groups, tax experts from dg taxud and independent experts also played a role in my decision. however, as the rapporteur rightly pointed out, the scope of the eu savings tax directive and the administrative cooperation directive is broadly similar, but not exactly identical. i therefore consider it of the utmost importance that the commission continues to monitor the existence of loopholes following the repeal in order to reduce the potential loss of tax revenue for member states.
in writing. ‒ in light of the above concerns about the potential for loopholes and the risk of burdensome double reporting, the rapporteur had to assess the specificity of possible loopholes and whether the burden of double reporting would be greater for a year than ensuring that such loopholes could not occur. the rapporteur has fully examined, with the involvement of experts and through a thorough analysis, any loopholes related to the repeal. it agreed to the repeal but only with three amendments that address its concerns and asked the commission to report on the results of the repeal, citing any loopholes that might arise. it encouraged the commission to take steps to ensure that these loopholes were closed, if necessary in the form of legislative proposals. it considered that these amendments would ensure that parliament fulfilled its role in reducing potential tax revenue losses to member states across the union. that's why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ with today’s vote we approved the draft council implementing decision on the launch of automated data exchange with regard to dactyloscopic data in sweden. the supply of personal data may not take place until the general provisions on data protection have been implemented in the national law of the territories of the member states involved. the verification that this condition has been met with respect to automated data exchange is done on the basis of an evaluation report based on a questionnaire, an evaluation visit and a pilot run. sweden has completed the questionnaire on data protection and the questionnaire on dactyloscopic data exchange. a successful pilot run has been carried out by sweden with austria. on 13 july 2015, the council concluded that sweden had fully implemented the general provisions on data protection and therefore, for the purposes of automated searching of dactyloscopic data, sweden should be entitled to receive and supply personal data pursuant to article 9 of decision 2008/615/jha.
in writing. ‒ pursuant to council decision 2008/615/jha on the strengthening of crossborder cooperation to combat terrorism and crossborder crime, the supply of personal data required by this decision may not take place until the member states concerned have transposed the general data protection provisions in force on their territory into national law. on 13 july 2015, the council, on the basis of the report submitted to it, concluded that the swedish legislation in force complies in all respects with the general provisions on data protection in chapter 6 of decision 2008/615/jha. the council therefore intends to authorise sweden to receive and supply personal data pursuant to decision 2008/615/jha. pursuant to article 39 (1) of the treaty on european union, as amended by the treaty of amsterdam, and article 9 of protocol no 36 on transitional provisions, the council is to consult the european parliament before adopting a decision. in its report, parliament's committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommended the council's draft for parliament's approval. i have accordingly supported the council's draft decision.

in writing. ‒ internet sales have significantly changed booking habits, so that many self-organised trips are now not covered by eu rules dating back to the 1990s or do not clearly articulate passenger rights. for this reason, i voted in favour of amending the eu consumer protection rules on travel, so that in future the same rules will apply to online bookings of air, hotel or car rental as those made at a travel agent. under the amended rules, before holiday homes sign the contract, tour operators or sellers of the trip must clearly explain that it is a package. in addition, passengers must be informed of their rights and of their financial responsibility in the event of a problem. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road, rail and inland waterway.
