in writing. ‒ online sales have significantly changed booking habits. today, many self-organised routes are not covered by the eu rules dating back to the 1990s or do not clearly define passenger rights. for this reason, i voted in favour of amending the eu consumer protection rules on travel. in future, therefore, the same rules will apply to online bookings of package holidays, including flights, hotel reservations and car rentals, as those purchased at a travel agency. the amended rules require tour operators or sellers of travel to clearly explain, before the holidaymakers sign the contract, if the package is linked to goods. in addition, passengers must be informed of their rights and of their financial responsibility in the event of a problem. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by road, rail and inland waterway.
in writing. if in a service sector it is appropriate to introduce or maintain regulation at european level, this is certainly true for tourism and related sectors. the amendment tabled by the efdd proposes to reject the regulation, which i find unacceptable because it is contrary to the principles of consumer protection. tourism as a cross-border economic and social sector can only be regulated at international level.
in writing. ‒ tourism plays a central role in the european economy today. the european tourism sector, with its 1.8 million enterprises (mostly smes) and 5.2% of the workforce, is one of the engines of growth in the union. the european travel and tourism sector, including related areas, generates around 10% of the union's gdp. however, the tourism market has undergone significant development since the adoption of directive 90/314/eec. the internet has become an increasingly important intermediary in the provision of travel services. many of the services thus offered fall within the grey area of the law or simply outside the scope of directive 90/314/eec. this has necessitated the modernisation of directive 90/314/eec in order to adapt the legal framework to market developments, to filter out ambiguous provisions and to close loopholes. to this end, the commission has proposed the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council. the european parliament adopted its position on this proposal at first reading. in this context, the committee on the internal market and consumer protection proposed that the ep should support the council's position at first reading at second reading. i voted on the bill accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the council's motion for a resolution and therefore did not support the effd proposal which sought to reject it.
i of course agree and welcome the fact that roaming charges will be abolished from 2017 and that this is what the european parliament has decided. even the most hardline eu sceptics are obviously happy about this, and they agree that there are of course decisions that need to be made at european level to make life easier and better for the people of europe. what we do not agree with is what the rapporteur said in his comment that the european union is so wonderful because it was necessary to abolish roaming charges. we don't think that the increasingly dictatorial, increasingly centralized, and increasingly sovereign european union of nation states is necessary to abolish roaming charges. why can't we do this in a much looser bond or in a cooperative form, and many other similar decisions.
in writing. ‒ roaming charges have been used in recent years as a tax on the free movement of persons, as a kind of extra profit, and the european parliament has been calling for their abolition for years. the european parliament has helped citizens and businesses doing business across borders by introducing price caps since 2007, and now it will finally be possible for citizens of the european union to talk to each other at domestic rates from 15 june 2017 at the latest. the abolition of roaming charges, the elimination of the tax on the free movement of people, is the first step towards the creation of a common europe! today's decision by parliament also addresses the issue of net neutrality. in this context, operators will be obliged to treat all traffic equally and will be prohibited from blocking or slowing down the transmission speed of different services. in addition, it will be possible to sell special services that guarantee high-quality internet access, but not at the expense of the basic internet service. internet access gives smes a level playing field across the eu. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the council's position at first reading, which may lead to the abolition of roaming charges.

in writing. ‒ the european commission, with this legislative proposal, has confirmed the earlier decision of the european parliament of 17 june 2010 concerning the amendment of the 'anti-torture good regulation' ec/1236/2005. the european people's party welcomes the amendment proposal, as it is important to regulate and condition the trade in goods that can be used for torture and the execution of the death penalty. customs authorities should be able to take effective action against market actors who are in breach of the rules. at the same time, it is necessary to ensure that these restrictions do not impede legitimate trade in such 'dual-use' goods. it is very important to strike a balance between the legitimate interests of the operators concerned and the restrictions contained in the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on trade in certain goods liable to be used for capital punishment, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on combating torture contributes to the global eradication of the death penalty and torture by introducing a ban on equipment and related technical assistance which can be used exclusively for torture and the execution of the death penalty, and by establishing a licensing system for products which, if misused, are suitable for torture and execution. the review of the union's control over the trade in instruments of torture has long been timely. the commission now proposes to strengthen the control of instruments suitable for torture. i fully agree with the aims of the motion and therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution, which, following several years of preparation, will allow the european parliament to modernise the nearly decade-old legislation, as it has already stated. i consider it important that the commission proposal updates the annex containing the list of dual-use items and authorizations for placing on the market, in addition to the annex containing prohibited articles for exclusive use (only for torture or execution), taking into account new pharmaceutical devices and substances. the inclusion of the targeted end-user clause is an equally important means of control. in general, i am reassured that the modernisation of the legislation places the right emphasis on the aspects of effective control, regular review of inventories and procedures and more efficient exchange of information, all without unduly disrupting or obstructing the normal flow of trade. overall, i believe that my vote and this resolution of the european parliament have contributed to the european union's continued role as an international leader in global efforts to reduce the use of the death penalty and to eradicate the practice of torture.
in writing. ‒ eu-wide export controls are a tool of external trade policy that serve broader policy objectives. regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 on the fight against torture is a unique instrument that contributes to the protection of human rights by controlling products and activities that may be used in the context of the death penalty, torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the torture regulation contributes to the global abolition of the death penalty and torture, which is a long-standing eu objective. it shall contribute to the achievement of those objectives by combining prohibitions with the requirements for authorisation of trade in the listed products. it introduces a ban on equipment and related technical assistance intended solely for torture and the execution of the death penalty and a licensing system for products which, if misused, are suitable for torture and execution by lethal injection. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. following the luxleaks scandal, the european parliament, through this report, expresses its determination to not tolerate tax fraud and tax evasion and to stand up for a fair distribution of the tax burden between citizens and companies, with which i fully agree. in its previous resolution, the european parliament stressed that the union should take a leading role in the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens. one of the most effective ways of doing this is to improve the exchange of information, in particular on member states' conditional tax rulings.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to the council to amend directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, as amended by directive 2014/107/eu, with regard to the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. the proposal would add a new article to the current directive, which defines the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic sharing of information on certain types of cross-border conditional tax rulings and transfer pricing arrangements. this obligation extends to decisions issued in the 10 years preceding the entry into force of the proposed directive and still in force at the time of its entry into force. the council is required by the treaty on the functioning of the european union to consult the european parliament before taking a decision. in its report, parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs recommends that the commission's proposal be approved with a number of amendments. i supported the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report, which contributes to the smooth and continuous operation of the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation. i welcome the amendment to the report which states that the european parliament does not tolerate tax evasion and avoidance and that it is in favour of a fair distribution of the tax burden between citizens and businesses. i also agree with the amendment that targeted and effective sanctions should be developed for failure by member states to share conditional tax rulings and rulings or agreements on advance pricing arrangements. this is the only way to ensure transparency, which is a prerequisite for increasing legal certainty and tax fairness and stimulating the development of smes, investment and innovation. the commission notes that the contested tax ruling does not provide for any advantage to luxopco in the form of a tax credit for luxopco. we expect the automatic exchange of information on conditional tax rulings within the eu to put an end to illegitimate practices by individual member states and contribute to the establishment of a stable tax system.
in writing. ‒ the problem of crossborder tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition has emerged as a growing challenge in recent years and has become a priority in the european union and worldwide. in its resolution of 21 may 2013, the european parliament stressed the need for the union to take a leading role in the global discussions on the fight against tax fraud, tax evasion and tax havens, in particular by promoting the exchange of information. under the current legal framework, member states share very little information with each other regarding their conditional tax rulings. the draft directive adds a new article to the current directive, which defines the scope and conditions for the mandatory automatic sharing of information on certain types of cross-border conditional tax rulings and transfer pricing arrangements. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report analyses the antecedents and consequences of the epidemic in the three affected west african countries where the ebola virus has caused a severe humanitarian crisis. it is important to support the reform and structuring of the health systems of the three countries at both international and global levels. i do not think that the european union alone should solve this problem by allocating more money from the common budget to finance the health infrastructure, the training and education of staff and the salaries of these countries. at the same time, it is important to point out the heavy responsibility of the imf and the world bank, since the loan facilities to help these countries were an important condition for keeping health expenditure and structural development to a minimum. it is time for these organizations to provide real support for the construction of health systems. i supported the adoption of the report, also in view of the amendments adopted.
in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the largest ebola outbreak to date occurred in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. this report is based on experience gained during the crisis. the ebola crisis posed a major challenge to the three countries mentioned above, as they were ill-prepared to deal with the situation due to the shortcomings of their health and education systems. this was a huge challenge for the international community and for the europeans who were involved in the crisis. the report concludes that no further emergency aid is needed, but that the eu should continue to work to improve the organisation and resilience of health systems. it is necessary to lay down the conditions for a permanent european system with the appropriate physical and human resources for rapid response. the report highlights that investments in health promote economic development and are thus an important factor in poverty eradication. the report calls on member states to contribute to the creation of a universal health fund (uhc) and to support the marshall plan, which can give a powerful boost to the development of countries in need. the report also hopes that the european development fund will also support the health system of countries with fragile infrastructure with its investments. in accordance with the above objectives, and following the line of the people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the largest ebola crisis to date occurred in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. this report is based on experience gained during the crisis. the ebola crisis posed a major challenge to the three countries mentioned above, as they were ill-prepared to deal with the situation due to the shortcomings of their health and education systems. this was a huge challenge for the international community and for the europeans who were involved in the crisis. the document states that no further emergency aid is needed, but that the eu should work to improve the organisation and resilience of health systems in the future. it is necessary to lay down the conditions for a permanent european system with the material and human resources necessary for rapid response. the report highlights that investments in health promote economic development and can therefore be an important factor in poverty eradication. the document calls on member states to contribute to the creation of a so-called global health fund and to support the marshall plan, which can give a powerful boost to the development of countries in need. in accordance with the above objectives, and following the line of the people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. i supported the report, whose key elements are the inadequate response of the international community, the shocking effects of border closures and restrictions on the population, the ineffectiveness of monitoring and alert mechanisms, the slow and inadequate response after the final mobilisation of support, the complete lack of leadership by who, and the partial lack of research and development for medicines, diagnostics and vaccines. many of us have the impression that it's only because of providence that it hasn't become a global pandemic yet.
in writing. ‒ the development committee report summarises the lessons learned from the worst ebola outbreak in world history, which has devastated sierra leone, liberia and guinea since march 2014. it underlines that the european union, as the world's most important actor for development, has a special responsibility to promote the universal right of access to healthcare. it expects the union to act more vigorously than the other actors. it takes the view that the union should lead the way in research, innovation, the establishment of a framework for emergency tasks, the deployment of medical personnel, the establishment of an evacuation system and longer-term efforts in the field of development cooperation. it considers that for the post-pandemic period, the union should focus its efforts on two areas: development aid, including through investment in health infrastructure, and support for economic recovery in the three countries. i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ in march 2014, the largest ebola outbreak to date occurred in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. this report is based on experience gained during the crisis. the ebola crisis posed a major challenge to these three countries, which were ill-prepared to deal with the situation due to the shortcomings of their health and education systems. this was a huge challenge for the international community and for the europeans who were involved in the crisis. the report concludes that no further emergency aid is needed, but that the eu should continue to work to improve the organisation and resilience of health systems. it is necessary to lay down the conditions for a permanent european system with the appropriate physical and human resources for rapid response. the report highlights that investments in health promote economic development and are thus an important factor in poverty eradication. the report calls on member states to contribute to the creation of a universal health fund (uhc) and to support the marshall plan, which can give a powerful boost to the development of countries in need. the report also hopes that the european development fund will also support the health system of countries with fragile infrastructure with its investments. following the line of the people's party, and in accordance with the objectives set out above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ since march 2014, sierra leone, liberia and guinea have been hit by the worst ebola outbreak in world history. the cross-border nature of the virus has made it easier for it to spread from one country to another. the three countries in question are among the lowest on the undp list in terms of human development. the average life expectancy of the population is at most 60 years, schooling rarely exceeds three years, and about 80% of the citizens live in extreme poverty. partnerships between the european union and the crisis-hit area can only be effective if liberia, guinea and sierra leone are able to take their own development into their own hands as soon as possible. the multiple challenges posed by the ebola crisis will require a future review of the european development fund (edf) programming for these three countries. it should also be noted that the mid-term review of the mff will no longer allow the risk of structural under-financing of the european union's humanitarian operations to be ignored. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because it deals with the issues of emissions measurement fraud by vw in a clear and understandable way. the text emphasises the protection of consumers and the enforcement of consumer rights. the additional public claims which consumers are disadvantaged by fraud under the existing motor vehicle taxation legislation of the member states should be borne by the manufacturers and not by the consumers. it is important that the new real-world emission measurements, contrary to the commission's proposal, should not only cover nox but all air pollutants. in several cases, the member states' supervisory authorities have been criticised, but the commission's research institute has already provided the commission with documents unknown to parliament from 2011 to 2013, which prove that the commission was already aware of the fraud before the scandal broke out, but did not inform the member states and their supervisory authorities.
in writing. statistics show that air pollution causes more than 430 000 premature deaths in the eu each year, so support for the motion for a resolution should not be in doubt. it is well known that nitrogen oxide emitted by diesel cars is one of the main pollutants, causing lung cancer, asthma, and many respiratory diseases, among others. one third of the eu's urban population is exposed to pollution levels that seriously endanger their health, and transport remains the main cause of poor air quality and related health consequences in cities. two questions arise: why, despite the dangers that have been known for decades, do some governments support these cars with tax breaks, or why do they buy them for the masses of thinking people at the expense of their own health, the health of their loved ones, and the health of innocent bystanders? the vw scandal that has just erupted is just the tip of the iceberg.
in writing. ‒ a motion for a resolution on the subject was tabled by six political groups: verts/ale, ppe, ecr, s&d, gue/ngl and alde. the verts/ale, the epp, the s&d and alde reached an agreement, and i supported the compromise proposal they submitted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe we need to reduce the consequences of exhaust emission tests in the automotive industry. the current system does not measure the car's emissions under real driving conditions, and i therefore agree with the proposal to strengthen this test protocol. poor practices can contribute to increasing air pollution levels, and high levels are estimated to be responsible for some 400 000 premature deaths in the eu each year. the current emission test works by measuring vehicle emissions under artificial conditions by the manufacturer, a practice that can be abused. i should note that during the scandal, it was not established how many companies knowingly distorted the results. in order to address this situation, the proposal - and the socialists and democrats among them - is to introduce a real driving emissions (rde) test procedure from 2017. i think this is a way to avoid their loopholes. but in addition to the environmental and health aspects, i think it's important to ensure that we don't have to lay off workers because of one bad management decision. i think the scandal could provide a basis for companies to invest more resources in the development of electric cars, for example.
in writing. ‒ the serious lack of enforcement of eu internal market rules, which has been brought to light by the us authorities, is regrettable. the s&d motion for a resolution urges the commission and the member states to take preventive measures and to launch an immediate investigation into the manipulation devices used in vehicles on the union market, as well as the emission limits characterising the normal performance of vehicles and the co2 values (g/km) displayed in advertisements. i voted in favour of the s&d group's motion.

commission work programme, which we have been communicating to the commission. maybe it is because of the agreement that there is not much excitement in the house or in the press outside about this; if it were voted down or there were no agreement, there would be much more excitement. but it is very important that parliament and the commission work together on this because this parliament, or most of this parliament, was elected so that the message of how the european institutions work should be changed considerably; they should be more effective. i can shortlist why the epp or in what on behalf of the ppe group.– madam president, there is nothing untoward in the european parliament looking to establish a common system of elections for itself. every parliament in the world does so, and it adds to transparency and predictability if the systems by which citizens choose their representatives in the eu are broadly similar – similar if not identical, given that there are 28 different political traditions involved. the sensitive issue here is that of a threshold. should there be a minimum percentage of votes that a party list has to attract before it acquires representation? in some member states there is no support for this, but in the great majority it is accepted practice. the threshold helps to weed out frivolous contestants whose sole interest is in attracting attention. there is a counter-argument that the institution of the threshold restricts the political marketplace by creating too high a barrier to entry. the answer is a balance between the two: to have a threshold but not to set it too high. that is what this report tries to attain – setting a threshold but not making that threshold insurmountable. from every standpoint, this is the sensible, rational solution.

in writing. - my fellow members of parliament! the draft parliament position on the amendment of the air quality directive is problematic in many respects. on the one hand, the proposed methane emission limits would have a devastating impact on hungarian livestock farming. the hungarian government is doing everything it can to encourage the increase of domestic cattle and pigs, which has fortunately led to an increase in both stocks. the proposed limit which according to expert calculations would require a 30% reduction of current emissions! would meet one of the most important objectives of the hungarian agricultural administration, the objective of increasing livestock. the reduction of methane emissions is already regulated and is covered by the community's commitment to reduce greenhouse gases. there are also serious problems with ammonia emission limits. the 2030 and 2020 limits are already unrealistic, but the proposed 2025 mid-term limit is downright outrageous. for hungary, this would require a reduction of almost 40%! furthermore, unnecessary legislation would be introduced here, as fertilisation methods are already regulated by the provisions of the mutual accountability scheme and other environmental rules in particular the nitrate directive. this would complicate the situation of farmers and result in unenforceable requirements. i therefore demand that the methane emission limit values be removed from the draft and the ammonia emission limits be reduced to a reasonable level, otherwise i will not be able to support the proposal.
in writing. yesterday we agreed that the issue of car emissions controls should be urgently investigated and that vehicle tests based on real driving conditions should be introduced without delay. we have told european citizens that it is no longer possible to break the rules designed to protect their health and the environment with impunity. so the only logical next step today is to change the legislation that limits emissions, based on the report of the environmental protection committee. if we do, we could save more than 74,000 people a year across europe from premature death according to the latest expert calculations (http://www.eeb.org/?linkservid=9168dfdd-5056-b741-dba5b64c92b81f9d&showmeta=0&aa). diseases caused by air pollution have significant economic costs in the health sector and due to lost working hours. in order to prevent this, binding targets should be adopted in europe for 2020, 2025 and 2030. mandatory limits for ammonia, methane and mercury are also required in the directive. earlier this week, i was doing air quality measurements in the center of budapest with the air task force. the results confirmed the need to reduce air pollution immediately: the amount of pollutants increased to 14 times the normal urban level when a diesel car passed by. the impact assessment of the committee on the environment (interactions between eu air quality policy and climate and energy policy (oct 2014) http://www.europarl.europa.eu/regdata/etudes/stud/2014/528802/eprs_stu%282014%29528802_rev1_en.pdf) showed that it would not cost more to achieve stricter targets than the european commission's original proposal, while saving tens of thousands of lives.

in writing. ‒ the increase in the number of judges at the court of justice of the european union has been on the agenda for several years. the court first proposed this in 2011 as the increased number of cases could not be dealt with effectively enough. as no compromise with the european council was reached on this issue until the 2014 european parliament elections, the european parliament adopted its position at first reading on 15 april 2014. in september 2014, the italian presidency requested a new draft proposal from the court of justice, as the member states could not agree in the council on the system for the selection of judges, as the proposed total of 12 judges could not be appointed fairly on a national basis. the new proposal finally resulted in an agreement between the member states in the european council, which was adopted by the european parliament's juri committee responsible for this dossier in the so-called second reading. it provides for a gradual increase in the number of judges to a total of 56 and for a balance between the sexes and the nationalities. the decision also contains a review clause, which provides for an impact assessment to be carried out after five years to determine whether the proposed solution fulfils the expectations, namely the processing of the backlog in order to ensure a balanced, rapid and professional legal system. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ parliament has to reject the council's proposal for a number of reasons. first, because it completely ignores the interests of the taxpayers. at a time when the eu is imposing severe austerity measures to balance member states' budgets and is calling on them to reduce public spending, such a frivolous increase in spending is pointless and difficult for europeans to accept. the doubling of the number of judges would also entail an increase in the number of legal advisers and assistants, thus increasing the number of judges to more than 100. given that each agency costs more than eur 1 million per year to run, the total remuneration would increase eu structural expenditure by more than eur 20 million per year. the second reason why parliament rejects the proposal of the cjeu is the very dignity of the judiciary, that is, the reputation and respect due to the judiciary. the union may not appoint judges in the same way as it appoints political commissioners. the selection of judges should be based on their professional experience and legal expertise in order to guarantee the quality of the decision-making, while the selection should also be based on their good character, which ensures integrity, honesty and impartiality. in addition, gender equality should be given special attention at the appointment stage. it is incomprehensible that the judiciary in the union is primarily in the hands of men. the proportion of male and female judges in the courts of the union should be strictly the same.
in writing. ‒ the increase in the number of judges at the court of justice of the european union has been on the agenda for several years. the court first proposed this in 2011 as the increased number of cases could not be dealt with effectively enough. as no compromise with the european council was reached on this issue until the 2014 european parliament elections, the european parliament adopted its position at first reading on 15 april 2014. in september 2014, the italian presidency requested a new draft proposal from the court of justice, as the member states could not agree in the council on the system for the selection of judges, as the proposed total of 12 judges could not be appointed fairly on a national basis. the new proposal finally resulted in an agreement between the member states in the european council, which was adopted by the european parliament's committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection (juri) in what is known as the second reading. it provides for a gradual increase in the number of judges to a total of 56 and for a balance between the sexes and the nationalities. the decision also contains a review clause, which provides for an impact assessment to be carried out after five years to determine whether the proposed solution fulfils the expectations, namely the processing of the backlog in order to ensure a balanced, rapid and professional legal system.
in writing. ‒ in 2011, the court of justice of the european union (cjeu) initiated the appointment of 12 additional judges to the general court. the parliament accepted the request for 12 additional judges at first reading, but the council did not appoint any of them, since the number of judges to be appointed was significantly below the number of member states, each of which wanted to appoint its own judge. the euj therefore proposed in october 2014 to double the number of ad hoc judges. the council approved the proposal, but parliament's legal affairs committee argues in its report that the proposal should be rejected. it points out that this proposal does not reflect the actual needs arising from the overload of judges, but rather the council's inability to reach an agreement due to the self-interest of the member states. the rejection proposal is justified on the one hand by budgetary considerations (whereas the other institutions have agreed to a 5% reduction in staff and a budget of around 0.5%, the budget of the eeas would increase by more than eur 20 million per year) and on the other by the dignity of the judiciary and the reputation and respect due to the judiciary. in the latter respect, it states that judges should be selected on the basis of their professional experience and legal expertise and not on the basis of their national origin. i found the arguments of the legal affairs committee to be well founded and therefore supported the referral.

in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of the adoption of the legislative amendment incorporating the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean. the recommendations also make it clear that the european union is obliged to limit its sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. the reasoned measures taken to maintain them have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the agreement of the european parliament and the council to transpose into eu law the recommendation of the agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, which provides an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation to promote the sustainable and low-risk development, protection, rational management and best possible use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea. i consider it important to emphasise that, as regards fishing gear and fishing gear used for the collection of red coral, the co-legislators agree that the use of underwater remotely controlled vehicles for the monitoring and searching of red coral in the waters under the jurisdiction of the member states should continue to be allowed, provided that such vehicles are not equipped with movable arms or any other accessories suitable for the cutting and collection of red coral.
in writing. ‒ since the council's position at first reading is the same as that agreed in the trilogue, the rapporteur has convinced the committee to accept it without further amendments.
in writing. ‒ the general hungarian position on gmos is well known. hungary has enshrined its gmo-free status in its basic law and has accordingly played an active role in the negotiations on the proposal to restrict public production. the new commission proposal before us is in line with hungary's gmo-free policy, as it would allow member states to ban the use of food and feed containing gmos on their territory. the commission's proposal should therefore not be rejected, despite its obvious errors and shortcomings, but negotiations should be continued in a constructive spirit. the cooperative approach was also the basis for the introduction of the joint production ban legislation, and this approach helped the parties through the difficult stages of the legislative process, which lasted for 5 years. if we don't give this proposal a chance to be debated, we may miss an opportunity that will not be followed by another. on the basis of all this, i did not support the report of mr la via to reject the proposal.

in writing. ‒ i am dissatisfied with the european commission's stance on the current gmo issue. the panel has put on the table a proposal that is unacceptable from all points of view, including the internal market, the feed supply and international trade. that's why i couldn't support this proposal, even though it's a hot topic. the european union now depends on imports for more than 70% of its feed, and last year's figures showed that 30 million tonnes of gm feed were being imported into the union each year. this raises serious public safety and health concerns. the response should not be an unenforceable and illegal legislative proposal. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu. in the meantime, we must work hard to reduce the eu's dependence on feed. a good example of this is the national speech programme launched by the hungarian government, which has been successful.
in writing. ‒ i take seriously the concerns raised in the report that member states should be able to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after the products have been authorised. in my view, such measures should in any event be compatible with both the internal market and the international obligations of the union. in this context, the rapporteur shares the serious concern expressed by the commission about the far-reaching implications of the proposal for the functioning of the internal market for food and feed and for the competitiveness of the union's agriculture. furthermore, i believe that the proposal is almost impossible to implement, as there are no longer any border controls within the eu agricultural sector. the reintroduction of such controls between member states would reverse the economic results achieved by the european customs union and the internal market. it is also unclear how member states with opt-outs would in practice ensure compliance with such measures in their territory.

in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the european commission proposed a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. the belgian chamber of deputies, the spanish parliament, the dutch house of representatives and the austrian federal council consider that the draft law is incompatible with the principle of subsidiarity. the report by parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety points out that the proposal could seriously jeopardise livestock farming and have a negative impact on eu agriculture. moreover, it explains that the proposal is almost unfeasible as there are no longer any border controls within the eu agricultural sector. in view of the above, it recommended that parliament reject the commission proposal. i voted in accordance with the recommendation of the parliamentary committee.
in writing. ‒ the issue of genetically modified (gm) food and feed is dividing eu decision-makers and a large part of the population is outright opposed to these products. parliament, the council and the commission have long been trying to find a way to treat these products under common eu rules without hindering scientific progress. the commission's present proposal, however, did not deal with the matter properly, which is why i voted in favour of the commission withdrawing the proposal and drawing up a new one. i believe that a short-term solution is for member states to decide whether to allow or prohibit the marketing of gm products. but it also requires a debate with the participation of society, based on analysis, to find a solution. we need to take into account global population growth, changes in consumption patterns, our dependence on imported protein, the effects of gm feed and the fact that the free movement of products within the eu single market cannot be restricted. i also see a strict labelling system as one possible solution if it is introduced at a later stage.
in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the commission presented, together with the communication on the review of decision-making procedures for genetically modified organisms, a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. i voted in favour of the report on this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the proposed definitions are far from satisfactory, do not create legal certainty and ultimately do not clarify the scope and definition of novel foods, which was one of the main objectives of the commission's new proposal. while i welcome the commission's intention to develop an extended concept for the definition of novel foods covering all types of food innovation, the elimination of categories has raised serious concerns. while all the food industry actors concerned agreed that the new definition was not workable, there was already a difference of opinion on what should replace it. in recognition of the scientific and technical progress in the food industry and the need to improve legal certainty, i believe that the most sensible step would be to introduce new categories of novel foods in a modern form in order to make the novel food provision future-proof against unexpected industrial developments. i also consider it important that the regulation is adapted to technical progress and new types of products entering the union market.
in writing. ‒ the rules on novel foods were laid down in regulation (ec) no 258/97 of the european parliament and of the council, which entered into force on 5 may 1997, and in commission regulation (ec) no 1852/2001 of 20 september 2001. the protection of human health and the interests of consumers require that a novel food or food ingredient be authorised before it is placed on the market. however, fundamental scientific and technical developments in the food industry have rendered the definition of novel foods in regulation (ec) no 258/97 obsolete and therefore it needs to be reviewed. the european commission proposed to modernise the regulation back in 2008, but the conciliation committee agreement was thwarted by the issue of the placing on the market of food derived from cloned animals. the commission therefore made a new proposal in december 2013 which includes the issues on which there was previously agreement, but does not address the issue of cloning the commission made separate proposals on the latter. parliament, in its report to the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, tabled more than 100 amendments to the proposal, but recommended the proposal to parliament for adoption. i voted on the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i consider the field of new foodstuffs to be an important area of innovation. these include chia seeds, flavonoids from licorice root, crab fragrance, but also products containing insects, nanomaterials, algae or certain dyes. the proposal aims to protect public health, food safety and to strengthen the functioning of the internal food market in relation to new products, while supporting the innovative food sector. i believe that only products that do not pose a moral, environmental or health risk should be authorised for human or animal consumption. this is why we need eu-wide regulation, plus tools such as labelling, consumer information or the introduction of an information campaign. the report takes steps towards the development of rules at eu level in the field of safety testing and authorisation of novel foods. while i supported most of the amendments, i abstained from the final vote because key points that were important to me were not included in the final text, such as the issues of cloning and nanomaterials.
in writing. ‒ the directive on the control of certain atmospheric pollutants is an important step towards reducing the adverse effects of air pollution on human health and improving air quality in europe. the achievement of the targets requires proportionate and realistic emission limit values, which also take into account national strategies. the adoption of legislation which ignores this principle would have a very bad impact not only on hungary's agriculture but on that of the whole union. an unrealistic methane emission reduction limit would undermine one of the hungarian government's key objectives, namely a significant increase in livestock numbers. methane is a greenhouse gas, so there's already a climate reduction obligation. the same applies to ammonia, where fertilisation methods are already regulated by the provisions of the cross compliance system, in particular the nitrates directive. this would complicate the situation of farmers and result in unenforceable requirements. no concrete reduction target for 2030 can be set at this time, as air pollution is affected by a number of variable factors and there is no linear reduction pathway. finally, it should be noted that the european commission only planned to tighten the thresholds after 2020, given that many member states are still struggling to meet the previous targets. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of all the amendments tabled by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection to the report adopted by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection, which seek to abolish methane and to make fundamental changes to the ammonia standards.

in writing. ‒ fact-based policymaking should be a cornerstone of eu law. although work is being done across the union to reduce air pollution, many member states are not complying with the standards adopted. in addition, the union is still far from meeting its long-term objective of the limit values for pollutants proposed in the who 2005 air quality guidelines. poor air quality contributes to premature death, sickness absence from work, high health costs, reduced productivity, lost yields and deterioration of buildings. in line with the rapporteur, i support the commission's newfound commitment to smarter, more reasonable regulation and to reducing the administrative burden on businesses and member states. it should also be emphasised that the ceilings for the target dates set out in the report should be set in such a way as to be realistic, proportionate and achievable, based on facts and not affecting any sector disproportionately.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the reduction of national emissions of certain atmospheric pollutants and amending directive 2003/35/ec. the commission proposal repeals and replaces the current directive on national emission limit values and sets new limit values for emissions of volatile organic compounds other than sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia and methane for 2020 and 2030 respectively, and extends the scope of the directive to particulate matter (pm2,5) from 2020 and methane from 2030. parliament, in its report to the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, tabled 118 amendments to the proposal, but recommended the proposal to parliament for adoption. i voted on the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that air pollution is a real problem and the draft proposes real solutions to create cleaner air. high levels of air pollution are estimated to be responsible for some 400 000 premature deaths in the eu each year, while the indirect harmful effects are unpredictable. i believe that the rate of emission of pollutants should be radically reduced. the commission is also proposing to introduce a new directive on the emission of pollutants from transport by road. the setting of the 2020 and 2030 commitments for so2, nox, nmvoc and ammonia (nh3), as well as fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4) for new member states is a major responsibility, but in my view also an opportunity. member states should set up a national air pollution control programme and monitor it every two years, but this could save hundreds of thousands of lives. they can also save money that they can easily spend on developing renewable, environmentally friendly technologies.
in writing. ‒ in the three years since the european citizens' initiative was set up as a new institution under the lisbon treaty, it has achieved a remarkable success: three out of 51 initiatives have met expectations 1 million signatures of support from 7 member states. the schöpflin report identifies the reasons for this procedural failure and makes suggestions, including better communication of the tool, creation of more user-friendly interfaces, simpler data requests, budget support, direct advice, and facilitating digital citizen participation, facilitating the participation of millions of citizens in an eu-wide initiative by building a digital citizenship of the union. the rapporteur emphasises the need to raise awareness of the initiative to a wider audience, as this tool is designed to directly involve citizens in european institutional decision-making. the report seeks to confirm this connection. i agreed with the report and called on the commission to review its existing rules of procedure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it criticises the current shortcomings of the legal institution of the european citizens' initiative, based on experience, and also contains a number of proposals for changes to make the system more effective, to give european citizens a genuine direct democratic experience and to produce concrete european legislation. for my part, i regard the european citizens' initiative as a potentially very important institution of european direct democracy, whose results so far have been disappointing, partly because of the lack of regulation, partly because of the lack of cooperation between member states, partly because of the restrictive approach of the commission to the reception of initiatives. i agree with the report that the possible direction of improvement is not to amend the treaty but to apply the current rules more flexibly, more closely to citizens and users, and to improve communication between the commission and the governments of the member states. to achieve this, the report provides a number of useful elements, which the european parliament will need to monitor in the future. in considering the importance of this issue, it was also important for me, as a hungarian representative, to note that in my country the government is currently pursuing a policy aimed at establishing direct democracy and making the institution of the referendum impossible; i hope that the better functioning of the european citizens' initiative will provide a positive european example that will help to prevent this aspiration.

in writing. ‒ in december 2012, the european council invited the commission to present its vision for a new strategy for the adriatic and ionian sea (eusair) before the end of 2014, and the commission presented its draft strategy accordingly on 17 june 2014. eusair is the third eu macro-regional strategy to build on the experience of the baltic and danube strategies. the adriatic and ionian region is home to over 70 million people and covers eight countries, including four eu member states (croatia, greece, italy, slovenia), three candidate countries (albania, montenegro, serbia) and bosnia and herzegovina as a potential candidate country. i voted in favour of the draft report in the plenary vote, as eusair provides a good opportunity for the countries of the region to promote sustainable development. the strategy's pillars (blue growth, development of the region's infrastructure links, environmental protection, sustainable and competitive tourism) and other priorities (eu integration of the western balkan countries, ensuring coherence between the three eu macro-regional strategies and national strategic projects) promote economic development and job creation. however, i think it is important to emphasise that for each macro-regional strategy an overall assessment of the results is needed. it is necessary to ensure that the strategies represent a genuine european added value and have a real, tangible positive impact in the region concerned.

in writing. ‒ in december 2012, the european council invited the commission to present a new european union strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair) by the end of 2014. the commission presented eusair on 17 june 2014. eusair is the third eu macro-regional policy after the eu strategies for the baltic sea region and the danube basin region. the strategy is based on cooperation within the region, notably the adriatic and ionian initiative launched in 2000 with the signing of the ancona declaration and the creation in 2006 of the adriatic and ionian euroregion, bringing together 26 regional and local authorities from the seven participating countries. eusair covers eight countries, and the region is home to over 70 million people. according to the motion for a resolution tabled by parliament's committee on regional development, eusair offers a unique opportunity for the region to overcome past economic and political problems through cooperation, guided by the commission, and to pursue prosperity and sustainable development. it shows that the region has enormous potential, which can only be exploited through the joint and coordinated efforts of all the countries in the region, with a significant involvement of local and regional authorities. it considers that eusair will prove to be of historic importance both for the participating countries and for the union as a whole.

in writing. ‒ the report makes concrete proposals for the review of cohesion policy and the eu 2020 strategy, assesses their current functioning and identifies future challenges. it also stresses the importance of a close link between the two: eu 2020 serves as a strategic framework for the design and programming of the european structural and investment funds for the period 2014-2020. the report highlights, in some points, certain elements of the strategy and cohesion policy, and makes recommendations, criticisms and suggestions to the commission, in part to provide guidance for the commission's review of the eu 2020 strategy before the end of 2015. although the report contains some positive ideas (positive emphasis on the role of cohesion policy as one of the main instruments to promote investment, encouragement of multi-level governance with the involvement of local and regional authorities), i did not support its adoption. cohesion policy is the most important tool for overcoming regional disparities. as a peripheral country, we would be lucky if the eu sought to address the problems of the region by adapting the cohesion policy instruments to the specific needs of the region as best as possible. instead, the purple fog aligns cohesion policy with the eu 2020 'imperial' objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and the review of the europe 2020 strategy at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. the report emphasises the crucial role of cohesion policy in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. cohesion policy is the only eu policy that contributes to all three europe 2020 objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth through its 11 thematic objectives, which are aligned with the five europe 2020 headline targets. the role of cohesion policy in the 2008 crisis, in particular the fact that it was able to continue to finance investments in the face of a sharp reduction in public funding, confirms the long-term relevance of the policy and demonstrates its resilience to external influences. given that the implementation of the 2014-2020 cycle has only just begun, it would not be effective to make substantial changes to cohesion policy in the europe 2020 strategy review this year or in the mff review next year. i agree with the rapporteur that the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy should be limited and focus on possible ways of better implementation without further increasing the administrative burden.

in writing. ‒ the proposal contains recommendations for article 23 of the regulation on the european structural and investment funds. under article 23, the commission may request a member state to review its partnership agreement or any of its programmes and, if the member state in the commission's view does not take effective action, may propose to the council that it suspend all or part of the payments made for the programmes or priorities concerned. parliament shall endeavour to ensure that such measures are taken only in the most justified cases and in the most balanced manner possible. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. it also notes that in certain areas it considers the suspension of aid to be particularly counterproductive. the report also recommends that parliament be involved in the adoption of a decision or proposal on the eve of a possible rescheduling or suspension. on these grounds, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the european structural and investment funds and good economic governance: guidelines for the implementation of article 23 of the common provisions regulation during the plenary vote in strasbourg. article 23 is probably the most debated part of the common provisions regulation. the european parliament's report recommended that all provisions on the macroeconomic conditionality be deleted from the text, but the macroeconomic conditionality was nevertheless included in the final text of the common provisions. the josé blanco lópez report only concerns the first part of article 23 (optional reprogramming, optional suspension of payments from the structural and investment funds). the european commission also recognises that reprogramming should be strictly limited to the minimum necessary and that the application of article 23 should take into account the specific economic and social situation of the member state. the application of the macroeconomic conditionality should be justified and advantageous for the achievement of the cohesion policy objectives for the region or regions concerned. it is unacceptable that local and regional authorities should be penalised by reprogramming or suspending funds because the macroeconomic conditions are not met at other levels of administration. the european parliament should play an active role in monitoring the application of article 23 on common provisions, which requires a constant, reliable flow of information between all actors concerned and full transparency at all stages of the process of possible application.

in writing.– we must not forget that our european external borders are being crossed daily by hundreds of thousands of travellers such as tourists and business people, who arrive at the proper border crossings with the appropriate documents. they are growing in number and they are a precious resource to our member states. free movement of persons is one of the most important achievements of the european union since its foundation. the absence of internal borders makes it therefore crucially important that our common external borders are controlled reliably and consistently. in order to better manage the growing flow of travellers, we need to modernise the european border control system, by increasing its efficiency and effectiveness. the result should be smooth and easy travel for the majority of third country travellers who cross the european borders yearly on one side, and an impossible mission for those who abuse free movement, such as organised crime and terrorist organisations, on the other side. i trust that the establishment of an efficient and cost effective integrated management system for external borders will serve the safety of our citizens and support the work of our law enforcement authorities.
the rapporteur. officer, my colleagues. i am pleased that, just one year after the start of the legislative process, the european parliament will hold a final vote on the new cepol regulation tomorrow. i would like to thank all the shadow rapporteurs for the smooth running of the process, in particular mrs flasikova-benova, whose support and cooperation were of great help during the negotiations. i also have great appreciation for the work of the latvian presidency, with special thanks to mrs indra bule, whose constructive approach and proactive approach helped the trilateral negotiations to proceed. we all know that the union's internal security has been facing serious challenges in recent times and we can expect similar challenges in the future. this is why we urgently need properly trained law enforcement agencies, law enforcement agencies that are able to respond quickly and effectively at a pan-european level to challenges such as cross-border crime, cybercrime, terrorism. we need policemen who can act with full professionalism in today's migration crisis. cepol can thus serve as a tool to consolidate a culture of professionalism among professional police officers, and to strengthen mutual trust and cross-border cooperation between member states. it can contribute to the creation of a genuine european policing culture based on respect for fundamental rights and european values. we in parliament therefore believe that a modernised, efficient, autonomous and adequately staffed cepol agency is essential. in the negotiations with the co-legislators, it remained important that cepol's basic structure its reliance on and close cooperation with the national police academies remain unchanged. cepol had to be given the powers and mandate required by the treaties as soon as possible. the governance structure of cepol has been made operational, taking into account the proposals made during the debate on the new europol regulatory framework. we believe that with this new regulation we have created the conditions for cepol to contribute to building a genuine european culture of law enforcement. this new regulation, which is about to be voted on, will modernise cepol's legal basis. it aligns it with the amendment to the treaty of lisbon and entrusts cepol with the implementation of the principles of the law enforcement and police training programme proposed by the commission in march 2013. this should include an assessment of the strategic training needs at union level, the accreditation of training, the sharing of common curricula, the sharing of positive examples and the identification of the minimum knowledge to be included in the curriculum of each police academy. cepol should therefore be able to provide training and trainers at union level. in recent years, cepol has been seen as a network. a network is not a legal entity and cannot be held accountable. this is precisely why cepol needed to become a union agency with clear mandates, tasks, responsibilities and, most importantly, accountability. as regards the use of taxpayers' money, cepol has come a long way to prove its cost-effectiveness. you've increased your training enrollment fivefold, and the demand for your training is growing, and it's going to be worth adjusting your budget to meet that. we will therefore continue to work to ensure adequate resources, which are a necessary precondition for a well-functioning eu agency, and to eliminate overlaps with other eu institutions. that's why i'm asking for your support in voting for this institution tomorrow.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution adopted today sets out recommendations for the next european council on employment policy to address long-term unemployment. the novelty of the decision is that the union has finally recognised the need to address the situation of the nearly 12 million long-term unemployed european citizens, whose numbers and proportions have increased significantly in recent years, particularly as a result of the financial and sovereign debt crisis, and which also vary widely across member states. it is therefore particularly important that the decision adopted today includes the need to take account of local and regional conditions in the fight against longterm unemployment, while respecting the current treaties. the decision also names specific eu member states where the employment crisis is particularly acute: portugal, slovakia, croatia, spain and greece. hungary in contrast has been able to increase employment significantly in recent years and to keep the number of longterm jobseekers below the eu average. this puts hungary between germany and the czech republic in the european ranking, which is a significant achievement. however, there is still a lot to do, and we need to keep working and remain open to all possibilities and working solutions.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the commission's initiative to propose a council recommendation on the integration of the longterm unemployed into the labour market and would like to stress that the earlier submission of the proposal and its adoption by the council could have partly prevented the current level of longterm unemployment. the report shares my concern that a council recommendation may not be sufficient to remedy the situation of the longterm unemployed quickly and urges the member states to achieve results as soon as possible. in particular, i support the three main elements of the proposal, namely the extension of the registration of the permanently unemployed with an employment service, with a view to full registration, the assessment of the individual skills, needs and job preferences of the permanently unemployed before reaching 18 months of unemployment, and the provision of a personalised, balanced and comprehensible labour market integration agreement between the permanently unemployed and the services concerned at the latest at the age of 18 months of unemployment.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament resolution adopted today sets out recommendations for the next european council on employment policy to address long-term unemployment. the novelty of the decision is that the union has finally recognised the need to address the situation of the nearly 12 million long-term unemployed european citizens, whose numbers and proportions have increased significantly in recent years, particularly as a result of the financial and sovereign debt crisis, and which also vary widely across member states. it is therefore particularly important that the decision adopted today includes the need to take account of local and regional conditions in the fight against longterm unemployment, while respecting the current treaties. the decision also names specific eu member states where the employment crisis is particularly acute: portugal, slovakia, croatia, spain and greece. hungary in contrast has been able to increase employment significantly in recent years and to keep the number of longterm jobseekers below the eu average, placing hungary between germany and the czech republic in european rankings, which is a significant achievement. at the same time, we must not stand back: we must continue to work and remain open to all possibilities and to all solutions that work.
in writing. ‒ the committee on employment and social affairs, in its proposal for a parliamentary resolution, welcomes the commission's initiative, but is concerned that a council recommendation will not be enough to remedy the situation of the long-term unemployed quickly, and therefore urges the member states to achieve results as soon as possible. it also supports the three main elements of the proposal, namely (1) the extension of the registration of the permanently unemployed with a view to a comprehensive registration, (2) the assessment of the individual skills, needs and job preferences of the permanently unemployed before reaching 18 months of unemployment, and (3) the provision of a personalised, balanced and understandable labour market integration agreement between the permanently unemployed and the services concerned at the latest after reaching 18 months of unemployment. however, it points out that this approach cannot exclude non-state actors, such as ngos working with the long-term unemployed, from the process. stresses, finally, that all the long-term unemployed should be helped, not just those who have been unemployed for at least 18 months, and considers it particularly important that member states' policies on short-term (less than 12 months) unemployment and youth unemployment (including the youth guarantee) should be fully integrated into policies to tackle long-term unemployment.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion because it aims to create a better european union. the economic crisis and its consequences have led to a doubling of the number of the permanently unemployed since 2007 and an eu-wide solution is needed to address this situation. i believe that there is a need for substantive action, reliable statistics and controls in this area. for example, hungary should not include in its employment data those who have jobs abroad, or count them as a statistical unit even if they have worked only one hour in a month. there should be no public service program that provides a wage of 150 euros a month for modern slavery. instead, i propose that governments adopt the recommendations of the motion, including the development of specific on-the-job training programmes and business development and investment plans that create sustainable and quality jobs for the long-term unemployed. this is because long-term unemployment often leads to poverty, inequality and social exclusion, and disproportionately affects those at risk of being disadvantaged in the labour market.

in writing. ‒ agrees with the rapporteur that the sector of remotely piloted aircraft systems urgently needs european and global regulation to enable the cross-border development of such systems and that a clear european legal framework is needed to ensure investment in a competitive european remotely piloted aircraft system sector and to develop the sector; stresses that, in the absence of any prior action, there is a risk that the full economic potential and benefits of remotely piloted aircraft systems will not be exploited. i accept and fully support the following five principles for the future development of remotely piloted aircraft systems set out in the riga declaration: remotely piloted aircraft systems should be treated as new types of aircraft and be subject to proportionate rules based on the risks of their operations; eu rules for the safe provision of services with remotely piloted aircraft systems should be established to allow for sectoral investment; technology and specifications for the full integration of remotely piloted aircraft systems into european airspace should be developed; social acceptance is key to the expansion of services provided with remotely piloted aircraft systems and operators of remotely piloted aircraft systems should be responsible for the use of these systems.

in writing. ‒ the report highlights that tourism is a key growth area of the european economy, accounting for 10% of eu gdp, including tourism-related sectors, and directly employing 13 million people, equivalent to at least 12% of eu jobs. it points out that europe is the world's number one tourist destination with a share of 52%; statistics show that the majority of eu citizens' trips abroad are still within the eu and forecasts show that the number of foreign tourists arriving in the eu will increase by 140 million per year by 2025. tourism is therefore a major socioeconomic activity in the eu, with a wide-ranging impact on economic growth, employment and social development, and can therefore play a crucial role in addressing the current economic and employment crisis. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the existing aid to the following areas: i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ tourism is almost the only sector that has performed well across europe during and after the crisis, contributing to the national economic performance of the countries concerned. two thirds of eu citizens spend their holidays in one of the eu member states, and the eu market generates around 50% of world tourism revenue. tourism plays a major role in the european union and the world economy, accounting for nine per cent of global gdp and five per cent of the european community's gdp, according to some estimates. according to surveys, tourism provides almost 20 million european jobs, or 4% of the employment rate in the european member states. the tourism sector therefore needs more attention. the de monte report is a great piece of work, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ given that the tragedies of air france flight af447 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 have highlighted the need to put in place new systems to ensure that aircraft involved in public air transport can be located at all times, even in remote locations, and that these global air traffic services control systems facilitate the determination of the position of aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident, i support the commission's action to rapidly develop a global performance-based system for tracking air traffic, which will enable air navigation service providers to determine the current position of aircraft engaged in public transport, even in remote locations. i would like to emphasise that this system must remain operational in the event of a normal on-board power failure and must not offer the possibility of switching off the system in flight. i believe that the development of such a system should be achieved through close cooperation between all stakeholders (e.g. industry, airlines, air navigation service providers, air safety and rescue services, safety investigation authorities and international organisations).
in writing. ‒ the airplane accidents of recent years have demonstrated the need for improvement in flight control systems. this development can be achieved by a satellite technology that can track aircraft anywhere on earth and send immediate alerts to the authorities of any problems. the global system will improve the safety of civil aviation and increase the amount of data available for investigations, which will explain the circumstances of the accident and thus prevent further accidents. as a member of the fidesz delegation, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the draft parliament resolution tabled by the committee on transport and tourism proposes that parliament should support commission action to rapidly develop a global performance-based system for the monitoring of air traffic, which would enable air navigation service providers to determine the current position of aircraft engaged in public transport. it emphasises that this system must remain operational in the event of a failure of the normal on-board power supply and must not offer the possibility of switching off the system in flight. lastly, it proposes to invite the commission to take the necessary steps to support the future development of a global air traffic monitoring satellite system by designating the radio frequency bands in view of the next world radiocommunication conference in geneva in november 2015. i supported the motion.

mr president, this is the fourth time that this parliament has dealt with what is essentially a single instrument for the coordination of economic policies in the european union. and this is where we really see the value of this new tool, because it gives us the opportunity to interpret, in a unified structure, the progress or the regression of the economic policies of different countries. obviously, in the case of budget, growth, employment, i.e. competition policies, comparisons are necessary, because otherwise we will never understand why there is a difference of almost 20 times in european wages, depending on which corner of europe we look at, and also in the case of taxation, where the problems arise. i accept, i believe that tax policy is a very important tool in the hands of any government. however, there may be cases, such as food, where it is only in the interests of the people, of the european citizens, that harmonized policies are worth pursuing. now, the experience of this time, and this is a new phenomenon in relation to the progress that has been made, is that the european commission, by restructuring, by restructuring the logic of the european semester, is almost crowding out the european parliament. it leaves far less time for the european parliament to do its job, and that is what we have to say - it gives european citizens less say. the five presidents' report also stressed the need for more democracy, and believe me, believe me, mr. commissioner, democracy has never hurt, never hurt economic development.
