in writing. in my view, the key to solving the refugee and migration crisis is to address emerging problems where they arise or as close as possible to where they arise. this is indicated by the fact that the european union has pledged a total of €5.6 billion in financial support for humanitarian purposes in recent weeks, as well as a fund for africa and syria, half of which (€2.8 billion) is from the eu budget and the other half from eu28 contributions. as at 30 october 2015, eur 2,23 billion was still missing from the eur 2,8 billion eu28 contribution pledged by heads of state or government at a summit. besides money, human and technical assistance are far below the required level. the commission's proposal is to set up a european network of national experts to assess the impact of the proposed directive on the environment. i therefore consider it extremely important that member states speed up their contributions to the fund, because every day that passes brings more groups of migrants on the move.
in writing. in 2015, europe faced the most severe migratory pressure in its recent history. the scale and nature of the problem require a common european solution to address the root causes of migration with global action. the european union has pledged a total of €5.6 billion in financial support for humanitarian purposes in recent weeks, as well as a fund for africa and syria, half of which (€2.8 billion) comes from the eu budget and the other half from eu28 contributions. in line with its commitment to help the most vulnerable communities where they live, hungary has offered, among other commitments, a contribution to the community funds of eur 3.4 million. this amount is similar to the contribution of countries of our region with similar capacity. we support our country's efforts to protect europe's borders and to address the conflicts that fuel the wave of immigration where they originate. only global and eu-wide action can effectively tackle the root causes of migration.
in writing.– the ppe has always advocated a holistic approach to migration. the crisis remains serious and the solution to end it is complex by nature. together with managing the migratory flows and protecting our external borders, we must tackle the root causes of migration. the number of africans trying to reach europe over the mediterranean is just the tip of an iceberg compared to the number of displaced people in africa. according to the un refugee agency unhcr, crises in countries like somalia, congo, nigeria, south sudan and the central african republic have forced 15 million people out of their homes. therefore i welcome the initiative of creating the two trust funds which through humanitarian and development aid should bring back stability, support resilience in syria and africa, and help refugees return to their homes. setting up these trust funds is a positive action, and we must make sure that the money will be used in the most efficient way. the support to refugees must be given as close as possible to the country of origin and special attention must be given to children, who are the main victims, deprived of a safe environment, schooling and often even food.
in writing. with the concept of financing funds for syria and africa, the european union is taking another step towards a community solution. hungary has tried to withdraw from previous initiatives that build solidarity between the eu and its member states, but instead the government has turned the country around and developed a refugee policy that is based on systematic rejection of asylum applications, accelerated procedures that violate fundamental human rights in many respects and a virtual disregard for the eu's core values. the european commission has recently written to express its concerns and questions about the hungarian legislation and the undermining of the eu's fundamental values, but the government has since done nothing more than reject the proposal for a quota system as a common solution by a parliamentary decision. it is worrying that while the government communicates its use of eu funds - which are otherwise often desperately corrupt - as its own success, it is using populist language to vilify the union in its handling of the refugee crisis. the hungarian government has so far shown little sign of cooperation, which is also a core value of the eu. despite the fact that the prime minister has already mentioned on several occasions that he does not consider the idea of a financial contribution to be diabolical in the case of turkey, he himself proposed it , on the basis of what has been said, one can only be afraid to trust that this initiative will not be swept off the table in principle.
in writing. i can personally support the commission's proposal to finance two separate funds for assistance to syria and the african countries concerned in response to migration-related burdens. it is, of course, a welcome aspect that this involves the use of resources outside the approved budgetary framework, which the member states offer to support these regions in addition to their other efforts at the expense of the development fund and other community budgetary chapters. at the same time, i consider it a priority that refugees from war-torn syria and from certain african countries subject to persistent migratory pressure are the most serious political and economic challenge facing the european union today, which must be addressed primarily in the sending countries. i believe that this is also in the european interest and that these two funds can make a significant contribution to creating the necessary conditions. i hope that the seriousness of the situation and the support of the ep will encourage the individual member states to replenish the two funds as soon as possible, while in this context i can only express my regret that my own government is so uncooperative in the joint eu response to the refugee crisis.

in writing. ‒ the report is about the creation of a programme for interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2). as such, it is a continuation of the isa programme, which provides public services in eu member states with easy access to each other's databases and requires only one digitisation of key information. the isa programme covered the period 2010 to 2015 and isa2 covered the period 2016 to 2020, and eur 131 million was approved for this purpose. interoperability means matching systems that cooperate in terms of access to, retrieval and processing of each other's databases. as an example of the content of the programme, directive 2012/17/eu of the european parliament and of the council in the area of company law requires that the central registers, commercial registers and companies registers of the member states be mutually accessible through a central platform. by linking business registers, the information contained therein is made accessible across borders, thereby allowing access to data on businesses at union level for both businesses and citizens, which enhances legal certainty in the business environment in the union. on these grounds, i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the commitment of member states is key to the rapid emergence of an interoperable e-society in the union and the involvement of public administrations in promoting the use of online procedures. furthermore, some adjustments to european administrations may be necessary in addition to the support provided by member states in order to create a more efficient, simpler and user-friendly egovernment. efficient online public services are key to enhancing business and citizens' trust in digital services. it is therefore important that the policy on interoperability and its possible uses is coordinated at union level in the most efficient and flexible way possible for the end-user. in order to eliminate fragmentation of the interoperability environment in the union, it is necessary to promote a common interpretation of interoperability accepted across the union and a comprehensive approach to interoperability solutions. the report points in that direction, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the first agreement reached between the ep and the council has provided a satisfactory solution to all the issues raised in the parliament's position, which i support. the text provides a good basis for overcoming electronic barriers between member states' administrations, ensuring cross-border interoperability, exploiting the opportunities offered by new technologies, creating an open and flexible environment to accommodate new challenges and opportunities, and introducing solutions to help smes. for these reasons, in accordance with the line of the european people's party, i voted in favour of adopting the text of the first lomé convention.
in writing. ‒ the isa programme will end on 31 december 2015 and will be replaced by the isa2 framework programme for 2016-2020. the objectives of isa2 are to develop a comprehensive approach to interoperability, to facilitate efficient and effective electronic communications across borders and sectors between european public administrations and bodies, and between businesses and citizens, and to explore, develop and operate interoperability solutions to support the implementation of union policies and activities. the visa information system, the second generation of the schengen information system, the european fingerprint identification system and the european e-justice portal are excellent examples of enhanced interoperability between member states. coordination at european level also plays an important role in the sharing and dissemination of best practice. as a member of the hungarian delegation to the people's party, i supported the new framework programme isa2 in accordance with the people's party proposal.
in writing. ‒ the inter-governmental data exchange programme has been serving the exchange of data within public administrations and between public administrations and the eu institutions since 1995. the commission has now proposed a decision of the parliament and the council to launch a programme that would open up the possibility to businesses and citizens alike. the report highlights the need to strengthen the service-providing nature of public administration, in particular by meeting the needs of the civil sector for data. i voted for the motion to pass.
in writing. ‒ the dismantling of the so-called e-border has been a process for several years and is now producing tangible results, for example in the functioning of the european institutions. programmes have been set up (ida, idabc and isa) which have made a significant contribution to the electronic exchange of information between the european institutions. i supported the report because i believe it is important to close the digital divide - not just the physical one - at all levels, for the benefit of the public sector, businesses and citizens. i agree with the report that interoperability offers significant opportunities for data protection and for stronger cross-border cooperation and that the responsible use of these opportunities can bring significant benefits in terms of growth and efficiency. i believe that this can also contribute to achieving the objectives of the european semester. the isa2 (2016-2020) programme, which replaces the isa programme, which expires on 31 december 2015, takes into account the conclusions of the impact studies carried out in recent years and i am confident that the approximately eur 131 million instrument will make measurable progress in digital interoperability.
in writing. ‒ the proposal provides for the launch of the programme on interoperability solutions for european public administrations, businesses and citizens (isa2), which is the long-awaited continuation and further development of the previous programmes (ida, idabc, isa). the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules on the application of this regulation. this ensures that data protection requirements are taken into account in the development phase of interoperability solutions for the processing of personal data. i voted in favor of the final motion.

in writing. ‒ meps do not act as representatives of their member states, but as representatives of the citizens of the union. however, the various political ideas and interests represented in the european parliament are not presented to voters in the run-up to the european elections. election campaigns are primarily conducted on the national political battlefield, so eu citizens are not aware of the actual politics that their vote may bring about. for many voters, the relationship between their national parties and their european political family is not even clear. voting is the main means of democratic participation, but the outdated system governing european elections prevents eu citizens from participating in european political debate. the current degree of heterogeneity of national electoral rules is contrary to the idea of european union citizenship and the principle of equality. citizens of the union, irrespective of their nationality, should be able to exercise their right to vote under similar conditions respecting democratic principles. the report of the constitutional affairs committee proposes that the european parliament should initiate a reform of the european electoral act in order to bridge the gap between the european institutions and the electorate separated by nationality and to ensure equal treatment for all eu citizens. i fully agree with the report and therefore support it unreservedly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the reform of the electoral law of the european union, which rightly highlighted the many differences in the electoral procedure for the european parliament in the member states, which prevent eu citizens from exercising their voting rights under the same conditions. as the report stressed, harmonisation in these areas would indeed promote the political dimension of european integration. the report highlighted a number of points, such as strengthening the role of european political parties in raising european political awareness, standardising the nomination procedure for candidates running for the european parliament elections, or banning the early publication of election results, which would not only increase the efficiency of the system for holding european elections, but also enhance the democratic legitimacy of the eu decision-making process. i also support the timing of the implementation of the reform well in advance of the 2019 european elections.
in writing. ‒ although the treaty of rome already provided for the possibility of developing a uniform electoral procedure based on universal suffrage in 1957, elections to the european parliament are still mainly determined by national electoral rules. the distribution of seats in the european parliament is not decided by a european election but by 28 national elections for national seats. this is in sharp contrast to the european parliament's role as a genuine european body and co-legislator on an equal footing within the eu's institutional framework. in addition to the need to strengthen the european dimension of european elections, the current degree of heterogeneity of national electoral rules is contrary to the idea of european union citizenship and the principle of equality. while harmonisation is not an objective, citizens of the union, irrespective of their nationality, should be able to exercise their right to vote under similar conditions respecting democratic principles. in order to bridge the gap between the european institutions and the electorate, which is separated by nationality, and to ensure equal treatment for all citizens of the union, the european parliament is determined to take the initiative to reform the european electoral charter, in accordance with its rights under article 223 (1) tfeu. i voted in favor of the final motion.

in writing. ‒ the commission's analysis of the schengen acquis and police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters found that 11 decisions of the schengen executive committee were obsolete because their content was taken over by later legislation, and council regulation (ec) no 189/2008 of 18 february 2008 on the testing of the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii) was obsolete when sis ii became operational on 9 april 2013. it therefore proposed that a decision of the european parliament and of the council be adopted repealing them. in its report, the committee on civil liberties, home affairs and justice recommended that the draft be adopted by parliament, proposing that the type of act be changed from a regulation to a decision, as a regulation is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all member states and better serves the purpose of the proposal. i supported the bill.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal because i attach great importance to the quality and transparency of european union legislation. this is particularly relevant in the case of regulation covered by the schengen agreement, in order to respond to new challenges that are emerging (such as terrorism). as the report points out, the acts proposed for repeal, or certain elements thereof, have been found to be outdated, replaced by new legislation or contain provisions which were partly intended to be transitional in nature, following a review after the transitional period provided for by the legislation. the proposed amendments also take account of the special legal relationship that the eu has with certain member states (denmark, united kingdom) and certain non-member states (iceland, norway, switzerland, liechtenstein) in its cooperation under the schengen agreement.
in writing. ‒ improving the transparency of eu law is an essential element of the strategy to improve the quality of legislation that is being implemented by the eu institutions. in this context, it is appropriate to remove from the existing legislation those which no longer serve any purpose. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ improving the transparency of eu law is an essential element of the strategy to improve the quality of legislation that is being implemented by the eu institutions. in this context, it is appropriate to repeal those of the existing acts which no longer serve any purpose. a number of acts adopted in the area of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters and included in the schengen acquis are no longer relevant, either because of their temporary nature or because their content has been taken over by subsequent acts. in agreement with the people's party delegation, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ we from the fidesz party (epp group) voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council repealing certain acts in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommended that the position of the european parliament adopted at first reading under the ordinary legislative procedure should amend the commission proposal. with this vote we change the type of act from ‘decision’ to ‘regulation’. in accordance with the article 288 tfeu a regulation is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all member states and will better serve the purpose of the proposal to repeal the acts deemed to be obsolete. the new text will improve the drafting of the act, including an addition in the title specifying that the repealed acts in question belong to the schengen acquis, and adapting the recitals to the uk’s position after the expiry of the transitional period set out in protocol no 36 to the treaties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report in which, in line with the relevant amendment proposed by the council in its general approach and adopted by the commission, the rapporteur proposes that the decision of the executive committee on the agreement on cooperation in road traffic infringement proceedings be included among the withdrawn acts. furthermore, in view of the amendments made by the council to the commission proposal, and after consulting the legal service of the european parliament, the rapporteur proposes to change the type of the act to a regulation on a decision. pursuant to article 288 tfeu, the regulation is to be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all member states and better serves the purpose of the proposal, which is to repeal acts deemed to be obsolete.
in writing. ‒ in its analysis referred to in the previous point, the commission found that the decisions of the schengen executive committee (sch/com-ex (93) 14 and (98) 52 (on the police handbook) on the fight against drug trafficking and the commission's statement (sch/com-ex (97) 13 decl rev 2 on the illegal conduct of minors) had become obsolete because their content had been taken over by subsequent acts. in addition, council decision 2008/173/jha on the testing of the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii) has become obsolete, as sis ii became operational on 9 april 2013. it therefore proposed that a decision of the european parliament and of the council be adopted repealing them. in its report, the committee on civil liberties, home affairs and justice recommended the draft to parliament for adoption, including the decision of the executive committee on the agreement on cooperation in road traffic offences among the acts withdrawn. that decision never entered into force and no member state has made a declaration under article 20 (3) concerning the application of the agreement between the member states which have ratified it. the report also proposes to change the type of act to a regulation on a decision, as a regulation is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all member states and better serves the purpose of the proposal. i supported the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of repealing the acts contained in the report, given that i attach great importance to the quality and transparency of european union legislation. in the case of legislation covered by schengen cooperation, it is particularly important and useful to clean up the agreement after the transitional period from elements that were intended to be transitional in nature or that have become obsolete or covered by new legislation, for which the report provides a precise overview and a well-founded proposal. i also considered the current aspect that it is precisely in the police and justice field that a transparent, flexible and modern legal environment that promotes effective law enforcement and law enforcement is most essential to respond to the new challenges facing europe today (terrorism, drug abuse, etc.).

in writing. ‒ we from the fidesz party (epp group) voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing certain acts in the field of police cooperation and judicial cooperation in criminal matters. the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommended that the position of the european parliament adopted at first reading under the ordinary legislative procedure should amend the commission proposal. among other things, we introduced a transitional provision stipulating that any european evidence warrant executed under framework decision 2008/978/jha shall continue to be governed by that instrument until the relevant criminal proceedings have been concluded with a definitive decision. the new text will improve the drafting of the act, clarifying the position of the uk in view of its decision in accordance with article 10(4) of protocol 36 and the use of a regulation as a legal instrument for repealing certain acts whose legal basis after the lisbon treaty requires adoption of a directive.
in writing. ‒ in order to ensure legal certainty and clarity, i agree with the priorities identified in the report. in line with the amendments proposed by the council in its general approach and adopted by the commission, and after consulting the legal service of the european parliament, the rapporteur proposes amendments to repeal the obsolete legal act concerning the convention of 17 june 1998 on the prohibition of driving and council act 98/c 216/01. this is an important issue because the convention needs to be ratified by all 15 signatory states for it to enter into force. however, only seven countries ratified the convention and it never entered into force. it has therefore lost its relevance in union law and should be repealed.
in writing. ‒ in its analysis of the schengen acquis and police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters referred to in point 1, the commission found that seven council joint actions were obsolete because their content had been taken over by subsequent acts. furthermore, the council act establishing the staff regulations of europol staff is outdated as it applies only to a very limited number of employment contracts concluded before the adoption of council decision 2009/371/jha on europol, of which very few are currently in force and are due to expire. in its report, the committee on civil liberties, home affairs and justice recommended the draft to parliament for adoption, proposing also the repeal of the convention on the prohibition on the use of motor vehicles of 17 june 1998 and of council act 98/c 216/01 and of council framework decision 2008/978/jha on the european evidence warrant for the purpose of obtaining objects, documents and data to be used in criminal proceedings. the former no longer applies to any member state and has therefore lost its relevance in union law, while the latter has been replaced by directive 2014/41/eu of the european parliament and of the council on european investigation decisions in criminal matters. finally, the report makes a recommendation to improve the wording of the legislation and to add a new recital. i supported the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the package of amendments to the report on certain areas of police and judicial cooperation between member states, in particular with a view to ensuring better quality, modernity and transparency of european union legislation. the report also highlights the issue of legal certainty, which i consider to be of paramount importance for citizens' confidence in eu cooperation. legislation that is outdated or that is not in force as originally intended (such as the convention on the driving ban) or that has been replaced by more modern and more far-reaching legislation (such as the 2014 framework decision on the european investigation order, which replaced the european evidence warrant) should be repealed. i am convinced that by approving these proposals, the ep will make a significant contribution to improving the effectiveness of police and judicial cooperation between member states, which is essential for the successful fight against cross-border crime and for strengthening the security of european citizens.

in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party's line, i voted in favour of the eu joining the commission for the protection of southern bluefin tuna as a regional economic integration organisation. the eu has so far fully adopted the recommendations of the committee, which clearly show that the european union is forced to limit its sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. the reasoned measures taken to maintain them have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries.

in writing. ‒ the regulation of insurance contracts and insurance intermediaries has been put on the agenda by all governments worldwide, including the hungarian government. the european commission has also recognised the importance of consumer protection, as in the past it has tried to support crossborder intermediation through various internal market measures, but we now know that consumer protection in itself promotes the growth of the internal market. a greater degree of harmonisation is necessary in the interests of all parties concerned, but for some member states the requirements may prove to be so stringent as to constitute a market barrier. as regards information requirements, i believe that there is a real need for transparency in the remuneration system if customers demand it, but top-down regulation can lead to unnecessary bureaucracy. i think we've finally developed a system that works for the benefit of consumers. of course, many times each of the 28 member states believes that its system is the best, but this does not mean a single internal market. if someone has passed a qualification scheme, it must be recognised in other member states. the current proposal will alleviate the often cumbersome operation of the current system, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ in 2012, the commission proposed the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council on insurance mediation. on the basis of the opinions of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and the committee on legal affairs, the economic and monetary affairs committee adopted a report on the proposal, which was discussed by the european parliament at its meeting of 26 february 2014, and on the basis of which it made amendments. in its decision of 18 september 2014, the conference of presidents listed the issue as an open issue for the seventh parliamentary term. in order to close the matter, the economic and monetary committee adopted an additional report recommending the commission's proposal to parliament for adoption, with amendments. i supported the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the supplementary report on insurance mediation, which added important safeguards to the original document. i think it is right that the report now includes the addition that member states can maintain even stricter provisions to protect customers, provided they are in line with eu directives. protecting consumers' rights and interests, and improving their quality of life and well-being, are among the fundamental values of the european union. the union should aim to ensure that these values are applied in all areas, including the sale of insurance products. i therefore welcome and support the new guarantees highlighted in the supplementary report which will help to achieve this. such as the requirement for close cooperation between host and home member states or the creation of a central information point to ensure a high level of service and effective consumer protection. i was pleased to see the rapporteur stress that consumers should enjoy the same level of protection despite differences between sales channels. this requires raising the level of consumer protection and ensuring a level playing field across europe.
in writing. ‒ insurance products can be sold by a variety of persons and institutions, such as agents, dealers, bank insurance brokers, insurance companies, travel agents or even car rental companies. the equal treatment of intermediaries and the protection of clients require the application of this directive to all those persons and entities. in order to ensure that the same level of protection applies regardless of the channels through which customers purchase an insurance product, whether directly from the insurer or indirectly from an insurance intermediary, this directive should cover not only insurers or intermediaries but also other market participants who sell insurance products in an ancillary manner, such as travel agents or car rental companies, unless they fulfil the conditions for exemption. i voted yes to the motion.

in writing. ‒ given the un convention on the rights of the child, which states that every child should have the right to education, health services, housing, protection, participation in decisions affecting them, leisure and free time, a balanced diet and to be raised in a family, i believe that the eu is unfortunately not doing enough. it is worrying that the proportion of children living in persistent extreme poverty is increasing (over a three-year period). social inequalities re-create disadvantages across generations, and the negative effects of poverty and social exclusion on children can last a lifetime. so i think that the wrong policy measures will have an irreversible negative impact on the lives of these people and on society. i support member states providing the support needed to ensure the right to culture, sport and leisure for all children, with a focus on children living in poverty, in remote areas, with disabilities and migrant children. in order to protect children from abuse, violence and neglect, it is important to strengthen social rights, which should be guaranteed by the state, by increasing the number of employees and professionals providing social services with a view to enhancing medical, psychological and social care for young people.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on reducing inequalities and in particular child poverty adopted today. the main elements of the decision were originally based on my own proposals, which underpinned the measures introduced by the hungarian government in recent years. nevertheless, the report adopted by the leftist majority took into account older statistics and survey figures, which significantly distorted data and trends about the current situation. i voted in favour of the people's party and agreed with the rapporteur that job creation is a priority, as are high energy prices and reducing taxes on income, which are also part of the fight against poverty. my amendment regarding the free and more general access to childcare was among the first priorities in the report, which supports the correct approach of the hungarian government so far. i also share the view that the reduction of household debt can and has significantly improved the situation of people, which has also been a priority of the hungarian government in recent years.
in writing. the aim of the report is clearly to be supported. his good intentions are beyond question, but his solutions are still improving. it would be fortunate to build and operate a public residential school system considered by the profession to be the best for achieving lasting results, which indeed requires more investment, but which is rewarding in social terms. with a fairer tax system that puts a proportionate burden on multinational companies, the hedge can be easily created.
in writing. ‒ the report of the employment and social affairs committee, based on statistical data and socioeconomic contexts, highlights a fundamental problem: the increase in social inequalities, including its most serious consequence, child poverty. it is undeniable that between 2008 and 2012 the number of children at risk of poverty or social exclusion increased by almost one million in europe, that the number increased by half a million between 2011 and 2012 alone, that the risk of poverty or social exclusion increased from 26,5% to 28% between 2008 and 2012, or that in 2013 26,5 million children in the eu28 were at risk of poverty or social exclusion. the problem raised in the report is very serious and the european union must certainly do something about it, even if not all the specific proposals put forward seem to be feasible, which is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. reducing inequalities, especially child poverty stresses that investing in the well-being of children and in lifting them out of poverty is not only a moral obligation but also a social and economic priority. the socialists and democrats group in the european parliament is calling for the introduction of a child guarantee funded from the european budget to end child poverty, which is supported by the dk in the light of the hungarian data. this guarantee would ensure that every child has free access to health care, education, childcare, decent housing and adequate nutrition. we believe that this is the only way to break the vicious circle of poverty, because it has to start at the youngest possible age. the child guarantee is a long-term instrument that provides equal opportunities for an entire generation and supports parents in their social integration and integration into the labour market. that is why i support the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report stresses that every child should be guaranteed the right to education, health services, housing, protection, participation in decisions affecting them, leisure and free time, a balanced diet and to be raised in a family (un convention on the rights of the child). however, the eu is far from satisfying the requirements of the convention. that is why i supported the report, because child poverty is on the rise in europe. it is regrettable that the hungarian government has abolished the statistics on poverty rather than providing solutions, even though it is known that some 4 million people are already living below the subsistence level and the number of hungry children has increased by more than half a million. unfortunately, the hungarian government fails to take into account that social inequalities re-create disadvantages across generations, and that the negative effects of poverty and social exclusion on children can last a lifetime. the european parliament voted that it is essential that member states increase the volume, amount, scope and effectiveness of benefits specifically for children and parents (such as unemployment benefits or extended parental leave). i believe that creating quality jobs and raising the minimum wage can be a direct and indirect solution to eliminate inequalities.
in writing. ‒ all reports indicate that child poverty is increasing in europe. between 2008 and 2012, the number of children at risk of poverty or social exclusion increased by almost one million in europe; in 2013, 26.5 million children in the eu28 were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, according to eurostat. in hungary, 41.4 percent of children, or nearly one in two, are forced to live in poverty. this also proves that in recent years a tragic social crisis has developed in hungarian society. three hundred thousand children live in extremely poor nutritional conditions, and fifty to sixty thousand children do not get proper nutrition every day. as a european democrat, i can only support any initiative that sets the goal of eradicating child poverty. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ there is currently no eu-wide definition of marginalised communities, so member states have to decide this using their national indicators. there are indicators that are closely linked to marginalisation, such as high long-term unemployment, low levels of education, extremely poor housing conditions, lack of access to healthcare and/or exposure to excessive health risks. the crisis had a direct negative impact on marginalised communities, further increasing poverty and social exclusion. cohesion policy plays an important role in supporting the economic, social and territorial integration of marginalised communities. the report suggests a number of ideas that are useful for the integration of marginalised groups. it stresses that education and employment are the best antidote to poverty and that projects relating to extra-curricular and lifelong learning should be encouraged. the report also stresses the importance of integrated housing, education and employment interventions, and the need to improve access to public services. i voted in favour of the report in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on regional development is about groups and communities in european societies that are structurally excluded and segregated from the majority society, with no access to even basic public infrastructure and services. these groups are often characterised by disproportionate poverty, unemployment and poor health. the report notes that the large reductions in public spending during the crisis have exacerbated existing problems (such as unemployment, lack of social security, poor housing and lack of public health services) in the member states. as a consequence, the crisis had a direct negative impact on marginalised communities. the report makes recommendations to counter these negative consequences. i supported the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ the report on cohesion policy and marginalised communities is most valuable for drawing attention to the inefficiency of eu support in reaching marginalised communities. it emphasises that the roma population is the largest such group in europe, stresses the importance of education in inclusion and that women are even more affected by exclusion than men. the report calls on the commission to define precisely the marginalized groups, to report on the resources allocated to support such groups, to analyse the data and to draw the necessary conclusions. it also calls on the commission to ensure that ngos are regularly involved in the monitoring of resources. overall, the report contributes to making more eu aid available to the most disadvantaged european citizens.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i agree that cohesion policy makes a significant contribution to increasing economic, social and territorial cohesion and reducing social inequalities. however, i believe that the opportunities offered by cohesion policy should be further developed and that further help can be given to member states to alleviate and eradicate poverty and exclusion. i agree that in all european societies there are groups and communities that live in structural exclusion and segregation from the majority society and do not have access even to basic public infrastructures and services. as a result, many of them are plagued by extreme poverty, unemployment, violence, and poor health. the situation of marginalised communities, including roma, can be improved by means of european-level instruments, while the change in the situation of these communities is primarily the responsibility of the member states. this cannot be solved by appearance politics, which is why the european commission's guidelines can help to take concrete steps. the report will provide detailed information on the effective use of funding opportunities for marginalised communities and the effective application of the european code of conduct (e.g. in terms of the partnership principle and the involvement of civil society). i believe that accountable, transparent and democratic structures should be established to ensure the integration of marginalised communities and to fight corruption and misuse of resources.
in writing. ‒ marginalized communities have been put at the centre of cohesion policy measures as concerns about social exclusion and a commitment to combating it have increased. including the situation of the roma and the long-awaited improvement of their living conditions. the proposal calls on the european commission to provide guidance on the definition of marginalised communities, defining the totality of the characteristics and attributes of marginalised groups, taking into account the specific situation, challenges and needs of each potential target group with a view to promoting their socio-economic integration. i voted yes to the motion.
in writing. ‒ the union's action at international level is based on the principles of democracy, the rule of law, equality, solidarity, the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms and respect for human dignity, as enshrined in article 21 of the treaty on the union. the report adopted today recalls that the principles and objectives of the eu's foreign policy are closely linked to those of the un. it underlines that the challenges facing the eu require global solutions and global problems require union action. it therefore needs global partners to achieve its objectives, namely in the areas of peace and security and the prevention of the spread of terrorism. the union should therefore continue to seek to strengthen global governance within the un. with regard to the migration and refugee crisis affecting europe, i voted in favour of the report, which inter alia calls on the union and the un to work together more closely than ever to deal with the crisis and inter alia to help remedy the economic situation and sustainable development of the countries of origin of migration. in view of the forthcoming un climate change conference in paris, i also voted in favour of the eu and the un stepping up their efforts to reach a legally binding agreement at this summit.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it provides a compelling argument for the need for the european union to finally take its place in the un in accordance with its actual international weight and importance, both in terms of its organisational structure and its global activities. i believe that the time has come - as the report suggests - for the eu member states, with the help of the european external action service, to make their positions and the interests of the union more coherent and stronger on the most important issues of international life. i agree that this requires accelerating the operational and organisational reform of the un, which is still reminiscent of the cold war, in particular the reform of the security council, including the elimination of the possibility of abusing the right of veto, in particular in cases involving violations of universal human rights. i hope that the ep's resolution will also contribute to the eu's long-term place in an enlarged eu. in formulating my opinion, i also took into account as an important virtue of the report that it urges greater emphasis on women's equality in the functioning and organisation of the world body, including the principles and practice of the election of the secretary-general. i also thought it important that the ep should also urge in this document that parliament should be given equal weight with the commission in shaping the eu's global role.

in writing. the paris terrorist attacks have made it clear that the european union must act to combat terrorism and prevent the radicalisation of eu citizens. while combating radicalisation remains a primary responsibility of the member states, a coordinated european approach is needed. it is estimated that more than five thousand european citizens have travelled to iraq and syria to receive training from terrorist organisations. this is a real security threat to the whole of europe. the paris attacks have shown that the current immigration and integration policy is bleeding from several wounds, as second and third generation immigrants leave for syria and become radicalized. these young people have grown up and are growing up in the heart of europe's great cities, in paris and brussels. all of this calls into question the western european model of education and integration, and it shows that it has failed. criminal justice alone is not enough. the union needs a new strategy based on prevention. according to information from european law enforcement and intelligence agencies, effective prevention of radicalisation should start where recruitment occurs.

in writing. brussels is on high alert for the fifth day, with the threat of terrorism looming. will the deaf also learn that the football game has been canceled, the malls have been closed, the subway is out of service, the kindergartens are closed? will they know in time when the danger is over? on monday night, all of belgium was watching tv with great anticipation as the belgian prime minister announced whether the level 4 terror alert would remain in place on tuesday, whether the subway would be restarted the next day, and whether children would be allowed to go to school. however, prime minister charles michel's words were not understood by the deaf because no sign-language interpreter was present at the press conference. it is unfortunate that neither after the paris attacks nor during the emergency in brussels was there any information available to the deaf and hard of hearing. there is no adequate solution in the european union, either at european or national level, and deaf people are therefore a particularly vulnerable group. hungary is a good example: during the recent floods in the danube, viktor orbán's press briefing was interpreted in sign language so that our deaf fellow citizens could receive accurate information in their mother tongue about what to do, the danger or its passing. in addition, the national disaster management service in our country operates an application called vész, which can be downloaded free of charge on smartphones and tablets, allowing anyone to receive instant written information on their smartphone about the dangers in their immediate vicinity, or even about the warnings and alarms issued nationally.
in writing. the terrorist attacks in paris on 13 november 2015 have dramatically awakened us all and, fortunately, most responsible european governments and leaders to the fact that the eu can only face this threat in full unity, both in europe and in the middle east. i believe it is time that the solidarity which is the foundation of the union should be extended to police, intelligence and military cooperation. in line with the member states' and joint initiatives to date, such as measures to restrict arms trafficking, control passenger traffic and eliminate the iad base, i stress that the end result cannot be the permanent closure of european borders or the abandonment of our european principles on civil liberties. faced with such a serious common challenge, it is particularly shocking that there are politicians in europe (especially hungarian prime minister viktor orbán) who use the current dramatic situation to spread populist demagogy and, even after paris, have allowed themselves to make public statements that 'every terrorist is an immigrant' or that the commission's proposal on the allocation of quotas for migrants 'aims to spread terrorism on our continent'. i am convinced that with joint international and european efforts we will one day finally defeat the horror of terrorism; however, the political poison that reinforces in our citizens the attitudes reflected in such statements will have a much longer effect. i therefore urge a firm and consistent common european rejection of such dangerous policies and rhetoric.

in writing. ‒ after considering all the possibilities for the transfer of commitment appropriations within chapters 3 and 4 of the 2016 eu budget, it has become necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument in favour of commitment appropriations. the european commission has therefore proposed to mobilise the flexibility instrument in order to supplement the resources of the general budget of the european union for 2016 with a commitment appropriation of eur 1 506 million in addition to the ceiling of chapter 3 to finance the actions under the european migration strategy. on the basis of the above, the european parliament has approved the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument in the form of commitment appropriations amounting to eur 1 530 million. as the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument is part of the package of agreements developed by the negotiating delegations of the european parliament and the council for the adoption of the 2016 eu budget, i supported the report in line with hungarian interests and the position of the ppe group.

in writing. ‒ the so-called flexibility instrument can be used to finance clearly defined expenditure which would not be financed under the ceilings for other chapters. the commission has identified the need for significant additional appropriations to finance measures to alleviate the migration and asylum crisis due to urgent needs and has therefore proposed the adoption of a decision of the parliament and of the council to supplement chapter 3 of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 with a commitment appropriation of eur 1 506 million and chapter 4 with a commitment appropriation of eur 24 million to be charged to the flexibility instrument. in its report, the committee on budgets considers the commission's proposal to be justified and recommends that parliament adopt it. i voted in favour of the motion accordingly.
in writing. ‒ after considering all the possibilities for the transfer of commitment appropriations within chapters 3 and 4 of the 2016 eu budget, it has become necessary to mobilise the flexibility instrument in favour of commitment appropriations. the european commission has therefore proposed to mobilise the flexibility instrument in order to supplement the resources of the general budget of the european union for 2016 with a commitment appropriation of eur 1 506 million in addition to the ceiling of chapter 3 to finance the actions under the european migration strategy. in addition to the eur 1 506 million over the ceiling of chapter 3, the conciliation committee convened for the 2016 budget also accepted the proposal of the parliament's delegation to mobilise an additional eur 24 million under the flexibility instrument over and above the ceiling of chapter 4 to address the external dimensions of the challenges posed by the refugee crisis. on the basis of the above, the european parliament has approved the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument in the form of commitment appropriations amounting to eur 1 530 million.
in writing. ‒ i myself voted to give the european parliament its approval for the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, with an additional amount of eur 1 530 million over the next four years, in addition to the 2016 budgetary allocation, to supplement the community and member states' expenditure related to the refugee crisis. in this context, it had to be acknowledged that, in the context of the current budgetary structure and regulation, the rigid budgetary chapter ceilings make it impossible to finance such urgent tasks within or above a given budget chapter (chapters 3 and 4 where appropriate). for this reason, this report has also stressed the importance of making budgetary training and regulation more flexible, which i myself consider to be urgent. i am also concerned that the use of the flexibility instrument now decided is essentially due to the transfer of residues formed in 2014 and 2015, while such residues cannot be expected to be formed in the flexibility instrument in 2017.
in writing. ‒ in the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, the flexibility instrument shall be mobilised to provide a commitment appropriation of eur 1 506 million in chapter 3 (security and union citizenship) and a commitment appropriation of eur 24 million in chapter 4 (global europe). those amounts should be used to finance measures to deal with the refugee crisis. the mobilisation of this instrument under article 11 of the mff regulation re-emphasises the crucial need for the union budget to be more flexible. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund was set up to enable the european union to respond to major natural disasters. the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 500 million, in addition to the ceilings of the relevant chapters of the financial framework. the proposal for the current decision of the european parliament and of the council is not related to a specific disaster. instead, it aims to allocate eur 50 million in the union budget for 2016 in the form of commitment and payment appropriations to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. the advance thus allows the disbursement of aid to the countries concerned to be accelerated before the final award decision is taken. i supported the adoption of the report because it is important that the countries and territories affected by the disaster receive the aid to which they are entitled as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the european union to respond immediately to major natural disasters and to express solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 500 million (2011 prices), in addition to the ceilings of the relevant chapters of the financial framework. the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council is not related to a specific disaster. the objective is to allocate eur 50 million in the union budget for 2016 in the form of commitment and payment appropriations to ensure that advances can be paid in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. the european parliament therefore agreed to enter the proposed amounts in the 2016 budget. as the proposal 'recourse to the eu solidarity fund for advance payments relating to the 2016 budget' is part of the package of agreements drawn up by the negotiating delegations of the european parliament and the council for the adoption of the 2016 eu budget, i supported the report in line with hungarian interests and the position of the ppe group.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the european union to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the mobilisation of the fund up to a maximum of eur 500 million per year. one of the provisions of regulation (eu) no 661/2014 amending the conditions for mobilising the fund provides for the possibility of accelerating the disbursement of assistance to the countries concerned by means of an advance payment of up to 10% of the expected financial contribution, paid before the final decision on the award is taken. the commission has proposed the adoption of a decision of the european parliament and of the council allocating eur 50 million in the 2016 union budget in commitment and payment appropriations to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster occurring in the following year. in its report, the committee on budgets of the european parliament recommends that parliament approve the draft decision. i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the european union to respond to major natural disasters and to express european solidarity with europe's disaster-stricken regions. the fund provides financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating accession in the event of 'major natural disasters'. the proposal for the current decision of the european parliament and of the council is not related to a specific disaster. instead, it aims to allocate eur 50 million in the union budget for 2016 in the form of commitment and payment appropriations to pay advances in a timely and efficient manner in the event of a disaster that may occur in the following year. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ eu funds to hungary were also provided in 2016. attempts to link the payment of cohesion funds to the implementation of the rules on quotas for the relocation of migrants were thwarted. the commission has also been able to increase the appropriations for programmes to help tackle the migration crisis by eur 2 billion. the majority of the surplus funds, in line with the hungarian government's position, will be spent in countries struggling on the front line of the crisis and will contribute to addressing the conflicts that are fuelling the wave of immigration at the point of origin. i consider the reversal of the reduction in the pre-accession fund (ipa) previously proposed by the council to be a success, as these instruments are decisive for the accession aspirations of the candidate countries, such as serbia and the hungarians in the former yugoslavia. in addition to the actual financial support, maintaining the level of the pre-accession fund also carries an important political message and encouragement for the candidate countries. i also supported the joint project 'diverse europe'. under this, €1 million will be available to applicants to finance minority programmes supporting the elimination of discrimination. on the basis of the above, and in line with the people's party's position, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ on 24 june 2015, the commission adopted the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016. on 17 september 2015, the council forwarded its position on the draft to parliament, which adopted a resolution on the subject and proposed budgetary amendments on 28 october 2015. on this basis, the conciliation committee on budgets between parliament, the council and the commission approved the joint text of the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, which was recommended to parliament for adoption in the report of parliament's delegation to the conciliation committee. i therefore voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament adopting the 2016 budget of the european union. i considered that, following the conciliation procedure, an interinstitutional compromise had been reached on the basis of which 155 billion at commitment level and almost 144 billion at payment appropriation level, broken down by chapter and by priority, would be sufficient to cover community expenditure for the following year. i considered that the main aspect was that the negotiations had led to a substantial increase in the proportion of european economic growth and job creation and in the proportion of aid for research and training within the budget. i consider it equally important that the resources needed to deal with the unexpected and burdensome refugee crisis for the eu at community and national level have been supplemented by an additional eur 800 million. in addition, the composition and the adoption process of the 2016 eu budget once again highlight that common tasks and challenges require more flexibility than at present and require a more cooperative approach and modern financial planning methods, in particular by the member states and the council. i trust that, and as a member, i will work to ensure that this aspect is taken into account in the forthcoming review of the mff in 2016.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the budgetary procedure, the conciliation committee approved the common draft text of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ phthalates are widely used to soften pvc. in terms of their environmental and health effects, studies carried out over many years have shown a clear distinction between phthalates with short hydrocarbon chains and phthalates with long hydrocarbon chains. a large number of studies, including those carried out by several independent organisations, have shown that high molecular weight phthalates do not pose any health risk to humans. the eu competent bodies therefore decided that they should not be given a restrictive label and should not be included in the list of substances awaiting authorisation. however, low-mass substances, which are also included in the list of substances of very high concern, have adverse effects on the mammalian hormonal system and have reproductive effects and are currently being considered for authorisation. since the commission is accountable to the european citizens and the protection of citizens and the environment from hazardous chemicals is a priority, i supported the resolution. accordingly, the commission should withdraw its draft implementing decision and submit a new draft decision to the parliament and the council refusing to grant the authorisation.
in writing. ‒ i consider that the draft commission implementing decision goes beyond the implementing powers set out in the relevant regulation. a number of questions arise regarding the authorisation of the use of these substances. i find it worrying that in the case of dehp, it has been shown to adversely affect the mammalian hormonal system by lowering testosterone levels. furthermore, scientific evidence shows that exposure to dehp at sensitive developmental times may cause irreversible effects on the developmental programme with serious effects on development and reproduction, and these effects are considered to be particularly serious for human health and wildlife. it is known that dehp can be substituted by a number of substances and the applicants have not provided a comprehensive analysis of the alternatives available on the market to replace the use of dehp in the applications requested. in the light of the above, i consider it appropriate to call on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft rejecting the applications for authorisation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp.
in writing. ‒ i supported the objection as proposed by the envi committee. since there is a high risk that dehp can affect the human reproductive system, and its application in pvc products is not well specified, i cannot support granting authorisation for use of this substance.
in writing. ‒ dehp is a widely used material in pvc, but it is not chemically bound to the plastic and thus easily leaches into the environment. there is scientific evidence of endocrine disrupting effects of dehp and of a causal relationship between these effects and adverse effects on human health. the commission has submitted a draft implementing decision to grant an application for authorisation of the use of recycled soft pvc containing dehp. parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety, in its report, points out that it considers that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 and therefore proposes that parliament calls on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft rejecting the applications for authorisation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the commission intends to identify dehp as a substance of very high concern by means of a draft implementing decision on the identification of bis (2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (dehp), di-butyl phthalate (dbp), benzyl-butyl phthalate (bbp) and di-isobutyl phthalate (dibp) as substances of very high concern in accordance with article 57 (f) of regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 of the european parliament and of the council. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the depleted public coffers and the burden of equity are increasingly pushing the member states of the european union to coordinate their efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the issue seems to have become a permanent feature of the ep, with a new committee set up to strengthen it. the first submission of this committee is this report. as we all see, the long economic crisis has had the side effect of increasing the demand for the discovery of hidden income in the eu and globally, which the european commission estimates is costing member states tens of billions of dollars a year. the need for fiscal adjustment and fair burden-sharing necessitated by the crisis appears to increase the capacity of eu member states, traditionally reluctant in tax matters, to step up and coordinate their action against tax fraud and tax evasion. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that we must continue to commit ourselves to accelerating the adoption of the eu proposals already put forward in tax evasion cases and to implementing the measures already adopted.

in writing. ‒ the special committee on tax evaluations and other measures similar in nature or effect was set up following the scandal of luxembourg tax evaluations, known as 'luxleaks'. in its report, the committee proposes that parliament declare that the european commission has failed to fulfil its role as guardian of the treaties, as defined in article 17 (1) of the treaty on european union, by failing to act on this matter and by not taking the necessary steps to inform the member states and enforce their obligations, despite evidence that they are not fulfilling their obligations. it also proposes that the commission should declare that it has failed to fulfil its obligations under article 108 of the treaty on the functioning of the internal market by not initiating an investigation of state aid earlier. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on conditional tax assessments, which is an important milestone in our fight against corporate tax fraud. the report provides detailed and clear guidance to member states and the commission on the means to curb tax avoidance by multinational companies. the country-by-country report, the sharing of information on national tax rulings, the blacklisting of tax havens, the common consolidated tax base and the establishment of uniform tax definitions are all proposals that contribute to the creation of a transparent tax system and ensure that the tax burden is no longer almost exclusively borne by smes and citizens. i was pleased to see that the report clearly states that taxes should be paid in the member state where the profits are generated, thus avoiding unfair competition. there is a need to establish a comprehensive legislative framework for corporate taxation in europe, which should be centred on this principle. there's a lot of hard work behind this detailed, in-depth report. if european governments commit themselves and take our recommendations into account, we can put an end to the practice of tax treaties in europe once and for all.

in writing. ‒ more than 4 000 workers die each year in work-related accidents and more than 150 000 die each year from work-related fatal diseases. ambitious policies in the field of health and safety at work have proven economic benefits, including productivity and labour market participation and increased sustainability of social security systems. the report of the employment and social committee argues that, as well as the significant economic costs, occupational accidents and diseases present significant challenges as carriers of many new and emerging risks, and as their management requires legislative and non-legislative initiatives, immediate action at union level is needed and further concrete measures should be complemented by the union strategy on health and safety at work 2014-2020. i supported the motion.

mr president, mr commissioner, mr minister, and my fellow members of parliament. we are past the valet summit, and the difficult weeks of the migrant crisis itself are now overshadowed, to say the least, by the terrorist attacks in paris, or rather, by the overwhelming ones. i think it is necessary to talk about the lines behind the growing popular movements. i ask you, were we struck by lightning in this sequence of events that we are witnessing, or were we expected? the arab spring experience has been clear about how much democracy can be exported to areas where the conditions are not yet understood. and it's from this failure that the mainstream social theories of western prosperity and the popularity of these theories have led to the current migration. my fellow members of the house of representatives! today we are in a race against time to save schengen. i heard with bad breath that we are starting to talk about mini-schengen as if we had given up on this race in the first place. you can't give up on a race. you have to fight to the end. schengen, free movement is part of european integration, which we can say is felt by every citizen within the european union. this is an achievement that, if it fails, my fellow mps, everything will fall! we must therefore use all means at our disposal to protect this symbol of our union. it is a sad fact for me that the european political elite always defends its dead-end policy by saying that the terrorists, the paris terrorists, are not new immigrants, but second- and third-generation immigrants, and that therefore their policy of getting caught is not dangerous and does not need to be changed. but the point is that the generational narrative is distracting from the fact that muslims who settled in the 1970s had jobs and prosperity, but today's immigrants don't. i'm asking you to reconsider our theory so we don't jeopardize the european union's achievements.
