that's a two-card answer. thank you very much, mr. deputy, for your question. this is not about the passport, mr. deputy, this is about the internal market. the point is that one of the greatest opportunities for the european union is to be able to complete the internal market. there is a technical part to this, and schengen is one of them. if it's just about the passport, i'll be happy to show my passport when i'm in your country. in fact, citizens understand little about the internal market, but they easily understand that there is a schengen. but we agree that we are making our laws to enforce them and we are sitting here to talk about economic growth and job creation as much as possible, and that requires the internal market and schengen.
since the beginning of the uninterrupted flow of migrants from the south and east, european crisis meetings and international meetings have followed one another, including the summits of the imf and the g20. while acknowledging the necessity and implications of these, we must agree with prime minister viktor orbán, who believes that they lead to "nowhere". on the contrary, the migrant crisis is worsening, and it has been accompanied by a threat of terrorism against europe of apocalyptic proportions. who is responsible for this? for the deaths of innocent people in paris, for the escalation of uncontrolled and illegal immigration, for the daily uncertainty and fear, for the impending collapse of europe's borders and the schengen system! our european and national identity, values and interests are being jeopardised by those who, with the demagogy of multiculturalism, openness and solidarity, are trying to protect our borders, who are unwittingly allowing the spread of islamic fundamentalism and who are contributing to the drastic reshaping of europe's ethno-religious map. before it is too late, the union's policies on migration and asylum and on terrorism need to be reviewed and radically changed!
in writing. i am addressing the debate on migration in europe today on the basis of my recent experience in the middle east. recently, i spent days in refugee camps in northern iraq with the papal aid organization church in need. i met with the religious leaders who coordinated the relief efforts, the church organizations. my primary experience is that what is needed is basically peace and local solutions to manage migration. i am convinced that the former colonial powers of europe should not be concerned with economic advantage in this situation. the resources actually available should be focused on investments and aid programmes. we need to focus all our efforts on programs that help people stay home. this is primarily in the interest of refugees, because there is no reason for these ancient communities to migrate thousands of kilometers, exposed to criminal networks, instead of living in their own culture. it's been my very specific experience that we need to help the internally displaced today in two ways. one is providing education, the other is finding jobs. these two areas are clearly in need of immediate help and are also keys to staying put. it's a very serious problem that our decision-makers didn't recognize the need for these steps much earlier. the situation is quite clear: either we help locally according to the above criteria, in a coordinated way, in cooperation with international donors, or the persecuted can no longer endure, leave their homeland and head for europe en masse.
in writing. at the valletta summit, eu leaders worked to tackle the real problems of asylum. the summit focused on the reasons why refugees are forced to leave their homelands. improving cooperation with african countries and better using development resources to improve the situation of people living there can have a significant impact on reducing the number of refugees. it is equally important that we do everything we can to resolve the current armed conflict and prevent new crises. turkey can also be an important partner in improving stability in the middle east region and in addressing the problems of refugees. however, this should not be a blank check: the eu must strictly monitor whether the turkish government is providing adequate care for refugees and is acting in accordance with its international obligations. we must be clear that europe's security now begins far beyond the borders of the union. in an age of global problems, the european union must also become a strong player on the international stage. stronger european cooperation, joint action, effective management of international crises is the way to help prevent mass migration, not the way to build fences, anti-foreigner propaganda and violations of international law.
in writing. i have asked to speak in today's debate as a member of the european union election observation mission to myanmar. based on my experience on the ground, i agree with all those who described the november 8 elections as a calm, well-organized and transparent event. in yangon and bago region, more than a dozen constituencies have been visited to ensure that those entrusted with the conduct of the elections have carried out their duties responsibly and with commitment. the elections were conducted smoothly and efficiently, despite the high turnout. it is also clear that the legal environment, the legal background and the pre-election process left much to be desired. discussions with representatives of civil society organisations, ethnic minorities and the media have highlighted a number of such shortcomings. the most obvious of these, of course, is the fact that a quarter of the seats in the house of representatives automatically went to the military. but on the whole, myanmar, which has been a dictatorship for decades, took a giant step toward democratic settlement on november 8. the indisputable need for further procedural reforms in relation to the elections is overshadowed by the historic fact that the citizens of myanmar have made a dignified and overwhelming vote of confidence in democracy. i am convinced that the european union made the right decision in supporting this peaceful transition process by organising an election observation mission.
mr president, i would like to thank the commissioner for his very optimistic summary of political developments in georgia. i wish, commissioner, you were fully justified in your assessment of what has happened lately. georgia has made tremendous progress since it regained its independence and, as my colleague mr štětina rightfully pointed out, going peacefully through both a constitutional change and a change of government is not a small feat. many of our countries could be proud of that as well. having said that, i need to point out that political stability is never a given – never something which we can take for granted. you should actively work on achieving political stability at all times, and this includes respecting the political opposition as a legitimate rival, which is a sine qua non for democratic politics. likewise, the political opposition is required to understand and work for a peaceful change in government within the bounds of democratic politics. one point i would like to make, the last poll published on 13 october showed that actually there is 12% support for openly pro-russian parties in georgia. that is the danger which we need to avoid.
i would like to add a few words to the agricultural chapter of the court's report, partly because it is rare for the european parliament to have a good word to say about the experts who carried out the court's audit and about the european commission itself, which was responsible for implementing the expenditure. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is imputable to the state. despite this, the rate of miscalculation has been reduced to an all-time low of around 2%. i think that these results really mean that the european institutional system can work in the most difficult areas. however, it is undeniable that we are approaching the time of the six-monthly review, and it will be appropriate to say a few words about the content of the various publications. what is certain is that in the agricultural sector, the money that european taxpayers spend should really go to farmers, not be passed on. thank you so much for the opportunity.

in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution calls for the continuation of the doha agenda, which will be discussed at the ministerial meeting in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015. efforts to liberalize trade and money flows within the wto are primarily in the interests of advanced industrial countries, and there too primarily in the interests of multinational corporations. instead of globalisation, which is about exploiting cheap labour for the benefit of the many, we should adopt the principle that each country should produce for itself what it needs, within the limits of its real capacity. so production for man and not man for production. the focus should be on sustainable development and increasing the population retention capacity of developing countries. in this regard, it is worth quoting perhaps the most respected economist of all, john maynard keynes: "financial calculations may show it to be advantageous to invest my savings in those parts of the world where the return on capital, or interest, is highest. but more and more experience suggests that the distance between the owner and the area of operation is bad for the relationships between people, it is likely, or rather certain, to lead to tensions and hostility in the long run, which invalidates the financial calculations. on these grounds, i rejected the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the doha round, launched in 2001, aims to create new trade opportunities, strengthen multilateral trade rules and address current imbalances in the trading system, which is reflected in the focus of the negotiations on the needs and interests of developing countries, and in particular the least developed countries. in my view, these objectives stem from the conviction that a multilateral system based on fairer and more equitable rules can contribute to the development of fair and free trade and poverty reduction, which are essential for the economic development of all continents. the above aspects should be given priority. these agreements are in line with wto requirements, are based on commonly agreed rules and create the conditions for a possible future multilateral framework. i therefore consider it important to reaffirm our full commitment to multilateralism with lasting value and to advocate a trade agenda based on free and fair trade in the interests of all parties and with development at its core.
in writing. the wto is designed to serve the interests of advanced industrial countries, including multinational companies, rather than to catch up with participating less developed countries. this is unsupportable. a wonderful birdlife developed on one of the galapagos islands until a ship was sent to bring in some snakes. the island was soon overrun with reptiles, and the birds had disappeared. then the snakes ate each other. then all animal life died out. if we choose to see birds chirping instead of dead snakes, then instead of globalization, the exploitation of cheap labor for the benefit of the multinationals, we should follow the principle that each country should produce for itself as much as it needs, as far as possible. that is, production for man and not man for production. foreign trade, and in particular international capital flows, should be kept to a minimum. and all of this is not about lending to developing countries, it's about giving them technology.
in writing. ‒ the international trade committee proposed the adoption of a parliamentary resolution ahead of the 10th wto ministerial conference to be held in kenya from 15 to 18 december 2015. the proposed resolution reaffirms the european parliament's full commitment to multilateralism and to free and fair trade, which serves the interests of all parties and is centred on development. it is in favour of trade liberalisation, which should be complemented by appropriate macroeconomic and microeconomic measures and accompanying policies including administrative simplification, education and training, institutional reforms and social policies, in order to fully exploit the benefits of trade reforms and to better distribute them, effectively offsetting any negative effects. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ this decision was adopted weeks before the 10th wto ministerial conference (kenya, 15-18 december 2015). the european parliament attaches particular importance to taking into account the specific needs of low-income developing countries (ldcs), which it considers necessary to achieve a clear definition of the concepts of low-income developing countries and emerging economies. this is particularly important for china, as in this sense china is still considered a developing country without any further distinction being possible. the european parliament supports the structural reform of the wto in order to better ensure an open, fair and non-discriminatory system that takes due account of the needs of the different economic actors (smes, micro-enterprises, innovative start-ups). the decision encourages wto members to make essential progress in nairobi towards the proper implementation of the doha round and calls on wto members to swiftly ratify and implement the trade facilitation agreement (tfa).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the current state of the doha development agenda, which calls for a system based on fair and free trade, in the interests of all parties. i also believe that it is important to put the interests of low-income developing countries and least developed countries at the centre of the negotiations. i also welcomed and supported the recommendation in the motion to give more attention to smes, micro-enterprises and innovative start-ups in order to ensure a more efficient trading system. an essential element of the proposal is that it calls for a further strengthening of the role of the european parliament. it is important that parliament remains closely involved in the preparation of the ministerial conference and that it is kept informed and consulted, if necessary, during the ministerial conference. the doha development agenda, which began 14 years ago, will be marked by the ministerial conference in nairobi in december, and it is essential that the round ends with the development mandate fulfilled.
in writing. ‒ in order to ensure the close and final conclusion of the doha development round and to facilitate the full participation of the least developed countries in world trade, the union should continue to play a leading role in promoting tangible progress on the ongoing wto negotiations. the resolution calls on the commission and the council to ensure that parliament remains closely involved in the preparations for the 10th ministerial conference and that it is kept informed and consulted as necessary during the 10th ministerial conference. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that ecuador's accession to the trade agreement with colombia and peru is another decisive step towards an alliance with like-minded, important and rapidly developing countries in a region that is increasingly turning towards asia and the pacific. it is also welcome that the ecuadorian government has invested usd 40.8 billion in the social sector over the last eight years - including in access to education, health care and social security - through specific programmes targeting the most vulnerable groups, such as children, the elderly and people with disabilities. in this context, i consider it important to urge the government of ecuador to take similar measures based on the action plans submitted by colombia and peru, as this provides an opportunity to improve the general living conditions of citizens, including human and labour rights, and the environment.
in writing. i cannot support the eu's trade policy towards developing countries, as there is clear evidence that with liberalised trade and capital flows, less developed countries are not able to catch up. the motion for a resolution concerns the accession of ecuador to the trade agreement previously concluded by the union with peru and colombia. the commission has also received comments from the ecuadorian authorities, which have not provided any information on the measures taken by the government of ecuador to prevent the introduction of the new product. such agreements unilaterally serve the interests of multinational corporations, thus making the developing countries even more vulnerable to them than they are now. that would mean that the resolution should be rejected, but i cannot overrule the decision of a sovereign country, so i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the eu concluded trade agreements with colombia and peru on 17 july 2014. the eu and ecuador have successfully concluded negotiations to accede to the agreement and initialled the protocol allowing ecuador to establish preferential trade relations with the eu by joining neighbouring colombia and peru on 12 december 2014. the international trade committee has proposed the adoption of a parliamentary resolution welcoming the conclusion of the negotiations, highlighting in particular the $40.8 billion invested by the ecuadorian government in the social sector over the last eight years, which has launched specific programmes targeting the most vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly and people with disabilities. it recommends that the strong growth of the ecuadorian economy over the past few years be recognised as having directly reduced poverty - especially extreme forms of poverty - and inequality, and as having increased the middle class. in writing. ‒ in line with the european people's party line, i voted in favour of the adoption of the political resolution on the eu animal welfare strategy. i do not think it is timely at all to talk about animal welfare issues in the current situation, when the eu is facing huge challenges such as the fight against migration and terrorism. animal welfare standards in the union are the most advanced and strictest in the world, and i therefore do not support any attempt to tighten standards or to introduce new standards. instead, the rules need to be simplified. the only reason for my support is that the report contains a large number of proposals to preserve the competitiveness of eu livestock farmers. on the one hand, we must require that farmers from non-eu countries also meet the same animal welfare standards as those in the eu, otherwise their products will not be allowed into the union. on the other hand, the cap must continue to receive an adequate budget to enable farmers to comply with strict agricultural and livestock standards. third, we need to significantly strengthen farmers' bargaining power in the food supply chain.
in writing. ‒ i believe that european citizens have a strong interest in animal welfare and want to be able to make informed decisions as consumers. this information is a fundamental right of consumers within the union. union legislation on animal welfare contributes to a level playing field within the union and thus to the proper functioning of the internal market. we also know that animal welfare is closely linked to animal and public health. for these reasons, i support the report in that it urges the commission to implement without delay the outstanding issues of the eu strategy for the protection and welfare of animals (20122015) and urges the commission to ensure that all categories of animals commercial, wild, research, pet and aquatic are covered by any harmonisation of the animal welfare legislative framework. i consider it important to also call on the commission to use the new eu animal welfare reference centres to assist in the implementation of existing rules by disseminating information and sharing best practices, providing training to competent authorities and enforcing the application of approved animal welfare indicators. animal welfare is one of the engines of economic development.
in writing. ‒ the alde, efdd, epp, gue/ngl, s&d and ecr groups tabled a motion for a resolution on this subject, and the alde, epp, s&d and ecr groups agreed on a joint compromise proposal. i supported this compromise motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint resolution because i believe that animal welfare measures are important and that their continuity should be ensured. this is because the eu-wide animal welfare strategy also contributes to the proper functioning of the internal market. i believe that the strategy should give priority to innovation, education and the creation of coherence between the different foundations. i also think it is important to put more emphasis on consumer information and transparency, because we need to know whether producers are complying with animal welfare rules when they buy food. however, i would point out that care must be taken to ensure that these rules do not become an obstacle to the functioning of the single market. animal welfare standards are already high in the eu, which helps to reduce the negative effects of intensive animal husbandry. it is difficult to raise this high level any further, and let us not forget that most farm animals would not survive in a domesticated, natural environment. instead, countries outside the eu should be encouraged to adopt our best practices. i agree that the commission should remove the consequences from the 2012-2015 strategy and integrate them into the 2016-2020 strategy to be developed in a way that does not create administrative burdens and price increases for producers or consumers.
in writing. ‒ animal welfare should be further improved in line with current scientific knowledge, taking into account the efficiency and competitiveness of livestock farming. the definition of good animal husbandry would facilitate the development of uniform animal welfare standards throughout the union. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the un estimates that 1 billion children live in conflict-affected areas, 250 million of them under the age of 5, and are deprived of their fundamental right to education. the protracted crises put some 65 million children aged 3 to 15 at risk of dropping out of school, and in crisis-affected countries, some 37 million children are out of school, but should be in primary school or lower secondary school depending on their age. add to this the estimated 175 million children who are affected by natural disasters each year. education in emergencies or uncertainty is a specific area where humanitarian and development actors need to work closely together to coordinate relief, recovery and development. i agree that the commission should develop mechanisms for effective responses in its own activities and those of its partners and participate in the work of the international platform to develop concrete tools for education in emergencies in the context of the 2016 humanitarian summit. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ today, some 65 million children live in crisis areas where, due to the situation, they do not have access to adequate education, as the sector is typically underfunded in these regions. the proposal aims to encourage member states to support the european commission's proposal to increase the proportion of eu humanitarian aid spent on education to 4%. the proposal also calls on member states to help integrate refugee children they have taken in into their national education systems. quality education should be a priority in crisis and disaster-affected areas, as it can be the key to the post-crisis recovery and stabilisation process in the longer term. strengthening education can also play a significant role in preventing children from becoming victims of radicalisation, which can lead them to become involved in terrorist groups and militaries. access to adequate education can also be an important tool in the fight against poverty. in accordance with the above objectives, and following the line of the people's party, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ despite the reformed cohesion policy for the financial planning period 2014-2020, which addresses simplification methods, the application, management, reporting and control of the european structural and investment funds continue to be difficult for both beneficiaries and managing authorities, especially those with lower administrative and financial capacity. the current over-regulation, including the process of transposition of rules into national law, causes delays and generates longer time-outs and indirect costs for potential beneficiaries requiring union funds, thereby reducing the investment impact of union funding and creating obstacles for beneficiaries, citizens and businesses, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises in the union. complex procedures can impose a significant burden on beneficiaries, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, non-governmental organisations and municipalities that need union funding. as these organisations generally lack the financial and human resources and expertise to successfully apply for and manage eu grants, i consider it necessary to further simplify the procedure and therefore voted in favour of the adoption of the report.
in writing. ‒ while considerable progress has been made in the area of cohesion policy to reduce administrative burdens and simplify, the administrative burden on final beneficiaries of the european structural and investment funds is still very high. this presents a particular challenge for smes, ngos and local authorities, which are in dire need of eu funding but do not have the financial and human resources to successfully apply and manage the funds received. in light of this, further simplification is essential for the efficient use of resources. avoid frequent changes in rules, standardise procedures, simplify the language used, support the introduction and dissemination of e-cohesion and one-stop-shop. the motion for a resolution on simplifying and making cohesion policy more performance-oriented for the period 2014-2020 contains a number of useful ideas on this subject, which is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution in the plenary vote in strasbourg on 26 november.

in writing. ‒ on 12 february 2015, the european parliament decided to set up a special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect, known as taxe, with its powers, number of members and term of office. the mandate of the special committee expired in the summer of that year, and its report was discussed and adopted by parliament on 25 november. in the light of the findings of the report, the conference of presidents proposed that parliament establish a special committee, with the same powers, staff and structure as the taxe special committee, to complete the work of the taxe special committee and monitor the implementation of the recommendations contained in the resolution of 25 november. i supported the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of setting up a special committee of the european parliament on tax rulings. the first taxe committee's recently adopted report gave an excellent overview of the harmful tax avoidance and tax evasion practices of individual member states and multinational companies to date and made clear and detailed recommendations to the european commission and the member states to deal effectively with this unacceptable situation. but the work did not end there. until we have completely eliminated harmful tax avoidance practices and achieved a fundamental change in political ethics in this area, close and continuous monitoring will be necessary. sadly, harmful tax practices have become almost the norm in some countries. in addition, new tax evasion schemes, loopholes are emerging. they must be monitored and brought to their attention. the new special committee will have a major role to play in this. i also think it is right that the new committee should retain the structure of the first taxe committee, along which the members have been able to work effectively over the past year.

in writing. ‒ the european union and liechtenstein signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 28 october 2015 to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. i am convinced that the agreement represents an important step forward in the efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the agreement establishes an automatic exchange of information between the eu and liechtenstein on the financial accounts of each other's residents as from 2017. the aim is to address situations where taxable persons seek to conceal income or capital representing assets for which tax has not yet been paid. a key element of the arrangement is also to ensure that the information exchanged covers not only income such as interest and dividends but also account balances and income from the sale of financial instruments. in this sense, i welcome the role of being able to identify precisely and clearly the taxpayers concerned and to apply and enforce their tax laws in cross-border cases and to assess the likelihood of tax fraud being committed.
in writing. ‒ the european union and liechtenstein signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information on 28 october 2015 to improve international tax cooperation and compliance. the agreement was submitted to the council for approval by the commission, which is obliged under the treaty on the functioning of the european union to consult the parliament before taking a decision. in its report, the committee recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report, which updates the 2004 agreement between liechtenstein and the eu, which ensures that the principality applies measures equivalent to the eu directive on taxation of interest income from savings. the eu-liechtenstein agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information concluded in october 2015 is of particular importance as it allows for more effective action to be taken against tax fraud and tax evasion. it is important that the eu conclude similar agreements with third european countries and update them if necessary, as this is the only way to effectively tackle tax fraudsters who try to hide their taxable income and assets from european tax authorities. the eu is welcome to consider liechtenstein as a partner in international tax cooperation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report because i consider the european ombudsman's proposals to be important and particularly timely. i agree with the approach that a common european response to the refugee crisis naturally requires strengthening the powers, resources and organisation of frontex, but we must not lose sight of the fact that our border guards are faced with a mass of vulnerable people who are fleeing real dangers and not hostile ones. the new challenge requires frontex staff to be both efficient and flexible, with a humane approach. the ombudsman's report provides the appropriate legal and human backing for this, in particular by introducing a new, transparent complaints mechanism that protects the rights and identity of complainants while minimising the possibility of abuse, in keeping with the letter and spirit of the charter of fundamental rights. i also believe that it is appropriate to give priority to humanitarian considerations and the human rights of refugees in frontex's work, because it is a fact that within the union - even at the level of the governments and heads of government of certain member states - there is a conscious combination of anti-refugee political sentiment, xenophobic incitement, the challenges of migration and international terrorism. in this political context, the ombudsman's report can only be welcomed as both a warning and a concrete package of proposals to protect common european values.
in writing. ‒ frontex's task is to ensure the effective implementation of common rules on requirements and procedures for the control and surveillance of external borders, while respecting fundamental rights, through closer coordination of operational cooperation between member states. as an integral part of its mandate, frontex should establish operational cooperation with non-eu countries in key areas such as information exchange, risk analysis, training, research and development, joint operations (including joint return operations) and pilot projects. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the primary objective of the report on sustainable urban mobility is to provide a solution to the congestion problems of large eu cities and the resulting greenhouse gas emissions. the report shall take into account the possibilities available under the greenery item. however, the report also contains some objectionable elements. it is based on a european approach to urban development, which takes account of the geographical, developmental and cultural diversity of the eu, and is based on eu rules and standards, and is coordinated by the commission, and goes beyond the subject of urban mobility. it thus limits the national competence of governments to formulate and implement development policies in their own territory. there is also a risk that the local development policy coordinated by the commission could have a negative impact on cities in the countries of central and eastern europe. the application of the transport 2050 strategy and the realisation of its objectives is a pipe dream. it is not possible at eu level to halve the use of all conventional motor vehicles by 2030 and to completely remove them from mobility by 2050. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measure is compatible with the internal market. despite these objections, the report is generally positive and i therefore supported its adoption.
in writing. ‒ sustainability and resource efficiency are essential for the long-term development of urban transport. joint european work should be undertaken to ensure the sustainability, preservation and development of urban mobility, which requires high levels of investment. these measures will have a positive impact not only on transport but also on the economy and the labour market. of course, there are many other positive effects that can be generated by this development, such as reducing co2 emissions, improving quality of life and health, developing infrastructure and stimulating innovation. we need to set ambitious targets, and our regions and cities need to work together to achieve them. the original approach was too green and the report had to be adapted several times. however, the amendments have led to a draft that is acceptable to the majority and is feasible, and which i personally supported by voting in favour of.

in writing. ‒ the committee on transport and tourism has proposed a resolution on sustainable urban mobility to the european parliament. in its report, the commission points out that 80% of europeans will soon live in cities. while mobility should be a right for all citizens, the excessive use of conventional fuel vehicles and the associated congestion limits this right. the car is the main means of mobility for 43% of the world's kilometres and for three quarters of european journeys; the total annual additional cost of congestion in european cities is estimated at around eur 80 billion. at the same time, 50% of trips within the urban area are less than 5 km, meaning that they could easily be made on foot, by bicycle or by public transport. the report therefore aims to shift urban mobility towards sustainable modes of transport. i voted for the motion.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on sustainable, energy-efficient urban mobility, as i share the view that this is a right for all citizens, including those with reduced mobility. more and more people live in cities, and that's why it's important to formulate principles that make it easier for people to move around in a sustainable way. this should be done in such a way that transport has the lowest possible environmental and health impact, for example by reducing the tax incentive for urban transport vehicles running on diesel. urban transport alone accounts for a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions, which need to be reduced to meet the european union's 2030 targets. as stated in a previous report, air pollution in the major cities of the european union causes about 400 000 premature deaths a year. this is often the case with fine particulate matter, which is largely emitted by diesel engines, which account for 55% of the european vehicle fleet. this trend, in my view, has not only environmental and health implications but also economic ones, as member states' energy dependence and energy bills are increasing. i therefore agree that immediate action is needed and that urban mobility today and in the future should be based largely on green mobility and cooperative networks.
in writing. ‒ mobility should not be an end in itself, but a right for all citizens. soon, 80% of europeans will live in cities, so mobility should make it easier for everyone, including people with reduced mobility, to get to school, work, and access culture, leisure and healthcare. this report sets out to move urban mobility towards sustainable modes of transport in order to meet the challenges of our century, protecting the climate, our health and environment, our well-being and our safety. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on visa-free short-stay travel is both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the country concerned, which is of great political importance, and a further means of strengthening economic and cultural links and encouraging political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the available data on mobility show a high level of trust in visa applicants and a low number of rejected applications. the country poses no threat to irregular migration, security or public order. i also consider it important that visa-free travel is not a negligible means of bringing the population of the european union and the citizens of the country concerned closer together. the visa waiver agreement will allow citizens to benefit fully, more cheaply and more easily from the opportunities offered by the partnership.
in writing. ‒ today we are giving our consent to the conclusion of the agreement with the eu, which has already been negotiated with the commission. the purpose of the proposal on visa facilitation agreement is the conclusion of an agreement on facilitating the issue of short-stay visas. the agreement also provides for visa-free travel for the citizens of the european union for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders) travelling for all kinds of purposes, except for the purpose of carrying out a paid activity. we support today’s resolution and believe that it is important to have a good agreement because it helps to fight organised crime and terrorist organisations.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on visa-free short-stay travel is both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the dominican community, which is of great political importance in the context of the cotonou agreement, and a further tool for strengthening economic and cultural ties and encouraging political dialogue on various issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the economy of dominica is primarily based on agriculture, which contributed an average of 11% of the country's gdp between 2000 and 2010. as a small island developing country, dominica has made significant efforts to diversify and has significant growth potential, for example in tourism and geothermal energy production. the agreement will boost tourism and strengthen trade and investment links. i voted in favour of the recommendation.

in writing. ‒ today we are giving our consent to the conclusion of the agreement with the eu which has already been negotiated with the european commission. the purpose of the proposal on visa facilitation is the conclusion of an agreement on facilitating the issue of short-stay visas. the agreement also provides for visa-free travel for the citizens of the european union for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (ordinary, diplomatic, service/official and special passport holders) travelling for all kinds of purposes, except for the purpose of carrying out paid activity. we support today’s resolution and believe that it is important to have a good agreement because it helps to fight organised crime and terrorist organisations.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on visa-free short-stay travel is both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the independent state of samoa, which is of great political importance in the context of the cotonou agreement, and a further tool for strengthening economic and cultural ties and encouraging political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the economy of samoa is one of the most dynamic in the pacific. the agricultural sector employs two thirds of the workforce and accounts for 90% of exports. the eu is currently negotiating a comprehensive economic partnership agreement with 14 countries in the pacific region, including samoa. the union and samoa shall cooperate in the following areas of economic cooperation: in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 539/2001 was amended by regulation of the european parliament and of the council of 20 may 2014 to include the independent state of samoa among the third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement when crossing the external borders of the member states. the commission subsequently negotiated between 19 november and 15 december 2014 the conclusion of a bilateral agreement to that effect between the european union and the independent state of samoa. the agreement was initialled in brussels on 28 may 2015 and has since been awaiting parliament's approval. i voted in favour of the draft agreement, as recommended by the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on visa-free short-stay travel is both a success in deepening relations between the european union and the united arab emirates and a further means of strengthening economic and cultural ties and encouraging political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. more than 150 000 european citizens have settled in the uae, the vast majority of them having moved there for economic reasons. some 1.6 million europeans visit the uae every year. in 2014, around 230 000 uae nationals travelled to europe, mainly for business or luxury tourism. according to the world organisation for migration, the most important obstacles to uae nationals travelling to europe are the visa requirement, the cost of the visa and the need to plan well in advance. the visa waiver agreement will allow many europeans to visit relatives in the uae more easily and to travel for business or personal reasons, including uae nationals. not to mention that it already has a number of direct flights to the european union. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the recommendation.
in writing. the vote on the report on cooperation between the uae and europol, which is increasingly becoming a centre for economic and financial crime, is on the agenda today. the proceeds of intra-eu fraud and money laundering are often reinvested there, and the criminals involved in these frauds have also found refuge there. so we're supposed to make it easier for criminals to get a visa? i could only vote no on that.

in writing. ‒ the draft implementing decision shall formalise the conclusion by eurojust of the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim) and eurojust, which falls within the remit of the committee on legal affairs under annex vi to the rules of procedure of the european parliament. the purpose of the memorandum of understanding is to promote cooperation between eurojust and the bphh in accordance with their respective mandates. eurojust and the bphh decided to conclude the memorandum of understanding because they are willing and able to establish strategic cooperation with each other to help achieve their respective objectives. the memorandum of understanding is in the common interest of eurojust and the bphh and should therefore be approved by the council. i voted for the settlement.

in writing. ‒ the current legislation relating to council decision 2007/436/ec, euratom had to be reviewed at the end of 2014 due to the particularly large vat and gni-based adjustment established for each member state. at the same time, the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) should be revised in the light of the experience gained from the 2014 adjustments. the european parliament stresses the need for effective rules on the way in which member states make their contributions to the eu budget available in a timely manner, as this will enable the commission to manage the fund efficiently. i support the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of the vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to reduce a significant part of the payment arrears of the previous year to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds, and to reduce the interest on late payments. the modification of the methods for adjusting the contributions is aimed at avoiding a situation similar to that of 2014. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.

in writing. ‒ explanation of vote resolution amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 609/2014 on the methods and mechanisms for providing traditional own resources accruing from vat and gni and on measures to address cash needs the legislation currently in force relating to council decision 2007/436/ec, euratom had to be reviewed at the end of 2014 due to the particularly large vat and gni adjustments established for individual member states. at the same time, the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) should be revised in the light of the experience gained from the 2014 adjustments. the european parliament stresses the need for effective rules on the way in which member states make their contributions to the eu budget available in a timely manner, as this will enable the commission to manage the fund efficiently. parliament supports the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to reduce a significant part of the payment arrears of the previous year to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds, and to reduce interest on late payments. the modification of the methods for adjusting the contributions is aimed at avoiding a situation similar to that of 2014. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the council to amend regulation (eu, euratom) no 609/2014 on the methods and procedure for making available own resources accruing from traditional own resources, from vat and from gni, and on measures to meet cash requirements. the amendment aims to introduce effective rules to ensure that member states make their contributions to the union budget in a timely manner. it also allows the commission to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of the vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year. in its report, the committee on budgets recommends that parliament approve the commission's draft, with amendments. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ the current legislation relating to council decision 2007/436/ec, euratom had to be reviewed at the end of 2014 due to the particularly large vat and gni-based adjustment established for each member state. at the same time, the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) should be revised in the light of the experience gained from the 2014 adjustments. the european parliament stresses the need for effective rules on the way in which member states make their contributions to the eu budget available in a timely manner, as this will enable the commission to manage the fund efficiently. parliament supports the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to reduce a significant part of the payment arrears of the previous year to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds, and to reduce interest on late payments. the modification of the methods for adjusting the contributions is aimed at avoiding a situation similar to that of 2014.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i agree with the objective of making the system for allocating member states' budgetary contributions more efficient, thereby helping the commission to better manage its cash. i think it is effective that the commission will now be able to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of the vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to reduce the payment arrears of the previous year for some european funds. it is of the utmost importance that both the payments and the payments to beneficiaries from the union budget are made in a timely and efficient manner. i also agreed with the point that political interference in the way the eu budget is financed should be avoided at all costs. i also supported the request to the commission to examine and make recommendations for greater coherence in the national accounting of member states' contributions to the eu budget.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers and self-employed persons made redundant as a result of globalisation, as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns, or as a result of the prolongation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis. on 12 june 2015, finland submitted an application, with reference number egf/2015/005 fi/computer programming, for a financial contribution from the egf, following redundancies in the regions of länsi-suomi, helsinki-uusima, etelä-suomi and pohjois- ja itä-suomi in finland. the application was supplemented by additional information in accordance with article 8 (3) of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013. the application complies with the requirements for determining the financial contribution from the egf as laid down in article 13 of regulation (eu) no 1309/2013. the european parliament therefore supported by a large majority the disbursement of a financial contribution of eur 2 623 200 to be granted on the basis of the request submitted by finland. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the proposal supports the possibility for the commission to ask member states to pay three-twelfths of vat and gni-based resources in the first half of the year, in order to enable the commission to reduce a significant part of the payment arrears of the previous year to the european agricultural guarantee fund and the european structural and investment funds, and to reduce the interest on late payments. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the prosecutor's office of the supreme court of the hellenic republic has requested the suspension of the immunity of georgios kyrtsos, member of the european parliament, in relation to possible legal action to be taken in relation to an alleged criminal offence. according to the request, the representative is accused of failing to pay part of the salary of one of their employees to two newspaper publishing companies that he once ran. as the committee on legal affairs points out in its report, the alleged act is not related to georgios kyrtsos' mandate as a member of the european parliament but to his previous activity as the head of two news publishing companies, and there is no reason to assume that the criminal proceedings were initiated with the aim of causing political damage to the member, since they were initiated several years before he became a member of parliament, and therefore it proposes that the parliament suspend the immunity of georgios kyrtsos. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ on 21 july 2015, the immunity of georgios kyrtsos was requested by the prosecutor's office of the greek supreme court from the ep in connection with a complaint concerning the non-payment of wages by the labour inspectorate of eastern acre. kyrtsos is accused of not paying part of the salary due to his former employee; the alleged act is not related to the mandate of georgios kyrtsos as a member of the european parliament, but to his previous activity as the head of two news publishing companies, and therefore the rapporteur proposed to suspend kyrtsos' immunity. i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the public prosecutor's office of the supreme court of the hellenic republic has requested the suspension of the immunity of mr stelios kouloglou, member of the european parliament, in connection with proceedings brought on charges of defamation and breach of trust. the charges relate to statements that stelios kouloglou allegedly made to the press in 2010 regarding the integrity of certain employees of the patras prison when he was working as a television reporter. as the committee on legal affairs points out in its report, the alleged offence is not linked to the mandate of mr stelios kouloglou as a member of the european parliament but to his activities as a television journalist at the time, and there is no reason to believe that the criminal proceedings were initiated with the aim of causing political damage to the member, since they were initiated several years before he became a member of parliament, and it therefore proposes that the parliament suspend the immunity of mr stelios kouloglou. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ on 7 august 2015, the prosecutor of the supreme court of greece requested the suspension of the immunity of stelios kouloglou in proceedings for defamation and libel. kouloglou allegedly made a statement insulting certain employees of the patras prison in 2010 when he was making television reports as a journalist. the rapporteur considers that the measure is not linked to the mandate of the ep of kouloglou and therefore proposes to suspend the right of immunity. i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide support for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis and to support their reintegration into the labour market. finland has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf, following the redundancies of 1603 workers in 69 enterprises in the 'computer programming, consultancy and related services' sector. finland plans seven types of measures for the benefit of the workers made redundant as a result of the aid: i. coaching and other preparatory measures, ii. employment and business services, iii. training, iv. salary support, v. start-up aid, vi. business incentives and services for new entrepreneurs, vii. reimbursement of travel, accommodation and relocation costs. the measures are expected to involve 1200 redundant workers. in its report, the committee on budgets concludes that the application fulfils the eligibility criteria set out in the egf regulation and therefore proposes that parliament approve the disbursement of a financial contribution from the egf of eur 2 623 200 to be granted on the basis of the application submitted by finland. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ the european commission proposes to incorporate the recommendations of the north-east atlantic fisheries commission (neafc) into eu fisheries legislation as regards rules for atlantic fishing activities. in line with the epp's guidelines, i voted in favour of approving the text of the political agreement. it is clear that the european union is forced to limit its sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. the reasoned measures taken to maintain them have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries.
in writing. ‒ the convention on future multilateral fisheries cooperation in the north-east atlantic, to which the european union is a party, aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum exploitation of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic, thereby providing sustainable environmental and social benefits. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal to extend the autonomous trade measures for the western balkan countries and territories participating in the stabilisation and association process for a further five years, until 31 december 2020, is welcomed. this preferential trade arrangement has contributed to the increase in imports of western balkan products into the union. in 2013, the eu was the largest trading partner of the region in terms of both imports (72,7%) and exports (81,8%). these trade preferences, complementing existing bilateral agreements, together support economic integration with the union and thus contribute to the political stability and economic development of the region. these measures should be understood in the wider context of the union's policy towards the western balkan countries, the ultimate aim of which is to bring them closer to the union. the suspension of trade preferences for bosnia and herzegovina should be seen as an incentive to resolve the current differences with the union regarding the adjustment of the interim agreement with the union. it is hoped that the new authorities in bosnia and herzegovina will be able to resolve this outstanding issue, taking advantage of the positive momentum of the new eu approach to the country adopted by the foreign affairs council on 15 december 2014.
in writing. ‒ the commission has proposed to the european parliament and the council to adopt a regulation of the european parliament and of the council suspending the application of council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 as regards bosnia and herzegovina. the liberalisation of trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is being achieved in the case of bosnia and herzegovina through a number of stabilisation and association agreements and an interim agreement. following the accession of croatia to the union on 13 july 2013, bosnia and herzegovina has not yet contributed to the adaptation of the interim agreement to take into account the preferential trade traditionally existing between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina before 1 july 2013 under the central european free trade agreement (cefta). as a result, the preferential quotas established in the interim agreement in 2008 for 27 eu member states are now used by 28 member states. after three rounds of negotiations with bosnia and herzegovina, no agreement was reached. the commission therefore proposes not to extend automatically the autonomous trade measures granted to bosnia and herzegovina. the eu and bosnia and herzegovina shall cooperate in the implementation of the agreement on trade facilitation and trade facilitation between the eu and bosnia and herzegovina. in its report, the committee on international trade recommends that parliament adopt the commission proposal with amendments. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report and the treaty amendments proposed in it, as i believe that it could fundamentally contribute to the fulfilment of the conditions for the european integration of bosnia and herzegovina. i consider it appropriate that the eu should grant unilateral trade preferences to bosnia and herzegovina alongside other western balkan countries with an extended effect until 2020 in order to further adapt to the accession conditions, but i also agree that the differences between the two parties arising from the implementation of the interim agreement should be resolved as soon as possible. this is the aim of the proposed amendment, which allows the unilateral concession to be suspended from 1 january 2016 if the necessary conditions are not met. i also think it is a good step to introduce the extension of democratic rights under european standards through a human rights clause in the terms of the agreement, thereby bringing the agreement more into line with the accession conditions under the copenhagen criteria. the european parliament resolution i am hoping will inspire the government of this important balkan partner to take immediate and effective measures in these areas as well, in order to meet the accession criteria as closely as possible.
in writing. ‒ the liberalisation of trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is being achieved through a number of stabilisation and association agreements and an interim agreement in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. the extension of the current preferences is intended to allow time for the beneficiary countries to adjust the preferences under the basic regulation and the preferences granted under the stabilisation and association agreements and the interim agreements. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ there are clear operational needs for europol to cooperate with the united arab emirates, since according to europol, the united arab emirates are increasingly relevant in the fight against organised crime. this proposal concerns the proposed approval of a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the united arab emirates. such agreements may concern the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. the operational cooperation agreement also includes the exchange of personal data. we support this strategic cooperation agreement with the united arab emirates, since it would aid and reinforce the fight against financial fraud and would contribute to enhancing international cooperation in the field of financial investigation and other relevant criminal matters.
in writing. ‒ article 23 (2) of the current council decision on europol (decision 2009/371/jha) requires the council to authorise the conclusion of international cooperation agreements with third countries or international organisations after consulting the european parliament. such an agreement may cover the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. the operational cooperation agreement shall also include the exchange of personal data. this proposal aims at the adoption of the proposed strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the united arab emirates. such a strategic agreement excludes the exchange of personal data, and therefore the issue of data protection is not relevant in this case. the information exchanged may include the field of expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analysis and information on criminal investigation procedures and crime prevention methods, as well as training activities and the provision of advice and support for specific criminal investigations. i voted in favour of the conclusion of a strategic cooperation agreement between the uae and europol as it would help and strengthen the fight against financial fraud and contribute to international cooperation in the field of financial investigations and other relevant crimes.
in writing. the uae is increasingly becoming a centre for economic and financial crime, according to europol. the proceeds of crimes such as vat fraud, intra-eu trader-disappearing fraud and money laundering are often reinvested in the eu, and the criminals involved in these frauds have also found refuge there. as with all reports that serve the judiciary, the fight against corruption and crime, i voted for this one.
in writing. ‒ the council proposed the adoption of a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the united arab emirates. europol has a clear operational need to cooperate with the united arab emirates. the country is playing an increasing role in the fight against organised crime, as it is becoming an increasingly important centre for economic and financial crime. proceeds from crimes such as vat fraud, intra-community disappearing trader fraud and money laundering are reinvested in the uae and key actors involved in these frauds have also found refuge here. the report of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs recommends that parliament give its consent to the conclusion of the strategic cooperation agreement, as it would help and strengthen the fight against financial fraud and contribute to international cooperation in the field of financial investigations and other relevant crimes. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament not objecting to the agreement between europol and the authorities of the united arab emirates providing for strategic cooperation in the prosecution of terrorism and other serious forms of international crime. i considered the fact that the focus of economic and financial crime - including money laundering, tax evasion, etc. - has shifted towards the gulf region in recent times. the commission should be able to provide the necessary information to the member states and to the commission in order to ensure that the criminal law is applied in a uniform manner. however, i am correct that the europol/eea agreement does not cover the exchange of personal data and therefore cannot raise concerns as regards the application of eu data protection standards and rules.
in writing. ‒ under the current council decision on europol, the council, after consulting the european parliament, is to authorise the conclusion of international cooperation agreements with third countries or international organisations. this proposal aims at the adoption of a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and the united arab emirates. it appears that europol has a clear operational need to cooperate with the united arab emirates. according to europol, the uae is playing an increasing role in the fight against organised crime as the country becomes an increasingly important centre for economic and financial crime. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the energy union report provides a balanced overview of the steps that can bring europe closer to a european energy policy for consumers. the report confirms that the european energy policy aims to strengthen security of supply, increase energy efficiency and at affordable prices. this will require, where necessary, the construction of new infrastructure, further harmonisation of the market and enforcement of legislation. the report anticipates that the energy union can boost europe's international competitiveness and create new jobs through, for example, technological research and development, stimulating innovation and investments in energy efficiency. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the report.

in writing. there were a number of amendments to the report which would have made it substantially more balanced, but unfortunately these were not voted on, so i chose to abstain. if the objective was to provide european citizens with stable and cheap access to clean energy, the construction of the south stream gas pipeline through bulgaria should have been supported. nuclear power plants should not have been shut down either, because they produce electricity with zero carbon dioxide, and in fact, nuclear plants do not emit radioactive material into the atmosphere, but coal plants do. at the current technological level, renewables are not a viable alternative to conventional power plants, but they are locally important, of course. if we do not want to be left behind in the quest for clean and economical energy, it is worth studying the new results, the fourth generation nuclear reactor, which is already operational and can produce energy from the cheap by-products of uranium enrichment.
in writing. ‒ the energy union is one of the juncker commission's key declared strategic objectives. the report by the committee on industry, research and energy strongly supports both this and the key objectives to be achieved, such as the secure supply of cheap energy to european citizens, the elimination of energy poverty, competitive energy prices for the development of european industry, energy saving, the achievement of the ambitious environmental objectives previously announced, in particular the radical reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the strong reduction of the eu's energy dependence. it takes account of previous decisions and declarations on this subject, addresses the main obstacles to the achievement of the energy union and proposes a european parliament resolution on a number of related issues, which may further guide the way in which the strategic objectives are to be achieved. i was pleased to vote in favour of the report as a demanding contribution to one of the union's main strategic objectives.

in writing. ‒ i believe that the concrete proposals contained in the motion for a resolution will bring us closer to the energy union, which is why i voted in favour of it. i agree that the energy union should adopt a common approach to achieving a fully integrated internal energy market, security of supply, the best use of the union's energy resources, reducing energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions. research and development and innovation should play a major role in this process. i believe that the energy union should be about people, not governments, who need to be provided with secure, sustainable and affordable energy. at present, some governments continue to support fossil or nuclear development for reasons visible or invisible, but the money for these should be used for renewable energy production. although nuclear energy is not fossil energy, safety issues, such as the storage of spent fuel, are encouraging many member states to switch to renewable energy. it should be noted that the switch to renewable energy is necessary not only for environmental reasons but also because it could save billions of euros globally.

in writing. ‒ the report is a response to the commission communication 'achieving the 10% target for energy interconnection'. the report welcomes the achievement of the 10% target for energy interconnection. it stresses that the interconnection of energy networks is a prerequisite for the achievement of an integrated internal electricity market, which, if properly designed, can help europe to meet its climate objectives. i agree with the report that the lengthy permitting process makes it very difficult to build new high voltage lines. it is important for member states to facilitate faster procedures. the report reinforces the regional approach to market linkages. in the case of hungary, the electricity interconnection indicator is 29% , thus far above the 10% interconnection target , and therefore does not impose any new obligations on the country. i agree with the principles and the direction set out in the report and therefore voted in favour of adopting the report.
in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report is a response to the commission communication 'achieving the 10% target for energy interconnection'. the report welcomes the achievement of the 10% target for energy interconnection. the report emphasises that the interconnection of energy networks is a prerequisite for the achievement of an integrated internal electricity market, which, if properly designed, can help europe to meet its climate objectives. the report notes that the lengthy permitting procedure makes it very difficult to install new high voltage lines; and calls on member states to facilitate faster procedures. furthermore, the report reinforces the regional approach in the context of market coupling. in the case of hungary, the electricity interconnection indicator is 29% , thus far above the 10% interconnection target , and therefore does not impose any new obligations on the country. i agree with the principles and directions set out in the report, and as a member of the hungarian delegation to the people's party, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on industry, research and energy reflects in particular the european commission's communication achieving the 10% interconnection target for energy networks, which it welcomes as a positive step towards achieving the 10% interconnection target and the more efficient functioning of the internal eu electricity market. it considers network interconnection as a means of creating an internal energy market which allows the free flow of energy. it stresses that interconnection is a strategic principle which not only allows for a more efficient management of the inevitable disruptions, but also for the increasing integration of energy from renewable sources into the european energy system. it points out that a fully integrated internal market for electricity would increase safety and reduce electricity price fluctuations, saving european consumers an estimated eur 1240 billion per year by 2030. it recalls that pan-european interconnection could reduce electricity prices by at least eur 2 per megawatt hour and would allow europe to meet most of its electricity needs from renewable energy sources. i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which contains proposals on an important part of the energy union. the report highlights that the 10% interconnection target for energy networks by 2020 is a useful target and an important step towards a common energy system. the report regrets that 12 member states, mainly on the periphery of the union, are not meeting the 10% target for electricity interconnection and thus remain largely isolated from the internal electricity market. i believe that this isolation is not conducive to the creation of an energy union. i share the view that in the medium term and up to 2030, there is a clear need for regions to agree on ambitious and evidence-based complementary interconnection targets. i agree that renewable energy, a sustainable energy architecture that leads to better energy efficiency and energy savings, and an internal energy market that allows the free flow of energy are important tools for a stable, secure, independent, inclusive, transparent and competitive energy system in the union. all of this creates high-quality jobs and wealth in a future-oriented, sustainable economy.

in writing. ‒ the european progress microfinance facility was originally set up to support growth and job creation and to combat social and financial exclusion. the newly adopted own-initiative report on the implementation of the instrument, which has been running as a pilot project since 2010, revealed a number of shortcomings. the project failed to achieve its main objective: the impact on job creation was lower than expected, despite the fact that without the microcredit many beneficiaries would have been completely excluded from the credit market. of all the enterprises supported by the facility, 44% were in operation for less than one year and only 56% were in operation the following year. the creditworthiness and entrepreneurial capacity of persons in long-term unemployment should not be overestimated when applying this instrument. the commission notes that the 2013 commission report on the implementation of the instrument is very general and does not contain any specifics.
in writing. ‒ the european progress microfinance facility , which receives financial contributions from the union and the european investment bank, is managed by the european investment fund (eif) and is expected to receive additional funding from private investors was originally set up to support growth and job creation and to combat social and financial exclusion. the newly adopted own-initiative report on the implementation of the instrument, which has been running as a pilot project since 2010, revealed a number of shortcomings. i voted for the people's party, with a few exceptions. it failed to achieve its main objective: the impact on job creation was smaller than expected, despite the fact that without microcredit many beneficiaries would have been completely excluded from the credit market. of all the enterprises supported by the facility, 44% were in operation for less than one year and only 56% were in operation the following year. the creditworthiness and entrepreneurial capacity of persons in long-term unemployment should not be overestimated when applying this instrument. the commission notes that the 2013 commission implementing report on the instrument is very general and does not contain any specifics. nevertheless, to include this tool in the solution to the migration crisis that emerged in 2015 is a very irresponsible, wishful thinking approach, given the skills and labour market competitiveness of migrants, their competencies and the complete lack of statistics and impact studies on this.
