in writing. ‒ progress microfinance is currently available in only 22 of the 28 member states. this is due to the different levels of development of european national economies, different market interests and different regulatory conditions. the progress microfinance facility has a social dimension and aims to facilitate access to micro-credit for the creation or promotion of micro-enterprises. progress is an important and effective tool for achieving the eu's employment and social objectives under the europe 2020 strategy. the progress tool helps people to (re) enter the labour market, unlock entrepreneurial potential, acquire new skills through training and mentoring, and gives people dignity by enabling them to take responsibility for their own destiny. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ in 2010, the union established the progress microfinance facility for the period 2010 to 2016, with a total amount of eur 205 million, to provide europe's socially and financially disadvantaged people with a chance to create decent living conditions by facilitating access to micro-credit to set up or promote micro-enterprises. the employment and social committee report found that progress has proved to be an important and effective tool for achieving the eu's employment and social objectives under the europe 2020 strategy. the newly created firms generate a significant number of new jobs, and about 85% of these jobs are created within micro-enterprises. the report points out that micro-credit in europe should be seen primarily as a social policy tool to give people in difficult social situations a chance, as there are other support options available to promote smes and innovative ideas. it stresses the need to reconsider the eu definition of microcredit and adapt it to the current situation. finally, it proposes to continue the progress microcredit programme. i supported the adoption of the report.

in writing. ‒ microfinance contributes to the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives, as microfinance can help people to escape poverty and unemployment, restore their dignity and enhance cohesion in communities by improving social inclusion and minimising social inequalities. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ in line with the epp guidelines, i voted in favour of the adoption of the non-legislative report. the debate on the powers of the european parliament and the council must be brought to an end, the adoption of fishing quotas and technical measures must be simplified and accelerated, and the range of scientific organisations involved in the preparation of the proposal must be widened. it is clear that the european union is forced to limit its sea fishing to the extent necessary to maintain marine fish stocks. 30% of the world's oceans are overfished, and marine fish stocks are in danger. the reasoned measures taken to maintain them have led to a continuous and significant decline in the amount of marine fish caught. the cfp should therefore pay much more attention to sustainable fisheries, i.e. aquaculture, and in particular freshwater fisheries. a significant part of the hungarian wetlands is located in natura 2000 areas. these fish farms do not represent any threat to the natural values of these areas. in fact, in many cases it is our closed systems of wetlands that have created and preserved unique associations of aquatic habitats. therefore, freshwater aquaculture should be given priority and maximum support from the union. moreover, this area should be freed from unnecessarily stringent and unnecessary sustainability standards that are justified only for marine fisheries.
in writing. ‒ the 2013 reform of the common fisheries policy included the objective of achieving maximum sustainable yield (msy) through an ecosystem-based approach. the primary means of achieving these objectives are technical measures and multiannual plans as safeguards . however, since 2009 very little progress has been made in the legislative documents on technical measures and multiannual plans. in the case of multiannual plans, this was due to an interinstitutional 'deadlock' caused by the inclusion of the allocation of fishing opportunities in the commission's legislative proposals for multiannual plans as part of the catch control rules, which led to differences of opinion in relation to article 43 tfeu. as regards technical measures, the difficulties arose from the need to align the legislation with the treaty of lisbon. the co-legislators must find a pragmatic solution to make rapid progress on the multiannual plans in the light of the case law of the european court of justice. in addition, effective participation of stakeholders in the preparation and implementation of multiannual plans should be enhanced. finally, the multiannual plans should be adopted as soon as possible. this avoids the regulation of long-term measures by means of discard plans, which by their nature should only contain transitional measures. i voted in favour of the report.

madam president, officer, i have to go. i welcome the fact that the new security package finally focuses on the protection of the external borders. because it's now clear what the hungarian government has been saying since august: we can't deal with the migration problem within europe until we secure our external borders. this is also a condition for safeguarding the schengen system. of course, the protection of schengen borders is primarily the responsibility and task of the member states. we can maintain an area without internal borders as long as the external border is protected. this conviction guided the decision of the visegrad four when, on behalf of the friends of schengen, they renewed their commitment to the protection of the external borders. any proposal that strengthens and makes more effective the protection of the external borders, which promotes prevention and return, is therefore welcome. at the same time, of course, caution is needed in the elaboration of the details surrounding the sensitive issue of national sovereignty. because otherwise it could lead to a debate that is neither timely nor necessary in the current crisis, which is all the more urgently needed for concrete action at the external borders.
madam president, please. the schengen system is one of the european union's few real achievements, with the free movement of borders between the countries within the system. but schengen is also one of the biggest failures of the european union. as the vice president said, a million and a half migrants have arrived this year at the schengen borders that should have been protected, and he's talking about "they finally want to act" and "they need to stop the dangerous elements at the external border". not only must we stop the dangerous elements, but also the millions of economic migrants. and on the liberal side, there is the incredible phrase that if a country protects its national border, which is also schengen, it is national egoism, and they want to deny the right of the nation states to protect their borders, and they are also projecting an image of a "united states of europe", which we will prevent.
in writing. the problems of refugee arrivals and terrorist attacks have made it clear that national solutions, the refusal to cooperate, the shifting of responsibility will only bring trouble to the european community. we also see that if we want to maintain the european achievement of free movement, the schengen area, we must also take on a shared responsibility and guarantee for the protection of borders. i therefore welcome and consider the commission's proposal to set up a single european border and coast guard to be an important step forward. i am convinced that this is the only way to ensure that the control of people entering the union is carried out in a humane but effective manner at all the external borders of the union. i find it outrageous that some member states want to use this plan to maintain a misconception of national autonomy, and thus risk the security of other member states and of the citizens of the union. it is particularly disgusting that the hungarian government, which has been saying up to now that we need to protect our external borders more strongly, to guarantee security, is among them. it has once again become clear that the orbán government is doing everything it can to prevent the european institutions from acting effectively and unitedly on the issues of asylum, counter-terrorism and the protection of eu borders, only to then falsely point to 'brussels' as the cause of the problems.

in writing. in recent weeks, representatives of some western governments have proposed the creation of a mini-schengen area, which would cover only a few, typically founding, member states. it is striking that the proposal would exclude from free movement the central and eastern european member states, which are the countries that most strictly adhere to the schengen agreement and have protected the union's external borders from uncontrolled immigration. central europe's commitment to schengen is demonstrated by the visegrad countries' joint patrols at the southern borders of the schengen area and the union, the serbian-hungarian and croatian-hungarian borders, and by the presence of more than 300 border guards at the borders of greece. the unilateral change of the schengen area is an unfair and absurd idea, which is an even worse response to a previous bad policy decision, and which clearly seeks to punish those member states which are effectively tackling illegal immigration. the free movement guaranteed by the schengen agreement is one of the european union's most important achievements, the dismantling or limitation of which would cause immeasurable economic damage to the entire continent. the reintroduction of border controls would not only make life more difficult for millions of european citizens, but would also cause serious damage to international transport, industry, trade or tourism. for all these reasons, we expect the european council to be the most resolute in its support for the preservation of the schengen system and the strict protection of the union's external borders.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support to workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. on 6 november, the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf for ireland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant by pwa international ltd and the reintegration into the labour market of 108 young people not in employment, education or training. the commission has concluded that the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf are met in the application, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the egf regulation. the personalised services for redundant workers comprise five types of measures: (i) career guidance, career planning and promotion, (ii) egf training aid, (iii) training and continuing education programmes, (iv) higher education programmes and (v) temporary grants. on the basis of the above, i voted in favour of the adoption of the proposal.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund aims to provide support for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade or made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis and to support their reintegration into the labour market. ireland has submitted an application for a financial contribution from the egf following 108 redundancies at pwa international ltd, operating in the machinery, equipment, plant and equipment repair and commissioning sector. ireland plans to provide five types of measures to the dismissed workers subject to the aid: (i) career guidance, career planning and promotion, (ii) egf training aid, (iii) training and continuing education programmes, (iv) higher education programmes and (v) limited duration grants. the measures are expected to involve all the workers made redundant. in its report, the committee on budgets notes that the application does not fulfil the traditional eligibility criteria for the number of redundancies laid down in the egf regulation, and that it has been submitted on the basis of the intervention criterion under article 4 (2) of that regulation, which allows for derogation in exceptional cases. the report agrees with the european commission that the arguments presented by ireland justify the application of the 'exceptional circumstances' criterion and that ireland is therefore entitled to a financial contribution of eur 442 293 under that regulation and therefore recommends that parliament approve the decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund following the request of ireland. i supported the motion.

in writing. ‒ under regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 of the european parliament and of the council on invasive alien species, the commission is to adopt, by means of implementing acts, a list of invasive alien species of union concern. the list in the draft implementing regulation d041932/01 adopted by the commission has been criticised on several occasions by the competent national authorities, interested parties and the public. the environmental protection committee report states that these criticisms are justified in many respects: the list does not take into account species that are among the most harmful invasive alien species in europe. certain terrestrial plant and mammal species are eligible and a well-founded risk assessment is available but are not included in the list, as are some mammal species that are among the most rapidly spreading invasive alien species in europe in recent years, and plant species with a large range and rapid spread with significant and well-documented adverse effects on human health. on the other hand, the list includes species that do not have significant adverse impacts on biodiversity, ecosystem services, human health and the economy, or for which the measures to be taken would result in disproportionate costs. the committee on the environment, public health and food safety considers that the draft commission implementing regulation therefore exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 and therefore proposes that parliament's resolution calls on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft. i voted for the report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament raised an objection in its motion for a resolution to the list of invasive alien species threatening the union, and i supported this objection by voting in favour. this union list is fully binding and directly applicable in all member states and i therefore consider it of the utmost importance that it is properly drawn up. the proposal calls on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft, as the draft exceeds the implementing powers set out in the related regulation. the process does not ensure that the methodology to be used in the risk assessment is applied uniformly by all member states, and therefore it cannot be ensured that member states use the same types of evidence and the same general standards. therefore, for example, the reasons for the inclusion of species in the union list may be based on political rather than scientific grounds. as we know, there are many invasive alien species in europe, and i agree that priority should be given to the regulation of those invasive alien species which are considered to be a threat to the union. the proposal states that an invasive species is considered to be of union concern if the extent of the damage caused by it in the member states concerned justifies the adoption of targeted measures applicable to the whole of the union, including member states not yet affected, even if it is unlikely that they will be affected.
in writing. ‒ the commission shall adopt, by means of implementing acts, a list of invasive alien species of union concern. since there are many invasive alien species, priority should be given to the regulation of those invasive alien species which are considered to be a danger to the union. i voted in favor of the motion.
in writing. ‒ the eu's gmo authorisation system is based on the precautionary principle. accordingly, the safety of genetically modified products should be ascertained before authorisation. a wide range of experts questioned the adequacy of the health safety studies on maize nk 603xt25. the risk assessment carried out shows the following deficiencies: the safety of the double-modified maize line nk603xt25 was established on the basis of the data from the single modifications. but in terms of agronomic and phenotypic characteristics, this genetically modified maize was different from its conventional counterpart. inconceivably, efsa did not consider any of the significant differences to be of such a degree as to require further studies. this and the disregard of the difference in composition between seeds and feed was confirmed by the efsa gmo panel. it should also be noted that longer-term animal feeding trials would have been necessary to establish that this product does not present a risk to human or animal health. the gm maize concerned is also resistant to herbicides containing the active substance glyphosate. therefore, during its cultivation, an increased use of these plant protection products may occur, which subsequently increases the level of residues in the crop. it is also important to note that in 2015, the who classified the herbicide glyphosate as 'probably carcinogenic to humans'. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the parliament's objection to the authorisation of genetically modified maize nk 603xt25.

in writing. ‒ on 17 may 2010, monsanto europe sa submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application to place on the market foods, food ingredients, and feed containing, consisting of, or produced from nk603 × t25 maize. the commission granted an authorisation by commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 on 4 december 2015 for this maize containing the protein cp4epsps, as described in the application, which confers resistance to glyphosate-containing herbicides, and the protein pat, which confers resistance to glufosinate-ammonium-containing herbicides. however, on 20 march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer classified glyphosate as a substance likely to cause cancer in humans. the report by the committee on the environment recommends that parliament should state that all implementing decisions authorising the placing on the market of products containing gmos adopted in accordance with the current, malfunctioning regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 should be suspended until a new regulation is adopted under the tfeu. at the same time, it invites the commission to submit a new legislative proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 taking into account the concerns often expressed by member states that are not only related to the risks posed by gmos to health or the environment. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. other i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the refusal to place on the market products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize, for two reasons. i supported it, firstly, because i consider that the implementing decision in question (and its drafting) are not in conformity with union law. secondly, because it is a genetically modified plant that the international agency for research on cancer, the who cancer agency, has identified as resistant to the potentially carcinogenic glyphosate. this is dangerous for human and animal health because it encourages the use of herbicides containing glyphosate, which can be stored in the plant if used incorrectly. i also think it is important to note that this case shows a systemic flaw, as the european parliament has repeatedly taken a position on genetically modified food and feed in order to protect the health of its electorate and the environment. i think it is right that the commission should take these resolutions into account. the current approval system for genetically modified food and feed does not function properly and needs to be corrected.

in writing. ‒ the proposals in the report reflect the determination of both the european parliament and the european people to prevent companies from jumping from one country to another and reducing their tax liabilities to almost zero through legislative changes. the luxleaks scandal revealed exactly how much tax companies were getting away with by avoiding paying money that could have been used to build schools, hospitals, or to reduce the national debt. corporate tax avoidance costs national budgets billions of euros a year, creates unequal competition between companies and undermines europeans' trust in the state and government. i believe that the swift implementation of the measures proposed by parliament and the oecd would not only make national tax collection more efficient, but would also open up the market to competition and reduce the cost of compliance for companies. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report of the economic and monetary committee, drawing partly on the draft report of the special committee on tax evaluations and other measures similar in nature or effect and partly on the devastating and increasingly damaging practice of aggressive tax planning, concludes that the corporate tax policies of the member states should be made transparent, harmonised and approximated in order to mitigate the losses caused by corporate tax avoidance. it therefore proposes that parliament invite the commission to submit one or more legislative proposals to parliament by the end of june 2016. it makes recommendations on the content of these legislative proposals, which are set out in detail in the annex to the report. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the transparency, harmonisation and approximation of corporate tax policies in the european union. the reporting agents correctly pointed out that the tax assessment system, in addition to being lawfully used, gives rise to abuse and distortion of competition. i agreed with the finding that legislative action at union level is needed to improve the transparency, consistency and convergence of corporate tax policies. recommendations to achieve these, such as public country-by-country reporting by multinational companies, the development of a 'good tax practice' label for companies, mandatory reporting of new tax measures, automatic exchange of information on tax rulings or the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, would all provide an effective solution to the unsustainable situation.
in writing. ‒ recent experience shows that member states cannot act alone against aggressive tax planning. the fact that we have a theoretical single market within the european union requires concerted action. the rapporteur believes that, while respecting the sovereignty of the member states in relation to tax policy, there is a need for eu legislative measures to ensure transparency, harmonisation and convergence of eu corporate tax policies. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ cooperation between the european union and china has a history of 40 years. their strategic relations were established in 1975, a trade and cooperation agreement was signed in 1985, and since then the eu has continuously supported china's sustainable development by strengthening its partnership on political, economic and social reforms. i voted in favour of the report as it reflects the high importance of bilateral strategic relations in addressing global issues such as global and regional security, dealing with the economic crisis, energy security, the prevention of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and nuclear weapons, climate change, the promotion of democracy and human rights, and the fight against organised crime and terrorism. at the same time, i consider it important that the decision calls on the chinese authorities to respect their international commitments in the field of the rule of law and human rights.

in writing. ‒ the world is currently dealing with a humanitarian crisis on a scale never seen before. the duration and severity of these crises are also unprecedented. as a result, there are now more refugees and internally displaced persons than there have been since world war ii. in may 2016, the first humanitarian summit will be held in istanbul, at the initiative of un secretary-general ban ki-moon, with the aim of transforming the current humanitarian system to make it more effective and adapted to new challenges. the report aims to provide clear guidance on this, in particular with regard to food security, population growth and climate change. in addition to reducing vulnerability and managing risk, the report places a strong emphasis on transformation through innovation and making finance more transparent. the report calls for the adoption of a five-year roadmap, including political commitments on development, as the final document of the conference.

in writing. ‒ as today's report shows, there is an unprecedented need for humanitarian assistance worldwide. the number of people in need has reached an unprecedented level. so when we're discussing how to help, we can only think in terms of broad partnerships. my personal experience is that the middle east is one of the focal points of aid today. in the refugee camps in iraq, i was struck by the fact that the eu did not build on the capacities and infrastructure of local church communities and their aid organisations in carrying out projects. well-known organisations such as aid to the church in need have implemented projects in the region worth over €40 million. they have a total of 38 different programs running in iraq alone, and over 100 in syria. these successfully provide basic needs for hundreds of thousands of people, such as housing, education and employment. and the reason these results are worth looking at is because these are the two countries where the current wave of immigration started and is still going to europe. the union must now make a huge effort to give the most deprived a perspective in their own country. it's in the interest of the persecuted. the union should therefore amend its aid rules to ensure that the most affected, including persecuted religious minorities, are included in aid projects. it is noteworthy that today's report is a rethinking of international humanitarian aid, which is why i voted in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the development committee report draws attention to the fact that humanitarian crises of unprecedented scale, severity and duration have resulted in a dramatic increase in the number of people in need of humanitarian assistance. to address these challenges and find solutions, the un secretary-general convened the first humanitarian summit in may 2016. the aim of the event is to transform and adapt the humanitarian system to the rapidly changing landscape of emergencies, making humanitarian action more effective, efficient and sustainable. there is a clear need for a closer link between the humanitarian and development communities and for a shift in focus from response to prevention and prediction. the report highlights that the global humanitarian aid system has reached its limits due to unprecedented levels of need and limited resources, while at the same time the fundamental values of decency, dignity, humanity and solidarity are at stake. the committee on development recommends that parliament should take a position that the union should take the lead and play a key role in the process leading up to the humanitarian summit, in order to achieve a decisive outcome guided by humanitarian principles and the needs of the beneficiaries. to this end, the union must present a firm common position and a united action in istanbul. the report proposes the details of such a position. i supported the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which sets out the tasks of the european union and its member states in preparing for the historic global humanitarian summit in may next year. i was mindful that the eu, as the world's largest donor and a leader in the international political promotion of humanity, has a special responsibility in these more challenging times than ever before. the proportion of people displaced by regional conflicts, especially wars in the middle east, and the resulting wave of migration are now affecting eu member states not only as members of the international community but also at their own borders. i agree that the only way to respond effectively is through a unified eu response, including through the humanitarian action plan. the report goes into detail on possible areas for improving eu humanitarian cooperation, such as international trade, development policy, enlargement and neighbourhood policy, and refugee and migration policy, which i myself consider to be of high importance. i also welcome the fact that the report focuses on addressing the humanitarian crisis situations that are particularly vulnerable for groups such as children, women and the elderly, and i have been trying for some time in my own political work in parliament to draw the eu's political attention to the importance of addressing their specific problems and vulnerabilities.

in writing. ‒ the european industrial metals industry (all kinds of steel, non-ferrous metals, metal alloys, rare earth metals) has recently faced a number of challenges: on the one hand, a significant drop in demand as a result of the crisis, and on the other, a significant increase in global competition from countries that do not have to comply with high standards similar to those in europe. the commission has not found any evidence that the union industry has been able to recover from past dumping. the commission has also concluded that the measures provided for in this decision are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of regulation (eu) no 525/2014. european trade defence measures for industrial metals are more of a belated remedy than a preventive measure. european trade policy cannot ignore the fact that these third countries exploit their relative advantage in terms of access to raw materials, often receive state aid and sometimes sell their products at prices below production costs. in the detailed vote, i supported the use of co2 adjustment measures at the border as an option. as a member of the hungarian people's party delegation, i supported the report because i believe that there is a need to renew european industrial policy.

in writing. ‒ the european steel industry has suffered huge losses in both capacity and jobs due to the fall in demand, which fell by 40 megatons in 2014 compared to 2007 levels. the capacity gap has reached such proportions that any renewed strengthening of european demand will create a deficit and create dependency unprecedented in the history of european trade, and the devastating impact of the loss of industrial know-how is certain to spill over into the upstream sectors, including passenger cars, construction and low-carbon technologies. we are in a period where emerging countries are developing their industrial metals industries (producing metals for which demand is again rising) and have thus become the main competitors on the world market for both steel and all industrial metals as well as rare earth metals, exploiting their relative advantage in terms of access to raw materials, sometimes coupled with the desire to sell them through state subsidies and dumping (i.e. selling below production costs). the eu needs to equip itself with flexible and reactive trade defence, adapting to the new global industrial environment, where the pace of decision-making needs to be accelerated in the face of the challenges posed by the potential proliferation of flows of raw materials and products, and of information and services. i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the report of the committee on industry draws attention to the problems of production and trade in industrial metals. the relatively high energy prices and the cost of carbon emissions severely limit the competitiveness of the european industrial metals industry on the global market, and this competitiveness is not improved by the very low investment in the european industrial metals industry for the same reasons. the report mentions the steel and aluminium industries as two major examples of the difficulties faced by industries that should be pursuing energy renewal and environmental modernisation in parallel. this would require an investment policy that few of them have the resources to pursue today. it considers the recycling of industrial metals and the creation of a circular economy to be absolutely vital, but points out that recycling alone cannot meet the future demands of europe as it embarks on the energy transition. in order to achieve the same installed capacity, wind and solar power plants consume 90 times more aluminium, 50 times more iron, copper and glass and 15 times more concrete (not to mention rare and critical metals) than conventional (oil, gas or nuclear-powered) thermal power plants currently in operation. the report seeks to address these very difficult problems, outlines possible solutions and recommends that parliament, in its resolution, urge a strong increase in efforts to address these concerns. i supported the report.

as the european union's action plan on human rights and democracy 2015-2019 shows, human rights are one of the most important pillars of our cooperation with the so-called third countries of the world. on an individual level, no one is arguing today that we need to make the world a place of basic human rights and protect the disenfranchised, the persecuted, the activists. but there is a collective dimension to this case. millions and millions of people around the world are persecuted because of their ethnic and/or religious affiliation, and they are violated in their collective rights as a minority. the rights of indigenous national minorities are not yet regulated in some countries of the union. even less so in the former communist countries of the eastern partnership, or in societies still under communist rule, and in most islamic countries. the plight of the tibetans and uighurs in china, as well as the unsustainable situation of christians who are being persecuted on a mass scale in the world, are striking examples. the excellent report by mr preda amongst other things identifies an important tool in eu enlargement policy for effectively enforcing human rights in the countries concerned. the countries of the western balkans, as well as the successor states of the former soviet empire, have an essential interest in breaking free from the legacy of communism and ensuring the human and community rights of all their citizens in accordance with the requirements of the union.
in writing. i would like to recall that the eu's enlargement policy is one of the most effective means of strengthening respect for human rights and democratic principles. i welcome the application of the new approach in the accession negotiations to the chapters on justice and fundamental rights and on freedom, security and justice, which takes due account of the time needed to properly implement the relevant reforms. the report shows that freedom of expression and freedom of the press are weakening in some accession countries and in many countries participating in the neighbourhood policy. freedom of expression and the media should continue to be monitored during the accession negotiations. the proper implementation of the legal framework for the protection of minorities remains a challenge. accession countries should step up their efforts to strengthen the culture of acceptance of minorities, for example by improving the involvement of minorities in decision-making processes and increasing their involvement in the education system. the report notes with concern the deterioration of the democratic political culture in some candidate and potential candidate countries, as well as in a number of countries participating in the european neighbourhood policy. i would like to recall that good governance, the rule of law, freedom of expression, respect for human rights, political dialogue, compromise and the involvement of all stakeholders in the decision-making process are at the heart of democratic systems.

madam president, my colleagues have already ably and wisely listed the political lessons and constitutional complications emerging from a peace accord which, at the time of its making, was both necessary and reasonable but which became dysfunctional over time. i would like to direct our attention to a different, and maybe even more broadly relevant, story and lesson from the 20-year history of the peace negotiations. we should bear in mind that the dayton process was the first resolution of a brutal – very brutal – war in the post-world war ii period in which international humanitarian law was not pushed into the background for the sake of a political deal. this was the first case of its kind after the second world war. indeed, no impunity was offered to those suspected of war crimes and crimes against humanity. had, for example, radovan karadžić not been indicted by the tribunal, he would have led the republika srpska delegation, and that would have meant that the peace negotiations would have collapsed before they started. so, for me, the lesson we should bear in mind is this: the policy of no impunity is not only the right policy – we all know that – but it is very often, at the same time, the best policy.

in writing. ‒ one of the important topics discussed by the european parliament today was the motion for a resolution on patents and plant breeding, which i also noted as a rapporteur and supported in the vote. the issue is food safety and it is therefore important to regulate it at european level. i believe that innovation, research and development should not be inhibited in any way, unless there is a risk to human or animal health. the european patent office should therefore help this process, and the intellectual property system is an important market- and competition-enhancing instrument. let's not forget that as a result of the work of ennoblement, we also produce public goods. it is important that the plant breeding sector has unrestricted access to biological material. in the interests of food security, biodiversity and adaptation to environmental change, i think farmers should even be allowed to produce their own seeds adapted to local conditions (if they meet certain criteria). this may be important in special cases such as organic farming. the regulation of this obviously needs to be improved: there is currently no coherence in the patent systems at eu or national level, plus there is no guarantee for plant breeders to have unlimited access to biological materials. in my speech i called for the relationship between this issue and ttip to be settled.

in writing. the democratic republic of congo is a vast country rich in both mineral and natural resources. as you know, it suffered unbridled exploitation during colonial times throughout its history. it is now formally a free country, but it remains threatened by the profiteering of multinational corporations. that's why i voted for the resolution that seeks to protect the national park by curbing mining. it may be time for the former colonialists to consider how they can at least partially compensate for their damage. we have only one earth, which is a unified ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo is africa's oldest national park, a unesco world heritage site, the most biodiverse park in africa and particularly famous for its mountain gorillas, which are listed as endangered in appendix i of the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) 1973. despite the park's status as a protected wilderness area, it has been threatened for decades by armed groups engaged in poaching, deforestation and other unsustainable and illegal forms of resource exploitation, which has resulted in virunga national park being declared a world heritage site in danger. the democratic republic of the congo (drc) has been in and around violent conflict for more than two decades and illegal mining, illegal exploitation of the park's natural resources (wood, charcoal) and poaching of endangered species, as well as other illegal trade in natural resources, are also sources of funding for rebels and the official army. the committee on development therefore proposes in its draft resolution to call on the european union, its member states, the european external action service, any relevant donors active in the drc and the drc authorities to do their utmost to protect the unique natural values of the park. i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution calls for the prevention of irreversible damage to virunga national park, which was declared a world heritage site by unesco in 1979 and a world heritage site in danger in 1994. the proposal seeks to draw attention to the irreversible damage that could be caused in virunga national park by illegal oil exploration and extraction activities. it also considers it unacceptable that the french oil company total and the british oil company soco international have obtained oil extraction rights in the national park, in breach of a number of international conventions. in view of all this, i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ virunga national park, located in the democratic republic of congo's north kivu province and orientale province on the border with rwanda and uganda, is africa's oldest national park and a unesco world heritage site. it is world-renowned for its unique habitats and rich biodiversity, being the most biodiverse park in africa. it is especially famous for its mountain gorillas. the european commission and some eu member states have provided support for the park's maintenance over the past 25 years. i voted for the resolution to protect him.
